functions.name: ProcessImeCompositionMessage
functions.comment:
Processes IME (Input Method Editor) composition messages for CJK text input.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 200-byte ANSI buffer (szAnsiBuffer) to zeros using REP STOSD
2. Call GetInitFlag() to retrieve HWND for IME context
3. Obtain IME context via ImmGetContext(hWnd)
4. If no IME context, skip to step 14
5. Initialize 64-element wchar_t buffer (awszWideBuffer) using Unicode default constructor
6. Check if GCS_RESULTSTR flag (0x800) is set in message lParam (offset 0xc):
   a. Query composition string length via ImmGetCompositionStringA(GCS_RESULTSTR)
   b. Clamp buffer length to 199 bytes max
   c. Retrieve composition result string into szAnsiBuffer
   d. Convert ANSI to Unicode via MultiByteToWideChar
   e. Concatenate to global input buffer if combined length < 127 chars
   f. Update g_dwStateFlags with string length
   g. Clear g_dwImeSecondaryState and g_awImeCompositionBuffer
7. Check if GCS_COMPSTR flag (0x8) is set in message lParam:
   a. Verify IME is open via ImmGetOpenStatus
   b. Query composition string length
   c. If length > 0, re-clear both buffers
   d. Clamp to 199 bytes and retrieve composition string
   e. Convert to Unicode via MultiByteToWideChar
   f. If converted length < 31, null-terminate at that position
   g. If length < 32, copy to g_awImeCompositionBuffer via strcpy
   h. Otherwise, truncate copy to 31 chars and call InitializeGameObjectProperties
8. Call GetInitFlag() again to get HWND
9. Release IME context via ImmReleaseContext
10. Set pMsgContext[0x18] = 1 (message handled flag)
11. Set pMsgContext[0x1c] = 0 (clear secondary status)
12. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to queue message context

Parameters:
  pMsgContext - Pointer to message context structure containing:
    +0x0c: LPARAM flags (GCS_RESULTSTR=0x800, GCS_COMPSTR=0x8)
    +0x18: Handled flag (set to 1 on completion)
    +0x1c: Secondary status (cleared to 0)
  IMPLICIT ESI - Pointer to source Unicode buffer (g_dwImeInputBuffer at 0x6fbf4554)
  IMPLICIT EDI - Pointer to destination Unicode buffer (g_dwInputStateFlags at 0x6fbf4350)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - If ImmGetContext returns NULL, skips all IME processing
  - Buffer overflow protection: composition strings clamped to 199 bytes
  - Unicode buffer limited to 32 wide characters (64 bytes)
  - Global buffer concatenation limited to 127 characters total

Magic Numbers:
  0x800 - GCS_RESULTSTR: Final composition result string
  0x8 - GCS_COMPSTR: Current composition string being edited
  0xc7 - 199: Maximum ANSI buffer size minus null terminator
  0x7f - 127: Maximum combined Unicode string length
  0x1f - 31: Maximum composition buffer length minus null
  0x20 - 32: Unicode buffer element count
  0x32 - 50: Loop counter for clearing 200-byte buffer (50 * 4 = 200)

Global Variables:
  g_dwStateFlags (0x6fbf55f4) - Accumulated string length counter
  g_dwImeSecondaryState (0x6fbf4554) - IME secondary state flag
  g_awImeCompositionBuffer (0x6fbf55a8) - Unicode composition buffer
  g_dwInputStateFlags (0x6fbf4350) - Input state tracking buffer
  g_wImeCompositionTerminator (0x6fbf55e6) - Composition terminator word

functions.name: InitializeImeStateAndRegisterNode
functions.comment:
Initializes IME (Input Method Editor) state to default values and registers a node in the cache system.

Classification: Initialization function

Algorithm:
1. Set IME open status flag to 1 (enabled)
2. Clear IME composition buffer to 0
3. Clear IME secondary state to 0
4. If language ID is English (9), set conversion mode to 4 (alphanumeric)
5. Set node field at offset +0x18 to 1 (active flag)
6. Set node field at offset +0x1c to 0 (clear state)
7. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to register node

Parameters:
  dwNodeHandle - Handle/pointer to node structure to initialize and register
                 Node structure fields:
                   +0x18: uint - Active flag (set to 1)
                   +0x1c: uint - State field (cleared to 0)

Returns:
  void

Globals Modified:
  g_dwImeOpenStatus (0x6fbf55e8) - Set to 1
  g_awImeCompositionBuffer (0x6fbf55a8) - Cleared to 0
  g_dwImeSecondaryState (0x6fbf4554) - Cleared to 0
  g_dwImeConversionMode (0x6fbf55fc) - Set to 4 if English

Special Cases:
  - Language ID 9 (English) triggers alphanumeric conversion mode (0x4)
  - Other languages retain existing conversion mode

Magic Numbers:
  9 - LANG_ENGLISH language ID
  4 - Alphanumeric IME conversion mode
  0x18, 0x1c - Node structure field offsets

functions.name: ResetImeStateAndInsertCacheNode
functions.comment:
Resets IME (Input Method Editor) state and inserts a cache node with a cookie value.

Algorithm:
1. Clear IME composition buffer (first word set to 0)
2. Clear IME secondary state flag
3. Set chat cursor position to 0xFFFFFFFE (invalid/reset state)
4. If language ID is 6 (Korean), clear IME open status flag
5. Set cache node field at offset +0x18 to 1 (mark active/valid)
6. Set cache node field at offset +0x1C to 0 (clear secondary field)
7. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to insert node into cache

Parameters:
  dwCookieValue - Cookie/identifier value for the cache node; also used as
                  base address for setting fields at offsets +0x18 and +0x1C

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Korean language (ID 6) receives additional IME open status reset
  - Cursor position 0xFFFFFFFE indicates no active cursor/reset state

Structure Layout (Cache Node accessed via dwCookieValue):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x18    4     dwActiveFlag    uint    1 = active, 0 = inactive
  0x1C    4     dwSecondary     uint    Secondary field, cleared on reset

Global State Modified:
  g_awImeCompositionBuffer (0x6fbf55a8) - First word cleared
  g_dwImeSecondaryState (0x6fbf4554) - Cleared to 0
  g_dwChatCursorPosition (0x6fbf55f8) - Set to 0xFFFFFFFE
  g_dwImeOpenStatus (0x6fbf55e8) - Cleared if Korean language

functions.name: ProcessImeNotification
functions.comment:
ProcessImeNotification - Handle IME notification messages for input method state changes

Algorithm:
1. Initialize context flags: set pImeContext[6]=1 (processed), pImeContext[7]=0 (no error)
2. Insert context into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
3. Get active window handle via GetInitFlag
4. Acquire IME context via ImmGetContext; exit early if NULL
5. Switch on notification type (pImeContext[2] - 2):
   - Case 2 (IMN_SETOPENSTATUS): Query keyboard layout, check if IME active, set conversion mode
   - Case 3 (IMN_OPENCANDIDATE): Get candidate list count and size for Japanese (lang=9)
   - Case 4 (IMN_CLOSECANDIDATE): Release candidate list allocation if present
   - Case 5 (IMN_CHANGECANDIDATE): Update candidate list - allocate, retrieve, validate
   - Case 6 (IMN_SETCONVERSIONMODE): Check conversion status for Chinese (7) or Korean (12)
   - Case 8 (IMN_SETSENTENCEMODE): Check open status for Simplified Chinese (6) or Japanese (9)
6. Release IME context via ImmReleaseContext before returning

Parameters:
- pImeContext: uint * - Pointer to IME context structure (24+ bytes)
  - [+0x08] (offset 2): Notification type code
  - [+0x18] (offset 6): Processed flag (set to 1)
  - [+0x1C] (offset 7): Error/result flag (set to 0)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Early exit if ImmGetContext returns NULL
- Language-specific handling based on g_dwLanguageId:
  - 6 = Simplified Chinese (zh-CN)
  - 7 = German/Chinese Traditional (zh-TW)
  - 9 = Japanese (ja-JP)
  - 12 = Korean (ko-KR)
- Candidate list with dwStyle=2 and dwCount=1 is released (single-char completion)

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x02: IMN_SETOPENSTATUS notification
- 0x03: IMN_OPENCANDIDATE notification
- 0x04: IMN_CLOSECANDIDATE notification
- 0x05: IMN_CHANGECANDIDATE notification
- 0x06: IMN_SETCONVERSIONMODE notification
- 0x08: IMN_SETSENTENCEMODE notification
- 0xDD (221): Line number for release allocation (before alloc)
- 0xDF (223): Line number for FogMemAlloc
- 0xE4 (228): Line number for release on single-char
- 0x13E (318): Line number for close candidate release

Globals Accessed:
- g_dwLanguageId (0x6fbf55ec): Current IME language identifier
- g_dwImeOpenStatus (0x6fbf55e8): IME open/active status byte
- g_dwImeConversionMode (0x6fbf55fc): Current conversion mode (0-4)
- g_pCandidateList (0x6fbf5600): Pointer to allocated CANDIDATELIST

Conversion Mode Values:
- 0: IME closed/disabled
- 1: Native input mode (Chinese/Korean)
- 3: Simplified Chinese open
- 4: Japanese IME open

functions.name: InitializeImeForLanguage
functions.comment:
Initialize IME (Input Method Editor) for current language environment

Algorithm:
1. Send initial message table (4 entries) to main window
2. Query active language configuration via Ordinal_10007
3. Validate language is IME-supported (6=Japanese, 7=Korean, 9=Chinese Traditional, 0xC=Korean Extended)
4. Initialize global IME state flags to 0
5. For Chinese Traditional (language 9):
   - Verify system language is 0x404 (Taiwan) or 0xC04 (Hong Kong)
   - If not IME-capable layout, simulate IME toggle hotkey (0x70)
   - Open IME context and set conversion mode to 4 (full-width)
6. For other languages (6, 7, 0xC):
   - Verify keyboard layout has IME capability
   - For Japanese (0x411): Open IME, set mode 3, send 7-message table
   - For Korean (0x412/0x812): Open IME, read/set conversion status, update mode flags
7. Send setup message table (7 entries) for confirmed IME languages
8. Release IME context handle

Parameters:
IMPLICIT EBX: Window handle (retrieved via Ordinal_10027)

Returns:
void - Updates global IME state flags

Special Cases:
- Early return if language not IME-supported (6, 7, 9, 0xC)
- Early return if IME context acquisition fails
- Japanese mode sets g_dwImeConversionMode to 3 on success, 0 on failure
- Korean mode sets g_dwImeConversionMode to 0 or 1 based on conversion status bit 0
- Chinese mode sets g_dwImeConversionMode to 4

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6 (6) - Japanese language ID
0x7 (7) - Korean language ID (variant 1)
0x9 (9) - Chinese Traditional language ID
0xC (12) - Korean language ID (variant 2)
0x404 (1028) - Taiwan Chinese LANGID
0xC04 (3076) - Hong Kong Chinese LANGID
0x411 (1041) - Japanese LANGID
0x412 (1042) - Korean LANGID
0x812 (2066) - Korean Extended LANGID
0x70 (112) - IME toggle hotkey ID
0x1 (1) - Conversion mode: Native input enabled
0x3 (3) - IME mode: Hiragana (Japanese)
0x4 (4) - IME mode: Full-width characters (Chinese)

Global State Updates:
g_dwActiveLanguageId - Set to Ordinal_10007 result (language configuration)
g_dwImeInitialized - Set to 1 after successful IME initialization
g_dwImeGlobalState - Reset to 0 at function start
g_dwImeSecondaryState - Reset to 0 at function start
g_dwImeOpenStatus - Set to 1 if IME opened successfully, 0 on failure
g_dwImeConversionMode - Language-specific mode (0, 1, 3, or 4)

Message Tables:
g_ImeInitMessageTable[4] - Initial 4-entry message sequence
g_ImeSetupMessageTable[7] - Setup 7-entry message sequence for IME activation

functions.name: DisableImeAndClearInputState
functions.comment:
Disables IME (Input Method Editor) and clears input state when transitioning UI modes

Algorithm:

1. Send basic UI initialization messages (4 messages from g_MessageArrayBasicUiInit)
2. If full UI mode enabled (g_bFullUiModeEnabled != 0):
   a. Send full UI initialization messages (7 messages from g_MessageArrayFullUiInit)
   b. Obtain IME context handle from window
   c. If IME context valid:
      - Disable IME open status
      - For Japanese (0x07) or Korean (0x0C) language IDs:
        * Get current conversion and sentence modes
        * Clear conversion mode to 0 (disable all IME conversion)
      - Release IME context handle
   d. Clear input state flags (g_dwInputStateFlags = 0)
   e. Clear IME composition state (g_dwImeCompositionState = 0)
   f. If timer active (g_dwTimerActive != 0):
      - Kill timer 600
      - Clear timer active flag

Parameters:

None (void function)

Returns:

void

Special Cases:

Language ID 0x07 (Japanese) and 0x0C (Korean) require IME conversion mode reset
Timer ID 600 is killed only when g_dwTimerActive flag is set

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x07 - Japanese language ID (LANG_JAPANESE)
0x0C - Korean language ID (LANG_KOREAN)
600 - Timer identifier for IME-related periodic events
0 - ImmSetOpenStatus FALSE parameter (disable IME)
0 - ImmSetConversionStatus mode parameter (clear all conversion modes)

Error Handling:

No error return - operates silently
If ImmGetContext returns NULL, IME operations skipped
MessageArray processing errors handled by ProcessMessageArray callee

functions.name: RenderChatInputInterface
functions.comment:
Renders the in-game chat input interface with multilingual text support and cursor animation

Algorithm:

1. Save current font context via SetActiveFont(0xd) and check if IME is enabled (g_bImeEnabled)
2. Initialize Unicode text buffer (20 ushorts) for input mode indicator display
3. Switch on language setting (g_dwImeInputMode) to display appropriate input mode text:
   - Case 0 (English): Convert "Alphanumeric" string to Unicode, position at screen_height - 0x80
   - Case 1 (Korean): Set hardcoded Unicode for Korean input mode (0xd55c, 0xae00)
   - Case 2/3 (Japanese): Set hardcoded Unicode for Japanese input mode (0x65e5, 0x672c, 0x8a9e)
   - Case 4 (Chinese): Set Chinese character (0x6f22), then render line history if available
4. For Chinese mode with line history (g_pChatLineHistoryList != NULL):
   - Calculate visible line range from history buffer (fields at +0x8, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18)
   - Limit display to 20 lines maximum
   - Loop through visible lines and render each with 15-pixel vertical spacing
   - Convert multibyte strings to wide characters using MultiByteToWideChar
5. Increment frame counter (g_dwChatInputFrameCounter) and render chat input box frame
6. Check if game system is enabled; if so, call ProcessUIStateChange(5, 1, 0)
7. Process input string if present (from implicit EDI register parameter):
   - Convert to Unicode in 512-ushort buffer
   - Word-wrap text using WrapUnicodeText with max width (screen_width - 0x109)
   - Render each wrapped line with 15-pixel vertical spacing at Y = screen_height - 0x58
   - If final line and IME composition active (g_bImeCompositionActive), draw cursor
8. Update cursor blink animation using GetTickCount:
   - Compare elapsed time against g_wCursorBlinkInterval
   - Toggle g_dwCursorVisibleState between 0 and 1
   - Update g_dwLastCursorBlinkTick with current tick
   - Use 100ms interval when visible, 500ms when hidden
9. Restore original font context via SetActiveFont

Parameters:

IMPLICIT ESI (uint cbInputStringLength): Length of input string in bytes
IMPLICIT EDI (char * lpszInputString): Pointer to current input string being typed

Returns:

void

Special Cases:

- If g_bImeEnabled is 0 (chat disabled), function only increments frame counter
- Chinese mode (case 4) is the only language that renders historical chat lines
- Word wrapping stops after 3 lines maximum
- Cursor animation uses alternating intervals: 500ms hidden, 100ms visible

Magic Numbers Reference:

functions.name: RenderBlinkingCursorForIme
functions.comment:
Render blinking cursor at specified position for IME text input.

Algorithm:

1. Calculate initial text width by calling strlen on implicit text parameter (EDI)
2. If text exists (length > 0):
   a. Get text width from Ordinal_10121
   b. Check if text extends beyond right screen boundary (g_dwScreenWidth - 0x109)
   c. If overflow detected, reset X position to 0x83 and advance Y by 0xf (15 pixels)
   d. Set render position with Ordinal_10117(nTextYPos, 4, 0)
3. Calculate second text width measurement with Ordinal_10121
4. Call strlen again to verify text length
5. If text still exists:
   a. Perform second boundary check with accumulated widths
   b. If overflow, advance Y position by 0xf
   c. Set render position again with Ordinal_10117
6. If global blink state flag (DAT_6fbb24ec) is 1:
   a. Call Ordinal_10004 to render cursor glyph
   b. Call Ordinal_10117 to finalize rendering
7. Get current system tick count with GetTickCount
8. Compare elapsed time against blink interval (DAT_6fbb24f0 & 0xffff):
   a. If interval expired:
      - Update last tick timestamp (DAT_6fbf5608)
      - Toggle blink state and update interval
      - If currently visible (DAT_6fbb24ec == 1): Hide cursor, set interval to 100ms
      - If currently hidden (DAT_6fbb24ec == 0): Show cursor, set interval to 500ms

Parameters:

nTextXPos (ECX) - Horizontal pixel position for text/cursor rendering
nTextYPos (EDX) - Vertical pixel position for text/cursor rendering

IMPLICIT:
lpszText (EDI) - Pointer to text string for width calculation (char *)

Returns:

void - No return value

Special Cases:

- If text string is empty (length 0), skips boundary checking and positioning
- Cursor blink uses asymmetric timing: 500ms visible, 100ms hidden
- Screen boundary constant 0x109 (265 decimal) represents right margin offset
- X position 0x83 (131 decimal) is left margin after line wrap
- Y increment 0xf (15 decimal) is line height for wrapping

Magic Numbers Reference:

functions.name: NavigateChatHistoryByKeycode
functions.comment:
Navigates chat history buffer in response to Up/Down arrow key presses.

Classification: Worker function - handles UI input for chat history navigation

Algorithm:
1. Set cache node fields: node+0x18 = 1 (active), node+0x1c = 0 (clear)
2. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to register the node
3. Check flag at node+0xc for bit 0x40000000 - if set, skip navigation and exit
4. Read keycode from node+0x8:
   - 0x26 (VK_UP): Navigate to NEXT entry in history (older)
   - 0x28 (VK_DOWN): Navigate to PREVIOUS entry in history (newer)
5. For VK_UP (0x26):
   a. Copy history entry at g_dwChatHistoryIndex to g_abChatInputBuffer (0x202 bytes = 257 wchar_t)
   b. Update g_dwChatInputLength with strlen of copied string
   c. Increment history index with wraparound: if >= 8, wrap to 0; if < 0, wrap to 7
   d. Check boundary: if g_wChatHistoryCount < 7 AND (8 - newIndex) > count, restore original index
6. For VK_DOWN (0x28):
   a. Decrement history index with wraparound (same logic as increment)
   b. Check boundary condition
   c. Copy history entry to input buffer
   d. Update input length
7. Update g_dwChatHistoryIndex with final calculated index

Parameters:
   pCacheNode - Pointer to cache node structure containing:
      +0x08: uint dwKeycode - Virtual key code (0x26=Up, 0x28=Down)
      +0x0C: uint dwFlags - Control flags, bit 0x40000000 disables navigation
      +0x18: uint dwActive - Set to 1 on entry
      +0x1C: uint dwReserved - Cleared to 0 on entry

Returns: void

Special Cases:
   - Flag 0x40000000 at node+0xc bypasses all navigation (early exit)
   - Keycodes other than 0x26 or 0x28 cause early exit with no navigation
   - Circular buffer of 8 entries (indices 0-7) with wraparound
   - Boundary check prevents navigation past valid history entries

Magic Numbers:
   0x26 - VK_UP (Windows virtual key code for Up arrow)
   0x28 - VK_DOWN (Windows virtual key code for Down arrow)
   0x40000000 - Control flag that disables history navigation
   0x202 - History entry size in bytes (257 wchar_t = 514 bytes, 0x202 hex)
   0x80 - DWORD count for REP MOVSD (128 DWORDs = 512 bytes)
   8 - Maximum history entries in circular buffer

Global Data:
   g_dwChatHistoryIndex (0x6fbf4594) - Current position in circular history buffer
   g_awszChatHistoryBuffer (0x6fbf4598) - Array of 8 wide string history entries
   g_abChatInputBuffer (0x6fbf4350) - Current chat input buffer (copied to/from)
   g_wChatHistoryCount (0x6fbf55f0) - Number of valid entries in history
   g_dwChatInputLength (0x6fbf55f4) - Length of current input string

functions.name: ParseChatCommandPrefix
functions.signature: bool ParseChatCommandPrefix(char * * lpszInputText, byte * pbCommandType, byte * pbOutputBuffer)
functions.comment:
Parses chat input to identify and extract a command prefix from a predefined command table.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output buffer to empty string
2. Copy input text to local buffer (max 256 chars)
3. Get current server port via GetCurrentServerPort
4. If not connected to server (port == 0), return FALSE
5. Iterate through command prefix table at 0x6FBB24F8 (5 entries, 10 bytes each)
6. For each entry, get prefix string length via SStrLen
7. Compare match type at offset +4:
   - Type 3 (exact): Input length must equal prefix length, compare with SStrCmpNI
   - Type 1 (prefix): Input length must exceed prefix length, compare prefix portion
8. On match, extract command type byte from table offset +4
9. If format string at offset +6 exists, parse next token and validate length <= 16
10. Advance input pointer past consumed prefix and optional format
11. Return TRUE on successful match, FALSE if no match found

Parameters:
  lpszInputText - [in/out] Pointer to input string pointer, advanced past matched prefix
  pbCommandType - [out] Receives command type byte (0-4) from matched table entry
  pbOutputBuffer - [out] Receives parsed format token if applicable (max 16 chars)

Returns:
  TRUE (1) - Command prefix matched and extracted successfully
  FALSE (0) - No matching prefix found or not connected to server

Command Prefix Table Structure (10 bytes per entry):
  Offset 0x00: char* szPrefix - Command prefix string pointer
  Offset 0x04: word wMatchType - Match type (1=prefix, 3=exact)
  Offset 0x06: char* szFormat - Optional format string for token parsing

Magic Numbers:
  0x6FBB24F8 - Command prefix table base address
  0x6FBB252A - Command prefix table end address (5 entries)
  0x100 (256) - Input buffer size
  0x10 (16) - Maximum format token length

functions.name: ParseBattleNetChatCommand
functions.comment:
Parse and execute BattleNet chat command with case-insensitive prefix matching

Algorithm:
1. Calculate length of lpszCommandName using manual strlen loop
2. Calculate length of pbInputBuffer using manual strlen loop  
3. Verify lpszCommandName length is less than or equal to pbInputBuffer length
4. Perform case-insensitive character-by-character comparison of prefix
5. Check character after prefix is space (0x20) or null terminator
6. Tokenize remaining input using space delimiter (0x0020 from g_wSpaceDelimiter)
7. Verify exactly one token remains after command name
8. If valid, call GetGameInterface and execute function pointer at offset +0x14
9. If invalid token count, format error message with correct usage template
10. Copy error message to secondary buffer and call message display function

Parameters:
  pbInputBuffer (byte *) - Input chat command buffer to parse
  lpszCommandName (char *) - Expected command name for prefix matching

IMPLICIT:
  ECX - pbInputBuffer passed in ECX register (__fastcall)
  EDX - lpszCommandName passed in EDX register (__fastcall)

Returns:
  1 (true) - Command matched prefix and was processed (success or error displayed)
  0 (false) - Command prefix did not match lpszCommandName

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 if lpszCommandName longer than pbInputBuffer
  - Returns 0 if case-insensitive comparison fails at any character
  - Returns 0 if character after prefix is not space or null
  - Returns 1 even if error message displayed (command was recognized)
  - Tokenization allows maximum 2 tokens total (command + 1 argument)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x20 (32) - ASCII space character for delimiter and validation
  0x0020 - Word-sized space delimiter loaded from g_wSpaceDelimiter at 0x6fbb25d8
  0xFFFFFFFF - Initial value for strlen countdown loop
  0x14 (20) - Offset to function pointer in GameInterface structure
  0x40 (64) - Loop counter for 256-byte buffer copy (64 dwords = 256 bytes)
  0x6fbb25f8 - Address of error message template "<BattleNet>: Correct usage is: %s"
  0x4 - Message priority value for error display
  0x3 - Message flags value for error display

Error Handling:
  - If tokenization yields 0 tokens or >1 tokens, displays usage error
  - Error message formatted with lpszCommandName as parameter
  - Error display uses FUN_6fb9a261 (sprintf-like) and FUN_6fb58150 (message display)
  - Function returns 1 after displaying error (command was recognized)

functions.name: ProcessWhisperCommand
functions.signature: int ProcessWhisperCommand(byte * pbCommandText, char * lpszCommandKeyword, int nValidatePlayer)
functions.comment:
Process Battle.net whisper command and send message to target player

Algorithm:

1. Calculate command keyword length using strlen-style loop (REPNE SCASB)
2. Calculate command text buffer length
3. Verify command text starts with command keyword (case-insensitive comparison)
4. Check if command text exceeds keyword length (has arguments)
5. Parse command arguments by tokenizing with space delimiter
   - Token 1: Target player name
   - Token 2: Message text
   - Token 3+: Additional message words (concatenated to token 2)
6. If exactly 2 tokens found, copy target name to abTargetNameBuffer
7. If 3 or more tokens found, calculate message offset and copy to szMessageText
8. If token count != 3, show usage error message "<BattleNet>: Correct usage is: %s (name) (message)"
9. If nValidatePlayer flag set, iterate through player roster to validate target exists
10. If target player found or validation disabled, build whisper packet and compress
11. If target not found, show error "%s %s %s" with player name
12. Call game interface method to transmit packet

Parameters:

pbCommandText - Pointer to command text buffer (e.g., "/w PlayerName Hello")
lpszCommandKeyword - Command keyword to match (e.g., "/whisper", "/w")
nValidatePlayer - Flag: 1 = validate target player exists in roster, 0 = skip validation

Returns:

1 - Command processed successfully (whisper sent or error displayed)
0 - Command validation failed (command text doesn't start with keyword or insufficient length)

Special Cases:

- If command text ends with space (0x20) or null (0x00), enters whisper processing
- Token parsing uses strtok-like function (FUN_6fb9ab79) with space delimiter (0x20)
- Case-insensitive command matching uses tolower function (FUN_6fb9ac1d)
- Validates player name against roster using GetRosterFieldAt0x66 comparison

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x20 - Space character delimiter for token parsing
0x02 - Packet type identifier in byPacketId2 field
0x03 - Packet subtype identifier in byPacketId3 field  
0x04 - Packet header identifier in byPacketId1 field
0x15 - Whisper packet opcode at abMessageBuffer[0]
0xFF - Maximum message length for strncpy truncation (255 bytes)

Structure Layout:

Whisper Packet Format (abMessageBuffer):
Offset  Size  Field Name         Type    Description
------  ----  -----------------  ------  ------------------------------------
0x00    1     byOpcode           byte    Packet opcode (0x15 = whisper)
0x01    1     byPacketType       byte    Packet type (0x02)
0x02    1     byLanguageId       byte    Language ID from g_dwLanguageId
0x03    N     szTargetName       char[]  Null-terminated target player name
N+3     M     szMessageText      char[]  Null-terminated message text

1. Check UI resource 0x0C (12 decimal) - first panel type
2. If resource exists (non-zero), return early (UI already loaded)
3. Check UI resource 0x17 (23 decimal) - second panel type  
4. If resource exists (non-zero), return early
5. Check UI resource 0x19 (25 decimal) - third panel type
6. If resource exists (non-zero), return early
7. If none exist, tail-call CheckExpansionMpqExists to validate expansion data

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No explicit return value; performs side effects via tail call

Special Cases:
- Early return if ANY of the three UI resources are valid (non-zero)
- Tail-call optimization to CheckExpansionMpqExists if no UI panels loaded
- No callers found - likely called via function pointer table or vtable

Magic Numbers:
- 0x0C (12) - UI resource ID for first panel type
- 0x17 (23) - UI resource ID for second panel type  
- 0x19 (25) - UI resource ID for third panel type

Function Classification: Leaf validation function - checks UI state before expansion check

functions.name: ProcessIdleTransitionHandler
functions.comment:
Processes idle state transition for player unit when stationary.

Classification: Callback/Handler - invoked by game loop or event system

Algorithm:
1. Clear global DWORD value to 0 (SetGlobalDwordValue(0))
2. Retrieve game context pointer (GetGameContext)
3. If no game context, exit early
4. Check always-run setting (GetAlwaysRunSetting)
5. If always-run is enabled (EAX != 0), exit early
6. Check unit type at offset +0x00, must be 0 (player type)
7. Check unit state at offset +0x0C, must be 3 (idle state)
8. If all conditions met:
   a. Call ClearUnitStateAndProcessTransition(pUnit, 2) - transition type 2
   b. Call QuerySystemInfoAndIncrementCounters with counter ID 0x54

Parameters: None (void)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Early exit if game context is NULL
- Early exit if always-run setting is enabled
- Early exit if unit type is not 0 (non-player unit)
- Early exit if unit state is not 3 (not in idle state)

Structure Layout (Unit at ESI):
Offset  Size  Field         Type  Description
0x00    4     dwUnitType    uint  Unit type identifier (0 = player)
0x0C    4     dwUnitState   uint  Current unit state (3 = idle)

Magic Numbers:
- 0: SetGlobalDwordValue parameter (clear value)
- 2: Transition type for ClearUnitStateAndProcessTransition
- 3: Idle state identifier in unit state field
- 0x54: Counter ID for QuerySystemInfoAndIncrementCounters

functions.name: EnableProcessingFlagBit0
functions.comment:
Thunk to enable bit 0 of the global processing flags.

Algorithm:
1. Set ECX to 0 (fDisable = false)
2. Jump to SetProcessingFlagBit0 to set bit 0 of g_dwProcessingFlags

Parameters:
- None (void function)

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- This is a tail-call thunk that passes 0 to SetProcessingFlagBit0
- Passing 0 causes bit 0 to be SET (enabled) via OR with 0x1
- Referenced from data at 0x6fbafa14 (likely function pointer table)

functions.name: ResetUIElement13AndClearSelection
functions.comment:
Deactivates UI element 0x0D and clears unit selection state.

Algorithm:
1. Call ProcessUIStateChange(0xD, 1, 0) to deactivate UI element 13
2. Tail-call ClearUnitSelectionState to reset selection flags

Parameters:
None (void function)

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- No callers found (orphan or callback registration)
- UI element 0x0D corresponds to a specific panel type
- nUIState=1 means deactivate in ProcessUIStateChange

Magic Numbers:
0x0D (13) - UI element ID being deactivated
0x1 - nUIState value for deactivation
0x0 - nScrollParam (no scroll adjustment)

functions.name: InvokeMouse3DownCallback
functions.comment:
Validate and invoke the mouse button 3 down event callback handler.

Algorithm:

1. Check if mouse3 down handler pointer is NULL, return early if unset
2. Validate handler is valid code pointer using IsBadCodePtr
3. If pointer is invalid (function moved/unloaded), trigger fatal assertion
4. Call error reporting function with callback name and source location
5. Terminate process with exit code -1
6. If pointer is valid, invoke the callback handler via indirect call

Parameters:

None (implicit: uses global g_pfnMouse3DownHandler function pointer)

Returns:

void - No return value (either invokes callback or terminates process)

Special Cases:

- If g_pfnMouse3DownHandler is NULL, function returns immediately without error
- If callback pointer is invalid code (unloaded DLL), triggers assertion failure
- Indirect jump at 0x6fafd8a2 prevents Ghidra from recovering normal control flow

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x336 (822 decimal) - Line number in CmdTbl.cpp where assertion fires
0xffffffff (-1) - Process termination exit code for fatal callback error

Error Handling:

- NULL pointer check: Silent early return allows graceful handling of unset callback
- Invalid code pointer: Calls Ordinal_10023 assertion function with diagnostic info
- Assertion provides callback name "sgpfnMouse3DownFn" and source file location
- Process termination via FUN_6fb9a10f ensures no continuation after fatal error

functions.name: InvokeMouse3LiftCallback
functions.comment:
Validates and invokes the registered Mouse3 lift callback function.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pfnMouse3LiftCallback is NULL
2. Return immediately if no callback is registered
3. Validate callback pointer with IsBadCodePtr
4. If pointer is invalid (not in executable memory):
   a. Call assertion handler with debug info (file: CmdTbl.cpp, line: 834)
   b. Terminate process with exit code -1
5. Invoke the callback via indirect jump

Parameters:
None (void function with no parameters)

Returns:
void - No return value under normal conditions. Does not return if callback
pointer validation fails (process termination occurs).

Special Cases:
- Early return if g_pfnMouse3LiftCallback is NULL (no callback registered)
- Fatal error path if IsBadCodePtr detects invalid function pointer
- Assertion context: CmdTbl.cpp:834, variable 'sgpfnMouse3LiftFn'
- Uses indirect JMP instead of CALL for tail-call optimization

functions.name: InvokeMouse4DownCallback
functions.comment:
Validates and invokes the registered Mouse4 down callback function.

Algorithm:
1. Check if Mouse4 down callback pointer is NULL, return immediately if NULL
2. Validate function pointer with IsBadCodePtr to ensure it points to executable memory
3. If pointer validation fails, call assertion handler with debugging information and terminate
4. Perform indirect jump to invoke the registered callback function

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value. Terminates process if callback pointer is invalid.

Special Cases:
- Returns immediately if g_pfnMouse4DownCallback is NULL (no handler registered)
- Calls Ordinal_10023 assertion handler with file/line/variable info if pointer is invalid
- Error context: CmdTbl.cpp:845 (0x34d) with variable name 'sgpfnMouse4DownFn'
- Terminates process with exit code -1 (0xffffffff) if validation fails

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x34d (845) - Line number in CmdTbl.cpp source file
0xffffffff (-1) - Process termination exit code indicating fatal error

functions.name: InvokeMouse4LiftCallback
functions.comment:
Invokes registered mouse button 4 (side button) lift callback with validation

Algorithm:
1. Check if callback pointer g_pfnMouse4LiftCallback is NULL
2. If NULL, return immediately (no callback registered)
3. Validate callback pointer using IsBadCodePtr to ensure it points to executable code
4. If pointer is invalid (IsBadCodePtr returns non-zero):
   - Call Ordinal_10023 assertion handler with source file and line number
   - Terminate process with FUN_6fb9a10f(-1)
5. If pointer is valid, invoke callback function indirectly via function pointer

Parameters:
  (none)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - 0x35a: Line number in CmdTbl.cpp where callback is expected to be valid
  - Indirect jump at 0x6fafd962 calls the validated function pointer

Error Handling:
  - NULL callback pointer: Early return without error
  - Invalid callback pointer: Triggers assertion with source location and terminates process
  - Assertion function Ordinal_10023 logs source file s_sgpfnMouse4LiftFn_6fbb2e4c
  - Process termination via FUN_6fb9a10f with exit code -1 (0xffffffff)

functions.name: InvokeMouse5DownCallback
functions.comment:
Invoke the registered mouse button 5 down callback function.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pfnMouse5DownCallback is NULL and return early if unregistered
2. Validate callback pointer is valid executable code using IsBadCodePtr
3. If callback pointer is invalid, trigger assertion failure with Ordinal_10023
4. Call FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) to terminate process after assertion
5. Execute the registered callback function via indirect call

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void - No return value (function either executes callback or terminates)

Special Cases:
  - Early return if g_pfnMouse5DownCallback is NULL (0x0)
  - Assertion failure if callback pointer is invalid (not executable code)
  - 0x366 (870 decimal) - Line number in source file for assertion
  - 0xffffffff (-1) - Termination exit code passed to FUN_6fb9a10f

Error Handling:
  - Invalid callback pointer triggers assertion with function name "sgpfnMouse5DownFn"
  - Process termination via FUN_6fb9a10f on invalid callback
  - IsBadCodePtr validation prevents execution of invalid function pointers

functions.name: InvokeMouse5LiftCallback
functions.comment:
Invokes the registered Mouse Button 5 lift callback function pointer with validation.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pfnMouse5LiftCallback is NULL
2. If NULL, return early (no callback registered)
3. Validate callback pointer using IsBadCodePtr()
4. If pointer is invalid (bad code address):
   a. Call Ordinal_10023 error handler with source location
   b. Pass "sgpfnMouse5LiftFn" variable name, file path, line 0x372
   c. Terminate process with FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff)
5. If pointer is valid, invoke callback function via indirect call
6. Return to caller

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Note: Function does not return if callback pointer validation fails (terminates process)

Special Cases:
  - NULL callback pointer: Silent early return (normal case when no handler registered)
  - Invalid callback pointer: Fatal error with debug info, process termination
  - Valid callback pointer: Executes user-registered callback function

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x372 (882 decimal) - Source line number in CmdTbl.cpp where validation occurs

Error Handling:
  - Validation Failure: IsBadCodePtr returns non-zero
    -> Triggers Ordinal_10023 with file "C:\Projects\Diablo2\Source\D2Client\Ui\CmdTbl.cpp"
    -> Passes variable name "sgpfnMouse5LiftFn" for debugging context
    -> Calls FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) which does not return (process termination)

Global Data References:
  g_pfnMouse5LiftCallback (0x6fbf5610) - Function pointer to mouse button 5 lift handler
    - Type: void (*)(void) function pointer
    - Initialized to NULL in mouse callback initialization
    - Set by external registration function
    - Called when mouse button 5 is released

functions.name: DispatchMouseWheelEvent
functions.comment:
Dispatch mouse wheel event to registered callback handlers based on wheel direction.

Algorithm:

1. Check wheel direction parameter (nWheelDelta)
2. If nWheelDelta > 0, handle mouse wheel up event:
   a. Check if g_pfnMouseWheelUpHandler is registered (non-NULL)
   b. Validate function pointer with IsBadCodePtr
   c. If pointer invalid, report error via Ordinal_10023 with "sgpfnMouseWheelUpFn" and terminate
   d. If valid, invoke g_pfnMouseWheelUpHandler callback
3. If nWheelDelta < 0, handle mouse wheel down event:
   a. Check if g_pfnMouseWheelDownHandler is registered (non-NULL)
   b. Validate function pointer with IsBadCodePtr
   c. If pointer invalid, report error via Ordinal_10023 with "sgpfnMouseWheelDownFn" and terminate
   d. If valid, invoke g_pfnMouseWheelDownHandler callback
4. If nWheelDelta == 0, return without action

Parameters:

nWheelDelta (int) - Mouse wheel rotation delta: positive for upward scroll, negative for downward scroll, zero for no scroll

Returns:

void - No return value (callbacks invoked directly)

Special Cases:

- If nWheelDelta == 0, function returns early without invoking any callbacks
- If callback pointer is NULL, function returns without error
- If callback pointer is non-NULL but invalid (IsBadCodePtr returns true), triggers fatal error through Ordinal_10023

Error Handling:

- Invalid function pointer detected: Calls Ordinal_10023 with debug string and source location (0x380 for wheel up, 0x388 for wheel down)
- After error reporting, calls FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) to terminate execution
- No recovery path - invalid pointers cause immediate termination

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x380 (896 decimal) - Source line number for mouse wheel up handler validation
0x388 (904 decimal) - Source line number for mouse wheel down handler validation
0xffffffff (-1 signed) - Termination error code passed to FUN_6fb9a10f

functions.name: InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks
functions.comment:
Initialize mouse button callback function pointers by scanning key binding table.

Algorithm:
1. Clear all mouse button callback globals (buttons 3, 4, 5 down/lift)
2. Initialize pointer to key binding table at 0x6fbf5628
3. Iterate through key binding entries (10-byte stride) until end at 0x6fbf5a9c
4. For each entry, check if button type ID > 0xDF and key code < 0x39
5. Calculate button type offset by subtracting 0x100 from button type ID
6. Use offset (0-4) as switch index to determine which button callbacks to set
7. Each case validates button availability then assigns callbacks from lookup table
8. Set appropriate global function pointer pair based on button type offset
9. Continue iteration until end of key binding table

Parameters:
  None (implicit: Key binding table at 0x6fbf5628)

IMPLICIT:
  Key binding table at 0x6fbf5628 with 10-byte stride entries

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Button type IDs <= 0xDF are skipped (not mouse buttons 3/4/5)
  - Key codes >= 0x39 (57 decimal) are skipped (out of valid range)
  - Switch covers offsets 0-4 mapping to buttons: 0=Mouse3, 1=Mouse4, 2=Mouse5, 3=Unknown, 4=Unknown
  - Jump tables at 0x6fafdef4, 0x6fafdf08, 0x6fafdf1c, 0x6fafdf30, 0x6fafdf44 contain validation routines

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0xDF (223): Minimum button type ID threshold for mouse buttons 3/4/5
  0x100 (256): Base offset subtracted from button type ID to get switch index
  0x39 (57): Maximum valid key code value
  0x6fbf5628: Start address of key binding table
  0x6fbf5a9c: End address of key binding table (1140 bytes = 114 entries)
  0x6fbb2ad8: Base address of callback function pointer lookup table
  10 (0xA): Stride between key binding entries

Key Binding Entry Structure:
  Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type   | Description
  -------|------|-----------------|--------|----------------------------------
  0x00   | 4    | dwKeyCode       | uint   | Key code for binding
  0x04   | 2    | wButtonTypeId   | ushort | Button type identifier
  0x06   | 4    | padding         | byte[4]| Unused padding

Global Variables Set:
  g_pfnMouse3DownHandler @ 0x6fbf5f14 - Mouse button 3 down callback
  g_pfnMouse3LiftCallback @ 0x6fbf5f18 - Mouse button 3 lift callback
  g_pfnMouse4DownCallback @ 0x6fbf5a9c - Mouse button 4 down callback
  g_pfnMouse4LiftCallback @ 0x6fbf5624 - Mouse button 4 lift callback
  g_pfnMouse5DownCallback @ 0x6fbf561c - Mouse button 5 down callback
  g_pfnMouse5LiftCallback @ 0x6fbf5610 - Mouse button 5 lift callback
  DAT_6fbf5f1c - Additional mouse callback (button type offset 3)
  DAT_6fbf5620 - Additional mouse callback (button type offset 4)

functions.name: ProcessKeyboardBindingStrings
functions.comment:
Builds and opens keyboard binding configuration file paths.

Constructs paths to .key files using save directory and optional alternate path.
Initializes three MAX_PATH (260-byte) stack buffers and attempts to create/open 
the keyboard binding file at the constructed path.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x30c bytes stack space for three MAX_PATH buffers
2. Copy save path prefix byte (g_bySavePathPrefix) to initialize all buffers
3. Zero-fill remainder of all three buffers via REP STOSD
4. Call GetSaveDirectoryPath to get base save directory into buffer1
5. Check g_szAlternateSavePath flag:
   - If set: Format alternate path, create directory, then create file
   - If not set: Skip to default path
6. Format final path as "<savepath><name>.key" using FormatString
7. Call CreateFileWrapper to open/create the .key file
8. Return (file handle in EAX on success, -1 on failure)

Parameters:
  nFirstParam (ECX): First parameter passed to CreateFileWrapper
  nSecondParam (EDX): Second parameter passed to CreateFileWrapper

Returns:
  void (file handle stored in hFileHandle local)

Callees:
  GetSaveDirectoryPath - Gets base save directory path
  FormatString (Ordinal_578) - Formats path strings with %s patterns
  CreateDirectoryRecursive (Ordinal_10114) - Creates directory tree
  CreateFileWrapper (Ordinal_10115/10107) - Opens/creates keyboard binding file

Phantom Variables (cannot be typed via decompiler - assembly-only):
  dwPathBuffer1Start [ESP+0x214] - char[260] save directory path buffer
  dwPathBuffer2Start [ESP+0xc] - char[260] formatted key file path buffer  
  dwPathBuffer3Start [ESP+0x110] - char[260] intermediate path buffer

Globals:
  g_bySavePathPrefix (0x6fbdc134) - First byte/drive letter for save paths
  g_szAlternateSavePath (0x6fbe90ec) - Alternate save path string (if set)

functions.name: PlayVideoFromStructure
functions.comment:
Save current keyboard bindings to registry and optionally to default.key file.

Algorithm:
1. Open registry key for keybinding data using FUN_6fafdf60(0x40000000, 2) - write access
2. If registry open fails (returns -1), exit without saving
3. Initialize local binding buffer (285 dwords = 1140 bytes) to zero
4. Set binding count header to 0x25 (37 entries)
5. Initialize all 114 key entry slots to 0xFFFF (unbound sentinel)
6. Copy current keybindings from g_KeyBindingTable to local buffer (285 dwords)
7. Write 0x476 bytes (1142) to registry via Ordinal_10111
8. Close registry handle via Ordinal_10109
9. Get base path string via Ordinal_10116 into szFilePath
10. Calculate length of "default.key" filename string
11. Find end of szFilePath string (strlen)
12. Append "default.key" to szFilePath (memcpy in dword+byte chunks)
13. Open/create file handle via Ordinal_10107(0, 0, 2, 0x80, 0)
14. If file open fails (returns -1), skip file write
15. Set file header: wFileMagic=0x5357 ("SW"), wEntryCount=0x25, wDataSize=0x47a
16. Write 6-byte header to file via Ordinal_10111
17. Write 0x474 bytes (1140) binding data via Ordinal_10111
18. Close file handle via Ordinal_10109

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - Function completes silently, errors handled by early returns

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x40000000 - HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE registry root (passed to FUN_6fafdf60)
0x11d (285) - Number of dwords in keybinding table (1140 bytes / 4)
0x25 (37) - Expected number of keybinding entries in header
0x72 (114) - Total keybinding slots (114 entries x 10 bytes stride)
0xFFFF - Sentinel value for unbound/empty keybinding slot
0x476 (1142) - Total bytes to write to registry (6 header + 1136 data)
0x5357 - File magic "SW" (little-endian) identifying key binding file
0x47a (1146) - File data size indicator in header
0x474 (1140) - Actual binding data bytes written to file
0x80 - File creation flags for Ordinal_10107
2 - Write mode flag for FUN_6fafdf60 and Ordinal_10107

Related Functions:
- LoadKeyboardBindings() - Caller that loads bindings before this saves them
- FUN_6fafdf60() - Opens registry key with specified access mode
- Ordinal_10107 - Creates/opens file handle for keybinding file
- Ordinal_10109 - Closes registry/file handle
- Ordinal_10111 - Writes data buffer to registry/file
- Ordinal_10116 - Gets game path string for building file path

functions.name: DisablePanelMessageState
functions.comment:
Disables panel message state by calling SetPanelMessageState with both parameters zeroed.

Algorithm:
1. Clear EDX and ECX registers to 0
2. Tail-call FUN_6faff390(0, 0) to disable panel state

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Notes:
- This is a simple wrapper that disables panel message handling
- Called during cleanup/shutdown sequence from FUN_6fb5a220
- The callee FUN_6faff390 manages DAT_6fbf5f20 (panel enable flag),
  DAT_6fbf5f24 (panel state), and DAT_6fbf5f28 (secondary state)
- Passing (0, 0) disables the panel and processes disable message arrays

functions.name: SetProcessingFlagBit0
functions.comment:
Loads keyboard binding configuration from file or data file archive.

Algorithm:
1. Get current locale string for localization
2. If nLoadFromFile is non-zero (load from file):
   a. Get install path and append "default.key" filename
   b. Open the file with CreateFileWrapper (GENERIC_READ, OPEN_EXISTING)
   c. Read 0x47a (1146) bytes into local buffer
   d. If read successful and size matches, allocate pool memory and copy data
   e. Jump to validation step
3. If nLoadFromFile is zero or file read failed:
   a. Format path using "%s\CMD\%s\default.key" pattern
   b. Call GetDataFilePath() and ReadAndProcessFileData() to load from archive
4. Validate loaded key data:
   a. Check magic signature: 0x5357 ("WS") at offset 0
   b. Check version marker: 0x25 (37) at offset 2
   c. Check data size: 0x47a (1146) at offset 4
   d. If valid, copy 0x11d (285) dwords to g_DefaultKeyBindingTable
5. Release pool allocation if data was loaded
6. Initialize g_aKeyBindingTable: set 0xFFFF at start of each 10-byte entry
   Loop from 0x6fbf562c to 0x6fbf5aa0 (stride 10, ~114 entries)
7. Copy g_DefaultKeyBindingTable to g_KeyBindingTable (0x11d dwords = 285 entries)
8. Call InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks() to set up mouse input

Parameters:
  nLoadFromFile (ECX): int - Non-zero to load from "default.key" file in install dir,
                             zero to load from data file archive

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - File not found or wrong size: falls back to loading from data archive
  - Invalid magic/version/size: skips copy to default table, still initializes tables

Magic Numbers:
  0x47a (1146) - Expected key binding file size
  0x5357 - Magic signature "WS" (little-endian)
  0x25 (37) - Version marker
  0x11d (285) - Number of dword entries to copy
  0x11e (286) - Dwords in buffer copy (285 + 1 word)
  10 (0x0a) - Stride of key binding table entries
  0xFFFF - Default/unbound key value

Global Data:
  g_DefaultKeyBindingTable (0x6fbb2660): Template key bindings loaded from file
  g_KeyBindingTable (0x6fbf5628): Active key bindings used at runtime
  g_aKeyBindingTable (0x6fbf562c): Extended binding table with 10-byte stride
  szDefaultKeyFilename (0x6fbb2ed8): "default.key"
  g_szDefaultKeyPathFmt (0x6fbb2eb4): "%s\CMD\%s\default.key"
  g_szCmdTblSourceFile (0x6fbb2df0): Source file for allocation tracking

functions.name: LookupKeyBindingByCommandId
functions.comment:
Lookup virtual key code for a command binding in the keybinding table.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize table pointer to g_adKeyBindingTypes (offset +6 in entry)
2. Initialize entry index counter to 0
3. Loop: Compare nCommandId with entry's command ID (at pointer - 6)
4. If command ID matches, compare nBindingType with entry's type (at pointer)
5. If both match, return keycode from g_awKeyBindingKeyCodes[index * 5]
6. Advance pointer by 10 bytes (entry stride) and increment index
7. Continue until pointer exceeds 0x6fbf5aa1 (end of table)
8. Return 0xFFFF if no matching binding found

Parameters:
nCommandId - Game command identifier to look up (e.g., 0x22 for keyboard config)
nBindingType - Binding type/slot index (primary=1, secondary=2, etc.)

Returns:
ushort - Virtual key code if binding found, 0xFFFF if unbound

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6fbf562e - Start of keybinding types field in table
0x6fbf5aa1 - End boundary of keybinding table (114 entries * 10 bytes)
0xFFFF - Sentinel value indicating unbound/not found

KeyBinding Entry Structure (10 bytes stride):
Offset | Size | Field        | Type   | Description
-------|------|--------------|--------|---------------------------
+0x00  | 4    | dwCommandId  | uint   | Game command identifier
+0x04  | 4    | dwBindingType| uint   | Binding slot (1=primary)
+0x08  | 2    | wKeyCode     | ushort | Virtual key code (VK_*)

functions.name: IsKeyCodeValidForBinding
functions.comment:
Validates whether a virtual key code can be used for key binding assignment.

Algorithm:
1. Extract lower 16 bits of key code (mask with 0xFFFF)
2. Check if key code is less than 0x2B:
   a. If exactly 0x2A (VK_PRINT): Return TRUE (valid)
   b. If in range 0x01-0x29, use switch table at PTR_caseD_5_6fafe410:
      - Valid (return 1): VK_TAB(0x09), VK_CLEAR(0x0C), VK_RETURN(0x0D), VK_SHIFT(0x10),
        VK_CONTROL(0x11), VK_MENU(0x12), VK_PAUSE(0x13), VK_CAPITAL(0x14),
        VK_SPACE(0x20), VK_PRIOR(0x21), VK_NEXT(0x22), VK_END(0x23), VK_HOME(0x24)
      - Ignored (fall through): VK_BACK(0x08), VK_CANCEL(0x03), VK_HELP(0x2F)
      - Invalid (return 0): Default cases
3. Check if key code >= 0x2B using switch table at 0x6fafe440:
   a. Invalid (return 0): VK_ADD(0x2B), VK_LWIN(0x5B), VK_RWIN(0x5C), VK_APPS(0x5D), VK_NUMLOCK(0x90)
   b. Valid (return 1): VK_SEPARATOR(0x2C) through VK_DIVIDE(0x2F), VK_NUMPAD0-9(0x60-0x69),
      VK_MULTIPLY(0x6A), VK_ADD(0x6B), VK_SEPARATOR(0x6C), VK_SUBTRACT(0x6D), VK_DECIMAL(0x6E),
      VK_DIVIDE(0x6F), VK_F1-F24(0x70-0x87), VK_SCROLL(0x91), VK_OEM keys(0xBA-0xC0, 0xDB-0xDE),
      Extended keys(0x100-0x104)
4. For unhandled key codes, check virtual key type flags:
   a. Call FUN_6fb9aafb with mask 0x103 - check if VK has valid modifier/extended flags
   b. If non-zero, return TRUE (valid)
5. Call FUN_6fb9ab29 with mask 0x04 - check if VK is control character
   a. If non-zero, return TRUE (valid)
   b. Otherwise return FALSE (invalid)

Parameters:
  wKeyCode - Virtual key code to validate (lower 16 bits used)

Returns:
  1 - Key code is valid and can be assigned to a key binding
  0 - Key code is invalid or reserved (Windows keys, NumLock, etc.)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x2A - VK_PRINT (Print Screen)
  0x2B - VK_ADD / VK_EXECUTE (reserved, invalid)
  0x5B - VK_LWIN (Left Windows key, reserved)
  0x5C - VK_RWIN (Right Windows key, reserved)
  0x5D - VK_APPS (Applications key, reserved)
  0x90 - VK_NUMLOCK (reserved, invalid)
  0x103 - Modifier/extended key flag mask
  0x04 - Control character flag mask

functions.name: RegisterKeyboardBinding
functions.signature: int RegisterKeyboardBinding(int nActionId, int nSecondaryActionId, ushort wKeyCode, ushort * pwErrorCode)
functions.comment:
Registers or updates a keyboard key binding for a game action.

Algorithm:
1. If pwErrorCode is non-NULL, initialize it to 0
2. If nActionId > 0x38, return 0 (action ID out of range)
3. Call IsKeyCodeValidForBinding with wKeyCode parameter
4. If key code is invalid, set error code 0xF8B and return 0
5. Switch on key code (values 0x100-0x104) for remote session checks:
   - 0x100: Call IsRemoteSessionActive
   - 0x101: Call IsRemoteSessionSupported  
   - 0x102: Call IsValidRemoteDesktopSession, then IsRemoteSessionHandlingReady
6. For remote session keys: if session not valid, check g_apRemoteSessionActionTable
   - If action blocked for remote session, set error 0xF8A and return 0
7. If key code is 0x2C (Print Screen), check g_apSpecialKeyActionTable
   - If action blocked, set error 0xF8B and return 0
8. Search g_aKeyBindingTable (114 entries, 10-byte stride) for matching key code
9. If found, clear entry (set key code to 0xFFFF) and store search index
10. Search table again for matching (nActionId, nSecondaryActionId) pair
11. If matching action found, update entry with new key code and return 1
12. If no duplicate key found (step 8), use empty slot index for new binding
13. Store new key code at calculated slot and return 0

Parameters:
nActionId - Primary action identifier (0x00-0x38 valid range)
nSecondaryActionId - Secondary action parameter for compound actions
wKeyCode - Key code to bind (passed as ushort value)
pwErrorCode - Output: error code (0xF89=remote session blocked, 0xF8A=remote action blocked, 0xF8B=invalid key)

Returns:
1 - Successfully updated existing action binding
0 - Created new binding, or error occurred (check pwErrorCode)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x38 (56) - Maximum valid action ID
0x72 (114) - Number of entries in key binding table
0x0A (10) - Byte stride of binding table entries
0x100-0x104 - Special remote session key codes
0x2C (44) - Print Screen key code
0xFFFF - Cleared/invalid key code marker
0xF89 (3977) - Error: Remote session blocks this key
0xF8A (3978) - Error: Remote action not available
0xF8B (3979) - Error: Invalid key code for binding

functions.name: BackupKeyBindingsAndReinitialize
functions.comment:
Copies key binding table to backup location and reinitializes mouse button callbacks.

Algorithm:
1. Save ESI and EDI registers to stack
2. Set copy count ECX = 0x11d (285 DWORDs = 1140 bytes)
3. Set source ESI = 0x6fbf5628 (g_KeyBindingTable)
4. Set destination EDI = 0x6fbf5aa0 (g_KeyBindingTableBackup)
5. Execute REP MOVSD to copy table in DWORD increments
6. Restore ESI and EDI registers
7. Jump to InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks to rescan and setup callbacks

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void (does not return directly, tail-calls InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks)

Special Cases:
- Uses REP MOVSD for efficient block copy (4 bytes per iteration)
- Tail-call optimization to InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks via JMP

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x11d (285): Number of DWORDs to copy (1140 bytes total)
  0x6fbf5628: Source address (g_KeyBindingTable)
  0x6fbf5aa0: Destination address (g_KeyBindingTableBackup)

Related Functions:
- InitializeMouseButtonCallbacks() - Called via tail-jump after copy
- LoadKeyboardBindings() - References both source and destination tables

functions.name: InitializeInputSystemBindings
functions.comment:
Wrapper function that plays a video and reconfigures graphics settings.

Classification: Thunk/Wrapper - calls PlayVideoById then tail-jumps to ReadResolutionAndConfigureGraphics.

Algorithm:
1. Extract video ID from pbVideoInfo[1] (offset +1 in structure)
2. Call PlayVideoById with the extracted video ID byte
3. Tail-jump to ReadResolutionAndConfigureGraphics to reload display settings

Parameters:
- pbVideoInfo (ECX, byte *): Pointer to video info structure where:
  - Offset +0: Unknown (not used by this function)
  - Offset +1: Video ID byte passed to PlayVideoById

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- This is a thin wrapper combining video playback with graphics reconfiguration
- Typical use case: after video cutscene, reload resolution/graphics settings

functions.name: ClearKeyBindingsByType
functions.comment:
Clears key bindings matching the specified type pair by setting their key code to 0xFFFF.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pointer to g_adKeyBindingTypes array (offset +6 to point at second int field)
2. Loop through all 114 entries in the key binding table (10 bytes each)
3. For each entry, compare first int field (at offset -6) with nKeyType1
4. If match, compare second int field (at offset 0) with nKeyType2
5. If both match, set the key code field (at offset -2) to 0xFFFF (unbound)
6. Advance pointer by 10 bytes to next entry
7. Continue until pointer reaches 0x6fbf5aa2 (end of table)

Parameters:
- nKeyType1 (int, ECX): First type identifier to match against entry offset +0
- nKeyType2 (int, EDX): Second type identifier to match against entry offset +6

Returns:
- void

Structure Layout (KeyBindingEntry, 10 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
------  ----  -----------   ------  -----------
0x00    4     nType1        int     First type identifier
0x04    2     wKeyCode      ushort  Virtual key code (0xFFFF = unbound)
0x06    4     nType2        int     Second type identifier

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0xFFFF (65535): Unbound key code value
- 0x0A (10): Size of KeyBindingEntry structure in bytes
- 0x6fbf562e: Start of g_adKeyBindingTypes array (offset +6)
- 0x6fbf5aa2: End of key binding table

functions.name: IsKeyBindingActive
functions.comment:
Checks if a key binding exists and is active for the given modifier and key code.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize binding index to 0 and entry pointer to key binding types table
2. Loop through key binding entries (10-byte stride):
   a. Compare modifier key at offset -6 from types pointer with input modifier
   b. Compare key code at types pointer with input key code
   c. If both match, exit loop and check if binding is active
   d. Otherwise, advance pointer by 10 bytes and increment index
   e. If pointer exceeds table end (0x6fbf5aa2), return false (no match)
3. Return true if matched entry's command ID is not -1 (0xFFFF)

Parameters:
- nModifierKey (ECX): Modifier key code (Ctrl, Alt, Shift combinations)
- nKeyCode (EDX): Virtual key code to search for

Returns:
- true: Key binding exists and has a valid command ID assigned
- false: No matching binding found or binding has invalid command (-1)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6fbf562e: g_adKeyBindingTypes base address (offset +6 in entry)
- 0x6fbf562c: g_aKeyBindingTable base address
- 0x6fbf5aa2: Table end boundary (116 entries * 10 bytes + base)
- 10 (0x0A): Key binding entry stride in bytes
- -1 (0xFFFF): Invalid/unassigned command ID marker

Related Functions:
- RegisterKeyboardBinding(): Adds new bindings to the table
- LookupKeyBindingByCommandId(): Reverse lookup by command ID
- SaveKeyboardBindingsToRegistry(): Persists bindings to registry

functions.name: LookupKeyBindingStringId
functions.comment:
Looks up a keyboard binding by command and type, returning a localized string ID.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize table index to 0 and pointer to key binding types table
2. Search g_adKeyBindingTypes for matching command and type pair
3. Each table entry is 10 bytes: command (4 bytes at offset -6), type (4 bytes at offset 0)
4. If no match found (pointer exceeds 0x6fbf5aa1), call Ordinal_10004 for default string
5. On match, retrieve string ID from g_aKeyBindingTable at index*5 (10-byte stride / 2)
6. If string ID is 0xFFFF (invalid marker), return default string via Ordinal_10004
7. For string IDs < 0xE0, use switch table to map virtual key codes to string IDs:
   - Cases 1-3: Mouse buttons, return default string
   - Cases 4, 8, 9, 0xC-0x29, 0x2A-0x2F: Standard keys, use jump table
   - Cases 0x5B-0x5D: Windows keys
   - Cases 0x60-0x6F: Numpad keys
   - Cases 0x70-0x87: Function keys F1-F24
   - Cases 0x90-0x91: Num/Scroll Lock
   - Cases 0xBA-0xC0, 0xDB-0xDE: OEM keys
8. For string IDs 0xE0-0x104 (extended keys), use secondary jump table
9. Default case: Store key code in g_szKeyBindingStringBuffer and return its address

Parameters:
nBindingCommand - Key binding command ID (ECX, __fastcall)
nBindingType - Key binding type/category (EDX, __fastcall)

Returns:
char* - Pointer to localized string ID, or direct key code string buffer

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6fbf5aa1 - End of key binding types table
0xFFFF - Invalid/unassigned binding marker
0xE0 - Threshold for extended key handling
0x100-0x104 - Extended key string IDs
0xEB2 - Default string ID (via Ordinal_10004)
0xEB3-0xF14 - Virtual key to string ID mappings

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10004 (D2Lang.GetStringById) - Returns localized string by ID
- RegisterKeyboardBinding - Registers new bindings in the table
- LoadKeyboardBindings - Populates binding table from registry

functions.name: GetKeyBindingStringId
functions.comment:
Returns a string ID for a key binding based on command and type.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize search index to 0, pointer to g_adKeyBindingTypes (0x6fbf562e)
2. Loop through key binding table entries (10 bytes each, up to 0x6fbf5aa2):
   a. Compare nBindingCommand with entry's command (at pointer - 6)
   b. Compare nBindingType with entry's type (at pointer)
   c. If both match, retrieve string ID from g_aKeyBindingTable[index * 5]
   d. If no match, advance pointer by 10 bytes, increment index
3. If table exhausted without match, use value 0xFFFF
4. Mask string ID to 16 bits, subtract 8 to get switch index
5. If switch index > 0xFC (252), fall through to LookupKeyBindingStringId
6. Use jump table (switchdataD_6faff024) indexed by byte table (switchdataD_6faff0a4)
7. Each case loads a specific string resource ID (0xF15-0xF4A) into ECX
8. Call Ordinal_10004 (D2Lang.GetStringFromIndex) with resource ID
9. Return string pointer from Ordinal_10004

Parameters:
- nBindingCommand (ECX): Key binding command identifier to look up
- nBindingType (EDX): Key binding type (primary/secondary)

Returns:
- ushort: String resource ID for the key binding, or result from fallback lookup

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x6fbf562e: Start of g_adKeyBindingTypes array (type field of entries)
- 0x6fbf5aa2: End boundary of key binding table search
- 0x0A (10): Stride of key binding table entries
- 0xFFFF: Sentinel value indicating no binding found
- 0xFC (252): Maximum valid switch table index
- 0xF15-0xF4A: String resource IDs for various key names

Related Functions:
- LookupKeyBindingStringId (0x6fafe760): Fallback for complex string lookups
- Ordinal_10004: D2Lang.GetStringFromIndex - retrieves localized string

functions.name: ProcessKeyDownEvent
functions.comment:
Processes keyboard key-down events and dispatches bound actions.

Searches the key binding table for a matching key code and executes the
associated action handler if found and valid.

Algorithm:
1. Check if key event has special processing flag (0x40000000) set - if so, exit
2. Initialize search at start of g_KeyBindingTable
3. Loop through binding entries (10 bytes each) until end of table (0x6fbf5a9c)
4. For each entry, check if key code matches pKeyEvent[2]
5. Validate command ID is not 0xFFFF (unbound) and within valid range (0x39-0xDF)
6. Verify action handler exists in g_apSpecialKeyActionTable[commandId * 3]
7. Calculate binding offset as nBindingIndex * 10
8. If binding requires Alt key (0x73), check Alt state via GetKeyState(VK_MENU)
9. If Alt pressed, skip this binding (return early)
10. If g_nGameModeState == 2, validate action in g_adwKeyActionValidationTable
11. Verify action function pointer with IsBadCodePtr
12. If bad pointer, call assertion (Ordinal_10023) and terminate (FUN_6fb9a10f)
13. Call the bound action handler function
14. Set pKeyEvent[6] = 1 (processed flag) and pKeyEvent[7] = 0
15. Call Ordinal_511 to finalize event processing

Parameters:
  pKeyEvent - Pointer to key event structure:
              [0x08] Key scan code (word at offset +8)
              [0x0C] Event flags (dword at offset +12, bit 30 = special processing)
              [0x18] Processed flag (set to 1 when handled)
              [0x1C] Result code (set to 0 when handled)

Returns:
  void - Returns early if event cannot be processed or no binding found

Special Cases:
- Alt+key combinations are blocked if binding flag is 0x73
- Game mode state 2 requires action validation before execution
- Invalid function pointers trigger assertion and program termination

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x40000000 - Special processing flag in event flags
  0xFFFF - Unbound key binding marker
  0x39-0xDF - Valid command ID range (57-223)
  0x73 - Alt key modifier flag ('s' ASCII)
  0x12 - VK_MENU (Alt key virtual key code)
  0x8000 - Key state pressed bit
  0x7D0 - Line number 2000 for assertion
  10 (0x0A) - Key binding entry stride in bytes
  12 (0x0C) - Action validation table entry stride

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_511 - D2Win event finalization
- Ordinal_10023 - D2Common assertion/error handler
- FUN_6fb9a10f - Program termination handler

functions.name: ExecuteKeyBindingAction
functions.comment:
Searches key binding table for a matching key code and executes the associated action handler.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize loop index to 0 and pointer to g_KeyBindingTable (0x6fbf5628)
2. Read key code from input event at offset +0x8
3. For each binding entry (10-byte stride):
   a. Compare binding key code (ushort at offset +4) with input key code
   b. Read command ID (dword at offset 0)
   c. Skip if command ID is 0xFFFF (invalid)
   d. Skip if command ID >= 0x39 (57, out of valid action range)
   e. Skip if command ID > 0xDF (223, secondary range check)
   f. Look up action handler at g_apRemoteSessionActionTable[commandId*0xC]
   g. Skip if handler is NULL
4. Exit if binding pointer exceeds 0x6fbf5a9b (end of table)
5. If g_dwRemoteSessionMode == 2, verify action allowed via g_adwKeyActionValidationTable
6. Validate handler with IsBadCodePtr to prevent crash
7. If validation fails, call assertion (Ordinal_10023) with source location
8. Call the action handler function via indirect call
9. Set input event processed flag at offset +0x18 to 1
10. Clear input event consumed flag at offset +0x1c to 0
11. Call Ordinal_511 to finalize input event processing

Parameters:
  nInputEvent - Pointer to input event structure containing key code at +0x8

Returns:
  void - Returns after executing bound action or if no binding found

Magic Numbers:
  0x6fbf5628 - g_KeyBindingTable base address
  0x6fbf5a9b - End of key binding table
  0x6fbb2adc - g_apRemoteSessionActionTable base (action handler pointers)
  0x6fbb2ae0 - g_adwKeyActionValidationTable (remote session validation)
  0x0A (10)  - Key binding entry stride in bytes
  0x0C (12)  - Action table entry stride in bytes
  0xFFFF     - Invalid command ID marker
  0x39 (57)  - Maximum command ID for primary range
  0xDF (223) - Maximum command ID for secondary range
  0x7F6 (2038) - Source line number for assertion

functions.name: SetPanelMessageStateBySessionMode
functions.comment:
Manages panel message state transitions based on session mode (active/inactive).

Algorithm:
1. Store session mode value in global state variable g_dwRemoteSessionMode
2. If session mode disabled (nSessionMode == 0):
   - Check if previously enabled: if DAT_6fbf5f24 == 1 (was enabled)
   - Mark messages as disabled: set DAT_6fbf5f24 = 0
   - Get main window handle from Ordinal_10027 (D2Win.GetHwnd)
   - Process 4 message array entries from main message table (DAT_6fbb2d88)
   - If caller requested message display (fShowMessages != 0) and disabled mode not set:
     - Process 2 message entries from secondary message table (DAT_6fbb2db8)
     - Mark secondary messages as enabled: set DAT_6fbf5f28 = 1
3. If session mode enabled (nSessionMode != 0):
   - Check if previously disabled: if DAT_6fbf5f24 == 0 (was disabled)
   - Mark messages as enabled: set DAT_6fbf5f24 = 1
   - If caller requested message display (fShowMessages != 0) and secondary messages active:
     - Process 2 message entries from secondary message table (DAT_6fbb2db8)
     - Mark secondary messages as disabled: set DAT_6fbf5f28 = 0
   - Process 4 message array entries from main message table (DAT_6fbb2d88)

Parameters:
- nSessionMode: Session mode flag (ECX: 0 = disable messages, non-zero = enable messages)
- fShowMessages: Boolean flag (EDX: non-zero = show secondary messages if applicable)

Returns:
- void: No return value; modifies global state variables DAT_6fbf5f24 and DAT_6fbf5f28

Special Cases:
- Early exit if session state unchanged (if param already matches current state)
- DAT_6fbf5f28 tracks secondary message panel visibility independent of session mode
- DAT_6fbf5f24 tracks whether messages are currently enabled (0=enabled, 1=disabled)

Related Functions:
- ProcessMessageArray() - Processes array of main message entries
- ProcessMessageEntryArray() - Processes array of secondary message entries
- Ordinal_10027 (D2Win.GetHwnd) - Retrieves main window handle for message dispatch

functions.name: UpdateDialogQuestState
functions.comment:
Updates dialog quest state and processes events on time interval.

Algorithm:
1. Load current game tick count via GetTickCount
2. Check if minimum time interval (80ms) has elapsed since last update
3. If time not elapsed, return early
4. Iterate through linked list of active dialogs starting at offset 0xb08
5. For each dialog, invoke virtual callback method at vtable offset 0x14
6. If callback returns 1, mark dialog as quest-triggered and exit:
   - Set quest active flag at offset 0x18 to 1
   - Clear quest state at offset 0x1c to 0
   - Call Ordinal_511 to process state change
7. Check for null dialog structure, trigger assertion if null
8. Call FUN_6faff510 to compute new quest state value
9. Compare new state to previous state at offset 0x44
10. Update both state offsets 0x44 and 0x48 with new value
11. If state changed and not error (-1), call FUN_6fb8d210 for UI update

Parameters:
pDialog (UnitAny *): Pointer to dialog/unit structure containing quest state fields

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Null dialog pointer triggers assertion and program termination. State value -1 is error code, suppresses UI update.

functions.name: SearchItemsByCoordinates
functions.comment:
Searches item list for entry matching target coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input: check if nItemBase is not null
2. Initialize: nItemIndex = 0, nOffsetAccum = 0, iVar3 = 0
3. Extract target X coordinate from upper 16 bits of nCoordStruct offset 0xc
4. Extract target Y coordinate from low 16 bits of nCoordStruct offset 0xc
5. Load item count from nItemBase offset 0x50
6. If item count <= 0, return -1 (no items to search)
7. Loop through item list starting at nItemBase + 0x158 (stride 0x110)
8. Check item active flag: pnCurrentItem[7] must equal 1
9. Check Y bounds: nItemBase[0x2c] + 0xf <= Y < nItemBase[0x34] - 0xf + nItemBase[0x2c]
10. Calculate item coordinate: nItemCoord = *pnCurrentItem + nItemBase[0x30] + nOffsetAccum
11. Check X bounds: nItemCoord - 0xb <= X < nItemCoord + 0x4
12. If all checks pass, return nItemIndex (found match)
13. Add current item size to accumulator: nOffsetAccum += *pnCurrentItem
14. Increment item counter and advance pointer: nItemIndex++, move to next 0x110-byte entry
15. Continue looping until all items checked or match found
16. Return -1 if no matching item found

Parameters:
nItemBase - Pointer to dialog/item manager structure containing item array
nCoordStruct - Pointer to quest/dialog structure with coordinates at offset 0xc

Returns:
int - Zero-based item index if match found, -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) if no match

Special Cases:
Note: Function uses 1 SSA temporary variable (uVar1) optimized away by decompiler during analysis.

functions.name: ProcessDialogInput
functions.comment:
Process dialog input event and perform associated callbacks.

Algorithm:
1. Load global dialog state pointer from g_pCurrentDialog
2. Extract event code (low 16 bits) and event data (high 16 bits) from dialog parameter at offset 0xc
3. Call validation functions to check if event is valid (FUN_6fb5d340 with 0x15, FUN_6fb38320 with event code and data)
4. If validation fails, initialize dialog failure state at offsets 0x18=1 and 0x1c=0
5. Call ordinal cleanup function (Ordinal_511) with dialog parameter
6. Verify global state pointer is valid, otherwise abort with fatal error (Ordinal_10023 + FUN_6fb9a10f)
7. If global state[0x10] is already set, skip processing
8. Check global state[0x4] flag to determine callback path:
   - If flag==1 (timer-based processing): Get current tick count, check timeout condition against global state[0]
   - Call FUN_6faff510 to calculate index
   - If index valid and callback exists at calculated offset, invoke callback at global state[index*0x44+0x5c]
   - If callback returns non-zero, return immediately
   - Reset state[0x4] flag
   - If flag!=1 (list-based processing): Iterate linked list at global state[0x2c2]
   - For each node, invoke callback at [*node].field_0x10
   - Continue until callback returns 1 or list exhausted

Parameters:
- pDialog (dword): Pointer to dialog structure containing event data at offset 0xc
  IMPLICIT: g_pCurrentDialog - Global dialog state structure pointer

Returns:
- void: No return value, modifies dialog and global state

Special Cases:
- Handles null global state pointer (fatal error path)
- Validates callback pointers before invocation to prevent null dereference
- Supports both timer-based (state[4]==1) and list-based callback mechanisms
- Clears processing flag (state[0x10]) to prevent re-entry

Magic Numbers:
- 0x15: Validation code passed to FUN_6fb5d340
- 0xc: Offset in dialog structure containing event code/data
- 0x18, 0x1c: Dialog failure state offsets
- 0x4: Global state flag controlling callback mode (timer vs list)
- 0x50: Timeout offset in global state
- 0x12, 0x14: Index bounds checking offsets in global state
- 0x11: Index multiplier offset in global state
- 0x44: Stride for index*0x44 calculation
- 0x5c: Callback function pointer offset within stride
- 0x2c2: Linked list pointer offset in global state
- 0x10: Processing flag offset in global state
- 0x48, 0x50: State management offsets for index validation

Related Functions:
- FUN_6faff510: Calculates current event index based on timing
- FUN_6fb5d340: Primary event validation function
- FUN_6fb38320: Secondary event validation with code/data check
- Ordinal_511: Dialog cleanup/finalization routine
- GetTickCount: Windows API for timing
- Ordinal_10023: Fatal error reporting
- FUN_6fb9a10f: Process termination

functions.name: UpdateAutomapViewAndCamera
functions.comment:
Updates automap viewport and camera position based on scroll window mode and input coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Verify automap config exists (g_pCurrentDialog); assert and exit if null
2. Get current tick count via GetTickCount()
3. If time since last update < 80ms (0x50), mark event as complete and return early
4. Iterate through UI element list at config[0x2c2] checking element callbacks
5. If any element callback returns 1, mark event handled and exit
6. Fetch previous view mode from config[0x11], set update flag at config[4]=1
7. Call SearchItemsByCoordinates() to find items at click location
8. Store new view mode at config[0x11] and config[0x12]
9. If view mode unchanged or returned -1, validate coordinate bounds:
   - Extract X coordinate as lower 16-bits from pEventData[3]
   - Extract Y coordinate as upper 16-bits (>> 0x10) from pEventData[3]
   - Check X within [config[0xb] - 4, config[0xd] + config[0xb] + 4]
   - Check Y within [config[0xc] - 4, config[0xe] + config[0xc] + 4]
10. If coordinates out of bounds:
    a. Try allocate resource 0x15 (render buffer) via FUN_6fb5d340()
    b. If success, validate allocation via FUN_6fb38320(dwX, dwY)
    c. Check callback at config[0x19] (on-render-complete); if null, try config[0x18]
    (pre-render)
    d. If config[0x18] null, assert and fatal error; otherwise invoke config[0x18]()
    e. Invoke config[0x19]() post-render callback
11. Allocate resource 6 (scroll layer) via FUN_6fb5d340(6)
12. Call FUN_6fb1ccd0() with scroll mode and coordinates for layer rendering
13. Allocate resource 7 (composite layer) via FUN_6fb5d340(7)
14. Call FUN_6fb1cd50() with scroll mode and coordinates for final composite
15. Mark event complete: pEventData[6] = 1, pEventData[7] = 0
16. Call Ordinal_511() (D2Win.D2WIN_DrawGame) to finalize frame

Parameters:
pEventData - Pointer to event data structure containing:
  +0xc - Mouse coordinates packed as (uint): lower 16-bits = X, upper 16-bits = Y
  +0x18 - Event completion flag (set to 1 on return)
  +0x1c - Event error code (set to 0 on return)

Returns:
void - Always returns after setting event completion flags

Special Cases:
- Early return at step 3 throttles updates to 80ms intervals to prevent UI thrashing
- View mode -1 indicates search found nothing; treated as unchanged
- Resource allocation failures (steps 10a, 11, 13) suppress further rendering
- All rendering callbacks at config[0x18] and config[0x19] must handle null pointers
- Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary variable optimized away by decompiler

Magic Numbers:
0x50 - 80ms interval threshold for update throttling (milliseconds)
0x2c2 - Offset to UI element linked list in config (offset 0xB08 in disasm)
0x4, 0xd, 0xe - Config offsets for viewport dimension validation
0x11, 0x12 - Config offsets for current/previous view mode storage
0x15, 6, 7 - Resource allocation IDs for render buffers, scroll/composite layers
0x18, 0x19 - Config offsets for pre/post-render callback pointers
0x6 (index 1), 0x7 (index 1) - Array indices for layer configuration

functions.name: InsertDialogCacheNodeAndTriggerCallback
