functions.name: SelectAvailableItemRarityMode
functions.comment:
Validates and selects an available item rarity display mode for the inventory filter UI

Algorithm:
1. Validate initial mode index (0-4); clear to 0 if exceeds max rarity level
2. Check if mode update timer is inactive (g_dwModeUpdateTimer == 0)
3. Initialize game state filter via InitializeGameState with mode parameter
4. Look up player unit in hash table using FindUnitInHashTable(mode, 1)
5. Verify unit has valid inventory pointer at offset 0x84
6. Iterate inventory linked list via GetUnitStat, GetInventoryNodeField, GetInventoryNodeNext
7. For each item, call GetItemQualityLevel and increment corresponding rarity count (0-4)
8. Build local array [nRarityCount..nRarityCount4] with counts per rarity tier
9. Update g_adwObjectTypeArray with availability flags (1 if count > 0, stride 0x12)
10. If preferred mode has no items, cycle through modes 0-4 (max 4 attempts)
11. Store final mode in g_chCurrentMode and set view marker at g_dwRarityModeViewMarker

Parameters:
nInitialMode (ECX, dword) - Preferred rarity mode index (0-4); values > 4 are normalized to 0

Returns:
void - Updates global state: g_chCurrentMode (selected mode), g_adwObjectTypeArray (availability), g_dwRarityModeViewMarker (UI flag)

Special Cases:
- Early exit if g_dwModeUpdateTimer != 0 (update already in progress)
- Early exit if InitializeGameState fails or unit lookup fails
- Early exit if unit has no inventory (offset 0x84 is null)
- Mode cycles at 0xFF boundary or when exceeding g_bConfigMode limit
- Maximum 4 search attempts before accepting current mode

Magic Numbers:
- 0x84: Unit structure offset to inventory pointer
- 0x21: Unit array index for inventory data (piVar4[0x21])
- 0x12: Stride between entries in g_adwObjectTypeArray
- 5: Maximum rarity levels (0-4 valid)
- 4: Maximum search attempts for alternative mode

7. Clear validation error code to 0 after reporting
8. Return to caller

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
This function performs unconditional state assignment with no validation or error checking.
State level 6 represents a specific operational mode in the global state machine.

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x06 (6) - Global state level 6 operational mode

Global Variables Modified:
g_dwGlobalState - Primary system state tracking variable

functions.name: InitializeGameConfigByMode
functions.comment:
Initializes game configuration arrays for specified game mode.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate base offset: (nGameMode * 5) in DWORDS or (nGameMode * 10) in WORDS
2. Set g_wConfigId1_renamed[nGameMode*10] = 0
3. Set g_dwConfigParam1[nGameMode*5] = 1
4. Set g_dwConfigParam2[nGameMode*5] = 1
5. Set g_dwConfigParam3[nGameMode*10] = 0
6. Set g_dwConfigParam4[nGameMode*5] = 0

Parameters:
  nGameMode (int) - Game mode index for config array initialization (__fastcall in ECX)

Returns:
  void

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Description
  0x00   | 2    | wConfigId1 | Configuration ID (cleared to 0)
  0x02   | 4    | dwConfigParam1 | Config parameter 1 (set to 1)
  0x06   | 4    | dwConfigParam2 | Config parameter 2 (set to 1)
  0x0A   | 2    | wConfigParam3 | Config parameter 3 (cleared to 0)
  0x0C   | 4    | dwConfigParam4 | Config parameter 4 (cleared to 0)

functions.name: ProcessGameInputMessage
functions.comment:
Processes game input messages including click events and screen coordinate validation.

Algorithm:
1. Get current game state (nGameState = FUN_6fb62880)
2. Check if game system is enabled (return if enabled)
3. Return if game state is 0
4. Check if processing flag (fIsProcessing) is set (return if set)
5. Extract screen coordinates from input data (dwScreenX, dwScreenY)
6. Validate coordinates against initial viewport boundaries
7. If out of bounds, check game mode (0x06, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x0e) and apply mode-specific boundaries
8. For mode 0x0c: load viewport bounds based on GetGlobalSystemState
9. For mode 0x0e: use mode-specific boundaries (g_dwMinScreenX_Mode14, etc.)
10. For modes 1-2: apply altmode boundaries (g_dwMinScreenX_Alt, g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2, etc.)
11. If coordinates within altmode bounds: validate and exit
12. If coordinates outside all bounds: check object type validation
13. For valid objects: set object data array to 0, validate with ordinal check
14. For selected unit: validate with FUN_6fb29fe0, get unit data with FUN_6fb60e10
15. Call HandleScreenClickEvent if all validations pass
16. Finalize by setting input data fields (offset +0x18 = 1, +0x1c = 0)
17. Call Ordinal_511(pInputData) to cleanup

Parameters:
- pInputData (uint): Pointer to input message data structure containing:
    Offset +0x0c: Screen coordinates (X in low word, Y in high word)
    Offset +0x08: Additional input flags
    Offset +0x18, +0x1c: Fields set to 1 and 0 respectively

Returns:
- void: No return value, modifies global state and input structure in-place

Special Cases:
- If game system enabled or game state = 0: returns immediately
- If processing flag set: returns without processing
- Screen coordinate mode depends on g_dwObjectType value
- Ordinal_10262 is used to check game state validity
- Ordinal_511 is called for input finalization at both entry and exit paths

Note: Function uses 2 stack-allocated temporaries (temp_79f87974120, temp_79fb2594d69) optimized away by compiler

functions.name: ResetGameUIStateAndCacheNode
functions.comment:
Resets game UI state and inserts cache node during object type transitions.

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type (1=Player, 2=Monster, 3=Object, 4=Missile, 9=Item)
2. Check UI resource buffer element 5 - only proceed if element is null
3. Clear object render initialized flag
4. Get game context and retrieve inventory owner unit
5. Set game state for the inventory owner unit
6. Configure cache node: set dwFlags (+0x18) to 1, dwPriority (+0x1c) to 0
7. Insert cache node into system via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
8. Clear UI color flag and process game state transition
9. Reset all interaction parameters and UI state to defaults
10. Clear selected unit/entity pointers
11. Reset viewport and cursor positions to -1 (invalid)

Parameters:
  pCacheNode (CacheNode *) - Pointer to cache node structure
    +0x18: dwFlags - Set to 1 (enabled)
    +0x1c: dwPriority - Set to 0 (default priority)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Early exit if object type is not 1, 2, 3, 4, or 9
- Early exit if UI resource buffer element 5 is non-null (resource still active)

Object Type Constants:
  1 = Player unit
  2 = Monster/NPC
  3 = World object
  4 = Missile/projectile
  9 = Item

Globals Reset:
  g_dwObjectRenderInitialized = 0
  g_dwUIColorFlag = 0
  g_dwInteractionParam0 = 0
  g_dwInteractionParam1 = 0
  g_pGameStateConfig = NULL
  g_dwUIFlag1 = 0
  g_pSelectedUnit = NULL
  g_pSelectedEntity = NULL
  g_dwViewportX = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
  g_dwUIState = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
  g_dwCursorScreenX = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
  g_dwCursorScreenY = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)

functions.name: ProcessViewportMouseClick
functions.comment:
Process mouse click events for main game viewport modes (0-4).

Algorithm:
1. Check g_dwObjectType is 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4 (main game modes) - exit if not
2. Extract mouse X from pClickEvent[3] lower 16 bits into dwScreenX
3. Extract mouse Y from pClickEvent[3] upper 16 bits into dwScreenY
4. Store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0/1 globals
5. Call GetInitializationFlag to check if system initialized
6. If initialized AND coordinates within viewport bounds (g_pRenderModeList_ObjectData to g_nMaxViewportX/Y) - exit early (already handled)
7. If g_dwObjectType == 0 - delegate to HandleUIMouseClickEvent
8. Call InitializeGameState to get game context
9. If game state valid, call FindUnitInHashTable to get player unit
10. If player unit found, get dwInputFlags from unit offset 0x84
11. Validate coordinates against outer viewport bounds (g_pRenderModeList_ObjectData to g_nMaxViewportX/Y)
12. If valid, set pClickEvent[6]=1 (processed), pClickEvent[7]=0 (no error)
13. Validate coordinates against inner screen bounds (g_nMinScreenX/Y to g_nMaxScreenX/Y)
14. If within inner bounds, call TransformCoordinatesForViewport with unit data
15. Set pClickEvent[6]=1, pClickEvent[7]=0, clear g_pUIPanel, return
16. If any validation fails, delegate to HandleUIMouseClickEvent

Parameters:
  pClickEvent - Pointer to click event structure
    [3] (0x0C): Mouse coordinates (X in low word, Y in high word)
    [6] (0x18): Result flag (1=processed, 0=not processed)
    [7] (0x1C): Error code (0=success)

Returns:
  void - Updates pClickEvent result fields and global state

Special Cases:
  - Only handles game modes 0-4 (main gameplay)
  - Modes 5+ delegated to HandleUIMouseClickEvent
  - Coordinates must pass two-stage validation (outer then inner bounds)
  - g_dwObjectType==0 always delegates to HandleUIMouseClickEvent

Global Variables:
  g_dwObjectType (0x6fbf8a64) - Current game/UI mode
  g_dwInteractionParam0/1 - Cached click coordinates
  g_pRenderModeList_ObjectData (0x6fbf6840) - Min viewport X
  g_nMaxViewportX (0x6fbf6844) - Max viewport X
  g_nMinViewportY (0x6fbf6848) - Min viewport Y
  g_nMaxViewportY (0x6fbf684c) - Max viewport Y
  g_nMinScreenX/Y, g_nMaxScreenX/Y - Inner screen bounds
  g_pUIPanel (0x6fbb36e4) - UI panel state
  g_chCurrentMode (0x6fbf8a78) - Current rendering mode

functions.name: ProcessMouseClickUIRegion
functions.comment:
Processes mouse click events across multiple UI regions and dispatches to appropriate handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Extract mouse X (low word) and Y (high word) from pMouseEvent[3]
2. Validate g_dwObjectType is in valid range (0-4); if not, mark event handled and return
3. Check if click is in close button region (ScreenWidth-0x12E to ScreenWidth-0x10E, ScreenHeight-0x60 to ScreenHeight-0x40)
   - If yes, set g_dwUIMode2Flag=1, call InitializeGameObjectProperties(4,...) and return
4. If initialization flag set and coordinate validation returns 1, clear object type data array and reset to inventory mode
5. If initialization flag set and coordinates within screen bounds:
   - Check screen state; if 6 (loading), return
   - Get unit from hash table, build tooltip text
   - Call ProcessUnitInteraction with coordinates and delay
   - Reset game state
6. If click in skill bar region (UIXOffset to ScreenWidth/2-1, ScreenHeight-0x1DF to ScreenHeight-0x1C1):
   - Check skill slot regions at +0x50, +0xA0, +0xF0, +0x140 pixel intervals
   - If slot enabled and not current mode, call InitializeGameObjectProperties(6,...) and SelectAvailableItemRarityMode
7. If click in belt slot region (g_pRenderModeList_ObjectData to g_nMaxViewportX, ScreenHeight-0x6D to g_nMaxViewportY):
   - Iterate belt slots checking if mouse within slot bounds (+0x2D width)
   - Update slot selection state and g_dwUIColorFlag
   - Handle inventory owner via GetGameContext and INVENTORY_GetOwner
8. If click in viewport region with object type 1 or 2:
   - Call ProcessMouseClickGameObject with unit data and current mode
9. All other clicks: delegate to HandleMouseInputEvents
10. Mark event handled (pMouseEvent[6]=1, pMouseEvent[7]=0) and call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie

Parameters:
  pMouseEvent - Pointer to mouse event structure:
    [0]: Event type
    [2]: Delay/timing value (dwInitDelay)
    [3]: Packed coordinates (low word=X, high word=Y)
    [6]: Handled flag (set to 1 when processed)
    [7]: Result code (set to 0 on success)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
  - Screen state 6 (loading): Early return without processing
  - Invalid object type (not 0-4): Mark handled and return immediately
  - Null unit from hash table: Early return

UI Regions (pixel offsets from UIXOffset):
  Skill Slot 0: 0x00-0x50
  Skill Slot 1: 0x50-0xA0
  Skill Slot 2: 0xA0-0xF0
  Skill Slot 3: 0xF0-0x140
  Belt Slot Width: 0x2D (45 pixels)

Global State Modified:
  g_dwObjectType, g_dwUIMode2Flag, g_dwUIColorFlag, g_dwModeUpdateTimer_renamed, g_adwObjectTypeData

functions.name: InitAndInsertCacheNode
functions.comment:
Initializes a cache node structure and inserts it into the cache system.

Classification: Initialization/Wrapper function

Algorithm:
1. Set cache node field at offset +0x18 to 1 (active/initialized flag)
2. Set cache node field at offset +0x1c to 0 (clear cookie/link field)
3. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to insert node into cache linked list

Parameters:
  pCacheNode (void *) - Pointer to cache node structure to initialize and insert
    Structure layout (partial):
      Offset  Size  Field          Description
      +0x18   4     dwActiveFlag   Set to 1 to mark node as active/initialized
      +0x1c   4     dwCookie       Cleared to 0 before insertion

Returns: void

Called Functions:
  InsertCacheNodeWithCookie - Thunk to external cache insertion routine (via IAT jump)

functions.name: ActivateInventoryUIAndInsertCacheNode
functions.comment:
Activates inventory UI (element 5) and inserts a cache node for processing.

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI element 5 (inventory) is already active via GetUIResourceBufferElement(5)
2. If inventory UI is active, exit early (already displayed)
3. Check if any modal dialogs are active via IsAnyDialogActive()
4. If dialogs active, exit (cannot activate inventory while dialog shown)
5. Check cache node flags at offset 0x0C - if 0x40000000 bit NOT set:
   a. Call ProcessUIStateChange(5, 0, 0) to activate inventory UI
6. Set cache node field at offset 0x18 to 1 (mark as active/ready)
7. Set cache node field at offset 0x1C to 0 (clear state/counter)
8. Insert the cache node via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie for further processing

Parameters:
pCacheNode - Pointer to cache node structure with layout:
             Offset 0x0C: dwFlags (dword) - 0x40000000 bit controls UI activation skip
             Offset 0x18: dwActiveState (dword) - set to 1 on activation
             Offset 0x1C: dwStateCounter (dword) - cleared to 0 on activation

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Early exit if inventory UI already active (g_dwUIResourceBuffer[5] != 0)
- Early exit if any dialog is active (prevents UI conflicts)
- Skip ProcessUIStateChange if cache node flag 0x40000000 is set

Classification: Worker function - called to activate inventory display and queue cache node

functions.name: ValidateMouseClickBounds
functions.comment:
Validates mouse click position against screen boundaries and routes to UI handler.

Algorithm:
1. Extract low 16-bits of input packet offset 0xc as X coordinate
2. Extract high 16-bits of input packet offset 0xc as Y coordinate
3. Verify X >= g_dwMinScreenX_Alt AND X < g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2
4. Verify Y >= g_dwMaxScreenY AND Y <= g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2
5. If all bounds checks pass, route click to HandleUIMouseClickEvent
6. Return 1 for valid click within bounds, 0 for out of bounds

Parameters:
pInputPacket - Pointer to input event structure; contains packed coordinates at offset 0xc

Returns:
1 if mouse click is within valid screen bounds and handler was called
0 if mouse click is outside bounds (no handler invoked)

Structure Layout (Input Packet):
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description
+0x0c  | 2    | nX            | short | Mouse X coordinate (low word)
+0x0e  | 2    | nY            | short | Mouse Y coordinate (high word)

functions.name: ValidateMouseCoordinatesAndHandleInput
functions.comment:
Validates mouse coordinates against screen bounds and processes input if valid.

Algorithm:
1. Extract lower word of panel data[3] as screen X coordinate (dwScreenX)
2. Extract upper word of panel data[3] as screen Y coordinate (dwScreenY)
3. Store extracted coordinates in global interaction parameters (g_dwInteractionParam0/1)
4. Set panel fields [6]=1, [7]=0 (initialization flags)
5. Call Ordinal_511 (unknown validation/preprocessing function)
6. Check if dwScreenX within [g_dwMinScreenX_Alt, g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2) bounds
7. Check if dwScreenY within [g_dwMaxScreenY, g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2] bounds
8. If ALL bounds checks pass, call HandleMouseInputEvents(pPanelData) and return 1 (success)
9. Otherwise return 0 (out of bounds)

Parameters:
pPanelData (dword *): Panel/viewport data structure, offsets used: [3]=coords, [6],[7]=flags

Returns:
1 - Mouse coordinates valid and input processed
0 - Mouse coordinates out of screen bounds

Special Cases:
- Ordinal_511 purpose unknown - may validate/preprocess panel state
- Bounds validation uses global screen limit variables, not hardcoded values
- Coordinates extracted from single DWORD as: lower WORD=X, upper WORD=Y
- Global parameters used: g_dwInteractionParam0 (X), g_dwInteractionParam1 (Y)

functions.name: HandleInteractionClick
functions.comment:
Process interaction click event and update UI state.

Algorithm:
1. Extract screen coordinates from unit structure: X = lower 16 bits of [pUnit+0xc], Y = upper 16 bits of [pUnit+0xc]
2. Store coordinates in global interaction parameters: g_dwInteractionParam0 = X, g_dwInteractionParam1 = Y
3. Initialize unit interaction fields: [pUnit+0x18] = 1, [pUnit+0x1c] = 0
4. Call Ordinal_511 to notify interaction event handler (Storm.dll ordinal)
5. Validate screen coordinates are within valid bounds:
   - Check X >= g_dwMinScreenX_Alt AND X < g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2
   - Check Y >= g_dwMaxScreenY AND Y <= g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2
6. If bounds valid, check for UI inventory panel click:
   - Calculate panel X range: (g_dwScreenWidth - g_dwUIXOffset - 0x12e) to (g_dwScreenWidth - g_dwUIXOffset - 0x10e)
   - Calculate panel Y range: (g_dwUIYOffset + g_dwScreenHeight - 0x60) to (g_dwUIYOffset + g_dwScreenHeight - 0x40)
   - If click within panel AND g_dwUIMode2Flag != 0: reinitialize fields, call Ordinal_511, invoke HandleUIInventoryClick
7. Clear UI mode flag: g_dwUIMode2Flag = 0
8. Return 1 if coordinates valid, 0 if out of bounds

Parameters:
  pUnit (UnitAny*) - Pointer to unit/interaction structure with screen coordinates and state fields

Returns:
  1 if click coordinates within valid screen bounds, 0 if coordinates out of bounds

Special Cases:
  Magic number 0x12e (302 decimal) = left boundary of inventory UI panel
  Magic number 0x10e (270 decimal) = right boundary of inventory UI panel
  Magic number 0x60 (96 decimal) = top boundary of inventory UI panel
  Magic number 0x40 (64 decimal) = bottom boundary of inventory UI panel
  g_dwUIMode2Flag controls whether inventory panel click processing is active

functions.name: CheckPointInUIViewport
functions.comment:
Checks if a screen point falls within the UI viewport panel bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Extract X coordinate (lower 16 bits) and Y coordinate (upper 16 bits) from param struct
2. Set initial state fields (offset 0x18=1, 0x1C=0) and call Ordinal_511 (Storm.dll viewport refresh)
3. Check X bounds: (ScreenWidth - UIXOffset - 0x12E) <= X <= (ScreenWidth - UIXOffset - 0x10E)
4. Check Y bounds: (UIYOffset - 0x60 + ScreenHeight) <= Y <= (UIYOffset - 0x40 + ScreenHeight)
5. If both bounds satisfied, set g_dwUIMode2Flag=1, reset state fields, call Ordinal_511, return 1
6. Otherwise return 0

Parameters:
nUIPanel (int): Pointer to UI panel structure containing X/Y coordinates at offset 0xC

Returns:
1 if point is within viewport bounds
0 if point is outside bounds

Magic Numbers:
0x12E = 302 (decimal) - Right bound offset from screen width
0x10E = 270 (decimal) - Left bound offset from screen width
0x60 = 96 (decimal) - Top bound offset from screen height
0x40 = 64 (decimal) - Bottom bound offset from screen height
Ordinal_511 = Storm.dll InvalidateViewport - refresh screen viewport after state changes

functions.name: CacheUIResourceFiles
functions.comment:
Cache UI resource files to memory on first access

Algorithm:
1. Check if BuySellTabs file cached (g_dwBuySellTabsFileLoaded == 0)
   - If not cached: Call Ordinal_578 to build path with s__s_ui_panel_buyselltabs
   - Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile to load and cache file
   - Store result in g_dwBuySellTabsFileLoaded
2. Check if MiniConvert file cached (g_dwMiniConvertFileLoaded == 0)
   - If not cached: Call Ordinal_578 to build path with s__s_ui_panel_miniconvert
   - Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile to load and cache file
   - Store result in g_dwMiniConvertFileLoaded
3. Check if InvChar6Tab file cached (g_dwInvChar6TabFileLoaded == 0)
   - If not cached: Call Ordinal_10227 to check some condition
   - If result non-zero: Call GetGlobalSystemState to check state
   - If state non-zero: Call Ordinal_578 to build path with s__s_ui_panel_invchar6tab
   - Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile to load and cache file
   - Store result in g_dwInvChar6TabFileLoaded

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - Function has no return value

Special Cases:
- InvChar6Tab file only cached if Ordinal_10227 and GetGlobalSystemState both return non-zero
- All files are 0x104 (260) bytes in buffer size during path construction
- Files cached with data global prefix s_DATA_GLOBAL_6fbae3e4

Magic Numbers:
0x104 - Buffer size for path construction (260 bytes)

functions.name: FlushValidationErrors
functions.comment:
Algorithm:
1. Load and check g_dwValidationErrorCode; if non-zero, call ReportValidationError and clear
2. Load and check g_dwValidationErrorStackA; if non-zero, call ReportValidationError and clear
3. Load and check g_dwValidationErrorStackB; if non-zero, call ReportValidationError and clear
4. Call GetGlobalSystemState() to determine if system is currently active
5. If system is active AND g_dwValidationErrorStackC is non-zero, call ReportValidationError and clear

Parameters:
(none - void function)

Returns:
(void - no return value)

functions.name: InitializeUIPanel
functions.comment:
Initialize UI panel based on mode (trade or inventory)

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI item flag or UI state flag is set
2. If either flag set, call FUN_6fb8d210 with parameters (3,0,0.0,0.0,0)
3. Clear UI item flag, UI state flag, and UI mode flag to 0
4. Branch on nPanelMode:
   - If nPanelMode == 0: Set g_dwObjectType to 0x0A, call SetScrollWindowMode(0)
   - If nPanelMode != 0: Clear last interaction time, set g_dwObjectType to 0x0B, call SetScrollWindowMode(3)
5. If nPanelMode != 0 and validation error code is 0:
   - Call Ordinal_578 to build path string into szBufferPath
   - Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile with szBufferPath and flag 0
6. Clear all UI flags (UIRefreshFlag, UIStateFlag, UIUpdateFlag, UIPanelFlag, UIVisibilityFlag)
7. Return void

Parameters:
nPanelMode (int in ECX via __fastcall): Panel mode - 0 for inventory, non-zero for trade

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x104: Path buffer size (260 bytes)
- Magic number 0x0A: Object type for inventory mode
- Magic number 0x0B: Object type for trade mode
- Function skips file operations if validation error already present

functions.name: ProcessUIClickRegionCheck
functions.comment:
Validates click event coordinates against three UI regions when object type is 0xb (inventory/interface mode).

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwObjectType == 0xb (UI interaction mode)
2. Extract screen X coordinate from low word of pClickEvent[3]
3. Extract screen Y coordinate from high word of pClickEvent[3]
4. Store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0 (X) and g_dwInteractionParam1 (Y)
5. Check Region 1 (Alt screen bounds): g_dwMinScreenX_Alt <= X < g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2 AND g_dwMaxScreenY <= Y <= g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2
6. If in Region 1, call HandleUIMouseClickEvent and return
7. Check Region 2 (Mode11 bounds): g_dwMinScreenX_Mode11 < X < g_dwMaxScreenX_Mode11 AND g_dwMinScreenY_Mode11 <= Y <= g_dwMinScreenY
8. If in Region 2, call HandleUIMouseClickEvent and return
9. Check Region 3: g_dwMinScreenX_Region3 < X < g_dwMaxScreenX_Region3 AND g_dwMinScreenY_Region3 <= Y <= g_dwMaxScreenY_Region3
10. If in Region 3, call HandleUIMouseClickEvent and return
11. If click outside all regions, reset UI state: set viewport/cursor to -1, clear selection pointers
12. Call InitializeStringBuffer with null/reset parameters

Parameters:
    pClickEvent (dword *) - Pointer to click event structure; pClickEvent[3] contains packed screen coordinates (low word = X, high word = Y)

Returns:
    void

Special Cases:
    - Only processes events when g_dwObjectType == 0xb
    - Click outside all regions triggers full UI state reset
    - Multiple globals reset to 0xffffffff indicating invalid/cleared state

Globals Modified:
    g_dwInteractionParam0 - Set to click X coordinate
    g_dwInteractionParam1 - Set to click Y coordinate  
    g_dwViewportX, g_dwUIState - Reset to 0xffffffff on miss
    g_dwCursorScreenX, g_dwCursorScreenY - Reset to 0xffffffff on miss (set twice, likely legacy)
    g_pGameStateConfig, g_dwUIFlag1 - Cleared to 0 on miss
    g_pSelectedUnit, g_pSelectedEntity - Cleared to 0 on miss

functions.name: HandleUIPanelButtonClick
functions.comment:
Handles mouse click events on UI panel buttons based on screen coordinates.

Classification: Callback handler - registered to process UI click events when g_dwObjectType == 0xb

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if g_dwObjectType != 0xb (not in correct UI mode)
2. Extract click coordinates from pClickEvent[3]: X = low 16 bits, Y = high 16 bits
3. Store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0 (X) and g_dwInteractionParam1 (Y)
4. Check if click is in minimap close button region (screen right side, offset -0x12e to -0x10e, Y offset -0x60 to -0x40)
   - If yes: Set g_dwUIMode2Flag = 1, mark event handled, call InitializeGameObjectProperties
5. Check bounds via ValidateCoordinateInBounds - if returns 1, exit (already handled)
6. Check if click in Alt screen region (g_dwMinScreenX_Alt to g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2, g_dwMaxScreenY to g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2)
   - If yes: Call HandleMouseInputEvents and return
7. Check if click in Mode11 screen region (Mode11 bounds)
   - If yes: Call HandleMouseInputEvents and return
8. Get game context and inventory owner via GetGameContext/INVENTORY_GetOwner
9. If owner exists: Clear all UI flags, call SendGameStatePacket
10. If no owner, check multiple button regions:
    a. Panel button 1 (UIXOffset+0xdf to +0xff): Toggle g_dwUIPanelFlag, handle refresh
    b. Panel button 2 (UIXOffset+0x113 to +0x133): Set visibility flags
    c. Mode1 button (screen right -0xed to -0xd9, Y -0x57 to -0x45): Set g_dwUIMode1Flag
11. Mark click event as handled: pClickEvent[6] = 1, pClickEvent[7] = 0
12. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to queue the processed event

Parameters:
  pClickEvent - Pointer to click event structure:
    [0x0C] (offset 3): Packed coordinates (low word = X, high word = Y)
    [0x18] (offset 6): Handled flag (set to 1 when processed)
    [0x1C] (offset 7): Reserved (set to 0)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Returns immediately if g_dwObjectType != 0xb
- Returns after ValidateCoordinateInBounds returns 1
- Different code paths based on whether inventory owner exists

UI Button Regions (relative to screen/UI offsets):
- Minimap close: (ScreenWidth - UIXOffset - 0x12e) to (- 0x10e), Y: -0x60 to -0x40
- Panel button 1: UIXOffset + 0xdf to + 0xff
- Panel button 2: UIXOffset + 0x113 to + 0x133
- Mode1 button: (ScreenWidth - UIXOffset - 0xed) to (- 0xd9), Y: -0x57 to -0x45

Global State Modified:
- g_dwInteractionParam0, g_dwInteractionParam1: Click coordinates
- g_dwUIMode1Flag, g_dwUIMode2Flag: UI mode toggles
- g_dwUIPanelFlag, g_dwUIRefreshFlag, g_dwUIColorFlag, g_dwUIUpdateFlag, g_dwUIVisibilityFlag

functions.name: ProcessMonsterCacheAndTransition
functions.comment:
Process monster cache node and conditionally transition to menu state.

Classification: Worker function (conditional cache insertion with state transition)

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwObjectType equals 0xb (monster object type)
2. If not monster type, return immediately (no-op)
3. Set cache node state flag at offset +0x18 to 1 (active/valid)
4. Set cache node counter at offset +0x1c to 0 (reset)
5. Insert cache node into system via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
6. Query UI resource buffer element at index 5
7. If element 5 is zero, call TransitionGameState to enter menu (state 7)

Parameters:
pCacheNode - Pointer to cache node structure to process
             Structure offsets:
             +0x18: dword - State/active flag (set to 1)
             +0x1c: dword - Counter/index (reset to 0)

Returns:
void

Magic Numbers:
0xb (11) - Monster object type identifier
0x18 - Offset to state flag field in cache node
0x1c - Offset to counter field in cache node
5 - UI resource buffer index for transition check
1 - Active state value
0 - Reset counter value

Special Cases:
- Function is a no-op if object type is not monster (0xb)
- State transition only occurs if UI resource element 5 is zero
- No callers found via xrefs - likely referenced via function pointer table

functions.name: SetUIItemState
functions.comment:
Conditionally update UI item and state flags based on current state.

Algorithm:
1. If both current flags are 0 (initial state), proceed to step 6
2. If either input flag is 0, reset display (call FUN_6fb8d210 with mode 3) and update flags, then return
3. If item flag is already 0, go back to step 6
4. If state flag is 0 or current state is set, update flags and return
5. If state flag is set, proceed to step 7
6. If item flag is non-zero, fall through to step 7
7. Call FUN_6fb8d210 with mode 1 (update display)
8. Update both flags to input values and return

Parameters:
- dwItemFlag (uint, ECX): Item selection flag; 0 clears selection
- dwStateFlag (uint, EDX): Item state flag; 0 clears state

Returns:
- void (modifies global state and display via FUN_6fb8d210)

Special Cases:
- When either input is 0, resets display before updating flags
- Skips update if item and state flags haven't changed from current state
- Calls FUN_6fb8d210 in mode 1 for most transitions, mode 3 for full reset

functions.name: IsObjectTypeValid
functions.comment:
Validates if current game object type is valid (Player, NPC, or Object).

Algorithm:
1. Load current object type from g_dwObjectType global variable
2. Compare against 0x01 (Player type) - if match, proceed to success path
3. Compare against 0x02 (NPC type) - if match, proceed to success path
4. Compare against 0x03 (Object type) - if match, proceed to success path
5. If no match found, clear EAX register and return 0 (invalid)
6. Return 1 to indicate valid object type

Parameters:
(none) - Uses global g_dwObjectType to determine object type

Returns:
1 (EAX=1) if object type is valid (matches 0x01, 0x02, or 0x03)
0 (EAX=0) if object type is invalid or unrecognized

Special Cases:
Object type constants: 0x01=Player, 0x02=NPC, 0x03=Object
Used during game state initialization and validation

functions.name: IsObjectTypeMonster
functions.comment:
Checks if current object type is Monster (type 4).

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwObjectType global value
2. Compare against constant 4 (Monster type identifier)
3. Return true if equal, false otherwise

Parameters:
None

Returns:
bool - true if object type is Monster (4), false otherwise

Magic Numbers:
0x4 - Monster type identifier in Diablo II object hierarchy

functions.name: GetLastError
functions.comment:
Returns the last Storm error code.

Algorithm:
1. Read the global error code variable (g_dwLastError)
2. Return the value to caller

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- Last error code set by SetLastError or 0 if none

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_465: Sets the error code (SetLastError wrapper)

functions.name: InitializeOrClearGameState
functions.comment:
Initializes or clears game state based on dialog state parameter.

Algorithm:
1. Store nDialogState value into g_nCurrentDialogState global
2. If nDialogState == 0: Clear all UI and viewport state
   - Set g_pGameStateConfig to NULL
   - Set all viewport coordinates (g_dwViewportX) to 0xFFFFFFFF (uninitialized)
   - Set all screen cursor coordinates (g_dwCursorScreenX, g_dwCursorScreenY) to 0xFFFFFFFF
   - Set UI flags and selection pointers to NULL
3. If nDialogState != 0: Only update g_nCurrentDialogState, exit without clearing state

Parameters:
nDialogState: int - Dialog state identifier; 0 = clear all state, non-zero = update and preserve state

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- State clearing is guarded by equality check with 0; any non-zero value skips reset
- Duplicate cursor coordinate assignments in assembly indicate possible field reuse or register reuse optimization
- Magic value 0xFFFFFFFF used for uninitialized coordinates (representing "no valid value")

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessUIMouseClick
functions.comment:
Validates mouse click coordinates against screen bounds and dispatches to UI handler.

This callback/event handler processes mouse click events for object types 0xC (12) and 0xD (13).
Extracts X/Y coordinates from the event structure, validates against multiple screen boundary
regions based on global system state, and either processes the click or resets UI state.

Algorithm:
1. Check g_dwObjectType equals 0xC or 0xD (inventory/interaction modes), exit if neither
2. Extract packed coordinates from pMouseEvent+0xC: low word = X, high word = Y
3. Store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0 (X) and g_dwInteractionParam1 (Y)
4. First bounds check: validate X in [g_dwMinScreenX_Alt, g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2)
   and Y in [g_dwMaxScreenY, g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2]
5. If outside first bounds, call GetGlobalSystemState to determine active region
6. Based on system state (EAX): select Mode12 bounds (state=0) or NoState bounds (state!=0)
7. Second bounds check against selected region
8. If inside bounds: delegate to HandleUIMouseClickEvent(pMouseEvent)
9. If outside all bounds: clear UI state (g_pGameStateConfig, g_dwUIFlag1,
   g_pSelectedUnit, g_pSelectedEntity = 0) and call InitializeStringBuffer to reset

Parameters:
  pMouseEvent - Pointer to mouse event structure
                Offset +0xC: Packed coordinates (low word = X, high word = Y)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - No direct callers found - likely registered as callback in UI event system
  - Object type must be 0xC or 0xD for any processing to occur
  - Multiple screen boundary regions handle different UI modes/states

Globals Accessed:
  g_dwObjectType (0x6fbf8a64) - Current interaction object type
  g_dwMinScreenX_Alt (0x6fbf6a40) - Primary region min X
  g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2 (0x6fbf6a44) - Primary region max X
  g_dwMaxScreenY (0x6fbf6a48) - Primary region min Y
  g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2 (0x6fbf6a4c) - Primary region max Y
  g_dwMinScreenX_Mode12 (0x6fbf6884) - Mode12 region min X
  g_dwMaxScreenX_Mode12 (0x6fbf6888) - Mode12 region max X
  g_dwMinScreenY_Mode12 (0x6fbf688c) - Mode12 region min Y
  g_dwMaxScreenY_Mode12 (0x6fbf6890) - Mode12 region max Y
  g_dwMinScreenX_NoState (0x6fbf68bc) - NoState region min X
  g_dwMaxScreenX_NoState (0x6fbf68c0) - NoState region max X
  g_dwMinScreenY_Alt (0x6fbf68c4) - NoState region min Y
  g_dwMaxScreenY_NoState (0x6fbf68c8) - NoState region max Y
  g_dwInteractionParam0 (0x6fbf69f8) - Stored click X coordinate
  g_dwInteractionParam1 (0x6fbf6a00) - Stored click Y coordinate
  g_pGameStateConfig (0x6fbf8a58) - Game state config pointer (cleared on invalid)
  g_dwUIFlag1 (0x6fbf8a5c) - UI state flag (cleared on invalid)
  g_pSelectedUnit (0x6fbf8a68) - Selected unit pointer (cleared on invalid)
  g_pSelectedEntity (0x6fbf8a6c) - Selected entity pointer (cleared on invalid)

functions.name: ProcessUIMouseClick
functions.comment:
Processes UI mouse click events and routes to appropriate UI region handlers.

Classification: Worker function - UI input router

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if g_dwObjectType is not 0xC (inventory mode) or 0xD (stash mode)
2. Extract mouse X coordinate from low word of pMouseEvent[3] (uVar9)
3. Extract mouse Y coordinate from high word of pMouseEvent[3] (uVar8)
4. Store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0/g_dwInteractionParam1
5. Check if game state active and coordinates valid via ValidateCoordinateInBounds
6. If inactive/invalid, check if click is in skill bar region (right side, 0x12E-0x10E from right edge)
   - If in skill bar Y range (0x60-0x40 from bottom), set g_dwUIMode2Flag=1, handle event
7. Call GetGlobalSystemState to determine UI layout mode
8. Check stash panel region based on state (Y: -0x1C7 to -0x1B6 if state, else -0x103 to -0xF2)
   - X range: UIXOffset+0x49 to UIXOffset+0x96
   - If hit, set g_fPanelStashVisibility=1, handle event
9. Check inventory panel close button region (X: UIXOffset+0x110/0x113 to +0x138, Y: near bottom)
   - If hit, set inventory flags and handle event
10. If ValidateCoordinateInBounds returns 1, clear all UI flags and return
11. Check primary screen bounds (g_dwMinScreenX_Alt to g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2, etc.)
    - If hit, call HandleMouseInputEvents and cache event
12. Check secondary screen bounds based on GetGlobalSystemState (Mode12 vs NoState bounds)
    - If hit, call HandleMouseInputEvents and cache event
13. Get game context, check if inventory has owner via INVENTORY_GetOwner
14. If no owner and click in help button region (-0x57 to -0x45 Y, -0xED to -0xD9 X from right)
    - Set g_dwUIMode1Flag=1, clear other flags, handle event
15. Re-check stash panel region (same as step 8) with different flag clearing
16. Check render mode list bounds (g_pRenderModeList_8/12 regions)
    - If hit, clear all flags, cache event and return
17. Call Ordinal_10005, if result != 2, clear flags and return
18. Additional ValidateCoordinateInBounds check, return if non-zero
19. Check if Y below screen bottom - 0x30, return if so
20. GetScrollWindowMode checks for modes 1 and 3 with left-half screen filtering
21. If GetScreenState returns 6, call SendResourceUpdate
22. Final fallback: set pMouseEvent[6]=1, clear g_pGameStateConfig/g_dwUIFlag1
23. Cache event via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie, clear inventory/panel flags

Parameters:
  pMouseEvent (uint *) - Pointer to mouse event structure
    [3] - Low word: X coordinate, High word: Y coordinate
    [6] - Event handled flag (set to 1 when processed)
    [7] - Event continuation flag (set to 0 when handled)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Exits immediately if object type not 0xC or 0xD (inventory/stash modes)
- Multiple overlapping region checks with priority ordering
- State-dependent coordinate bounds (GetGlobalSystemState affects thresholds)
- Scroll window mode affects left-half screen click filtering

Globals Modified:
- g_dwInteractionParam0/1 - Mouse coordinates
- g_dwUIMode1Flag, g_dwUIMode2Flag - UI mode indicators
- g_fPanelStashVisibility - Stash panel visibility
- g_dwUIPanelFlag, g_dwUIRefreshFlag, g_dwUIColorFlag - UI state flags
- g_dwGameObjectCount, g_dwInventoryItemCount - Object counts
- g_pGameStateConfig, g_dwUIFlag1 - Game state config

Callees:
- IsGameStateActive, ValidateCoordinateInBounds, GetGlobalSystemState
- HandleMouseInputEvents, GetGameContext, INVENTORY_GetOwner
- InitializeGameObjectProperties, InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
- Ordinal_10005, GetScrollWindowMode, GetScreenState, SendResourceUpdate

functions.name: HandleInventoryPanelClick
functions.comment:
Handles mouse click events on inventory/stash UI panels.

Processes click coordinates from message structure and determines which UI region
was clicked, then triggers appropriate UI state changes or panel initializations.

Algorithm:
1. Check g_dwObjectType for 0xC (inventory mode) or 0xD (stash mode)
2. If neither mode active, clear g_dwUIColorFlag and return early
3. Extract click coordinates from pMsg[3]: low word = X, high word = Y
4. Clear UI mode flags and store coordinates in g_dwInteractionParam0/1
5. Get game context and player inventory pointer at offset +0x84
6. Check if game state active and validate coordinates in bounds
7. If no inventory owner and click in close button region (right side):
   - X: screenWidth - UIXOffset - 0x12E to - 0x10E (302 to 270 from right)
   - Y: screenHeight + UIYOffset - 0x60 to - 0x40 (96 to 64 from bottom)
   - Call ProcessUIStateChange(0x19, 1, 0) to close panel
8. Check belt slot region based on GetGlobalSystemState():
   - X: UIXOffset + 0x110/0x113 to + 0x138/0x13B (40 pixel width)
   - Y: screenHeight + UIYOffset - 0x64 to - 0x3C
   - If clicked and g_dwGameObjectCount != 0, send packet 0x4F/0x12
9. Set pMsg[6] = 1 (handled), pMsg[7] = 0 and call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
10. Check character panel button region (lower left):
    - X: UIXOffset + 0x49 to + 0x96 (73 to 150 from left)
    - Y varies by GetGlobalSystemState() return
    - Call InitializeGameStatePanel(3) for skills, (4) for quests
11. Final ValidateCoordinateInBounds check - if returns 1, clear panel flags
12. Handle UI color flag reset and refresh flag management
13. Always mark message as handled before returning

Parameters:
  pMsg - Pointer to UI message structure:
         +0x00: Message type
         +0x0C: Packed coordinates (low word = X, high word = Y)
         +0x18: Handled flag (set to 1 when processed)
         +0x1C: Result code (set to 0)

Returns:
  void - Modifies global UI state flags and message structure

Globals Modified:
  g_dwUIColorFlag, g_dwUIMode2Flag, g_dwUIMode3Flag, g_dwGameObjectCount,
  g_dwInventoryItemCount, g_dwUIPanelFlag, g_dwUIRefreshFlag,
  g_fPanelStashVisibility, g_dwUIMode1Flag, g_dwInteractionParam0/1

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if g_dwObjectType not 0xC or 0xD
  - Close button detection uses screen-relative coordinates
  - Belt slot and panel regions use UI offset-adjusted coordinates
  - GetGlobalSystemState() affects coordinate calculations by 1 pixel

functions.name: ResetUIStateOnObjectTypeMatch
functions.comment:
Resets UI state and clears selection when object type matches expected value (0xC)

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwObjectType equals 0xC (specific game mode/object type)
2. If not matching, exit immediately (early return)
3. Set cache node flags at offset +0x18 to 1 (active flag)
4. Set cache node flags at offset +0x1C to 0 (clear secondary flag)
5. Insert cache node with cookie value into cache system
6. Get UI resource buffer element at index 5
7. If UI resource element is non-zero, exit (resource still active)
8. If UI resource element is zero, perform full UI state reset:
   a. Process UI state change with parameters (0x19, 1, 0)
   b. Send packed data packet (0x4F, 0x12, 0, 0) to notify server
   c. Clear g_pGameStateConfig to NULL
   d. Set viewport/cursor coordinates to -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) indicating invalid
   e. Clear g_dwUIFlag1 to 0
   f. Clear g_pSelectedUnit and g_pSelectedEntity to NULL

Parameters:
dwCacheNodeCookie - Pointer to cache node structure with flags at +0x18 and +0x1C

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Object type 0xC appears to be a specific game mode requiring UI cleanup
- UI resource buffer element 5 acts as a guard; reset only occurs when zero
- Multiple globals are set to -1 as sentinel values for invalid coordinates

Magic Numbers:
0xC (12) - Object type that triggers this cleanup routine
5 - UI resource buffer index checked for cleanup condition
0x19 (25) - UI state change type parameter
0x4F (79) - Packed data message type
0x12 (18) - Packed data subtype
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Invalid/uninitialized coordinate sentinel value

Global Variables Modified:
g_pGameStateConfig - Cleared to NULL
g_dwViewportX (0x6fbb36e8) - Set to -1
g_dwUIState (0x6fbb36ec) - Set to -1  
g_dwCursorScreenX (0x6fbb36f0, 0x6fbb36f8) - Set to -1
g_dwCursorScreenY (0x6fbb36f4, 0x6fbb36fc) - Set to -1
g_dwUIFlag1 - Cleared to 0
g_pSelectedUnit - Cleared to NULL
g_pSelectedEntity - Cleared to NULL

functions.name: InitializeCacheNodeAndInsert
functions.comment:
Initialize a cache node and insert it into the cache system.

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI screen flag (bit 0x40000000) is clear at offset +0xc
2. If flag clear, call EnableUIScreen31() to enable UI screen 31
3. Set node state at offset +0x18 to 1 (mark as active/inserted)
4. Set node state at offset +0x1c to 0 (clear secondary state)
5. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to add node to cache

Parameters:
pCacheNode - Pointer to CacheNode structure (passed as uint)
  +0x0c: dwFlags - Node flags (bit 0x40000000 = UI already enabled)
  +0x18: dwActiveState - Active/insertion state (1 = active)
  +0x1c: dwSecondaryState - Secondary state field (cleared to 0)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- EnableUIScreen31 is skipped if UI flag 0x40000000 is already set
- No callers found in code (likely called via function pointer or external)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x40000000 - UI screen enabled flag in node flags field
0x0c - Offset to flags field in CacheNode structure
0x18 - Offset to active state field in CacheNode
0x1c - Offset to secondary state field in CacheNode
1 - Active/inserted state value
0 - Clear/reset state value

functions.name: InitializeExpansionCacheNode
functions.comment:
Initializes expansion resources and inserts cache node into system.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global system state is active (GetGlobalSystemState)
2. Early exit if system state is inactive (EAX == 0)
3. Check cache node flags at offset +0x0C for 0x40000000 bit
4. If flag not set, check UI resource buffer element 5
5. If UI resource is 0, verify expansion MPQ exists
6. If expansion exists and system state active:
   a. Initialize game object properties (mode 1)
   b. Query system info and increment counters
   c. Get game context and extract resource array at offset +0x84
   d. Get array element 4 and initialize if non-null
   e. Get array element 5 and initialize if non-null
7. Set cache node field +0x18 to 1 (initialized flag)
8. Set cache node field +0x1C to 0 (clear state)
9. Insert cache node via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie

Parameters:
pCacheNode (dword *) - Pointer to cache node structure
  +0x0C: Flags field (bit 30 = 0x40000000 skip expansion init)
  +0x18: Initialization status (1 = initialized)
  +0x1C: State field (cleared to 0)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Exits early without inserting if global system state is 0
- Skips expansion initialization if flag 0x40000000 is set at +0x0C
- Skips expansion initialization if UI resource element 5 is non-zero
- Always sets +0x18=1, +0x1C=0 and inserts node if system state active

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x40000000 - Bit 30 flag: Skip expansion resource initialization
0x5 - UI resource buffer index for expansion check
0x84 - Offset in game context to resource array pointer
0x4, 0x5 - Array indices for resources to initialize
0x18 - Cache node offset for initialization flag
0x1C - Cache node offset for state field

functions.name: InitializeCharacterStorageFiles
functions.comment:
Initialize character storage files (bank and trade stash)

Algorithm:
1. Reset secondary flag to 0
2. Check if bank storage file already initialized (g_pCharacterBankStorage == NULL)
3. If not initialized, construct bank file path by concatenating strings using Ordinal_578
4. Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile with bank path (return value written to g_pCharacterBankStorage)
5. Check if trade stash is available via Ordinal_10227 (returns 1 if enabled)
6. If trade stash enabled, construct and initialize trade stash storage path using Ordinal_578
7. Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile with trade stash path (return value written to g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage)
8. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Function only initializes storage files on first call (checks g_pCharacterBankStorage)
- Trade stash storage only initialized if Ordinal_10227 returns non-zero
- Buffer size is fixed at 0x104 (260 bytes)
- Uses global flags _g_dwSecondaryFlag and g_dwSecondaryFlag

Magic Numbers:
- 0x104 (260) - path buffer size

Ordinals:
- Ordinal_578 - String path concatenation function (constructs UI panel paths)
- Ordinal_10227 - Trade stash availability check function

functions.name: ProcessObjectStateAndValidationErrors
functions.comment:
Processes pending object state transitions and reports accumulated validation errors.

Algorithm:
1. Load current object type from g_dwObjectType
2. Check if object type is 0xc (12) or 0xd (13) indicating portal/waypoint objects
3. If match found:
   a. Reset g_dwObjectType to 0
   b. Call FUN_6fb5d370 with parameters (0x19, 1, 0) to process object-specific logic
   c. Call SendPackedData(0x4f, 0x12, 0, 0) to transmit state update packet
4. Check g_pCharacterBankStorage for pending validation error code
   a. If non-zero error: Call ReportValidationError() to handle error
   b. Clear error code by writing 0 to g_pCharacterBankStorage
5. Check g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage for pending validation error code
   a. If non-zero error: Call ReportValidationError() to handle error
   b. Clear error code by writing 0 to g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage
6. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none) - Function operates on global state only

Returns:
void - No return value; side effects modify global state and may transmit packets

Special Cases:
- If g_dwObjectType is neither 0xc nor 0xd: Skip object type processing, proceed to error reporting
- Zero error codes: Validation error checks skip ReportValidationError() calls
- Multiple errors: Both error globals are checked independently; order of reporting is g_pCharacterBankStorage then g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xc (12): Portal object type ID
0xd (13): Waypoint object type ID
0x19 (25): Object processing command passed to FUN_6fb5d370
0x4f (79): Packet command for state update transmission
0x12 (18): Packet subtype for state update
0: Success/reset value written to error tracking globals

functions.name: ClearCharacterStorageAndResetObjectType
functions.comment:
Clear character bank and trade stash storage, resetting object type if Difficulty or Difficulty+1.

Algorithm:
1. Read current g_dwObjectType from global
2. If g_dwObjectType == 0xc (Difficulty) OR 0xd (Difficulty+1):
   - Reset g_dwObjectType to 0
   - Call FUN_6fb5d370 (0x19, 1, 0) to clear temporary storage
3. If g_pCharacterBankStorage != NULL:
   - Call ReportValidationError to log error
   - Clear g_pCharacterBankStorage = 0
4. If g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage != NULL:
   - Call ReportValidationError to log error
   - Clear g_pCharacterTradeStashStorage = 0

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Only clears storage if both bank and trade stash are populated
- Object type reset only on specific difficulty values (0xc, 0xd)

functions.name: ProcessMode14MouseClickEvent
functions.comment:
Processes mouse click events for game mode 14 (type 0xE).

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwObjectType equals 0xE (mode 14), return immediately if not
2. Extract X coordinate from pClickEvent[3] (lower 16 bits) into g_dwInteractionParam0
3. Extract Y coordinate from pClickEvent[3] (upper 16 bits via SHR 0x10) into g_dwInteractionParam1
4. Check click coordinates against primary viewport bounds (g_dwMinScreenX_Alt to g_dwMaxScreenX_Alt2, g_dwMaxScreenY to g_dwMaxScreenY_Alt2)
5. If within primary bounds, forward to HandleUIMouseClickEvent for processing
6. If outside primary bounds, check secondary bounds (g_dwMinScreenX_Mode14 to g_dwMaxScreenX, g_dwMinScreenX_Mode14 to g_dwMaxScreenY_Mode14)
7. If within secondary bounds, forward to HandleUIMouseClickEvent
8. If outside all valid regions, clear UI state:
   - Set g_pGameStateConfig = 0
   - Set g_dwUIFlag1 = 0
   - Set g_pSelectedUnit = 0
   - Set g_pSelectedEntity = 0
   - Call InitializeStringBuffer with null/reset parameters

Parameters:
  pClickEvent - Pointer to click event structure
    [+0x0C] (dword) - Packed mouse coordinates (X in lower 16 bits, Y in upper 16 bits)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Function returns early if object type is not 0xE
  - Uses dual-region boundary validation (primary and secondary viewport regions)
  - Resets all UI interaction globals when click is out of bounds

Magic Numbers:
  0x0E - Game mode 14 object type identifier
  0x10 - Bit shift amount for Y coordinate extraction (16 bits)

functions.name: InitializeConfigPathCache
functions.comment:
Initializes config path cache on first call, building path from UI panel and global data directory.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cache already initialized (g_dwConfigStatus != 0)
2. If not initialized, allocate 260-byte local buffer for path
3. Call Ordinal_578 to construct path from UI panel and global directory references
4. Call ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile to process the constructed path
5. Store result in g_dwConfigStatus to mark initialization complete
6. Return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Cache is initialized only once on first invocation. Subsequent calls skip processing if g_dwConfigStatus is non-zero.

Magic Numbers:
0x104 (260 decimal) - Buffer size for config path string

functions.name: InitializeGameStateForMode
functions.comment:
Initialize game state for specified mode (Single Player or Multi-Player)

Algorithm:
1. Query current game handle state via FUN_6fb2a190
2. If mode is Single Player (0x20747368 "hst "):
   - Validate game handle exists (return if NULL)
   - Call Ordinal_11107(handle, 10, 0x0b) to set Single Player mode
   - Return on validation failure
3. Else if mode is Multi-Player (0x20326671 "1fq "):
   - Validate game handle exists (return if NULL)
   - Call Ordinal_11107(handle, 0x12, 0x0b) to set Multi-Player mode
   - Return on validation failure
4. Call Ordinal_11108 to finalize mode configuration
5. Set global game state flags to active (0x01)
6. Reset game state counter to 0
7. Record initialization timestamp via GetTickCount
8. If game data file not yet initialized (g_dwGameDataFileHandle == 0):
   - Call Ordinal_578 to build config file path in local buffer
   - Write initialized file data via ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile

Parameters:
- nGameModeId (dword in ECX): Game mode identifier
  - 0x20747368 = Single Player mode ("hst ")
  - 0x20326671 = Multi-Player mode ("1fq ")

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Function returns silently if game handle is NULL
- Invalid mode causes early exit after validation failure
- File initialization only occurs once per session
- Note: Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary (uVar1) optimized away in decompilation

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb2a190 - Query game session handle
- FUN_6fb667e0 - Caller, initiates mode initialization
- Ordinal_578 - Path construction
- Ordinal_11107 - Channel validation/assignment
- Ordinal_11108 - Mode finalization
- ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile - File initialization

functions.name: ResetGameStateAndValidationErrors
functions.comment:
Clears game state flags and validation error code, reporting pending validation errors before reset.

Algorithm:
1. Load validation error code from g_dwValidationErrorCode
2. If error code != 0, call ReportValidationError with the error code
3. Clear validation error code to 0
4. Clear game state flags (g_dwGameStateFlags, g_dwSessionStateValue, g_dwConfigurationFlags) to 0
5. Return

Parameters:
None - Operates on global game state

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Only reports validation errors if g_dwValidationErrorCode is non-zero
- Clears three separate game state tracking variables in sequence
- Called during game state transitions

Related Functions:
- ReportValidationError() - Reports pending validation errors

functions.name: InitializeObjectTypeConfig
functions.comment:
Initialize configuration for object type rendering with opcode data.

Algorithm:
1. Set global g_dwObjectType to 1 (object type identifier)
2. Call GetGraphicInfo() to retrieve graphics resource handle
3. Fetch graphics data offset via Ordinal_10262 (D2Common function)
4. Call FUN_6fb8f0c0 to validate/process graphics data
5. Construct configuration structure on stack:
   - Offset 0: bOpcode = 0x5A (90 decimal, texture/graphics opcode)
   - Offset 1: bValue = 0x0E (14 decimal, variant/mode identifier)
   - Offset 2: bFlag = 0x01 (enable flag)
   - Offset 3: dwReserved = 0x00 (padding)
6. Pass configuration to FUN_6fb573f0 for application/registration

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Configuration structure size is 7 bytes but stored within 8-byte stack allocation
- g_dwObjectType is a global flag indicating object rendering type
- Ordinal_10262 appears to be offset accessor for graphics resource structure

functions.comment:

4. Initialize game object properties with viewport setup (ECX=1, EDX=0)
5. Update system statistics and counters
6. Get game context and extract resource handle at offset 0x84
7. Get array element at index 4; if present, initialize resource
8. Get array element at index 5; if present, tail-call to initialize resource

Parameters:
  None (void)

Returns:
  void - Side effects only (initializes expansion resources)

Special Cases:
- Self-recursive call pattern at entry for expansion validation
- Tail-call optimization used for second resource initialization
- Resources at indices 4 and 5 correspond to expansion MPQ data

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x84: Offset to resource handle array in game context structure
- 4, 5: Array indices for expansion MPQ resource elements
- 1: Viewport/rendering initialization mode parameter

functions.name: RenderInventoryPanels
functions.comment:
Render inventory panel graphics for character equipment slots.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize adPanelData array (18 dwords) to zeros
2. Load unit stat from pUnit->field_0x84 (unit state/inventory)
3. If unit exists: Query stat 3 (armor slot active) via Ordinal_10257
4. If stat 3 inactive/missing: Render armor panel (Slot 1) at g_pPanelArmorInv+offset
5. If unit exists: Query stat 1 (helm/glove slot) via Ordinal_10257
6. If stat 1 inactive/missing: Render helm/glove panel (Slot 3) at g_pPanelHelmGloveInv+offset
7. If no unit: Set dwCheckResult=0, dwWeaponType=0, fIsDualWield=false, goto armor section
8. If unit exists: Query stat 4 (purpose unclear, result unused) via Ordinal_10257
9. Query stat 5 (weapon type) via Ordinal_10257, store in dwWeaponType
10. Get dual-wield state via Ordinal_10291(pUnit, dwUnitStat) - result 2=dual-wield
11. If dwWeaponType zero: Skip to weapon panel section, render secondary slot
12. Check if dwCheckResult nonzero: If true, return early (inventory locked/invalid)
13. Render primary weapon/hand panel (Slot 2) at g_pPanelWeaponsInv+offset
14. If dwWeaponType zero: Render secondary weapon slot (Slot 0) at g_pPanelWeapons2Inv+offset
15. If dwWeaponType nonzero and NOT dual-wield: Render secondary slot (Slot 0), return

Parameters:
  pUnit (UnitAny*) - Character/monster unit; pUnit[0x84] contains inventory/state field
  
Returns:
  void - Renders panel graphics to screen via Ordinal_10072 calls; no return value

Special Cases:
  - NULL unit (iVar1==0): Renders minimal layout (armor, helm, weapons basic)
  - Stat query returns 0: Panel rendered as available
  - Weapon stat==0: Single weapon mode (renders secondary slot empty)
  - Dual-wield (Ordinal_10291 returns 2): Both weapon slots rendered
  
Magic Numbers:
  0x84 - Offset from pUnit to inventory/state field
  0x1,0x3,0x4,0x5 - Stat IDs for unit query (helm, armor, unknown, weapon type)
  0x2 - Dual-wield indicator from Ordinal_10291
  0xffffffff - Render color mask (full white/enabled)
  5 - Render layer/priority value
  18 - Panel data array size (dwords)

functions.name: CheckSnowButtonClick
functions.comment:
Checks if a mouse click occurred within the snow button UI region and enables snow mode if so.

Classification: Worker function - Handles snow mode toggle via UI button click detection

Algorithm:
1. Get game context via GetGameContext()
2. Search for player unit using FindNodeBySearchCriteria with type 7
3. If search returns -1 (not found), call ProcessUIStateChange(0x24, 2, 0) and exit
4. Look up unit in hash table with FindUnitInHashTable(unitId, 1)
5. If unit not found, call ProcessUIStateChange(0x24, 2, 0) and exit
6. Initialize pUIState[6] (clicked flag) to 0
7. Calculate screen bounds: maxY = screenHeight - 49, halfWidth = screenWidth / 2
8. Get cursor position via GetCurrentResourceID() (X) and GetResourceFlags() (Y)
9. First bounds check: cursor must be within (0 to halfWidth, 0 to maxY)
10. If outside first bounds, return without updating UI state
11. Calculate snow button region:
    - X bounds: UIXOffset + 272 to UIXOffset + 304
    - Y bounds: UIYOffset + screenHeight - 95 to UIYOffset + screenHeight - 63
12. Get cursor position again for second bounds check
13. If cursor is within snow button region:
    - Set g_fSnowModeEnabled = 1
    - Set pUIState[6] = 1 (clicked in snow button)
    - Set pUIState[7] = 0
    - Initialize snow effect via InitializeGameObjectProperties(4, 0, 0.0, 0.0, 0)
    - Insert UI state into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
14. If cursor in screen bounds but outside button region:
    - Set pUIState[6] = 1
    - Set pUIState[7] = 0
    - Insert UI state into cache

Parameters:
  pUIState - Pointer to UI state structure
    +0x18 (index 6): BOOL clicked - Set to 1 if click processed
    +0x1C (index 7): uint reserved - Always set to 0

Returns: void

Globals Used:
  g_dwScreenHeight (0x6fbae0e8) - Screen height in pixels
  g_dwScreenWidth (0x6fbae0e4) - Screen width in pixels
  g_dwUIYOffset (0x6fbfd800) - UI Y coordinate offset
  g_dwUIXOffset (0x6fbfd7fc) - UI X coordinate offset
  g_fSnowModeEnabled (0x6fbf8d28) - Snow mode enabled flag (1=enabled)

Magic Numbers:
  0x31 (49) - Bottom margin offset for clickable area
  0x130 (304) - Snow button right edge X offset from UIXOffset
  0x110 (272) - Snow button left edge X offset from UIXOffset
  0x3F (63) - Snow button top edge Y offset from bottom
  0x5F (95) - Snow button bottom edge Y offset from bottom
  7 - Search criteria type for player unit
  1 - Unit type for hash table lookup
  0x24 - UI element ID for ProcessUIStateChange
  4 - Game object type for snow effect

functions.name: ProcessNpcShopHitTest
functions.comment:
Performs hit testing for NPC shop inventory grid slots.

Determines if the cursor is hovering over a valid NPC shop inventory slot
and updates selection state globals accordingly. Used when player opens
NPC shop interface to track which slot the mouse cursor is over.

Algorithm:
1. Get game context and find player unit via FindNodeBySearchCriteria(type=7)
2. Look up player unit in hash table with FindUnitInHashTable
3. If no player found, trigger UI state change (0x24=close shop, mode=2)
4. Clear pUIContext[6] (interaction state offset 0x18)
5. Calculate valid cursor bounds: X in [0, screenWidth/2], Y in [0, screenHeight-0x31]
6. Get current cursor position via GetCurrentResourceID/GetResourceFlags
7. If cursor out of bounds, exit early
8. If snow mode enabled, check cursor against snow region bounds:
   - X bounds: [UIXOffset+0x110, UIXOffset+0x130]
   - Y bounds: [UIYOffset+screenHeight-0x5f, UIYOffset+screenHeight-0x3f]
   - Disable snow mode if cursor outside region
9. Get inventory data from player unit at offset 0x84 (piVar4[0x21])
10. If inventory data exists, reset all selection globals to -1/NULL
11. Get inventory owner via INVENTORY_GetOwner
12. If no owner (player viewing NPC shop), iterate shop display table:
    - Table at g_pNpcShopDisplayTable (0x6fbf8bb0), 11 entries of 20 bytes each
    - Entry format: [minX, maxX, minY, maxY, unused] (5 DWORDs)
    - For each valid entry (minX > 0):
      a. Get cursor position
      b. Check if cursor within entry bounds
      c. If within bounds and slot valid, update selection globals:
         - g_dwUIFlag1 = 1
         - g_dwViewportX = horizontal center of slot
         - g_dwUIState = minY of slot
         - g_dwCursorScreenX/Y = slot coordinates
         - g_pSelectedUnit/Entity = slot unit pointer
13. Return

Parameters:
  pUIContext - Pointer to UI context structure. Offset 0x18 (index 6) is cleared.

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - If player unit not found: calls ProcessUIStateChange(0x24, 2, 0) to close shop
  - If inventory owner exists: skips shop slot iteration (player inventory mode)
  - Snow mode region check prevents selection in decoration area

Magic Numbers:
  0x7     - Search criteria type for player unit
  0x1     - Unit type for hash table lookup
  0x24    - UI state: close shop dialog
  0x31    - Bottom margin offset (49 pixels)
  0x3f    - Snow region upper Y offset (63 pixels)
  0x5f    - Snow region lower Y offset (95 pixels)
  0x110   - Snow region left X offset (272 pixels)
  0x130   - Snow region right X offset (304 pixels)
  0x84    - Inventory data offset in unit structure
  0x14    - Shop entry stride (20 bytes = 5 DWORDs)

Structure Layout - Shop Display Entry (20 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field    Type   Description
  0x00    4     minX     int    Left boundary of slot
  0x04    4     maxX     int    Right boundary of slot
  0x08    4     minY     int    Top boundary of slot
  0x0C    4     maxY     int    Bottom boundary of slot
  0x10    4     (unused) int    Reserved

Global Variables Modified:
  g_dwViewportX        - Horizontal center of selected slot
  g_dwUIState          - Top Y coordinate of selected slot
  g_dwCursorScreenX/Y  - Selected slot coordinates
  g_pSelectedUnit      - Pointer to unit in selected slot
  g_pSelectedEntity    - Same as g_pSelectedUnit
  g_dwUIFlag1          - Set to 1 when slot selected
  g_pGameStateConfig   - Reset to 0
  g_fSnowModeEnabled   - Cleared if cursor outside snow region

functions.name: ValidateAndInsertCacheNodeInBounds
functions.comment:
Validate resource position within screen bounds and insert cache node if valid.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate max Y bound as screen height minus 49 (0x31) pixels
2. Calculate max X bound as half screen width (screen center)
3. Get current resource X position via GetCurrentResourceID()
4. Get current resource Y position via GetResourceFlags()
5. Validate X position: must be >= 0 and <= half screen width
6. Validate Y position: must be >= 0 and <= adjusted screen height
7. If both coordinates valid:
   a. Trigger UI state change with element ID 0x25, state 1 (deactivate), scroll param 0
   b. Clear targeting state to reset targeting system
   c. Set cache node flag at offset 0x18 to 1 (active/valid)
   d. Clear cache node flag at offset 0x1c to 0 (pending cleared)
   e. Insert cache node into system via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie()

Parameters:
pCacheNode - Pointer to cache node structure. Structure has fields at:
             +0x18: dword - Active flag (set to 1)
             +0x1c: dword - Pending flag (cleared to 0)

Returns:
void - No return value. Side effects occur only if position valid.

Special Cases:
- Position check uses signed comparison (JL/JG instructions)
- Returns early without action if position out of bounds
- The 0x31 offset accounts for UI panel/border height

Magic Numbers:
0x25 - UI element ID for this cache operation
0x31 - Vertical offset subtracted from screen height (49 pixels)
0x18 - Structure offset for active flag
0x1c - Structure offset for pending flag

Global Dependencies:
g_dwScreenHeight (0x6fbae0e8) - Current screen height in pixels
g_dwScreenWidth (0x6fbae0e4) - Current screen width in pixels
