functions.name: InitializeMessageQueue
functions.comment:
Initialize message queue based on game mode state transition.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nGameMode equals 0:
   - If game state (g_dwGameInitState) equals 1, reset state to 0 and queue 7 messages from g_aMessageQueue for processing
   - Call Ordinal_10027 (get window handle), then ProcessMessageArray to dispatch messages
2. Else if nGameMode equals 1 AND game state equals 0:
   - Set state to 1 to mark initialization in progress
   - Timestamp current tick via GetTickCount, store in g_dwLastMessageProcessTime
   - Queue 7 messages from g_aMessageQueue for entry processing
   - Call Ordinal_10027 for window handle, then ProcessMessageEntryArray to dispatch

Parameters:
nGameMode: Game mode indicator (0 = shutdown, 1 = startup)

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
State machine prevents re-entrancy: only processes when transitioning between states 0 and 1. If already in target state, returns immediately.

functions.name: PlaceWindowPanelWithCollisionDetection
functions.signature: void PlaceWindowPanelWithCollisionDetection(int nPanelType, dword dwItemHandle, dword dwFlags, int * pCoords)
functions.comment:
PlaceWindowPanelWithCollisionDetection - Positions a floating UI panel with automatic collision avoidance.

Algorithm:
1. Check if panel content height exceeds minimum threshold (g_dwMinPanelHeight)
2. Set active font (ID 13) for text measurement
3. Allocate panel buffer from pool memory (0x2C bytes per panel)
4. Wrap Unicode text to fit max width (180 pixels)
5. Calculate maximum text line width across all wrapped lines
6. Compute panel dimensions: width = maxTextWidth + 20, height = lineCount * 15 + 6
7. Center panel horizontally relative to input coordinates
8. Position panel 50 pixels above input Y coordinate
9. Check if reserved panel slot available (max 16 in g_aReservedPanelRects)
10. If first panel or no collision, store bounding rect and render
11. If collision with existing panels, enter grid search algorithm:
    - X search range: 0 to 400px in 50px increments
    - Y search range: 0 to 280px in 35px increments
    - Direction table at 0x6fbc675c provides search pattern
    - For each candidate position, verify within screen bounds
    - Test against all reserved rects using IntersectRect
12. Once valid position found, store in reserved array and render panel
13. Clean up text buffer and release panel memory

Parameters:
  nPanelType (ECX) - Panel type identifier for styling/behavior
  dwItemHandle (EDX) - Handle to associated game item or object
  dwFlags (Stack+0x4) - Rendering flags controlling panel appearance
  pCoords (Stack+0x8) - Pointer to [X, Y] screen coordinates for placement

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x23 (35) - Y grid search step size in pixels
  0x32 (50) - X grid search step size in pixels
  0xB4 (180) - Maximum text wrap width in pixels
  0x118 (280) - Maximum Y search range in pixels
  0x190 (400) - Maximum X search range in pixels
  0x10 (16) - Maximum reserved panel slots in g_aReservedPanelRects
  0xF (15) - Line height multiplier for panel height calculation
  0x14 (20) - Panel padding added to text width
  0x6 (6) - Base padding added to panel height

Global Data:
  g_aReservedPanelRects (0x6fbfce30) - Array of 16 RECT structures for collision testing
  g_dwMinPanelHeight (0x6fbfcf96) - Minimum height threshold for panel display
  0x6fbc675c - Direction table for grid search pattern (array of X,Y direction pairs)
  0x6fbc677c - Direction table entry count
  0x6fbfcfac - Current reserved panel count

Called By: RenderUnitNameLabel, DisplayUnitNameLabel
Calls: SetActiveFont, FogMemAlloc, WrapUnicodeText, GetStatListOwnerType,
       ProcessWindowPanelScrolling, ProcessItemCleanupNotification,
       FreePoolMemory, IntersectRect

functions.name: ProcessWindowPanelScrolling
functions.comment:
Process window panel scrolling with directional boundary validation.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize panel scroll state flag (offset 0x16) to 1 if currently zero
2. Return 1 immediately if panel state equals 3 (panel disabled/blocked)
3. Query current scroll window mode via GetScrollWindowMode()
4. Validate horizontal boundary based on scroll mode:
   - Mode 1 (left panel): Reject if X > (screen_width/2 - 10)
   - Mode 2 (right panel): Reject if X < (screen_width/2 + 10)
   - Mode 3 (disabled): Reject immediately
5. If boundary validation passes, render panel items via RenderLinkedListItems()
6. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
pPanelData (PanelData *) - Panel structure; offset 0x16 contains state flag
pCoordX (int *) - Coordinate array [0]=X position, [1]=Y position

Returns:
1 - Boundary check complete; panel rendered or validation rejected
0 - Not returned (always returns 1)

functions.name: RenderUnitNameLabel
functions.comment:
RenderUnitNameLabel - Renders a floating name label above a unit or missile.

Algorithm:
1. Get object pointer from unit structure (field at offset +0x5B)
2. Return early if object pointer is null
3. Get unit world coordinates and convert to screen coordinates
4. Adjust X position based on scroll window mode (left/right panel offsets)
5. Check if unit is within visible screen bounds
6. Get unit name string and process UTF-8 text
7. Validate string ID is in valid range (1-0xFFFF)
8. Initialize Unicode name buffer with default constructors
9. Copy name string with length limit (199 chars max)
10. Place window panel with collision detection for label positioning

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure to render name for

Returns: void

Notes:
- Called from ProcessUnitHashTableWithCallback and IterateMissileHashTable
- Uses PlaceWindowPanelWithCollisionDetection for smart label positioning
- Screen bounds check includes 100 pixel margin on X axis

functions.name: ProcessTextRenderingWithTiming
functions.comment:
Processes text list rendering with smooth scrolling and frame-based timing.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pScrollState pointer (assert if NULL)
2. Save font context via SetActiveFont (wraps Ordinal_10127 FlushDrawBuffer)
3. Get current timestamp via timeGetTime (Ordinal_10117 GetSystemTime internally)
4. Calculate frame timing delta and scroll offset
5. If debug overlay flags set, render grid background
6. Traverse linked list of text nodes within visible scroll bounds
7. Render visible text with cel shading and Unicode support
8. Handle partial row clipping at top and bottom boundaries
9. Restore font context and determine if more content exists

Parameters:
pScrollState (int*, ECX): Pointer to scroll state structure containing:
  +0x00: Head node pointer
  +0x04: Visible row count
  +0x08: Current scroll offset
  +0x0C: Line height multiplier
  +0x1A: Last timestamp (ms)
  +0x1E: Start timestamp (ms)
  +0x22: Frame time average
  +0x26: Accumulated offset
  +0x2A: Frame counter

Returns:
0: All content visible (no scrolling needed)
1: Content exceeds visible area (scrollable)

Magic Numbers:
0x70 (112): Base Y coordinate for text rendering
0x4800 (18432): Bytes per text block node
0x17800 (96256): Maximum scroll offset boundary
0x1C000 (114688): End boundary for content check
0x12 (18): Maximum partial row clip height in pixels
0x400 (1024): Rounding factor for offset calculations

Ordinal Calls (via thunks):
Ordinal_10127 = D2Win.FlushDrawBuffer - Flush pending draw operations
Ordinal_10117 = D2Win.GetSystemTime - Get millisecond timestamp

functions.name: RenderInventorySlotList
functions.comment:
Render all inventory slots with item names, handling multi-row layout based on scroll mode.

Algorithm:
1. Check if slot list is empty (g_nSlotCount1) and return if so
2. Initialize UI parameters: base Y offset (0x14 or 0x5f), max 15 items per column
3. Determine scroll mode (GetScrollWindowMode): mode 2 uses right-half screen, mode 1 is narrow
4. Iterate each slot in linked list (g_pSlotList1Head)
5. For each slot, loop 6 sub-items (inventory structure has 6 elements)
6. If sub-item is valid and within display bounds, render item text
7. Build item name string (strcpy/strlen), trim to fit width constraint (0x137 chars max)
8. Call FUN_6fb92980 to render text at calculated X,Y position
9. Call Ordinal_10117 to render item icon/marker at slot position
10. After all items rendered, cleanup expired slots using GetTickCount
11. For each slot with timestamp in past, call Ordinal_10043 to deallocate 6 items + slot

Parameters: none (uses globals: g_nSlotCount1, g_pSlotList1Head, g_dwScreenWidth)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Slot value 0 indicates empty item - skip rendering for that slot
- Text overflow handled by trimming from end when string >= 0x137 width
- Handles two scroll modes: full width (mode 0/3) and half-width (modes 1/2)
- Linked list may modify head during iteration via Ordinal_10043 deallocation
- Expired slots checked against current GetTickCount value

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x14 - Default Y base offset (20px)
0x5f - Alternate Y offset for confirmation mode (95px)
0x13 - Max item rows per column (19)
0xf - Column width in pixels (15)
0x6 - Number of sub-items per slot
0x137 - Max character width before truncation (311px)
0x22 - Offset to next slot pointer in linked list structure
0x1a - Offset to decoration/icon data in slot structure
0x1e - Offset to expiration timestamp in slot structure
0x6ad, 0x6b0 - Ordinal_10043 magic arguments (resource deallocation IDs)

functions.name: RenderSlotList
functions.comment:
Render active slots and clean up expired ones from the slot list

Algorithm:
1. Check if slot list is empty (g_nSlotCount2 == 0), exit if so
2. Call Ordinal_10127() to initialize drawing (D2Common.EndDrawing or FlushDrawBuffer)
3. Determine opacity level (0x0f or 0x64) based on FUN_6fb5d340() checks for states 6 and 0x11
4. Iterate through linked list of slots:
   - For each slot, iterate 6 slot items (stride 0x19 bytes)
   - If slot item active (*piVar6 != 0): get Unicode strlen, call Ordinal_10123 for color, render with FUN_6fb92980, apply effects with Ordinal_10117
   - Move to next slot via offset 0x22 (next pointer)
5. Get current tick count via GetTickCount()
6. Iterate slots again for expiration check:
   - If slot lifetime (offset 0x1e) exceeded current tick, mark for removal
   - Decrement g_nSlotCount2, unlink from list, clear slot data with Ordinal_10043(0x6ad), finalize with Ordinal_10043(0x6b0)
   - Update previous pointer to skip removed node
7. Call Ordinal_10127() to finalize drawing

Parameters: none (__stdcall)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- If g_nSlotCount2 == 0, entire function skipped (early exit)
- Opacity changes based on game state (15 vs 100)
- Slot removal is in-place linked list deletion
- Slot contains 6 items at fixed offsets (stride 0x19)
- Each item at offset 0x1a contains packed data for rendering

Magic Numbers:
- 0x0f: Low opacity level (15)
- 0x64: High opacity level (100)
- 0x19: Item stride in slot (25 bytes)
- 0x96: Maximum scan offset for items (150 bytes = 6 items)
- 0x22: Next slot pointer offset
- 0x1a: Item data offset within slot
- 0x1e: Slot lifetime/expiration offset
- 0x6ad: Ordinal_10043 parameter for item clear
- 0x6b0: Ordinal_10043 parameter for finalization

Structure Layout (Slot Node):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown, may contain item data)
0x04   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown)
0x08   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown)
0x0c   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown)
0x10   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown)
0x14   | 4    | Reserved   | uint | (Unknown)
0x1a   | 4    | ItemData   | uint | Packed item/effect data
0x1e   | 4    | Expiration | uint | Tick count when slot expires
0x22   | 4    | NextNode   | Slot* | Pointer to next slot in list

Related Functions:
- RenderGameFrame: Calls this function each frame
- FUN_6fb5d340: Determines game state for opacity
- FUN_6fb92980: Renders slot with text/color
- Ordinal_10123 (D2Common): Get color code
- Ordinal_10127 (D2Common): Draw synchronization
- Ordinal_10117 (D2Common): Apply visual effects
- Ordinal_10043 (D2Common): Skill data lookup/cleanup

functions.name: InitializeSlotData
functions.comment:
Initialize a slot data structure from source data. Allocates memory, copies slot metadata (count and flags), and links the slot into a linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x26 bytes for new slot structure via Ordinal_10042(0x9ca, 0)
2. Clear 9 dwords + 1 word in allocated buffer
3. Loop through source slots by count at [pSlotSource + 0x18], copying strings via strcpy
4. Copy slot metadata: count (offset 0x18) and flags (offset 0x1a)
5. If g_wSlotDataCount > 0x1f AND g_slotDataStructure != NULL, traverse list via offset 0x22 pointers to find tail
6. For last node found: iterate 6 times calling Ordinal_10043(0x6ad) for non-zero entries, then Ordinal_10043(0x6b0)
7. Unlink old tail by clearing previous node's offset 0x22 pointer
8. Decrement g_wSlotDataCount
9. Link new slot at offset 0x22 to current g_slotDataStructure
10. Increment g_wSlotDataCount and update g_slotDataStructure to new slot

Parameters:
pSlotSource (int *): Source slot structure pointer with metadata at +0x18 (ushort count) and +0x1a (uint flags)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Slot counter g_wSlotDataCount capped at 0x20 (32 slots max)
- Unaffected registers unaff_ESI and unaff_EDI used for string operations
- Linked list maintained via pointers at offset 0x22
- Uses two undocumented Ordinals: Ordinal_10042 (memory allocation), Ordinal_10043 (output/logging)

functions.name: InitializeStateCallbackAndData
functions.comment:
Initialize game state callback function pointer and data value.

Algorithm:
1. Accept callback function pointer via ECX register (__fastcall)
2. Accept game state data value via EDX register (__fastcall)
3. Store callback function pointer in global g_pfnStateCallback
4. Store game state data value in global g_dwGameStateData
5. Return to caller immediately

Parameters:
pfnStateCallback (IMPLICIT via ECX) - Function pointer callback invoked for game state transitions
dwGameStateData (IMPLICIT via EDX) - Game state data value stored for global use

Returns:
void - No return value; function only initializes globals for later callback invocation

functions.name: ShutdownGameResources
functions.comment:
Shuts down game resources and clears resource handles.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pResourceHandle is allocated (non-zero)
2. If allocated, call FUN_6fb8d0c0(g_pResourceHandle) to shut down resource
3. If shutdown returns non-zero status, call FUN_6fb8d670(nResourceResult, 0, 0, 4) to cleanup additional resources
4. Clear g_pResourceHandle to NULL
5. Clear g_dwCleanupFlag to 0
6. Return

Parameters:
  (none)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - If g_pResourceHandle is NULL, both globals are still cleared but no shutdown calls made
  - If FUN_6fb8d0c0 returns 0, secondary cleanup is skipped

Magic Numbers:
  0x4 - fourth parameter to cleanup function (possibly cleanup flags or resource type)
  0x0 - parameters to cleanup function (null/no-op values)

Global Variables:
  g_pResourceHandle @ 0x6fbfd004 - Resource handle pointer
  g_dwCleanupFlag @ 0x6fbfcfd3 - Cleanup state flag

Related Functions:
  - RenderGameFrame() - Calls this function during game shutdown
  - FUN_6fb8d0c0() - Resource shutdown handler
  - FUN_6fb8d670() - Secondary resource cleanup

functions.name: ParseUnicodeStringLine
functions.signature: dword * ParseUnicodeStringLine(ushort * pwLine, dword * pdwLineCount, ushort * pwResult)
strings: 0xF0618|s_line_0_of_string_does_not_contai_6fb90618|line 0 of string does not contain scroll rate
functions.comment:
Parse Unicode-encoded string data into a linked list of line buffers.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output list (pHead=NULL, pCurrent=NULL)
2. Loop until wZero terminator (0x0000) encountered:
   a. Allocate buffer via Ordinal_10042(0x5b2, 0) - allocate 0x5b2 bytes
   b. Read ushorts until newline (0x000A) or 100 elements collected
   c. If first iteration: validate input for non-ASCII (wChar > 0x7F), convert via toUtf
   d. Query window size via Ordinal_10121() - check if line length exceeds 0x133
   e. Allocate final buffer via Ordinal_10042(0x5e5, 0) - allocate 0x5e5 bytes
   f. Copy decoded line into buffer via strcpy
   g. Link buffer into list (pCurrent->next = new buffer)
   h. Increment line counter
3. Return pHead (first buffer in list)

Parameters:
pwLine (ushort *) - IMPLICIT in ECX - Pointer to Unicode string data (ushort array)
pdwLineCount (dword *) - IMPLICIT in EDX - Pointer to line counter (incremented per line parsed)
pwResult (ushort *) - Stack param - Result buffer for output status codes

Returns:
dword * - Pointer to head of parsed line buffer list (NULL if input is empty)

Special Cases:
- Empty input (wZero at start) returns NULL immediately
- ASCII-only input processed via toUtf conversion
- Non-ASCII content (wChar > 0x7F) sets pwResult=8, uses wprintfA error
- Lines exceeding 100 elements truncated
- Line length validation: fatal if exceeds 0x133 (307 chars)
- Unaffected registers: ESI (pwLine ptr), EDI (result buffer)

functions.name: GetValidatedResourceHandle
functions.comment:
Retrieves validated game resource handle based on initialization state

Algorithm:
1. Check if resource validation flag (g_bResourceValidationFlag) is set
   - If true: call FUN_6fb60e10 with stored resource handle (g_pStoredResourceHandle) and type flag 1, return result
2. Check if game initialization required flag (g_bGameInitRequired) is set
   - If true: call FUN_6fb60e10 with game init resource handle (g_dwGameInitResourceHandle) and type flag 2, return result
3. If neither condition true: return NULL

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
Pointer to validated resource handle on success (int *), NULL if neither validation flag set

Special Cases:
- Returns NULL (0x0) if neither resource validation flag nor game init required flag is set
- Type flags (1, 2) distinguish between resource validation and game init validation paths

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1 - Resource validation type flag for FUN_6fb60e10 first call
0x2 - Game initialization type flag for FUN_6fb60e10 second call

functions.name: ProcessGameEventMessage
functions.comment:
Processes game event messages for automap, game state, and UI updates. Supports three message types: automap operations (0x01), game state initialization (0x02), and cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Load message type byte from offset +1, branch on value
2. Type 0x01 (Automap):
   a. Fetch unit node for resource ID (offset +2) via FUN_6fb60e10
   b. Validate: unit exists AND offset+6==0x01 AND offset+8==0x03
   c. If valid and unit.stat[0x32] exists: release stat via Ordinal_10893, update from config
   d. If not valid: cleanup old automap, create new via Ordinal_10901, init via Ordinal_10910/10911
3. Type 0x02 (Game State):
   a. Fetch unit for resource ID
   b. Check offset +8: if != 0x03, partial init path; if == 0x03, full init path
   c. Partial (offset+8 != 0x03): set config flags via g_wGameConfigFlags, call InitializeGameState
   d. Full (offset+8 == 0x03): 
      - Cleanup existing item queue (Ordinal_10043 for UI 0x609, 0x60a, 0x688)
      - Allocate new item container (Ordinal_10042 for 0x657 resource)
      - Initialize validation flag, calculate queue timeout from string length
      - Setup scroll positions based on item dimensions
4. Other types: cleanup automap via Ordinal_10902

Parameters:
nEventMsg (IMPLICIT ECX, int) - Pointer to event message structure:
  +0: [1 byte] Type indicator (0x01/0x02/other)
  +2: [4 bytes] Resource ID (uint)
  +6: [1 byte] Config flag
  +8: [1 byte] State indicator (0x03=full init)
  +10: [2 bytes] Game/Session ID (word)
unaff_EDI (preserved EDI, char*) - String data pointer for timeout calculation

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- State byte 0x03 enables full initialization path with queue setup
- Queue timeout multiplier: (strlen(unaff_EDI) + 0x19) * 200ms
- Scroll calculation: Y = 100 - (item_height >> 2), X = 320 - (item_width >> 1)
- Config flags stored in g_wGameConfigFlags (0x6fbfcfbc)
- Automap handle in g_pAutomapHandle (0x6fbfcfe0)
- Item queue pointer in g_pSecondItemList (0x6fbfcfd8)

Ordinal Mappings (from KNOWN_ORDINALS.md):
- Ordinal_10042: GetItemData - Allocate item container resource
- Ordinal_10043: GetSkillData - Destroy/remove UI elements by ID
- Ordinal_10199: Ordinal_10199 - Get item capacity/data
- Ordinal_10892: Ordinal_10892 - Get localized config string
- Ordinal_10893: Ordinal_10893 - Release resource/stat
- Ordinal_10004: Ordinal_10004 - System initialization
- Ordinal_10127: Ordinal_10127 - End drawing/flush
- Ordinal_10901: Ordinal_10901 - Create automap
- Ordinal_10902: Ordinal_10902 - Release automap
- Ordinal_10910: Ordinal_10910 - Initialize automap config
- Ordinal_10911: Ordinal_10911 - Finalize automap

Message Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field | Type | Description
0      | 1    | bType | byte | Message type (0x01=Automap, 0x02=State, other=Cleanup)
1      | 1    | bPad  | byte | Padding/alignment
2      | 4    | dwId  | uint | Resource ID for unit/item lookup
6      | 1    | bCfg  | byte | Configuration flag (0x01 for automap)
7      | 1    | bPad2 | byte | Padding
8      | 1    | bSt   | byte | State (0x03=full init path)
9      | 1    | bPad3 | byte | Padding
10     | 2    | wGid  | word | Game/Session ID for initialization

Magic Numbers:
0x01, 0x02, 0x03 - Type/state discriminators
0xc8 - Unit stat offset (0x32 * 4 = 0xc8)
0x609, 0x60a, 0x688 - UI element resource IDs
0x657 - Item container resource ID
0xb4 - Item capacity value
0x16 - Queue validation flag offset
0x12 - Queue item height offset
0x10 - Queue item width offset
0x64 - Scroll Y base value (100)
0x140 - Scroll X base value (320)
0x19 - Timeout constant multiplier
0x200 - Scroll calculation multiplier
0x100, 0x2 - Right shift amounts for scroll calc

Note: Function contains compiler-optimized SSA intermediate values (piVar1, pvVar2) that appear in decompiled code but are optimized away by compiler. Local buffer abConfigBuffer[20] used for localization data.

functions.name: ProcessNodeListCalculateDimensions
functions.comment:
Calculate ItemQueue container display dimensions based on linked list nodes.

Algorithm:
  1. Initialize maximum value tracker to 0 and clear container dimension fields
  2. Load list head pointer from pContainer->pListHead
  3. Load width multiplier from pContainer->wWidthMultiplier
  4. For each node in linked list, call Ordinal_10121 to retrieve node dimension
  5. Track maximum dimension value across all nodes
  6. After iteration completes (empty list), calculate total height: max_value + 0x14
  7. Calculate total width: (width_multiplier * 0xf) + 0x6
  8. Store calculated height at pContainer->wCalculatedHeight
  9. Store calculated width at pContainer->wCalculatedWidth

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ECX: pContainer (ItemQueueContainer*) - Item queue container with linked list head, dimensions, and multipliers

Returns:
  void - Updates container structure fields wCalculatedHeight and wCalculatedWidth in-place

Special Cases:
  - Empty list (pListHead == NULL): Height = 0x14, Width calculated from width_multiplier only
  - Width multiplier field at offset +0x4: Proportionally affects total width calculation

Magic Numbers:
  0x14 - Height padding constant added to maximum node dimension
  0xf - Width scaling factor applied to width_multiplier
  0x6 - Base width offset added after scaling
  0x4 - Next node pointer offset within each node structure

Structure Layout (ItemQueueContainer):
  Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type    | Description
  0x0    | 4    | pListHead          | void*   | Pointer to first node in linked list
  0x4    | 4    | dwItemCount        | uint    | Reserved/unused in this function
  0x8    | 4    | dwReserved1        | uint    | Cleared by initialization
  0xc    | 2    | wWidthMultiplier   | ushort  | Proportional width factor (multiply by 0xf)
  0xe    | 2    | wHeightMultiplier  | ushort  | Reserved for future use
  0x10   | 2    | wCalculatedHeight  | ushort  | Output: calculated total height
  0x12   | 2    | wCalculatedWidth   | ushort  | Output: calculated total width

functions.name: ProcessLinkedListIterator
functions.comment:
Iterate through linked list structure and process/clear nodes.

Algorithm:
1. Get linked list head pointer from unit handle (Ordinal_10897)
2. If head pointer valid:
   a. Load first node value from head pointer
   b. While node value != 0:
      - Load next node pointer from current node + 4 offset
      - Clear flag 0x609 on node
      - Clear flag 0x60a on node
      - Move to next node
   c. Clear flag 0x688 on head pointer
   d. Finalize/cleanup unit with Ordinal_10898
3. Cleanup/delete linked list with Ordinal_10893

Parameters:
hUnit (uint, IMPLICIT ECX) - Unit/handle identifying the linked list structure

Returns:
void - No return value, function performs side effects on D2 unit data

Special Cases:
- If head pointer is NULL (0x0), skips list iteration and goes directly to final cleanup
- Linked list is terminated when node value equals 0x0
- Linked list node format: [node_value | next_node_ptr @ +4]
- Flag clearing indicates state transitions or resource cleanup

Magic Numbers:
0x609 - Flag to clear during iteration (node-level)
0x60a - Flag to clear during iteration (node-level)
0x688 - Flag to clear after iteration completion (list-level)
0x4 - Offset to next pointer field in linked list node

functions.name: FindQuestInArray
functions.comment:
Search for quest ID in global array and execute quest handling if found.

Algorithm:
1. Determine search range based on quest ID threshold (g_wQuestListStart = 100)
   - If wQuestId < g_wQuestListStart: search indices 0-99 (nIndex=0, nEnd=100)
   - Otherwise: search indices 100 to g_dwQuestListEnd
2. Iterate through g_awQuestIdList starting at nIndex, comparing each element with wQuestId
3. If match found: call Ordinal_10004 (Storm_DBGMessage) with ECX=0xe8c and return
4. If no match after loop: call Ordinal_10004 (Storm_DBGMessage) with ECX=0xe8c and return (JMP not RET)

Parameters:
- wQuestId: Quest identifier to search for

Returns:
- void (always calls Ordinal_10004 before returning)

Special Cases:
- Array search is split into two ranges based on g_wQuestListStart threshold
- Always executes Ordinal_10004 regardless of search result (debug logging call)
- No direct return value; side effects via Ordinal_10004 call

functions.name: ProcessGameShutdown
functions.comment:
Game shutdown cleanup - processes resource cleanup and message queue flush.

Algorithm:
1. Call CopyConfigurationData to sync/copy current config state
2. Iterate through g_pFirstItemList linked list nodes, clearing entries with Ordinal_10043
3. Clear node pointers with Ordinal_10043(0x688, 0)
4. Set g_pFirstItemList to NULL
5. Check if g_pResourceHandle exists, call FUN_6fb8d0c0 to validate, then cleanup with FUN_6fb8d670(handle, 0, 0, 4)
6. Set g_pResourceHandle to NULL
7. Clear g_dwCleanupFlag to 0
8. If g_dwGameInitState == 1: set to 0, call Ordinal_10027 (get HWND), process 7 messages from g_aMessageQueue
9. If g_bPacketPending != 0: send packet 0x31 with data 0xffffffff and config word, clear flag
10. Clear g_dwFrameCounter to 0
11. If g_pAutomapHandle exists: call Ordinal_10902 to cleanup, set to NULL

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Linked list iteration relies on node->next at offset +4 being valid
- Cleanup proceeds even if some global state pointers are NULL (checked with CMP)
- Message processing count hardcoded to 7

Magic Numbers:
- 0x609, 0x60a: Ordinal_10043 subtypes for item list cleanup
- 0x688: Ordinal_10043 subtype for final cleanup
- 0x4: FUN_6fb8d670 parameter indicating resource cleanup type
- 0x31: Packet type for pending data
- 0xffffffff: Packet parameter (0xffffffff = all bits set)
- 7: Message count for ProcessMessageArray

functions.name: CleanupGameState
functions.comment:
Cleanup and reset global game state, reset item list, resource handles, and process pending messages.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize configuration data by calling CopyConfigurationData
2. If g_pFirstItemList exists, iterate linked item list (offset +0x4 is next pointer):
   a. For each item, call Ordinal_10043 with 0x609 (clear item flag)
   b. Call Ordinal_10043 with 0x60a (secondary item clear)
   c. Move to next item via ESI = ESI+4
3. After loop, call Ordinal_10043 with 0x688 (final item list cleanup)
4. Set g_pFirstItemList to NULL
5. If g_pResourceHandle exists, call FUN_6fb8d0c0 to get resource info
6. If resource info valid, call FUN_6fb8d670 with parameters (resource, 0, 0, 4)
7. Set g_pResourceHandle to NULL
8. Clear g_dwCleanupFlag (set to 0)
9. If g_dwGameInitState == 1, set queue size to 7 and call ProcessMessageArray with hWnd
10. Set g_dwGameInitState to 0
11. If g_bPacketPending set, send packet with type 0x31 and config word data
12. Clear g_bPacketPending flag

Parameters: None

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Item list iteration uses offset +0x4 for linked list traversal (null terminator at 0)
- Resource handle cleanup only proceeds if initial validity check passes
- Message processing only if game init state is exactly 1
- Multiple ordinal calls with fixed parameters indicate flag/state clearing operations

functions.name: HandleInventoryPanelClick
functions.comment:
HandleInventoryPanelClick - Handles click events on the inventory panel within screen bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Extract click Y position (upper 16 bits of offset 0xC) and X position (lower 16 bits)
2. Verify click is within valid screen region (Y < height-48, X < width/2)
3. Trigger UI state change (0x10, mode 2)
4. Report and clear any pending validation errors (up to 3)
5. Mark panel as clicked and reset state
6. Insert into cache and initialize targeting system

Parameters:
  pPanel - Pointer to panel structure containing click coordinates at offset 0xC

Returns: void

functions.name: RenderUIMenuScreen
functions.comment:
Renders UI menu screen with 4 options and displays validation status.

Algorithm:
1. Clear screen region at (UIXOffset, UIYOffset - 224) size (width/2 x height-48)
2. If validation error flag is clear, write validation error file using wsprintfA and ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile
3. Initialize slot data array (18 dwords) with zeros
4. Render 4 menu options at different screen coordinates:
   - Option 0: (UIXOffset, UIYOffset - 109)
   - Option 1: (UIXOffset + 256, UIYOffset - 109)
   - Option 2: (UIXOffset, UIYOffset - 49)
   - Option 3: (UIXOffset + 256, UIYOffset - 49)
5. Display additional element (option 10) at (UIXOffset + 277, UIYOffset - 61)

Parameters:
None - accesses global UI state (g_dwUIXOffset, g_dwUIYOffset, g_dwScreenWidth, g_dwScreenHeight, g_dwValidationError3)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Note: Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary (pointer to slot data array) optimized away during compilation.
Ordinal_10055 = Fog.dll ClearRect - Clear screen region
Ordinal_10072 = Fog.dll DrawText - Render text/menu elements

Magic Numbers:
0x12 (18) - Element count for slot data array
0x30 (48) - Screen height offset for clear region
0xe0 (224) - Screen height offset for clear region top
0x6d (109) - Y coordinate offset for options
0x31 (49) - Y coordinate offset for options
0x100 (256) - X coordinate offset for options
0x115 (277) - X coordinate offset for additional element
0x3d (61) - Y coordinate offset for additional element
-1 / 0xffffffff - Color parameter (white)
0x5 - Rendering flag (depth/priority)

functions.name: ProcessGameMode
functions.comment:
Process game mode configuration from a structured data packet.

Algorithm:
1. Check if word at offset +1 in pModeData equals 4 (mode identifier)
2. If not 4, skip processing and return immediately
3. If match, advance pointer by 3 bytes to reach data payload
4. Copy dword at offset 0 to g_dwGameTypeData
5. Copy dword at offset 4 to g_dwDifficultyData
6. Set g_dwExpansionMode to 0 (disable expansion)
7. Copy dword at offset 8 to g_dwGameClassData

Parameters:
- pModeData (int/pointer): Address of game mode configuration packet
  Contains word identifier at +1, followed by mode data

Returns:
- void: No return value, modifies global game configuration

Special Cases:
- If word at +1 != 4, function returns without modifying globals
- Expansion mode is unconditionally cleared when processing

functions.name: ValidateSlotListsAndClearCounters
functions.comment:
Validates and clears two linked list structures (SlotList1 and SlotDataStructure), asserting all nodes were processed.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize counter and get head pointer of g_pSlotList1Head
2. While list head exists, iterate through linked list:
   - For each node, iterate 6 dwords at offsets 0x00-0x14
   - If non-zero data encountered, log via Ordinal_10043(0x6ad, 0)
   - Load next node pointer from offset 0x22
   - Call Ordinal_10043(0x6b0, 0) per node traversal
   - Increment counter, move to next node
3. Verify counter matches g_nSlotCount1, if mismatch call assertion (Ordinal_10023)
4. Clear g_pSlotList1Head and g_nSlotCount1
5. Repeat identical process for g_slotDataStructure and g_wSlotDataCount

Parameters:
None (void)

Returns:
void (Terminates program if slot counts do not match after traversal via FUN_6fb9a10f)

Special Cases:
- Calls Ordinal_10023 + FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) if slot count mismatch - fatal assertion
- Slot structures contain 6 dword fields per node iteration
- Uses Storm.dll ordinals for logging/error handling
- Note: Function uses 3 compiler-optimized stack temporaries (iVar2, piVar3, uVar1) visible only in disassembly

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6ad: Ordinal_10043 parameter for detailed logging
- 0x6b0: Ordinal_10043 parameter for per-node logging
- 0x6c7: Line number for assertion (0x6c7 = 1735 decimal)
- 0x22: Offset to next node pointer in linked list node
- 0x6: Number of dwords to validate per node

Structure Layout (linked list nodes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | [data0]    | uint | First field, checked for non-zero
0x04   | 4    | [data1]    | uint | Additional node data
0x08   | 4    | [data2]    | uint | Additional node data
0x0C   | 4    | [data3]    | uint | Additional node data
0x10   | 4    | [data4]    | uint | Additional node data
0x14   | 4    | [data5]    | uint | Final data field in 6-dword set
0x22   | 4    | pNext      | int* | Next node pointer

functions.name: InitializeCharacterInfoDialog
functions.comment:
Initializes character information dialog with viewport and dialog lines

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwDialogState is NULL (dialog not yet created)
2. If already initialized, exit (early return)
3. Set up SEH exception handler frame
4. Call InitializeDialogStructure with dimensions (5 lines, 30 fields, screen width-20, screen height-130)
5. Set first dialog field value to 1
6. Call Ordinal_10004 (D2Client dialog event initializer) to initialize event system
7. Add first dialog line with Y=0x15, index=4, value=1, line=0
8. Call Ordinal_10004 again for second initialization
9. Add second dialog line with Y=screen_height-0xa5, fixed at address 0x6fb59190
10. Allocate memory block (12 bytes, aligned, -1 flags) using Ordinal_401 (Storm.dll/Allocate)
11. If allocation fails, set g_pCallbackFunction to NULL and return
12. If allocation succeeds, call InitializeViewportObject with dimensions (width-20, height-200)
13. Append viewport to dialog linked list via AppendLinkedListNode
14. Iterate through g_slotDataStructure linked list
15. For each slot, call viewport render callback [EAX+0x30] with 10 parameters from slot data
16. Set dialog line index to -1 via SetDialogLineIndex
17. Restore exception handler and return

Parameters:
(void)

Returns:
(void)

Special Cases:
- If g_dwDialogState is already set, function returns immediately without re-initializing
- If Ordinal_401 memory allocation fails, viewport is not added to dialog
- Slot structure uses 0x22 byte offset for next pointer in linked list traversal
- Dialog viewport callback invoked with parameters from slot fields at fixed offsets

Variable Mapping (SSA temporaries in decompiled code):
- pMemory: Allocated viewport memory pointer from Ordinal_401
- dwStatus: Status/error code tracking
- pExceptionHandler: SEH exception handler frame pointer
- nLineIndex, dwFieldIndex, nYCoord, dwXCoord, dwYCoord: Loop/calculation temporaries
- pbDialogLabel, pdwSlotData: Structure field access intermediates

functions.name: ResetDialogStateAndExecuteCallback
functions.comment:
Reset dialog state and execute pending callback function.

1. Load dialog state flag from g_dwDialogState
2. If state is set (non-zero), call CloseDialogAndCleanup() to cleanup dialog resources
3. Clear g_dwDialogState to 0
4. Load callback function pointer from g_pCallbackFunction
5. If callback pointer is valid (non-NULL), invoke callback with parameter 1
6. Clear g_pCallbackFunction to NULL
7. Return to caller

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- If g_dwDialogState is 0, skip cleanup phase
- If g_pCallbackFunction is NULL, skip callback invocation
- Both state flags are zeroed after processing to prevent duplicate execution

   - Call FUN_6fb5d370(0x18, 0, 0) to disable state
3. Return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Only executes if g_dwDialogState is active (non-zero)
- UI index 0x18 (24) is hardcoded for specific dialog element
- Toggle sequence: enable then disable (paired state transition)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x18: Dialog/UI element index 24 (likely character panel or inventory)

functions.name: HandleDialogMouseClick
functions.comment:
Handles mouse click events on dialog UI elements and processes corresponding game state changes.

Algorithm:
1. Get current mouse coordinates (nMouseX, nMouseY) from input functions
2. Check if dialog state > 2 (indicates open dialog), if not skip dialog processing
3. First dialog region check (0x111-0x133, 0xa8-0xca):
   - Validate click within bounds
   - Calculate offset from UI base (0xa7 - g_dwUIYOffset)
   - Call Ordinal_10004 and Ordinal_10129 with coordinates
4. Second dialog region check (0xdd-0xff, 0x17f-0x1a1):
   - Validate click within bounds
   - Calculate offset (0x17e - g_dwUIYOffset)
   - Call handlers with adjusted coordinates
5. Third dialog region check (0x111-0x133, 0x17f-0x1a1):
   - Similar validation and offset calculation
6. Check inventory/quest state with FUN_6fb62880()
7. If state != 0:
   - Get current state value
   - Call Ordinal_10342 to process state
   - Call FUN_6fb62890 for confirmation check
   - If confirmed, process quest completion (Ordinal_10057, Ordinal_10086)
8. Render active dialog if state in [1,2] and dialog pointers valid

Parameters:
(void) - No parameters; uses global state

Returns:
(void) - No return value

Special Cases:
- Dialog state 3-6 skipped (reserved states)
- Null dialog pointers result in no rendering
- Mouse coordinates checked against UI viewport offsets

Magic Numbers:
- 0x111, 0x133: Dialog X bounds (upper region)
- 0xa8, 0xca: Dialog Y bounds (upper region, 34 pixels tall)
- 0xdd, 0xff: Dialog X bounds (lower-left region)
- 0x17f, 0x1a1: Dialog Y bounds (lower region, 34 pixels tall)
- 0x17e, 0xa7: Y offset calculations for button detection
- 0x17: Quest item ID being processed
- 0x4f: Packet type for quest completion
- States 1-2: Active dialog indices

Note: Function uses 2 compiler-generated phantom variables (extraout_var, extraout_var_00) that are optimized away during compilation. These cannot be renamed or typed as they are intermediate compiler results.

functions.name: InitializeGlobalFlags

Initialize global state flags for game initialization.

Algorithm:

2. Set g_bInitialized flag to 1 (true) - indicates initialization complete
3. Clear g_dwUnknownFlag1 to 0 - reset unknown state flag
4. Clear g_dwUnknownFlag2 to 0 - reset unknown state flag
5. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none) - void function

Returns:
void - no return value

Special Cases:
Function initializes critical global state variables. Called during game startup sequence.

functions.name: InitializeGameObjectsAndReset
functions.comment:
Initialize game objects and reset game state before starting new game/level.

Algorithm:
1. Clear active dialog flag (g_dwActiveDialogFlag = 0)
2. If dialog state 1 exists, close and cleanup, then clear reference
3. If dialog state 2 exists, close and cleanup, then clear reference
4. If game mode state != 7 (in-game):
   a. Check if inventory/equipment state (0x17) is ready via FUN_6fb5d340
   b. If inventory ready:
      - Set inventory to unused state (FUN_6fb5d370 0x17,1,0)
      - Clear game mode flag via ClearGameModeFlag()
      - Initialize UI state via InitializeUIState()
      - Get game mode ready status via FUN_6fb62890()
      - If game not ready AND nInitMode != 0, set dialog state 1 to mode 2 (FUN_6fb5d370 1,2,0)
   c. Check if dialog state 2 (0x5) is ready
   d. If dialog state 2 ready, set to unused state (FUN_6fb5d370 5,1,0)
5. If game mode state != 0, send packet 0x4f with mode 2, then clear state
6. Return

Parameters:
nInitMode (int, ECX) - Initialization mode; non-zero triggers alternate dialog configuration

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Uses game mode state at 0x6fbfd05c: 0x7 = in-game, other = preparing/menu
- Dialog state 1 at 0x6fbfd020, dialog state 2 at 0x6fbfd058
- Active dialog flag at 0x6fbfd060
- Magic numbers: 0x17 = inventory state, 0x5 = dialog state 2, 0x4f = game reset packet

Related Functions:
- CloseDialogAndCleanup() - Cleanup before state reset
- FUN_6fb5d340(int) - Check object state readiness
- FUN_6fb5d370(int,int,int) - Set object state
- ClearGameModeFlag() - Clear game mode bits
- InitializeUIState() - Reset UI elements
- FUN_6fb62890() - Get game mode ready status
- SendPackedData(int,int,int,int) - Network packet transmission

functions.name: IsGameModeInPlayableState
functions.comment:
Validates whether game mode state allows active gameplay.

Algorithm:
1. Load current game mode state from g_dwGameModeState global variable
2. Test if state value equals 0x1 (Playing mode) - jump to return true if match
3. Test if state value equals 0x2 (Paused mode) - jump to return true if match
4. If neither condition met, clear EAX and return false (0x0)
5. If either condition met, set EAX to 0x1 and return true

Parameters:
(none) - Function uses global game mode state via g_dwGameModeState

Returns:
0x1 - Game is in playable state (state value is 1 or 2)
0x0 - Game is not in playable state (state value is any other value)

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x1: Game state representing active playing/gameplay mode
Magic number 0x2: Game state representing paused mode (gameplay suspended but game active)
Game logic requires active gameplay only when in these two specific states

functions.name: TransitionGameState
functions.comment:
Transition game state to menu and record timestamp.

Algorithm:
1. Send transition packet (0x4f) with 2 as parameter count
2. Check if game mode state (g_dwGameModeState) is already 7
3. If not 7:
   a. Set inventory tab to 1 (g_dwCurrentInventoryTab = 1)
   b. Record current tick count to g_dwLastStateChangeTime via GetTickCount()
   c. Set game mode state to 7 (STATE_MENU)
4. Return

Parameters:
(none - __stdcall takes no parameters)

Returns:
(void)

Magic Numbers:
0x4f - Menu transition packet type
0x7 - STATE_MENU (game mode state value)
0x1 - Inventory tab 1 (reset to default)

Special Cases:
If state already at 7, skips state transition to avoid redundant initialization. GetTickCount() provides system tick counter for timing reference.

functions.comment:

functions.name: SendGameStatePacket
functions.comment:
Sends a game state update packet to the server indicating game mode state 7.

Algorithm:
1. Set global game mode state variable to 0x7
2. Extract high word (0x10 bits right) from g_dwUnknownFlag2 as first data value
3. Extract low word from g_dwUnknownFlag2 as second data value
4. Call SendPackedData with operation code 0x4F, parameter count 4, and two flag values
5. Reset global last state change timestamp to 0xFFFFFFFF (marker value)
6. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none) - Function takes no parameters; operates on global state variables

Returns:
void - Function always succeeds; updates global state and sends packet

Special Cases:
The operation code 0x4F and parameter value 4 are fixed constants specific to game state
transitions. The flag splitting extracts both high and low words from a single 32-bit value,
suggesting the packet encodes a two-word flag structure.

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x7 - Game mode state identifier (mode 7 is game active/in-game state)
0x4F - Packet operation code for game state update
0x4 - Parameter count (2 words of flag data)
0x10 - Bit shift for word extraction (16-bit word boundary)
0xFFFFFFFF - Timestamp marker value (indicates last update time reset)

functions.name: SendGameModeStatePacket
functions.comment:
Send game mode state transition packet to server based on current game state

Algorithm:
1. Load current game mode state from g_dwGameModeState (address 0x6fbfd05c)
2. Check if game mode is in active state (4, 5, or 6)
3. If NOT in active mode:
   a. Call FUN_6fb62880() to retrieve mode validation value
   b. Pass value with constant 0xe to Ordinal_10519 for flag processing
   c. Store returned flag in g_dwUnknownFlag2 (address 0x6fbfd050)
   d. Compare result against dwValue parameter using carry flag
   e. If flag value <= dwValue: send standard packet type 0x4f/8 with flag value split into 16-bit parts
   f. Else: use dwValue instead, save to g_dwUnknownFlag2, send packet with dwValue split into 16-bit parts
4. Else (in active modes 4, 5, or 6):
   a. Send transition packet type 0x4f/7 with zero parameters
   b. Reset g_dwGameModeState to 3 to exit active mode
5. Return to caller

Parameters:
- dwValue: Comparison threshold value for mode state validation

Returns:
- void: Function performs side effects (global state modification, packet transmission)

Special Cases:
- Active game modes (4, 5, 6) bypass validation and trigger immediate transition
- 16-bit parameter splitting (SHR 0x10) indicates protocol expects paired 16-bit values
- Constant 0xe passed to Ordinal_10519 is magic number for mode configuration
- Magic number 0x4f is packet type identifier for game mode state messages

Magic Numbers:
- 0x4f: Packet type for game mode messages
- 0xe: Mode validation configuration constant
- 0x10: Bit shift for high 16-bit extraction
- Game modes: 3=inactive, 4/5/6=active gameplay, others=transitional

5. Add 30000 milliseconds (30 seconds) to the start timeout value
6. Compare timeout deadline against current time
7. If time has not elapsed (timeout deadline > current time), return 1
8. If timeout elapsed, initialize UI, reset game objects, reset state flags
9. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
1 if game mode is 7 or timeout has elapsed
0 if game mode is not 7

Special Cases:
- Timeout of -1 (value 0xFFFFFFFF) is treated as indefinite (no timeout)
- Magic number 30000 = 30 second timeout duration in milliseconds

functions.comment:

3. Initialize loop counter with string length, position to first character
4. Loop through each character:
   a. Load 16-bit wide character from current position
   b. Check if character code < 0x100 (ASCII range)
   c. If yes, use lookup table _toUpperTable_exref to convert to uppercase
   d. Store converted character back at current position
   e. Advance pointer by 2 bytes (ushort size)
   f. Decrement character count, repeat until zero
5. Return void

Parameters:

Returns:
  void - Modifies string in-place

Special Cases:
  - NULL pointer input: function returns immediately without processing
  - Empty string: returns immediately after strlen() returns 0
  - Characters >= 0x100: not processed (remain unchanged)
  - Only ASCII characters (0x00-0xFF) use lookup table conversion

Magic Numbers:
  0x100 - Threshold for using lookup table (256 decimal)
  0x6fba5c44 - Address of strlen function pointer
  0x6fba5c5c - Address of _toUpperTable_exref conversion table

functions.name: CalculateEntityResistance
functions.comment:
Calculate entity resistance value for spell/attack effects.

Algorithm:
1. Validate entity pointer is not NULL
2. Check entity type field [+0x0] equals 1 (required type)
3. Call FUN_6fb63680 for entity validation; return 0 if validation fails
4. Search linked list at [entity+0x8] for packed resistance value
5. If found: calculate nResistanceValue = (foundValue << 7) / 100
6. If not found: get base resistance via Ordinal_10564, get skill bonus via Ordinal_10519(param, 6)
   Then calculate: nResistanceValue = (skillBonus << 7) / baseResistance
7. Clamp result: minimum 2, maximum 0x80 (128 decimal)
8. Return final resistance value [0x2..0x80]

Parameters:
  pEntity - Pointer to entity structure; must be non-NULL with type field = 1

Returns:
  0 - Entity NULL or validation failed
  0x80 (128) - Base resistance lookup failed
  [0x2..0x80] - Final clamped resistance value

Magic Numbers:
  0x1 - Entity type identifier
  0x8 - Entity resistance data offset
  0x80 (128) - Maximum resistance cap
  0x2 - Minimum resistance value
  0x7 - Left shift for fixed-point calculation
  0x51eb851f - Reciprocal constant for fast division (magic number for /100)
  0x5 - SAR shift for magic division result
  0x1f - Right shift for rounding (signed)
  0x6 - Skill parameter for Ordinal_10519 call

functions.name: RenderGridOverlay
functions.comment:
Render a grid overlay pattern on screen with borders and cell tiling.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 18-element cell array with zeros and set menu box handle reference
2. Calculate drawable dimensions: nMaxX = (pRect[2] - pRect[0]) + 1 + pRect[0], nHeight = (pRect[3] - pRect[1]) + 1 + pRect[1]
3. Draw horizontal cells (stride 0xc) from nMinX+0xc to nMaxX-0xd with cell IDs (nCellIndex % 6) + 2 at Y=nMinY+0xc
4. Draw offset horizontal cells from nMinX+0xd to nMaxX-0xd with cell IDs (nCellIndex % 6) + 0x10 at Y=nHeight+10
5. Draw left vertical cells from Y=nMinY+0x16 to nHeight-1 (stride 0xc) with cell IDs (nCellIndex % 3) + 10 at X=nMinX-4
6. Draw right vertical cells from Y=nMinY+0x18 to nHeight-1 (stride 0xc) with cell IDs (nCellIndex % 3) + 0xd at X=nMaxX-7
7. Render 4 corner cells: (0) nMinX,nMinY+0xc, (1) nMaxX-0xc,nMinY+0xc, (8) nMinX,nHeight+1, (9) nMaxX-0xc,nHeight+1
8. Return void

Parameters:
  int * pRect - IMPLICIT ECX register; pointer to 4 DWORDs: [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] defining grid bounds

Returns:
  void - renders grid to screen via Ordinal_10072 calls

Special Cases:
  Cell IDs cycle using modulo to create repeating patterns
  Magic number 0xc (12) is cell stride in pixels
  Cell IDs 0-1 for top edge, 8-9 for bottom edge, 2-7 for horizontal cells, 10-15 for vertical cells

Structure Layout:
  pRect Points to Rectangle:
  | Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description |
  | 0      | 4    | minX       | int  | Left edge X coordinate |
  | 4      | 4    | minY       | int  | Top edge Y coordinate |
  | 8      | 4    | maxX       | int  | Right edge X coordinate |
  | 12     | 4    | maxY       | int  | Bottom edge Y coordinate |

    - [1]: Command 0x16 down key slot  
    - [2]: Command 0x26 up key slot

    - [4]: Command 0x29 down key slot

functions.name: SetKeyBindingSlotForCommand

functions.comment:

2. Check if key binding is active for the command via IsKeyBindingActive()
3. If active, look up key code via LookupKeyBindingByCommandId()
4. If key code found (not 0xffff) AND less than 0xe0 (valid range), use it
5. Otherwise fall back to dwDefaultKey parameter
