    - Else if g_dwGameDataMode == 2: Set to 1, clear buffer, optionally call FUN_6fb8f0c0
14. Call FUN_6fb8d210 with state parameters
15. Retrieve window via Ordinal_10027, call ProcessMessageArray with 8 messages
16. If g_hDialogHandle non-zero: Call CloseDialogAndCleanup, clear handle
17. Call ProcessUIStateChange(0xE, 1, 0) to update UI
18. Call CopyConfigurationData(nullptr) to sync config
19. Return

Parameters:
  pUnit: Pointer to UnitAny - unit entity being interacted with

Returns:
  void - Function modifies global game state and UI

Special Cases:
  - g_dwGameDataMode values: 1=Init, 2=Normal, 3=Special (returns early)
  - g_dwUIViewportMode=0 compresses data, non-zero triggers game state transition
  - Dialog handle cleanup occurs if set from previous UI interaction

Magic Numbers:
  0x18: UnitAny.dwActId offset
  0x1C: UnitAny.pAct offset
  0xC: UnitAny.dwUnitId offset
  0x10: Shift amount for unit type extraction
  0x84: Entity data offset for state value
  0x44: CompressPackedData code parameter
  0x8: Message array count
  0xE: UI state code for viewport interaction
  0x1: Flag value for initial action ID
  0x2, 0x3: g_dwGameDataMode state constants
  
Related Functions:
- HandleInteractionClick() - Validates click within game bounds
- ProcessStructureClickEvent() - Routes structure-specific input
- CheckPointInUIViewport() - Viewport boundary validation
- Ordinal_511() - Initial state notification
- Ordinal_10262() - Entity state extraction
- Ordinal_10027() - Window handle retrieval
- FUN_6fb8d210() - State change notification with parameters
- FUN_6fb8f0c0() - Entity display update
- ProcessGameStateTransition() - Complex game state change
- CompressPackedData() - Data compression for transmission
- ProcessMessageArray() - Message queue processing
- CloseDialogAndCleanup() - Dialog cleanup
- ProcessUIStateChange() - UI state manager update
- CopyConfigurationData() - Config synchronization

functions.name: ProcessStructureClickEvent
functions.comment:
Handles mouse clicks on structure/building objects in the game world.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through all active structures in the global structure array
2. For each structure, check if the click coordinates fall within its bounding box
3. If coordinates match a structure:
   a. Call FUN_6fb8d210 with parameter 1 (initial setup)
   b. If this is the first structure (index 0):
      - Check if game data mode is 2 (world state)
      - Call FUN_6fb8d210 with parameter 2 (secondary setup)
      - Initialize new dialog with dimensions 0x96 x 0x82
      - Set dialog field value to 0
      - Call Ordinal_10004 (D2Common ordinal - initialization function)
      - Add dialog line with resource ID 0xd19
      - Set game data mode to 3 (dialog active)
      - If g_dwGameDataFlag is 0: compress packed data with mode 0x44
      - Otherwise: send game status update
   c. If not first structure and game data mode is not 3:
      - If mode is 2: retrieve ordinal function result (Ordinal_10262)
      - Call FUN_6fb8f0c0 with retrieved value
      - Call FUN_6fb8d210 with parameter 1
      - If g_dwGameDataFlag is 0: compress packed data with mode 0x44 and flag 2
      - Otherwise: call ProcessGameStateTransition
      - Set game data mode to 0
      - Handle mode transition logic for modes 1 and 2
      - Clear message array (8 entries) using Ordinal_10027
      - Close dialog if handle is valid
      - Call ProcessUIStateChange(0xe, 1, 0)
      - Call CopyConfigurationData with NULL
      - Set return value to 1 (click handled)
4. After checking all structures, clear the structure array (set bytes to 0)
5. Return 1 if click was handled, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
  nX (int) - X coordinate of mouse click in game world coordinates
  nY (int) - Y coordinate of mouse click in game world coordinates

Returns:
  1 if click was handled (structure clicked), 0 if no structure at coordinates

Special Cases:
  - g_dwGameDataFlag determines whether to compress data or send update
  - Magic number 0x44 is used as compress mode indicator
  - Magic number 0xd19 appears to be a dialog resource ID
  - Structure iteration uses 0x28 byte stride (structure record size)
  - Each structure has X/Y bounds at offsets: min_x at [+0xbba], max_x at [+0xbbe], min_y at [+0xbc2], max_y at [+0xbc6]
  - Note: Function uses 2 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away by compiler (local_4, local_8)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x96 (150) - Dialog width in pixels
  0x82 (130) - Dialog height in pixels
  0x28 (40) - Structure record size in bytes
  0xd19 (3353) - Dialog resource/string ID
  0x44 (68) - Data compression mode flag
  0x0f (15) - Dialog line parameter (purpose unknown)
  0xe (14) - UI state change code
  0x3 (3) - Game data mode: dialog active
  0x2 (2) - Game data mode: world state
  0x1 (1) - Game data mode: menu state
  0x0 (0) - Game data mode: no state

Ordinals Used:
  Ordinal_10004 - Initialization/validation function (D2Common)
  Ordinal_10262 - Retrieves value from game state structure (D2Common)
  Ordinal_10027 - Gets window/context handle for message processing (D2Common)

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0x00   | 1    | bActive    | byte | Structure active flag (0 = inactive)
  0xbba  | 4    | nMinX      | int  | Minimum X coordinate of structure
  0xbbe  | 4    | nMaxX      | int  | Maximum X coordinate of structure
  0xbc2  | 4    | nMinY      | int  | Minimum Y coordinate of structure
  0xbc6  | 4    | nMaxY      | int  | Maximum Y coordinate of structure

functions.name: GetUnitX
functions.comment:
Get X coordinate of unit. Returns 0 (stub implementation).

Algorithm:
1. Return 0

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*): Unit pointer

Returns:
- dword: X coordinate (always 0 in this stub)

functions.name: CheckStructuresInViewport
functions.comment:
Checks all structures in game against viewport bounds and marks matching ones as active.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize: Load structure count from g_nStructureCount
2. Clear phase: Reset bytes at offsets 0x00 and 0x01 for all structures (40 bytes/structure)
3. Query loop: For each structure, check if rectangular bounds contain viewport position
4. Bounds check: Validate param_1 (nMinX) within [field-4, field+0] AND param_2 (nMinY) within [field+4, field+8]
5. If match: Call FUN_6fb8d210(1,0,0.0,0.0,0) and set bytes at offsets 0x10 and 0x11 to 1

Parameters:
nMinX (int, ECX): Viewport minimum X coordinate for intersection test
nMinY (int, EDX): Viewport minimum Y coordinate for intersection test

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies structure state directly

Structure Layout (g_pStructureViewportData):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 1    | (cleared)  | byte | Reset indicator
0x01   | 1    | (cleared)  | byte | Reset indicator  
0x04   | 4    | nMinY      | int  | Min Y coordinate for bounds check
0x08   | 4    | nMaxY      | int  | Max Y coordinate for bounds check
0x10   | 1    | (set)      | byte | Active flag
0x11   | 1    | (set)      | byte | Active flag

Note: Structure array uses 40-byte (0x28) stride per element. Uses __fastcall convention with implicit register parameters.

functions.name: CompleteGameDataTransition
functions.comment:
CompleteGameDataTransition - Finalizes a game data transition and performs UI cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Marks cache node as complete (sets flags at offsets 0x18 and 0x1c)
2. Inserts cache node with cookie
3. Based on g_dwGameDataMode:
   - Mode 1: Transitions to mode 2 and sets game state
   - Mode 2: Compresses packed data with game context
4. Resets g_dwGameDataMode to 0
5. Updates game object properties based on player unit
6. Processes pending UI messages
7. Closes any open dialogs
8. Triggers UI state change (type 0xE)
9. Copies configuration data to finalize

Parameters:
  pCacheNode - Pointer to cache node structure being completed

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessGameStateTransition
functions.comment:
Handle game state transitions between different modes (initialization, active gameplay, shutdown)

Algorithm:
1. Check game mode flag: if 0 (uninitialized), log error and exit
2. If game is running (FUN_6fb62890), proceed to state machine transition
3. State machine transitions:
   - Mode 1 (ACTIVE): Transition to 2 (GAME_LOADED). Load game buffer, call initialization
   - Mode 2 (GAME_LOADED): Transition to 1 (ACTIVE). Unload game buffer
4. After transition, notify UI system with ProcessUIStateChange (0xe = game state notification)
5. Process message queue with 8 pending messages
6. Close dialog if open and update configuration

Parameters:
None

Returns:
None (void)

Special Cases:
- If game mode is 0 on entry, logs critical error with source file location
- If game buffer cannot be loaded, returns early without state change
- No return value, but modifies global game state (g_dwGameDataMode, g_pGameDataBuffer)

functions.name: SetUnitAttribute
functions.comment:
Processes game state command messages from the message queue, managing data mode transitions and viewport updates.

Algorithm:
1. Extract command code from byte at offset +5 of message structure
2. Dispatch based on command code (0-7) using jump table at 0x6fb5fd64
3. Code 0: Clear message prepare flag and initialize game data path; call FUN_6fb5fd90 for initialization
4. Code 1,5,6,7: Handle state transitions - toggle between modes 1 and 2, manage data buffer lifecycle
5. Code 4: Set mode to 2 and close dialog if window handle is non-zero
6. Default (8+): Log critical error with code location and invoke non-returning exit handler
7. For transition codes: call FUN_6fb62880 to retrieve data item, extract handle from offset +0x84
8. Set mode flag (0x1 or 0x2) at global g_dwGameDataMode address 0x6fbfda1c
9. Initialize viewport coordinates (flOffsetX=0.0, flOffsetY=0.0, nFlags=0)
10. Call FUN_6fb8d210 to update viewport with initialized parameters
11. Call Ordinal_10027 to get main window handle
12. Process message array (size 8) using ProcessMessageArray
13. Close dialog if g_hDialogHandle is non-zero by calling CloseDialogAndCleanup
14. Call ProcessUIStateChange(0xE, 1, 0) to update UI element state
15. Call CopyConfigurationData(NULL) to write current configuration
16. Return

Parameters:
  pGameStateMsg (GameStateMessage*) - Pointer to game state message structure with fields:
    +0x01: DWORD dwGameDataPath - Game data storage path or buffer reference
    +0x05: BYTE byCommandCode - Message command code (0=init, 1=toggle, 4=mode2, 5-7=transition)
    +0x06: CHAR cModeIndicator - Null for mode 3, non-null for mode 5
    +0x84: Nested structure handle - Data item state reference

Returns:
  void - No return value; side effects include modifying game mode state, updating viewport, and processing messages

Special Cases:
  - Default case with invalid command invokes critical error logging and non-returning exit (0xFFFFFFFF)
  - Null dialog handle prevents closure attempt
  - Zero data item handle skips viewport update
  - Magic number 0x8 represents fixed message array size
  - Magic number 0x84 offset contains data item state reference

functions.name: ProcessGameInitialization
functions.comment:
Orchestrates game initialization and state transitions, managing mode switches and configuration.

Algorithm:
1. Clear UI message queue (ProcessUIStatesByResourceBuffer)
2. Set game data mode to 1 (active initialization)
3. Cache current tick count (_g_dwGameDataPath4)
4. Initialize message queue with 8 entries from Ordinal_10027 window
5. Initialize game mode (InitializeGameMode)
6. Trigger UI state change event (0xe = game init event)
7. If event returns non-zero:
   a. Initialize targeting system
   b. Create 16-byte local config buffer with values:
      - [0..3]: 0x6b (107 decimal, unit type flag)
      - [4..7]: 0x5b (91 decimal, skill type flag)
      - [8..11]: 0xde (222 decimal, item flag)
      - [12..15]: 0x116 (278 decimal, config version)
   c. Copy config buffer to global config (CopyConfigurationData)
   d. Return early
8. If message prepare flag clear:
   a. Get game data structure via FUN_6fb62880
   b. Compress packed data block 0x44 with specified buffer
9. Else: Process game state transition (ProcessGameStateTransition)
10. Reset game data mode to 0
11. Get game data structure again via FUN_6fb62880
12. Retrieve ordinal data from offset 0x84 via Ordinal_10262
13. Check game data mode for state machine transitions:
    - Mode 1->2: Set new game data buffer, reset offsets, call FUN_6fb6bc10
    - Mode 2->1: Clear game data buffer, toggle mode back
14. Call FUN_6fb8d210 with offsets and mode flag
15. Finalize: Process remaining messages, close dialog if open
16. Trigger final UI state change (0xe = 1 to finalize)

Parameters:
(void) - No parameters

Returns:
(void) - Returns void

Special Cases:
- Early return if UI state change (0xe) succeeds
- Magic number 0x44 appears to be a packed data block identifier
- Config values (0x6b, 0x5b, 0xde, 0x116) are hardcoded initialization constants
- Game data mode uses values 0, 1, 2 for state machine transitions
- Dialog handle cleanup ensures no dangling window references
- Message queue size fixed at 8 entries

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6b - 107 decimal, Unit type classification constant
0x5b - 91 decimal, Skill type classification constant
0xde - 222 decimal, Item type classification constant
0x116 - 278 decimal, Configuration version identifier
0xe - 14 decimal, Game initialization UI event identifier
0x44 - 68 decimal, Packed data block identifier
0x84 - Offset into game data structure for ordinal data
0x8 - Message queue size constant

functions.name: InitializeGameDataAndProcess
functions.comment:
Initialize game data flag and process initialization sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Set global game data flag (g_dwGameDataFlag = 1) to indicate initialization state
2. Store input game data parameter into global path variable (g_dwGameDataPath3 = dwGameData)
3. Call ProcessGameInitialization() to execute initialization sequence

Parameters:
dwGameData (uint): Game data value/handle passed via ECX register (__fastcall)

Returns:
void - No return value, initialization is performed as side effect

functions.name: InitializeDialogBox
functions.comment:
Initialize the UI dialog box system.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_11148(0) to initialize the dialog box manager (Ordinal_11148 = D2Win.DialogBoxInit)
2. Store the dialog handle in g_pDialogBox
3. Set g_bUIInitialized flag to 0 (false)
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Dialog box handle stored globally for subsequent UI operations
- Initialization flag allows other functions to check if UI is ready
- This is called during UI system initialization (InitializeUISystem)

functions.name: ProcessUIInitializationAndDialogs
functions.comment:
Process UI initialization and cleanup dialog resources.

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI not initialized (g_bUIInitialized == 0x00)
2. If not initialized, call FUN_6fb62880() to get initialization result
3. If result nonzero, call FUN_6fb62880() again to get resource handle
4. Pass handle to Ordinal_10342() (D2Common.GetUnitStat - validate resource) for validation
5. If validation passes, send packet 0x49 with g_dwUIPacketCode via SendPacketData()
6. Set g_bUIInitialized = 0x01
7. Check if g_pDialogBox is non-zero
8. If true, call Ordinal_11149(0, g_pDialogBox) to close dialog window
9. Clear g_pDialogBox = 0
10. Check and report 3 validation errors: g_pValidationError2, g_pValidationError1, g_pValidationError3
11. Report each error via ReportValidationError() and clear the error flag

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- If UI already initialized (g_bUIInitialized != 0), skips initialization and goes to cleanup
- Initialization may fail at two points: FUN_6fb62880() return or Ordinal_10342() return
- Three separate validation error queues checked and cleared sequentially
- Dialog cleanup happens regardless of initialization success state

functions.name: HandleUIMessageEvent
functions.comment:
HandleUIMessageEvent - Processes UI message events for state initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit for specific message types (0x102/9 and 0x104/0x73)
2. On first valid event (g_bUIInitialized==0):
   - Validate game context and room exist
   - Send packet 0x49 with UI code to server
   - Set g_bUIInitialized flag
3. Call ProcessUIStateChange(0x14, 1, 1) to update UI state
4. Set message fields +0x18=1, +0x1c=0
5. Insert message into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie

Parameters:
  pMessage - Pointer to UI message structure with fields:
    +0x04: Message type (0x102, 0x104)
    +0x08: Message subtype (9, 0x73)
    +0x18: Processed flag
    +0x1c: Result/status

Returns: void

Called from: Jump table (UI message dispatch)

functions.name: InitializeUIAndSendPacket
functions.comment:
Initialize UI system and send initial UI packet to game server

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI is already initialized (g_bUIInitialized flag)
2. If not initialized, call FUN_6fb62880() to perform initial setup
3. Validate setup success by checking returned value against zero
4. If setup succeeded, call FUN_6fb62880() again to obtain packet handle
5. Pass packet handle to Ordinal_10342 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) for processing
6. Check if ordinal call succeeded
7. If successful, send UI packet with code 0x49 and stored UI packet code
8. Mark UI as initialized by setting g_bUIInitialized to 0x01
9. Return to caller

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void (no return value, sets global state on success)

Special Cases:
- If UI already initialized, function returns immediately without processing
- If initial setup call fails (returns 0), function returns without sending packet
- If ordinal call fails (returns 0), function returns without marking UI initialized

Magic Numbers:
0x49 - UI packet type code (packet opcode for UI initialization)
0x01 - Boolean true value for UI initialized flag
0x00 - Boolean false value for initialization state check

Note: Function uses 2 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away by compiler (uVar1, iVar2).

Related Globals:
g_bUIInitialized - UI initialization state flag (byte at 0x6fbfda61)
g_dwUIPacketCode - UI packet code to send (dword at 0x6fbfda59)

functions.name: InitializeUIViewportDialog
functions.comment:
Initialize UI viewport dialog and targeting system with packet data

Algorithm:
1. Call ProcessUIStateChange(0x14, 0, 1) to request UI state change
2. If state change successful (result == 1):
   a. Initialize targeting system via InitializeTargetingSystem()
   b. Obtain resource object from FUN_6fb62880()
   c. Chain validation: apply Ordinal_10342, then Ordinal_10057 to object
   d. If any validation returns NULL, set resource flag to 0
   e. Otherwise extract resource flag byte via Ordinal_10001 conversion
   f. Call FUN_6fb60740 with resource flag (0 or extracted byte)
   g. Update UI state via FUN_6fb60860()
   h. Store packet data fields: UI packet code from offset +1, dialog pointer from global
   i. Pass packet data offset +5 to dialog initialization (Ordinal_11150)
   j. Clear UI initialization flag (g_bUIInitialized = 0)
   k. Final UI state update via FUN_6fb60860()

Parameters:
pPacketData (ECX, IMPLICIT) - Pointer to UI packet data structure with fields at offsets +1 and +5

Returns:
void - Updates global UI state and initializes dialog system

Special Cases:
- If ProcessUIStateChange returns non-1, function returns early without initialization
- If any object validation step fails (NULL result), resource flag defaults to 0

Magic Numbers:
0x14 - State change request code (20 decimal)
0x1 - Success flag value for ProcessUIStateChange
0xff - Byte mask for resource flag conversion (isolates lower 8 bits)

Related Ordinals:
Ordinal_10342 - D2Common ordinal function for object processing
Ordinal_10057 - D2Common ordinal function for object processing
Ordinal_10001 - D2Common ordinal function extracting resource flag
Ordinal_11150 - D2Common ordinal function for dialog initialization

functions.name: ValidatePlayerSkillSlots
functions.comment:
Validates player skill slots and updates active slot index.

Algorithm:
1. Clamp nSlotIndex to valid range [0, g_dwMaxSlots)
2. Use switch on nSlotIndex to select validation cascade path
3. For slots 4,3,2: cascade validation through preceding slots
4. Each validation: GetSlotDataBase() then IsNpcTradeFlagSet() check
5. If slot fails validation, decrement to previous slot index
6. Write final validated slot index to g_nPlayerSlotIndex

Parameters:
nSlotIndex (dword, ECX) - Requested player skill slot (0-based)

Returns:
void - Result written to global g_nPlayerSlotIndex

Special Cases:
- If nSlotIndex >= g_dwMaxSlots, clamped to 0
- If all slots fail validation, slot index set to 0
- Cascades: slot 4 checks 4->3->2->1, slot 3 checks 3->2->1, etc.

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x07 (7)  - Right hand skill slot offset
0x0f (15) - Chest skill slot offset
0x17 (23) - Left hand skill slot offset
0x1c (28) - Helm skill slot offset

Related Functions:
- GetSlotDataBase() - Retrieves skill slot base data pointer
- IsNpcTradeFlagSet() - Validates skill slot availability

functions.name: InitializeViewportDialogs
functions.comment:
Initialize viewport dialogs for UI rendering

Algorithm:
1. Clear viewport data structures (DAT_6fbfda66, DAT_6fbfda6a)
2. Get active game viewport via FUN_6fb62880()
3. Get current unit (Ordinal_10342) and unit stat count (Ordinal_10057)
4. Zero-initialize dialog data array (0x5-element stride array at 0x6fbfda76)
5. Validate viewport index (must be less than 5)
6. Mark viewport as initialized in slot table at 0x6fbc9cd0
7. Iterate through unit count range, populate min/max dialog indices via Ordinal_11152
8. Scan dialog range, query dialog properties via Ordinal_11146 and Ordinal_11153
9. Build filtered dialog list (exclude viewport unit ID from active dialogs)
10. Increment counters for valid dialogs (DAT_6fbfda66, DAT_6fbfda6a)

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
(void) - Modifies global dialog state at 0x6fbfda6a-0x6fbfda76

Special Cases:
- Viewport index 5+ causes early return without initialization
- Dialog entry -1 in table means uninitialized slot
- Matching viewport unit ID vs query result skips dialog marking

functions.name: HandleUISlotMouseClick
functions.comment:
Processes mouse click events for UI inventory slots and handles slot selection/activation.

Algorithm:
1. Extract mouse X/Y coordinates from nMouseCoordinates (lower 16 bits = X, upper 16 bits = Y)
2. If click is within UI slot region, return (handled by IsPointInUISlotRegion)
3. If click within screen bounds and below top menu (Y < screen_height - 0x31):
   a. Adjust X/Y to UI coordinate space using g_dwUIXOffset/g_dwUIYOffset
   b. If g_bUISlotDragging is false and g_nUISelectedSlot != -1:
      - Iterate through slot array to find matching coordinates
      - Each slot has bounds [X-0x118 to X], [Y to Y+0x1e], and active status flag
      - On match: Set state to deselecting (0x18=1, 0x1c=0), send packet 0x49, reset globals
   c. Else if g_bUISlotDragging is true and coordinates in drop zone (0x110-0x135 X, 0x182-0x1a5 Y):
      - Call ProcessUIStateChange, check g_bUIInitialized
      - Call FUN_6fb62880 twice to get unit ID
      - Call Ordinal_10342 to perform drop action
      - Send packet 0x49 if successful
4. Reset drag state: g_bUISlotDragging=0, g_nUISelectedSlot=-1
5. Restore mouse state: 0x18=1, 0x1c=0, call Ordinal_511

Parameters:
nMouseCoordinates (int) - Packed mouse coordinates: bits [31:16]=Y, bits [15:0]=X

Returns:
void - Updates global UI state and sends network packets as side effects

Special Cases:
- If click outside screen bounds, only resets drag state without processing slots
- Coordinate validation prevents negative indexes into slot array
- Drop zone coordinates (0x110-0x135, 0x182-0x1a5) are hardcoded screen positions

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x0c - Offset to mouse coordinates in nMouseCoordinates structure
0x10 - Bits to right-shift for Y coordinate extraction
0x118 - Slot width (280 pixels)
0x1e - Slot height (30 pixels)
0x31 - UI menu height (49 pixels)
0x110 - Drop zone left boundary (272 pixels)
0x135 - Drop zone right boundary (309 pixels)
0x182 - Drop zone top boundary (386 pixels)
0x1a5 - Drop zone bottom boundary (421 pixels)
0x49 - Packet type for slot action
0x14 - State change type parameter
0x8b7 - Magic animation/state ID

functions.name: HandleUISlotClickMessage
functions.comment:
HandleUISlotClickMessage - Processes mouse click events on UI slot regions.

Algorithm:
1. Extract click coordinates from message (+0x0C: X in low word, Y in high word)
2. Early exit if click is in active UI slot region
3. If click is right of center or below threshold:
   - Initialize UI if needed (send packet 0x49)
   - Process UI state change (0x14, 1, 1)
4. Determine which skill slot was clicked based on coordinates:
   - Expansion mode: 4 slots with different X thresholds (0x40, 0x80, 0xC0, 0x100)
   - Classic mode: 4 slots with different X thresholds (0x50, 0xA0, 0xEF)
5. If slot changed, reinitialize game object properties
6. Validate player skill slots and initialize viewport dialogs
7. Check for waygate selection in slot bounds table
8. Cache message with processed flag

Parameters:
  pMessage - Pointer to click message structure:
    +0x0C: Packed coordinates (low word = X, high word = Y)
    +0x18: Processed flag
    +0x1C: Result status

Returns: void

Globals Modified:
  g_nPlayerSlotIndex - Current selected skill slot
  g_nUISelectedWaygate - Selected waygate index (-1 if none)
  g_bUISlotDragging - Dragging state flag
  g_bUIInitialized - UI initialization flag

functions.name: FindUnitInHashTable
strings: 0xF2C20|s_current_unit_is_%d,_table_is_sup_6fb92c20|current unit is %d, table is supposed to be %d
functions.comment:
Find and return a unit node from the hash table by unit ID and slot type.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate hash table entry: index = (nUnitId & 0x7f) + nSlotType * 0x80 in g_ppUnitHashTable
2. Get first node in chain at calculated index
3. If node is NULL, return NULL (not found)
4. Check if node.field[2] == nUnitId (ID field at offset 8 bytes)
5. If ID matches and node.field[0] == nSlotType, return node (found match)
6. If ID matches but slot differs, trigger assertion error - inconsistent state
7. If node.field[0] != nSlotType after assertion, crash with abort code
8. Move to next node in chain: pnCurEntry = pnCurEntry[0x42] (next pointer at offset 0x108)
9. Repeat from step 3 until found or NULL

Parameters:
- nUnitId (dword): Unit/entity identifier to search for, hashed using low 7 bits (0x7f)
- nSlotType (int): Slot type or category index, used for secondary hash calculation

Returns:
- int *: Pointer to found unit node if match found, NULL (0x0) if not found
- No match with valid state raises assertion error and crashes

Special Cases:
- If unit ID found but slot type mismatch detected, assertion error indicates memory corruption
- Function never returns after assertion failure - calls FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) to abort
- Hash table uses 128-slot primary index (0x80 * slot count) with linear probe chains

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x7f: Hash mask for primary index (128 slots, items 0-127)
- 0x80: Secondary hash multiplier (128 units per slot type)
- 0x42: Offset 0x108 (bytes) to next pointer in chain (66*4 or equivalent)
- 0x57: Error code 87 passed to assertion handler

functions.name: FindUnitInHashTable
strings: 0xF2C20|s_current_unit_is_%d,_table_is_sup_6fb92c20|current unit is %d, table is supposed to be %d
functions.comment:
Find and return a unit node from the hash table by unit ID and slot type.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate hash table entry: index = (nUnitId & 0x7f) + nSlotType * 0x80 in g_ppUnitHashTable
2. Get first node in chain at calculated index
3. If node is NULL, return NULL (not found)
4. Check if node.field[2] == nUnitId (ID field at offset 8 bytes)
5. If ID matches and node.field[0] == nSlotType, return node (found match)
6. If ID matches but slot differs, trigger assertion error - inconsistent state
7. If node.field[0] != nSlotType after assertion, crash with abort code
8. Move to next node in chain: pnCurEntry = pnCurEntry[0x42] (next pointer at offset 0x108)
9. Repeat from step 3 until found or NULL

Parameters:
- nUnitId (dword): Unit/entity identifier to search for, hashed using low 7 bits (0x7f)
- nSlotType (int): Slot type or category index, used for secondary hash calculation

Returns:
- int *: Pointer to found unit node if match found, NULL (0x0) if not found
- No match with valid state raises assertion error and crashes

Special Cases:
- If unit ID found but slot type mismatch detected, assertion error indicates memory corruption
- Function never returns after assertion failure - calls FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) to abort
- Hash table uses 128-slot primary index (0x80 * slot count) with linear probe chains

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x7f: Hash mask for primary index (128 slots, items 0-127)
- 0x80: Secondary hash multiplier (128 units per slot type)
- 0x42: Offset 0x108 (bytes) to next pointer in chain (66*4 or equivalent)
- 0x57: Error code 87 passed to assertion handler

functions.name: GetUnitFromHashTable
strings: 0xF2C20|s_current_unit_is_%d,_table_is_sup_6fb92c20|current unit is %d, table is supposed to be %d
functions.comment:
Searches hash table for unit matching ID and type, returning pointer or NULL.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit not NULL; exit with error if NULL
2. Check if unit has type tracking flag (0x400 at offset 0xec)
3. If flag not set, return NULL (unit not tracked)
4. Read nUnitType from offset 0xb8
5. Read dwUnitId from offset 0xbc
6. If nUnitType == 3 (type 3 special case):
   - Use g_ppUnitTypeHashTable indexed by (dwUnitId & 0x7f) as entry point
   - Walk linked list via offset 0x108 (pUnitNode->next)
   - Compare field at offset 0x8 (pUnitNode->dwId) against dwUnitId
   - If match and type matches, return pUnitNode
   - If match but type mismatch, call Ordinal_10029 (update), verify type changed, return on success or error exit
7. Else nUnitType != 3:
   - Use g_ppUnitHashTable indexed by (dwUnitId & 0x7f) + nUnitType*0x80 as entry point
   - Walk linked list via offset 0x108 (pUnitNode->next)
   - Compare field at offset 0x8 against dwUnitId
   - If match and type equals nUnitType, return pUnitNode
   - If match but type mismatch, call Ordinal_10029 (update), verify type changed
   - If list exhausted, return NULL
8. On type mismatch error (type still wrong after update), exit with error via Ordinal_10023

Parameters:
- pUnit (int * IMPLICIT ECX): pointer to unit structure with ID/type at offsets 0xbc/0xb8
- (implicit) g_ppUnitTypeHashTable: pointer to type-3 hash table (128 slots)
- (implicit) g_ppUnitHashTable: pointer to type-specific hash tables (128*n slots)

Returns:
- pUnitNode (int *): pointer to matching unit in hash table, NULL if not found
- Never returns if unit NULL or type verification fails (calls non-returning Ordinal_10023)

Special Cases:
- Type 3 has dedicated hash table (g_ppUnitTypeHashTable), type-specific have combined table
- Hash index computed as: (dwUnitId & 0x7f) + nUnitType*0x80 for non-type-3
- Both hash tables searched as linked lists, allowing multiple units at same hash slot
- Field at offset 0x108 is next pointer in linked list (offset 0x42 DWORDS = 0x108 bytes)
- Field at offset 0x8 is ID field for comparison (dwId)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x400: Flag mask at offset 0xec indicating unit is tracked in hash tables
- 0xec: Offset to flags field in unit structure
- 0xb8: Offset to unit type (nUnitType) in unit structure
- 0xbc: Offset to unit ID (dwUnitId) in unit structure
- 0x8: Offset to ID field in unit node for comparison
- 0x108: Offset to next pointer in linked list (0x42 * 4 bytes)
- 0x7f: Bitmask for hash slot selection (0-127)
- 0x80: Stride for type-specific hash table rows (128 slots per type)
- 0x3: Unit type constant for special case handling

functions.name: RemoveUnitFromHashTable
functions.comment:
Remove unit from hash table and cleanup resources.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate hash bucket index: (nUnitType * 128) + (nUnitId & 0x7F)
2. Load bucket head pointer from g_ppUnitHashTable[bucket]
3. If bucket empty, return (unit not found)
4. Traverse collision chain: pUnitNode->dwNextUnit (offset 0x108)
5. For each node, check if pUnitNode->dwUnitId == nUnitId AND pUnitNode->nUnitType == nUnitType
6. If not found after traversal, return (unit not in table)
7. If found and pUnitNode is bucket head (pUnitPrev == NULL), update bucket pointer to pUnitNode->dwNextUnit
8. If found and pUnitNode is in chain (pUnitPrev != NULL), link pUnitPrev->dwNextUnit to pUnitNode->dwNextUnit
9. Call cleanup callback FUN_6fb62360(pUnitNode)

Parameters:
nUnitId - Unit identifier (0-127 hash, full ID stored in unit)
nUnitType - Unit type/class index (0-127, multiplied by 128 for bucket offset)

Returns:
void - Always succeeds silently (no return value for not-found case)

Special Cases:
- Empty bucket: returns immediately
- Unit not in chain: returns silently after chain exhausted
- Bucket head removal: must update g_ppUnitHashTable directly
- Chain node removal: must preserve link chain via dwNextUnit field

Magic Numbers:
0x7F - Hash mask (unit ID modulo 128)
0x80 - Hash table stride (128 buckets per type)
0x108 - Offset 266 bytes - Next unit pointer in linked list collision chain
0x8 - Offset 8 bytes - Unit ID field in UnitAny structure

Structure Layout (UnitAny):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | nUnitType  | int  | Unit type identifier
0x8    | 4    | dwUnitId   | dword| Unit unique ID
0x108  | 4    | pNextUnit  | void*| Pointer to next unit in hash chain

functions.name: UnitInsertIntoHashTable
strings: 0xF2C20|s_current_unit_is_%d,_table_is_sup_6fb92c20|current unit is %d, table is supposed to be %d
functions.comment:
Insert unit into unit hash table or linked list with validation and collision handling.

Algorithm:
1. Extract unit ID (field [0]) and unit table ID (field [8]) from pUnit
2. Check if unit has 0x200000 flag set - determines hash table type (link list vs hash)
3. If link list mode: validate unit not already in list by scanning list
   a. Calculate table index: (unitTable & 0x7f) + (unitId * 0x80)
   b. Scan linked list using next pointer at offset 0x42
   c. For each node: verify unit table ID matches (field [8])
   d. If found: verify unit ID matches (field [0]), return 0 if duplicate
   e. Log mismatch errors via Ordinal_10029 (D2Common.DebugMsg)
4. If unit not found in validation: call FUN_6fb619b0 to search again, error if found
5. If hash table mode: similar validation against g_ppUnitHashTable
6. Scan hash table again with same logic to verify unit location
7. Call FUN_6fb897a0(pUnit, 1) to update unit flags/state
8. Recalculate table pointer based on flag
9. Determine insertion point by scanning table at dwTableIdx
   a. Find position where unit's field [8] is less than current node's field [8]
   b. Track previous node in dwTableIdx variable
10. If previous node exists: link pUnit after it (set previous->offset_0x108 = pUnit)
11. If no previous node: insert at table head (ppTable[dwTableIdx] = pUnit)
12. Set pUnit->offset_0x42 to next node pointer (for linked list traversal)
13. Return 1 for success

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny * in ECX) - Pointer to unit structure containing ID, table ID, and linked list pointers

Returns:
0 - Unit duplicate detected or insertion validation failed
1 - Unit successfully inserted into hash/link table

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x200000: Controls hash table vs linked list mode selection
- Magic number 0x7f: Hash table size mask (128 slots per ID range)
- Magic number 0x80: Hash table row stride (128 rows per unit ID)
- Offset 0x108: Next pointer in hash/link table chain
- Offset 0x42: Alternative linked list next pointer
- Offset 0xe8: Flags field (0x200000 = link list mode)
- Offset 0x8: Unit table ID field
- Offset 0x0: Unit ID field
- Error codes: Ordinal_10023 (D2Common.AssertMsg - fatal), Ordinal_10029 (D2Common.DebugMsg), FUN_6fb9a10f (exit)

Magic Numbers:
0x200000 - Flag enabling linked list mode (field at offset 0xe8)
0x7f - Hash table slot mask (selects 7 LSBs for table offset)
0x80 - Hash table row multiplier (128 rows per unit ID)
0x108 - Offset of primary linked list next pointer
0x42 - Offset of secondary linked list next pointer
0x8 - Offset of unit table ID field in unit structure
0xe8 - Offset of unit flags field

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | dwUnitId   | uint | Unit identifier (0-indexed)
0x8    | 4    | dwTableId  | uint | Unit table ID (controls hash slot)
0x42   | 4    | pNextLink  | UnitAny * | Next unit in linked list chain
0xe8   | 4    | dwFlags    | uint | Flags field (bit 0x200000 = link list mode)
0x108  | 4    | pNextHash  | UnitAny * | Next unit in hash table chain

Note: Function uses 3 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away by compiler (pUVar3, puVar2, pvVar1)

functions.name: FindUnitInTypeList
functions.signature: UnitAny * FindUnitInTypeList(UnitAny * pTypeList, uint dwTypeIndex, uint dwTypeId, uint dwUnitId)
strings: 0xF2C20|s_current_unit_is_%d,_table_is_sup_6fb92c20|current unit is %d, table is supposed to be %d
functions.comment:
Find unit in linked list by type id and unit id.

Algorithm:
1. Load unit list head from array indexed by dwTypeIndex at pTypeList base (offset: pTypeList[dwTypeIndex])
2. Loop through linked list of units (offset 0x108 = next pointer):
   a. If pUnit is NULL, return NULL (list end reached)
   b. Load unit type from pUnit[2] (offset 0x8), compare with dwTypeId
   c. If types match: load unit id from pUnit[0], compare with dwUnitId
   d. If unit id matches, return pUnit (found)
   e. If unit id mismatch: call Ordinal_10029 for validation, recheck pUnit[0]
   f. If still mismatched after validation, log error with Ordinal_10023 and abort
   g. Move to next unit: pUnit = pUnit[0x108], repeat
3. If type doesn't match (pUnit[2] != dwTypeId), skip to next unit without id check

Parameters:
pTypeList (UnitAny *) - Base pointer of unit type list array
dwTypeIndex (uint) - Array index to load unit head: pTypeList[dwTypeIndex]
dwTypeId (uint) - Unit type identifier to match (field offset 0x8)
dwUnitId (uint) - Unit identifier to match (field offset 0x0)

Returns:
UnitAny * - Pointer to unit matching both dwTypeId and dwUnitId, or NULL if not found or error

Special Cases:
- If unit found but Ordinal_10029 validation fails, Ordinal_10023 logs error and function aborts
- Offset 0x8 contains type field, offset 0x0 contains unit id field
- Offset 0x108 is linked list next pointer (constant for all units in list)
- Calling function guarantees valid pTypeList base and dwTypeIndex range

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type     | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwUnitId   | uint     | Unit identifier (primary key)
0x04   | 4    | field_4    | uint     | Unknown field
0x08   | 4    | dwTypeId   | uint     | Unit type identifier
0x108  | 4    | pNext      | UnitAny* | Pointer to next unit in linked list

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10029 (D2Common) - Validates unit type with assertion logic
- Ordinal_10023 - Logs assertion failure with file/line info
- FUN_6fb9a10f - Abort handler (called on validation failure)

functions.name: ValidateUnitStateChange
functions.signature: void ValidateUnitStateChange(int * pUnit, byte bNewState, byte bOldState)
functions.comment:
Validates and applies unit stat modifications on state transition.

Algorithm:
1. Verify unit flag == 0x1 - Unit must be active
2. Verify bNewState != bOldState - State must actually change
3. Call Ordinal_10342 (GetUnitStat) to retrieve current stat value
4. If stat valid (non-zero):
   a. If bOldState == 0x0: Call Ordinal_10100 (RemoveStat) - Remove stat
   b. Else if bNewState == 0x0: Call Ordinal_10101 (ResetStat) - Reset stat
5. Call Ordinal_10214 (CommitStateChange) to finalize modification
6. Return void

Parameters:
- pUnit: int * (IMPLICIT ECX) - Pointer to unit structure
- bNewState: byte (IMPLICIT DL) - New state byte value
- bOldState: byte (Stack[0x4]) - Previous state byte value

Returns:
- void (no return value, state applied via ordinal functions)

Special Cases:
- Early exit if unit flag != 0x1
- Early exit if bNewState == bOldState (no change needed)
- Early exit if Ordinal_10342 returns zero (no stat found)
- Ordinal_10100 and Ordinal_10101 only called if stat exists

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1: Unit active flag value
- 0x0: Null state indicator

functions.name: AllocateUnitCopiesFromTemplate
functions.comment:
Allocate and initialize copies of units from a template list

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10055(dwUnitType) to get first template unit in linked list
2. Loop through linked list (iterating via puVar1[7] offset to next node)
3. For each template with flag bit 0x1 set at offset +0x14:
   a. Call Ordinal_10034(dwUnitType, &nOffsetX) to get position offset
   b. Load template coordinates: x=puVar1[3], y=puVar1[4]
   c. Add offsets: finalX = x + nOffsetX, finalY = y + nOffsetY
   d. Call AllocateAndInitializeUnit(puVar1[1], finalX, finalY, *puVar1, puVar1[2])
4. Continue to next template via puVar1[7] until NULL

Parameters:
dwUnitType (IMPLICIT ECX) - Game unit type identifier for template lookup

Returns:
void - Units allocated as side effect

Special Cases:
- Only processes templates with flag 0x1 set (initialization flag)
- Coordinates stored on stack at ESP+8 (nOffsetX) and ESP+12 (nOffsetY)
- Uses fastcall: dwUnitType passed in ECX register
- nOffsetY calculated from nOffsetX via stack frame (derived value)

Magic Numbers:
0x1 - Flag bit indicating unit should be allocated/initialized
0x4 - Offset multiplier for structure field access (dword field spacing)
0x7 - Linked list node pointer offset (next node at +0x1c = [7]*4)

functions.name: InitializeUnitHashTables
functions.comment:
Initialize unit and link list hash tables to zero.

Algorithm:
1. Set pdwTable to g_ppUnitHashTable pointer (0x6fbfdaa0)
2. Loop 0x300 (768) times: zero each dword entry in unit hash table using REP STOSD
3. Set pdwTable to g_ppLinkListTable pointer (0x6fbfe6a0)
4. Loop 0x300 (768) times: zero each dword entry in link list table using REP STOSD
5. Return void

Parameters:
(None)

Returns:
(void)

Special Cases:
- Uses REP STOSD (repeat store dword) for fast memset - EAX=0, ECX=768, EDI=table base
- Magic Numbers: 0x300 (768 entries per table), 0x6fbfdaa0 (g_ppUnitHashTable), 0x6fbfe6a0 (g_ppLinkListTable)

functions.name: CleanupAllUnitTables
functions.comment:
Cleans up all units in both hash and link-list tables by iterating through all game groups and slots

Algorithm:
1. Loop through each game group (from g_nUnitTableStartIndex to 0x6fba9ad8)
2. For each group, iterate through all 0x80 (128) unit hash table slots
3. For each non-empty slot, walk the unit chain and cleanup each unit via CleanupGameContextAndResources
4. Advance to next slot in unit chain via unit[0x42] (next pointer)
5. Repeat steps 1-4 for link-list table (0x6fbfe6a0)

Parameters: none

Returns: void

Variables:
- pUnitNext (pdVar1): Pointer to next unit in chain, loaded from pUnitCurrent[0x42]
- pUnitCurrent (pdVar2): Current unit being processed from hash/link-list table
- Note: SSA temporaries (piVar3, iVar4) optimized away in decompiler but visible in assembly

Magic Numbers:
- 0x80 (128): Number of hash table slots per group
- 0x7: Left shift to compute group offset (128 = 2^7)
- 0x42 (66): Offset to next pointer in unit structure
- 0x108 (264): Offset to next pointer alternate (used in loop)
- 0x6fbfdaa0: Base address of unit hash table
- 0x6fbfe6a0: Base address of link-list table
- 0x6fba9ac0: Start index for table iteration
- 0x6fba9ad8: End boundary for table iteration

Related Functions:
- CleanupGameContextAndResources() - Cleans individual unit resources

functions.name: DeactivateAllUnits
functions.comment:
Deactivates all units across all hash tables and clears linked unit references.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate player, unit type, item, monster, ghost, unit, and missile hash tables
2. For each unit in table, extract next node pointer (offset 0x108), unit type (offset 0x8), unit ID (offset 0x0)
3. Call FUN_6fb85e00 to deactivate the unit
4. For unit type, item, and monster tables only: lookup linked unit via FindLinkListNodeByIdAndIndex
5. If linked unit found (non-null), check state field (offset 0x0): 1=call FUN_6fb782f0, 2=call FUN_6fb7f9b0
6. After all iterations, call FUN_6fb627f0 on ghost and item tables with step 0x6fb62820
7. Call FUN_6fb627f0 on ghost, item, and unit type tables with step 0x6fb62830
8. If server mode (g_dwServerPort != 0), call FUN_6fb627f0 on unit type and unit tables with step 0x6fb64150

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Units contain linked list pointers at offset 0x108 for traversal
- State-dependent cleanup: state 1 uses FUN_6fb782f0, state 2 uses FUN_6fb7f9b0
- Server mode flag g_dwServerPort determines if additional cleanup passes required
- Hash tables are pointer arrays with fixed bounds

Magic Numbers:
0x108 - Next node pointer offset (dword offset 0x42)
0x8 - Unit type ID field offset
0x0 - Unit ID field offset and state field offset

functions.name: IterateHashtableBucketsAndInvoke
functions.comment:
Iterate through hash table buckets and invoke callback for each linked list node.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize bucket count to 128 (0x80) to iterate all buckets
2. Load first node pointer from current bucket array entry
3. Walk linked list by following offset 0x108 (next pointer)
4. Invoke callback for each non-NULL node
5. Move to next bucket array entry and repeat until all 128 buckets processed

Parameters:
  ppBucketArray - Pointer to array of bucket heads (each entry is pointer to first node)
  pfnCallback - Function pointer invoked for each node in all 128 buckets

Returns:
  void - No return value, operates for side effects

Special Cases:
  - Empty buckets (NULL head) skip inner loop and continue to next bucket
  - 128 is hardcoded bucket count - matches hashtable size constraint
  - Callback invocation at EDX register - assumes __fastcall or register parameter passing

functions.name: InitializeGameContextAndState
functions.comment:
Initialize game context and UI state with validation.

Algorithm:
1. Check if current game context (g_pGameContext) is valid (non-NULL)
   - If valid, call InitializeGameStateWithValidation() to reinitialize state
2. If provided context pointer (pGameContext) is non-NULL:
   a. Extract skill slot value from context offset +0x4 (BYTE)
   b. Retrieve unit data reference at context offset +0x38 (DWORD pointer)
   c. Call Ordinal_10161 with unit data and parameter 0 (likely skill initialization)
   d. Store extracted skill slot into g_byCurrentSkillSlot global
   e. Call SetGlobalStateFlag(0) to reset game state flags
   f. Call InitializeGameUIAndState() to setup UI and game state
3. Update global context pointer g_pGameContext to new value

Parameters:
pGameContext (int *) - Pointer to game context structure, or NULL to clear context
  - Non-NULL: Contains unit data at offset +0x38 and skill slot at offset +0x4
  - NULL: Clears active game context without initialization

Returns:
void - No return value, performs state initialization

Special Cases:
- NULL Context: If pGameContext is NULL, only clears g_pGameContext, skips UI/state setup
- Double-Initialization: If g_pGameContext already valid AND pGameContext provided, reinitializes state before switching context
- Skill Slot: Skill slot value at context+0x4 stored as byte in global (BYTE range 0-255)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x04 - Offset to skill slot value within context structure (BYTE)
0x38 - Offset to unit data reference within context structure (DWORD pointer)
0x00 - Parameter to Ordinal_10161 (skill initialization mode)

Globals Modified:
g_pGameContext - Active game context pointer
g_byCurrentSkillSlot - Current skill slot (0-255)
via SetGlobalStateFlag and InitializeGameUIAndState - Multiple state variables

Related Functions:
- InitializeGameStateWithValidation() - Resets existing state
- InitializeGameUIAndState() - Sets up UI and game state
- SetGlobalStateFlag() - Manages global state flags
- Ordinal_10161() - Skill/unit initialization (D2Common function)

functions.comment:
Check if game is in menu state (0x11).

2. If NULL, return true (inactive)

4. Compare state value with 0x11 (menu state)

functions.name: GetGfxInfoPointer
functions.comment:
Retrieve pointer to graphics info data from a gfx structure.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input gfx data pointer is NULL
2. If NULL, return 0 (null pointer)

functions.comment:
Search unit hash table for unit matching ID and type, validate consistency, invoke callback.

Algorithm:
1. Compute hash bucket from unit type and ID: bucket = ((dwUnitId << 7) | (nUnitType & 0x7f))
2. Load hash chain head from g_ppUnitHashTable[bucket]
3. Loop through linked list (chain via offset 0x108):
   a. Check if unit ID [offset 0x8] matches dwUnitId
   b. If match found, verify unit type [offset 0x0]:
      - If matches nUnitType, jump to callback (success path)
      - If mismatch, log validation error via Ordinal_10029, call abort via FUN_6fb9a10f
   c. Load next unit pointer from [offset 0x108]
4. If no match found in chain, set pCurrentUnit = NULL
5. Invoke callback Ordinal_10344(dwCallbackParam, pCurrentUnit)

Parameters:
- dwCallbackParam: Context parameter passed to callback handler (Ordinal_10344)
- nUnitType: Unit type to match (0=player, 1=monster, etc) [EBP]
- dwUnitId: Unit ID to search for [EDX]

Returns:

Special Cases:
- Type mismatch during iteration triggers assertion and terminates process
- Empty hash chain results in NULL callback
- Hash table uses 128 buckets per type (0x80 entries)

functions.name: ValidateUnitProperties
functions.comment:
Validates unit/item property compatibility by type classification.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10262 on pUnitData[0x21] - if non-zero result, return 0 (validation passed/skip)
2. Check if *pUnitData (type field) is 0 - if so, return 0 (validation passed/skip)
3. Switch on pUnitData[3] (unit type code):
   - Type codes 0,4,7,8,9,10,11,12,17,19: Pass through with return 0
   - Type 13: Accept only if pUnitData[1] == 3, else return 1 (failure)
   - Type 14: Accept only if pUnitData[1] == 6, else return 1 (failure)
   - Type 15-16: Accept only if pUnitData[1] in (4,5,6), else return 1 (failure)
   - Type 18: Special validation with nItemCode parameter:
     - Call Ordinal_10963(nItemCode) to get item type
     - For types 0x29 or 0xe6: Check if (pUnitData[0x11] & 0xffffff00) - 0xa00 >= 0
     - For type 0x10a: Check if (pUnitData[0x11] & 0xffffff00) - 0xd00 >= 0
     - If overflow flag != sign, return 1 (failure)
     - Otherwise continue
   - All other types: return 1 (failure)
4. Return 0 (pass)

Parameters:
pUnitData (int *) - Pointer to unit structure, accessed at offsets:
  [0] = type/classification field
  [1] = subtype/classification field
  [3] = unit type code
  [0x11] = resource/capability field (checked against 0xa00 or 0xd00 thresholds)
  [0x21] = flag field passed to Ordinal_10262
nItemCode (int) - Item code passed to Ordinal_10963 for type classification

Returns:
0 - Validation passed/allowed
1 - Validation failed/not allowed

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 early if pUnitData[0x21] validation ordinal returns non-zero
- Returns 0 early if pUnitData[0] type field is 0
- Type 18 has conditional validation based on item type codes (0x29, 0xe6, 0x10a)
- Uses flag/sign bit comparison (SBORROW4) for threshold validation on type 18

Magic Numbers:
0x29 - Item type code constant
0xe6 - Item type code constant  
0x10a - Item type code constant
0xa00 - Resource threshold for types 0x29/0xe6
0xd00 - Resource threshold for type 0x10a
0xffffff00 - Mask to extract upper 24 bits from pUnitData[0x11]

3. If flag not set, load unit type from pUnit[0] and subtype from pUnit[3]
4. For type 0: accept subtypes 0x00 or 0x11, reject others
5. For type 1: accept subtypes 0x0c or 0x00, reject others
6. For any other type: reject (return 0)
7. Return 1 (success) if type/subtype combination valid, 0 (failure) if invalid

        [0x00] = unit type (0=Player, 1=Monster, ...)
        [0x03] = unit subtype/class

0 - Unit type/subtype combination is not allowed

functions.comment:

1. Load unit state value from pUnit[3] (offset 0xc)

   - Type 0: Return true if state == 0x11
   - Type 1: Call Ordinal_10582(pUnit[1]) to get unit data, check byte at +0x343 is null and state == 0xc
   - Type 2: Call Ordinal_10626(pUnit[1]) to get unit data, check flags at +0x1c7: bit 1 (0x2) set, or bit 0 (0x1) set AND state == 0x2
   - Type 3: Check if flag 0x10000 set at pUnit[0x3a]
   - Type 4: Return true if state == 0x3
3. Return false if no conditions matched

Parameters:
pUnit (undefined4 *): Pointer to unit structure containing type, sub-id, and state fields. Fields accessed:
  [0] = unit type (0-4)
  [1] = unit sub-id/reference
  [3] = unit state value (compared against 0x11, 0xc, 0x2, 0x3)
  [0x3a] = unit flags (tested for 0x10000)

Returns:
true: Unit matches the validation condition for its type
false: Unit does not match validation condition

Special Cases:
- Ordinal_10582 and Ordinal_10626 return pointers to external unit data structures
- All returned checks are independent per type; no cross-type conditions
- Type values > 4 default to false return

functions.name: CompareUnitsByAttributes
functions.comment:
Compares two units by their attributes, types, and relationships to determine compatibility.

Algorithm:
1. Extract unit indices from both unit structures at offset 0x8
2. Extract unit types from both unit structures at offset 0x0
3. Call GetUnitRoom on pUnit1 to obtain the entity room
4. Call ValidateEntityDrlgSubType to check room validity (extraout_EAX contains result)
5. If validation passes (extraout_EAX != 0):
   a. If pUnit2->type=0 AND (flag 0x10000 set OR subtype=0 OR subtype=0x11):
      - Call CheckPlayerPermission; if fails, return 0
   b. If pUnit1->type=0 AND pUnit2->type=1:
      - Search unit2 index in linked list
      - Call IsPlayerSlotQuestActive; if both checks pass, return 0
   c. Otherwise return 1 (compatible)
6. If validation fails (extraout_EAX == 0), normalize types:
   a. If unit1 type=1, search and replace index, set type=0
   b. If unit2 type=1, search and replace index, set type=0
7. If normalized types AND indices match, return 0 (same unit)
8. If both types normalized to 0:
   a. Check permission conditions again
   b. Compare using CheckLinkedListValueWithMask
9. If unit2 type=1, check monster stats/properties
10. Final comparison using CheckUnitsSameTeam

Parameters:
pUnit1 - int* to first unit structure (ECX, __fastcall)
pUnit2 - int* to second unit structure (EDX, __fastcall)

Returns:
1 (TRUE) - Units are compatible/different teams
0 (FALSE) - Units are incompatible/same unit/permission denied

Magic Numbers:
0x10000 - Unit attribute flag at offset 0xe8
0x11 - Special unit type (NPC or interactive entity)
0xFFFFFFFF - Invalid linked list search result

Phantom Variables (Ghidra-generated for CONCAT31 bool return):
extraout_var, extraout_var_00, extraout_var_01, extraout_var_02 - Upper 3 bytes of EAX after bool returns

functions.name: IsPlayerSlotQuestActive
functions.comment:
Validate whether a player slot meets active quest criteria.

Algorithm:
1. Verify both slot index and player node pointers are non-null
2. Check if slot[0] is 0 OR player[0] is 1 (quest state conditions)
3. If true, iterate through two slot references (Ordinal_10321 and Ordinal_10322)
4. For each slot reference that exists:
   - Get unit descriptor via Ordinal_10963
   - Retrieve detailed unit data via Ordinal_10594
   - Check if byte at offset +0x84 is non-zero (quest flags)
   - Set fSlotValid=true if any slot has flags set
5. If fSlotValid is true OR second slot check passes, continue validation
6. Call SearchLinkedListByKey with player[2] to find matching quest entry
7. Return true if search result equals slot[2] (quest IDs match)

Parameters:
pSlotIndex (int *) - Pointer to slot data structure [0]=quest state
pPlayerNode (int *) - Pointer to player node [0]=player state flag, [2]=quest ID

Returns:
true - Slot is active and quest IDs match player quest record
false - Invalid pointers, failed conditions, or quest mismatch

Special Cases:
- Quest validation requires BOTH first condition (state checks) AND second condition (ID match)
- Offset 0x84 contains quest flags; non-zero indicates active quest status
- SearchLinkedListByKey failure (returns 0) results in false return
- Note: Function uses 1 register-based temporary (local_EAX_103) optimized away in decompilation

functions.name: ValidateUnitAvailable
functions.comment:
Validates if a unit has availability for skill execution based on target area and player state

Algorithm:
1. Validate inputs: both pUnitAny and pSkillData must be non-NULL
2. Check pSkillData[0] state: must be 0 (idle) or 1 (specific mode)
3. Get unit skill state via Ordinal_10321(pUnitAny)
4. If state valid, retrieve unit skill info via Ordinal_10963()
5. Get status data via Ordinal_10594() and check offset 0x85 for required area flag
6. Repeat steps 3-5 for secondary unit skill via Ordinal_10322()
7. Validate at least one required area is present
8. If pSkillData[0] == 1, search player list via SearchLinkedListByKey(pSkillData[2])
9. Return 0xFFFFFFFF if player not found
10. Verify both units target same area via CheckPlayersHaveSameTargetArea()
11. Return true if area matches, false otherwise

Parameters:
pUnitAny (int *): Pointer to primary UnitAny structure - skill source unit
pSkillData (int *): Pointer to skill request data - [0]=mode, [2]=player search key

Returns:
true (1): Units have skill availability and target same area
false (0): Validation failed (NULL inputs, invalid state, mismatched areas, player not found)

functions.name: ProcessUnitCleanup
functions.comment:
Performs comprehensive cleanup operations for a game unit/entity before destruction.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6fb90bc0(pUnit) - Perform initial unit state cleanup
2. Call Ordinal_10810(pUnit) - Check if unit has active inventory (returns non-zero if true)
3. If inventory active (dwResult != 0):
   a. Call EnumerateAndRemoveItemsFromUnit(pUnit, 0) - Remove all items from unit inventory
   b. Get item list at pUnit[0x21] offset (item slot pointer)
   c. Call Ordinal_10241(item_list) - Deallocate item structure
   d. Clear pUnit[0x21] = 0 (zero item list pointer)
4. Call Ordinal_10527(pUnit) - Cleanup unit-specific rendering/display data
5. Check if global render context active (g_hRenderContext != 0):
   a. Call Ordinal_10352(pUnit) - Update unit visibility/viewport state
   b. Call Ordinal_10342(pUnit) - Get unit screen coordinates
   c. Call Ordinal_10389(dwScreenData, pUnit) - Perform screen-space cleanup (returns non-zero on success)
   d. If screen cleanup succeeded (dwResult != 0):
      - Call Ordinal_10386(pUnit) - Finalize unit rendering cleanup
6. Return from function

Parameters:
  pUnit (int *) - Pointer to unit structure to cleanup (typically UnitAny in Diablo II context)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Function only processes inventory if unit has active inventory (Ordinal_10810 check)
  - Render context dependent operations only execute if g_hRenderContext is non-zero
  - Screen cleanup (Ordinal_10389) may fail; error is silently handled

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x21 - Offset in unit structure to item list pointer field
  0x84 - Offset in unit structure to item list pointer (alternative access path)

0x1 - Byte offset in pNodeData for item type
0x3 - Dword offset in pNodeData for unit pointer

Related Functions:
- FindUnitInHashTable(0x..., byte) - Retrieves unit from hash table
- ProcessUnitItemProperties(int*, int) - Processes unit item list and flags

functions.name: ProcessUnitItemInteraction
functions.comment:
Process a unit entry from hash table with optional secondary operation

Algorithm:
1. Extract unit reference from entry struct at offset +3 (DWORD)
2. Extract primary index from entry struct at offset +1 (BYTE)
3. Call FindUnitInHashTable to locate unit by reference and index
4. If unit found (non-null result), extract secondary parameter from entry struct at offset +2 (BYTE)
5. Call FUN_6fb671e0 with found unit pointer in ECX and secondary parameter in EDX
6. Return via RET instruction

Parameters:
pEntry (ECX register): Void pointer to entry structure - contains unit reference, indices, and parameters
  - Offset +0: Unknown field (not accessed in this function)
  - Offset +1: BYTE - Primary index for hash table lookup
  - Offset +2: BYTE - Secondary parameter passed to FUN_6fb671e0
  - Offset +3: DWORD - Unit reference identifier used for hash lookup

Returns:
void - No explicit return value

Structure Layout (Entry):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 1    | (unused)   | byte | Unknown field
0x01   | 1    | byIndex    | byte | Primary lookup index for hash table
0x02   | 1    | byParam    | byte | Secondary parameter for operation
0x03   | 4    | dwUnitRef  | dword| Unit reference identifier

Notes:
Calling convention: __fastcall - pEntry passed in ECX register
Structure type unknown - define appropriately when discovered
No error handling - if unit not found, function silently returns

Related Functions:
- FindUnitInHashTable() - Locates unit by reference and index in hash table
- FUN_6fb671e0() - Performs operation on found unit with secondary parameter

functions.name: InitializeResourceIfNeeded
functions.comment:
Initialize or reuse resource handle with callback registration.

Algorithm:
1. Query existing resource handle via Ordinal_10480 with magic 0x36
2. If handle exists (non-zero): Set init flag and return
3. If handle not found (zero):
   a. Create new resource via Ordinal_10470 (args: 0, 2, 0x19, *param_1, param_1[2])
   b. Mark as initialized via Ordinal_10478(resource, 0x36)
   c. Register ResourceCallbackThunk callback via Ordinal_10477
   d. Link resource to parent via Ordinal_10475(param_1, resource)
4. Return void

Parameters:
- pResourceParams (dword *): Pointer to 3-element array
  - [0]: Parent resource ID
  - [2]: Additional resource parameter

Returns:
None (void)

Special Cases:
- Magic value 0x36 indicates resource initialization flag
- Ordinal values 10470, 10475, 10477, 10478, 10480 are Storm.dll resource management functions
- ResourceCallbackThunk (0x6fb6e170) is registered as event handler

Related Functions:
- ValidateResourceState() - Called before this function
- HandleResourceEvent() - May invoke registered callback
- ProcessResourceCleanup() - Called on resource disposal

functions.name: IsGamePaused
functions.comment:
Check if game session is paused or inactive

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10481(pGameSession, 2) to check session pause state with flag 2
2. If returns non-zero (paused/inactive), return 1 (true)
3. Retrieve game context via GetGameContext()
4. If game context is valid, call Ordinal_10487(pGameContext, 0x36) to check context state
5. If returns non-zero (context invalid/paused), return 1 (true)
6. Return 0 (false) - game is active and not paused

Parameters:
pGameSession: void* - Game session handle (passed in ECX, __fastcall)

Returns:
1 (true) - Game is paused/inactive (either session or context check failed)
0 (false) - Game is active and running

Note: Uses Diablo II Storm ordinal calls - Ordinal_10481 and Ordinal_10487 check session/context validity

functions.name: GetItemDamageValue
functions.comment:
Retrieve damage value for specified item damage stat index

Algorithm:
1. Clear EAX register and load byDamageIndex into AL
2. Compare index against g_wMaxItemDamageStatIndex limit
3. If index >= limit, jump to return 0
4. If index < limit, extend index to 32-bit ECX
5. Access g_pdwItemDamageTable[index*8] for dword lookup
6. Return damage value in EAX, or 0 if out of bounds

Parameters:
byte byDamageIndex - Item damage stat index value (0-based)

Returns:
dword - Damage value from table entry, or 0 if index exceeds max

Special Cases:
Out of bounds index safely returns 0
Magic number 0x8 scales index for dword offset calculation

functions.comment:
UNITS_GetBeltRows - Returns belt rows capability for a unit.

3. If unit type is 0 (player), extract bit from unit flags at offset 0x3a
4. Returns 0 otherwise

Returns: 1 if unit has belt rows capability, 0 otherwise

functions.name: InitializeUnitResources
functions.signature: void InitializeUnitResources(UnitAny * pUnit, dword nX, dword nY, dword nDestX, dword nDestY)
functions.comment:
Initialize unit resources and attributes for a unit based on difficulty class and apply state flags.

Algorithm:
1. Validate difficulty/class via Ordinal_10589(nDestY) - returns pResData or 0
2. If validation fails, log error and terminate with code -1
3. Initialize unit state via Ordinal_11115(pUnit)
4. Retrieve class index from [pResData + 0x63] and apply via Ordinal_10348
5. Position unit on map via Ordinal_10152(0, nX, nY, nDestX, pUnit, 1)
6. Load attribute pointer from [pUnit + 0x38]
7. Check equipped flag at [pResData + 0x64]: 0x00 means not equipped, non-zero means equipped
8. Call Ordinal_10182 to set attribute value (0 if not equipped, 0x40 if equipped)
9. Get attribute index from [pResData + 0x63] and lookup in g_pdwAttributeValues table
10. Apply attribute via Ordinal_10184
11. Check feature flag at [pResData + 0x69]: if set enable (OR 0x04), if clear disable (AND 0xfb)
12. Apply final state mask: set bits while clearing specific flags

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX): Pointer to unit structure to initialize
  nX (EDX): Starting X coordinate on game map
  nY (Stack[0x4]): Starting Y coordinate on game map
  nDestX (Stack[0x8]): Destination X coordinate for pathfinding
  nDestY (Stack[0xc]): Encoded difficulty and class index passed to Ordinal_10589

Returns:
  void - Modifies pUnit structure in-place with initialized resources and attributes

Special Cases:
  Magic values: 0x40 (equipped), 0x04 (feature bit), 0xfb (mask), 0xf5 (mask), 0x20 (state)

functions.name: CleanupRenderResources
functions.comment:
Cleanup render context resources for game context type 3

Algorithm:
1. Ordinal_11214(pRenderData) - D2Gfx initial cleanup for render context
2. Ordinal_11116(pRenderData) - D2Gfx secondary cleanup for render context  
3. FUN_6fb97a00(pRenderData) - Common resource deallocation shared by all context types
4. FUN_6fb90bc0(pRenderData) - Type 3 render context specific cleanup routine
5. Load g_hRenderContext global to check if render context is initialized
6. If g_hRenderContext is non-zero: execute Ordinal_10228(pRenderData) and Ordinal_10386(pRenderData) for surface operations
7. Extract field value from pRenderData structure at offset 0x38
8. Ordinal_10156(0, extracted_field) - Final cleanup on extracted field value

Parameters:
  pRenderData (RenderContext *) - Pointer to type 3 render context structure being destroyed, contains sub-field at offset 0x38

Returns:
  void - Always succeeds, releases all render context resources

Special Cases:
  - Ordinal_11214: D2Gfx render context cleanup 1
  - Ordinal_11116: D2Gfx render context cleanup 2
  - Ordinal_10228: D2Gfx conditional surface operation 1 (only if g_hRenderContext active)
  - Ordinal_10386: D2Gfx conditional surface operation 2 (only if g_hRenderContext active)
  - Ordinal_10156: Final cleanup with null first param and field value from offset 0x38

functions.name: ProcessCircleWithinDistance
functions.signature: void ProcessCircleWithinDistance(int * pUnit, int nBaseX, int nBaseY, int nRadius, dword dwFlags, int nRandom)
functions.comment:
Process all walkable tiles within a circular distance from a center point.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit flags from item code parameter using Ordinal_10589
2. Check if unit pointer is already resolved (values 0 and 1 are reserved), otherwise call GetUnitFromHashTable
3. Initialize local processing array (22 dwords) to zeros
4. Set default flags (0x201) and item code in processing structures
5. Calculate squared radius (nRadius * nRadius) for efficient distance check
6. For each Y coordinate from -nRadius to +nRadius:
   - For each X coordinate from -nRadius to +nRadius:
     - Check if (X^2 + Y^2) <= (nRadius^2) - point is within circular distance
     - If nRandom parameter is set, call RandSeed to validate random number
     - Calculate absolute tile coordinates: nLocalX = nDistX + nBaseX, nLocalY = nDistY + nBaseY
     - Check if unit has active state flag (test at [nFlagsOffset + 0x5c])
     - If flag set, seed random number generator
     - Get item data using GetItemData ordinal
     - Call Ordinal_10042 with item code and coordinates to process tile
     - If return value non-zero, call FUN_6fb77720 with processing array

Parameters:
pUnit (int *) - Unit pointer or reserved value (0=NULL, 1=player)
nBaseX (int) - Center X tile coordinate
nBaseY (int) - Center Y tile coordinate
nRadius (int) - Search radius in tiles (both positive and negative checked)
dwFlags (dword) - Unit flags/item code for state lookup
nRandom (int) - Random seed parameter (0=skip random, non-zero=validate)

Returns: void - Processing happens through callback function FUN_6fb77720

Special Cases:
- Radius values can be negative; function uses absolute value for distance calculation
- Processing continues even if some tiles fail validation
- Random seed call is conditional on nRandom parameter value
- Active flag check at [nFlagsOffset + 0x5c] determines random seeding behavior
- Ordinal_10589 resolves item code to flags offset

Magic Numbers:
0x16 - Array size in dwords (22 dwords = 88 bytes for local processing structure)
0x201 - Default processing flags value
0x5c - Offset within item code structure to active flag check
0x64 - Total stack frame size (100 bytes local storage)

Related Functions:
- GetUnitFromHashTable - Resolve unit pointers to processing units
- Ordinal_10589 - Get flags offset from item code
- Ordinal_10918 - RandSeed for random number generation
- Ordinal_10342 - GetUnitStat for unit state queries
- Ordinal_10042 - Get item data structure
- FUN_6fb77720 - Process tiles matching criteria

functions.name: CreateAreaEffectMissile
functions.comment:
CreateAreaEffectMissile - Creates a circular area effect using missile type 0x29.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile template record for type 0x29
2. Assert template exists, exit on failure
3. If unit provided, resolve via GetUnitFromHashTable if not already resolved
4. Initialize projectile data structure (22 dwords zeroed)
5. Set flags (0x20), target coords (0,0), missile type (0x2a), random flag (1)
6. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to spawn the base missile
7. Get radius from missile template offset 0x78
8. Call ProcessCircleWithinDistance with flags 0x109 to create area effect

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit pointer (can be NULL or hash table reference)

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x29 (41) = Area effect missile template index
  0x2a (42) = Secondary missile type for projectile data
  0x109 (265) = ProcessCircleWithinDistance flags
  0x20 = Projectile data control flags
  0x78 = Offset in missile template for effect radius

functions.name: SpawnMissileSubProjectile
functions.comment:
SpawnMissileSubProjectile - Spawns a sub-projectile for specific missile types.

Algorithm:
1. Return early if nMode != 0
2. Get missile class ID and map to sub-missile type:
   - 0x110 -> 0x158
   - 0x111, 0x112, 0x1a1 -> 0x159
   - Default: 0x284
3. Get owner unit from hash table
4. Initialize projectile creation params (22 dwords zeroed)
5. Create new projectile via InitializeAndAllocateProjectile
6. Set new projectile direction from source missile path
7. Set target X offset to 0x80

Parameters:
  pMissile - Source missile unit spawning the sub-projectile
  nMode - Mode flag, only spawns when 0

Returns: void (EAX set to 1 on success, 0 on early return)

functions.name: CreateMultiProjectileEffect
functions.comment:
CreateMultiProjectileEffect - Creates a multi-projectile visual effect pattern with concentric rings of missiles.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve source unit from global hash table using pUnit
2. Initialize offset arrays with predefined spread patterns (-4 to +5 range)
3. Determine missile ID based on unit class:
   - 0x85 (champion/boss) -> missile ID 0xAB
   - 0x234 (special unit) -> missile ID 0x118
   - Other units -> missile ID 0x38
4. Get missile range, owner GUID, and Y coordinate for targeting
5. Zero out 22 DWORDs of projectile configuration buffer
6. Create first wave: 5 projectiles with type 0x67, flags 0x4001
7. Create central projectile: type 0x9A, flags 0x8001 with light radius 12
8. Create second wave: 3 projectiles with type 0x69, flags 0xC001
9. Create remaining 15 projectiles with type 0x68 until index reaches 18

Parameters:
  pUnit (UnitAny*) - Source unit originating the projectile effect (passed in ECX)

Returns: void (implicitly returns 1 in EAX)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x85 - Champion/boss unit class ID
  0x234 - Special unit class ID
  0xAB, 0x118, 0x38 - Missile type IDs by unit class
  0x67, 0x68, 0x69, 0x9A - Sub-missile type IDs for different waves
  0x4001 - First wave projectile flags
  0x8001 - Central projectile flags (with light)
  0xC001 - Final wave projectile flags
  0xC (12) - Light radius for central projectile
  0x16 (22) - Number of DWORDs to clear in config buffer
  0x14 (20) - Byte offset for 5 projectiles (5 * 4)
  0x48 (72) - Byte offset for 18 projectiles (18 * 4)

Structure Layout (ProjectileConfig at ESP+0xD8):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x00    4     dwFlags       Projectile behavior flags
  0x04    4     pSourceUnit   Pointer to source unit
  0x10    4     nSubType      Sub-missile type ID
  0x14    4     nTargetX      X coordinate offset
  0x18    4     nTargetY      Y coordinate offset
  0x2C    4     nLevel        Missile range/level

Offset Array Pattern:
  First 5 projectiles use indices 0-4 for X, indices 0-4 (+0x14) for Y
  Next 3 projectiles use indices 5-7 for X, indices 0x17-0x19 for Y
  Remaining projectiles use scaled indices for outer ring spread

functions.name: CreateRandomMissileFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateRandomMissileFromUnit - Creates a random missile/projectile from a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Gets a random value 0-2 for missile type variation
2. Gets the missile range from the source unit
3. Validates the unit and gets target from hash table if needed
4. Initializes a projectile structure with size 0x20 (32 bytes)
5. Sets missile type to base 0xA3 (163) + random offset
6. Allocates and creates the projectile

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit to create the missile from

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateRandomProjectileEffect
functions.comment:
CreateRandomProjectileEffect - Creates a projectile with random visual variation.

Algorithm:
1. Generate random value (0-2) for missile visual variation
2. Get missile range from source unit
3. Validate source unit pointer
4. If unit type is not player/monster, get unit from hash table
5. Initialize 0x58-byte projectile structure
6. Set missile ID to 0x6f + random variation (0x6f-0x71)
7. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create the missile

Parameters:
  pSourceUnit - Source unit that fires the projectile

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateMissileEffectForUnit
functions.comment:
CreateMissileEffectForUnit - Creates a missile visual effect centered on a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Gets missile template record for missile type 0x3E
2. Validates template exists (asserts and exits if null)
3. If unit ID valid, resolves unit from hash table (unless type 0 or 1)
4. Initializes 88-byte projectile structure on stack (22 DWORDs zeroed)
5. Sets projectile size (0x20), effect type (0x2A), coordinates, and flags
6. Calls InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create the missile
7. Calls D2Common ordinals and ProcessCircleWithinDistance with missile radius

Parameters:
  pUnitId - Pointer to unit ID or unit pointer (type determined by first dword)

Returns: void

functions.name: InitializeSkillChargeTable
functions.signature: void InitializeSkillChargeTable(int nUnitId, uint dwSkillId, int nMode)
functions.comment:
Initialize skill charge animation table with frame data

Algorithm:
1. Query skill data via Ordinal_10589 to get frame information
2. Initialize a 33-element configuration array with control values
3. Build charge lookup table by:
   - Setting array indices with animation frame numbers
   - Marking valid (0x1), invalid (0x2), or terminator (0xffffffff) entries
   - Clearing remaining entries (0x0)
4. Retrieve unit, skill level, and mana requirements via GetUnitFromHashTable and ordinals
5. Calculate skill offset: (frame_index << 7) from ordinal data at offset 0x78
6. Loop through initial table (8-byte stride) and call FUN_6fb77720 for each entry
7. If mode is 2 or 3:
   - Recalculate offset from ordinal data at offset 0x7c
   - Loop through offset table with stride 4 (mode 3) or 8 (mode 2)
   - Call FUN_6fb77720 for each offset entry
8. Return (void)

Parameters:
nUnitId (int) - Unit/player ID to initialize skills for
dwSkillId (uint) - Skill ID to process
nMode (int) - Animation mode (2=normal, 3=alternate)

Returns:
void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Mode 2 uses stride of 8 bytes per entry
- Mode 3 uses stride of 4 bytes per entry
- Other modes skip the offset table processing
- Array contains both animation frame indices and validity markers

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1f - Array terminator marker
0x20 - Array stride offset (32 dwords)
0x40 - Offset table start position (128 bytes)
0x7c - Offset into skill data structure for secondary offset calculation
0x78 - Offset into skill data structure for primary offset calculation
33 - Array size (132 bytes total)
0xffffffff - Invalid/disabled entry marker
0xfffffffe - Animation frame skip marker

functions.name: CreateProjectileFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateProjectileFromUnit - Creates a projectile from a unit using default configuration.

3. Initialize projectile config struct (0x16 dwords cleared via STOSD.REP)
4. Set config: flags=0x20, projectile type=0x1d, source and resolved unit pointers
5. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create the missile

Returns: void (projectile creation handled by InitializeAndAllocateProjectile)

functions.name: CreateUnitProjectile
functions.comment:
CreateUnitProjectile - Creates a projectile from a unit or GUID reference.

2. Resolves unit from hash table if needed (type check != 0 or 1)
3. Initializes projectile structure (0x58 bytes)
4. Sets skill ID to 0x2a (ranged attack)
5. Calls InitializeAndAllocateProjectile

Parameters:
  pUnitOrGUID - Pointer to unit or GUID to create projectile from

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateScatterProjectiles
functions.comment:
CreateScatterProjectiles - Creates two projectiles for scatter shot effect.

Algorithm:
1. Get random value 0-2 for projectile variant selection
2. Create base projectile (type 0x33) if unit is valid
3. Create variant projectile (type 0x34-0x36 based on random value)
4. Set finalization flag on variant projectile

Parameters:
