Returns: void

functions.name: InitializeUnitSkillArray
functions.comment:
Initialize unit skill array with default values and retrieve unit properties.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 17 dword skill table array on stack
2. Set skill values: indices 0,1,3,7,9,10,11 = 0x02, indices 4,5,8,12 = 0xfffffffe (initialized values)
3. Clear remaining slots via REP STOSD loop (22 dwords)
4. Call GetMissileTemplateRecord (D2Common.Ordinal_10589) to get missile template record
5. Call GetUnitFromHashTable to lookup unit structure by ID
6. Call GetUnitOwnerGuid (D2Common.Ordinal_10326 = UNITS_GetOwnerGuid) to get unit owner GUID
7. Call GetUnitY (D2Common.Ordinal_10329 = UNITS_GetUnitY) to get unit Y coordinate
8. Read offset [class_struct + 0x78] and shift left 7 bits for base experience
9. Call GetMissileRange (D2Common.Ordinal_11120) to get missile range value
10. Loop through skill indices (8 iterations, step 4 bytes): load skill data, call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to process
11. Return void

Parameters:
IMPLICIT ECX: int nUnitId - Unit hash table ID
IMPLICIT EDX: dword* pSkillData - Pointer to skill data array

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies stack array and executes side effects

Ordinal References:
D2Common.Ordinal_10589 = GetMissileTemplateRecord - Gets missile template data record
D2Common.Ordinal_10326 = UNITS_GetOwnerGuid - Gets unit owner GUID
D2Common.Ordinal_10329 = UNITS_GetUnitY - Gets unit Y coordinate
D2Common.Ordinal_11120 = GetMissileRange - Gets missile range value

Special Cases:
- Skill table uses fixed initial values (0x02 and 0xfffffffe) to mark type/state
- Loop processes 8 skill slots (0x20 / 4 bytes per DWORD)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | [0]        | uint | Skill type marker
0x04   | 4    | [1]        | uint | Skill type marker
0x08   | 4    | [2]        | uint | Skill data placeholder
0x0c   | 4    | [3]        | uint | Skill type marker
0x10   | 4    | [4]        | uint | Skill type marker (0xfffffffe)
0x14   | 4    | [5]        | uint | Skill type marker (0xfffffffe)
0x18   | 4    | [6]        | uint | Skill data placeholder
0x1c   | 4    | [7]        | uint | Skill type marker
0x20   | 4    | [8]        | uint | Skill data placeholder
0x24   | 4    | [9]        | uint | Skill type marker
0x28   | 4    | [10]       | uint | Skill type marker
0x2c   | 4    | [11]       | uint | Skill type marker
0x30   | 4    | [12]       | uint | Skill type marker (0xfffffffe)
0x34   | 4    | [13]       | uint | Skill type marker (0xfffffffe)
0x38   | 4    | [14]       | uint | Skill type marker (0xfffffffe)
0x3c   | 4    | [15]       | uint | Skill data (0x1f constant)
0x40   | 4    | [16]       | uint | Skill data placeholder

functions.name: CreateMissileWithRangeScaling
functions.comment:
CreateMissileWithRangeScaling - Creates a missile projectile with range-based damage scaling.

Algorithm:
1. Resolve target unit from hash table via GetUnitFromHashTable
2. Get missile range from unit via GetMissileRange
3. Return early if no valid target unit found
4. Initialize projectile config struct (0x16 dwords = 88 bytes)
5. Set config: flags=1, target unit, skill ID from unit field_4
6. Get coordinates via Ordinal_10326/10329 (D2Common coordinate functions)
7. Check for special skills (0xf9, 0xfc, 0xff) - apply 0x8000 flag and scaled damage
8. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create missile
9. Set missile direction based on path target direction

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit initiating the missile attack

Returns:
  1 on success (missile created), return value discarded on early exit

Magic Numbers:
  0xf9, 0xfc, 0xff - Special skill IDs requiring damage scaling
  0x96 (150) - Base damage multiplier for GetMonsterLevelScaledValue
  0x8000 - Config flag for alternate damage calculation

functions.name: InitializeMissileTrajectory
functions.comment:
InitializeMissileTrajectory - Sets up missile trajectory using precomputed trigonometric lookup tables.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize trajectory lookup tables with sine/cosine-like values for 64 directions
2. Get target unit from hash table, exit early if none
3. Calculate missile range and get target direction
4. Validate direction is within bounds (0-63)
5. Look up X/Y velocity components from trajectory tables
6. Initialize projectile allocation with computed values
7. Set rotated target direction (offset by 19, wrapped to 64 directions)
8. Process final unit stats

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to the missile unit being initialized

Returns: void

functions.name: UpdateUnitDisplayPosition
functions.comment:
Update the visual display position of a game unit based on game state.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_11125 (GetUnitState) - get initial unit classification
2. Check if returned value < 6 (valid unit range)
3. If invalid, check special case using bitwise AND 0x80000001 for even/odd conditions
4. If value is not 0/1, exit without updating display position
5. Load display configuration from unit[0xe] (offset 0x38)
6. Call Ordinal_11141 to get X dimension
7. Call Ordinal_11143 to get Y dimension
8. Calculate center and half-offset: nCenterY = (X-Y)/2, nCenterX = (X+Y)/2
9. Call Ordinal_10329 to get Y base, add nCenterX for final Y coordinate
10. Call Ordinal_10326 to get X base, add nCenterY for final X coordinate  
11. Call Ordinal_10170 to update viewport coordinate
12. Call Ordinal_10142 to set unit state/appearance with flag 0
13. Call Ordinal_11140 with nCenterY parameter
14. Call Ordinal_11142 with nCenterX parameter
15. Call FUN_6fb771e0 to finalize unit display update

Parameters:
pUnit: uint* - Pointer to unit data structure (passed in ECX via __fastcall)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Units with classification >= 6 are skipped (inactive/invalid)
- Even/odd classification check via bitwise manipulation of flag bit 0x80000001
- Coordinate calculations use signed division with arithmetic shift for center positioning
- Note: Function uses 9 SSA temporaries (dwFlags, nOffsetX/Y, nCenterX/Y + register spillovers) optimized away in decompilation view

functions.name: CreateMissileNovaFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateMissileNovaFromUnit - Creates a ring of missiles emanating from a source unit in a nova pattern.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize sine/cosine lookup table with 64 angle offsets for X and Y coordinates
2. Validate mode parameter (only executes when nMode == 0)
3. Get target unit from hash table using source unit
4. Initialize missile creation parameters (flags=2, missile ID=0x106)
5. Loop through 16 directions, creating missiles at 22.5 degree intervals
6. For each missile, set the target unit and target unit ID

Parameters:
  pSourceUnit - The unit that is firing the nova pattern missiles
  nMode - Mode flag, function only executes when 0

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessUnitQuestOverlayOrProjectile
functions.comment:
ProcessUnitQuestOverlayOrProjectile - Processes monster unit data to either initialize a projectile or display a quest overlay.

Algorithm:
1. Validates pMonsterData is not null
2. Gets player slot from unit hash table
3. If monster type is 1, checks monster init stats for projectile flags
4. If projectile flags set (offset 0x2F0/0x2F1), initializes projectile data structure
5. Otherwise checks if player slot has active quest and unit is available
6. If quest conditions met, initializes overlay with type 0x1A (quest indicator)

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the unit (monster) being processed
  pMonsterData - Pointer to monster data array, [0]=type, [1]=monster class ID

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessAreaUnitsAndEffects
functions.signature: void ProcessAreaUnitsAndEffects(int nUnitType, int nRadius, int nSpecialFlags)
functions.comment:
Processes area-of-effect abilities by iterating over a circular region and applying elemental effects to valid tiles and units within range.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate center coordinates (nCenterX, nCenterY) from source unit position
2. Compute radius squared for efficient circular distance checks
3. Initialize 88-byte work buffer for effect parameters
4. Retrieve unit hash table for the specified unit type
5. If special flags set, enable high bit flag (0x8000) for enhanced processing
6. Iterate Y from -radius to +radius (outer loop)
7. Iterate X from -radius to +radius (inner loop)
8. For each (X,Y) offset, calculate squared distance: dx*dx + dy*dy
9. Skip positions outside circular radius (distSq > radiusSq)
10. Query tile field data and validate entity DRLG subtype
11. Skip boundary tiles (type 4) to prevent edge effects
12. Find region by world coordinates and validate field data initialization
13. For special flag mode: add random offset (0-24) to seed calculation
14. Select effect type via random (0-2): Fire(0x45), Ice(0x68), Lightning(0x69)
15. Apply effect by calling InitializeAndAllocateProjectile if random trigger passes

Parameters:
  nUnitType (ECX) - Unit type identifier for hash table lookup
  nRadius (EDX) - Radius of area effect in world units
  nSpecialFlags (Stack+0x4) - Non-zero enables enhanced processing with random offset

Returns:
  void - Effects applied directly to game state

Special Cases:
  - Boundary tiles (type 4) are skipped to prevent edge bleeding
  - Zero nSpecialFlags uses standard processing without random seed offset
  - Effect type selection is random each iteration

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x45 - Fire effect type
  0x68 - Ice effect type
  0x69 - Lightning effect type
  0x8000 - Enhanced processing flag bit
  0x19 (25) - Random range for seed offset
  0x3 - Random divisor for effect type selection
  0x4 - Boundary tile type (skip processing)

functions.name: FinalizeEntityCleanup
functions.comment:
Finalize entity cleanup and prepare for destruction.

Algorithm:
1. Call validation check (Ordinal_10378) to determine entity finalization readiness
2. If validation succeeds (non-zero return):
   a. Set entity finalization flag to mark for cleanup
   b. Clear audio context reference to remove audio resources
   c. Return
3. If validation fails (zero return):
   a. Call post-finalization processing routine

Parameters:
pEntity (uint *) - IMPLICIT ECX: Pointer to entity/unit structure to finalize

Returns:
void - No explicit return value; operations performed in-place on entity

Special Cases:
- Validation success path: performs dual cleanup operations then exits
- Validation failure path: delegates to alternative processing routine
- Audio context cleanup critical for resource management

Related Functions:
- SetEntityFinalizationFlag() - Marks entity for destruction
- ClearAudioContextReference() - Cleans up audio resources
- FUN_6fb771e0() - Post-finalization processing when validation fails
- Ordinal_10378() - Entity readiness validation check

functions.name: CheckAndRenderUnitVisibility
functions.comment:
Checks if a unit is within viewport bounds and toggles render visibility.

Algorithm:
1. Check if unit is active/allocated using Ordinal_10378
2. If active, set finalization flag via SetEntityFinalizationFlag
3. Clear previous hover/selection state via Ordinal_10146 on unit field offset 0x38
4. Get unit's X coordinate via Ordinal_10333
5. Validate X coordinate within viewport: viewport_x <= unitX <= viewport_x + viewport_height
6. If X valid, get unit's Y coordinate via Ordinal_10334
7. Validate Y coordinate within viewport with 0x40 buffer: viewport_y <= unitY <= viewport_y + viewport_height + 0x40
8. If both X and Y valid, set visibility flag 0x80 via Ordinal_11123
9. Call FUN_6fb771e0 for render setup
10. If out of bounds, call FUN_6fb773b0 to hide/remove unit with parameters (NULL, 0)

Parameters:
  pUnit (dword *): Pointer to unit structure being visibility-tested
  IMPLICIT ECX: First parameter (Diablo II __fastcall convention)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Out-of-bounds units are handled via FUN_6fb773b0 (likely despawn/hide)
  - Viewport height has 0x40 (64-pixel) buffer on Y axis for partial rendering
  - Finalization flag set regardless of visibility (cleanup path)

Magic Numbers:
  0x0e: Offset into unit structure for state field
  0x38: Offset into unit structure for hover/selection state
  0x80: Visibility flag set via Ordinal_11123
  0x40: Y-axis viewport buffer (64 pixels)

functions.name: CreateProjectileForUnit
functions.comment:
CreateProjectileForUnit - Creates a projectile effect for a given unit.

Algorithm:
1. Validates skill ID and unit pointer are non-null
2. Resolves unit from hash table if unit type is not 0 (Monster) or 1 (Player)
3. Initializes projectile info structure with default values
4. Sets projectile type to 0xCC and flag to 1
5. Calls InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create the projectile

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the unit that will generate the projectile
  nSkillId - Skill identifier for the projectile

Returns: void

functions.name: UpdateMissileHomingTarget
functions.comment:
Updates a missile's homing target by validating current target and finding a new one if needed.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve missile data from hash table using stored GUID
2. Validate target unit exists and is in valid state
3. Check room validity and DRLG subtype compatibility
4. If owner check enabled, verify missile owner matches target
5. Check missile flags for tracking mode (0x1=locked, 0x2=seeking, 0x4=disabled)
6. If seeking mode with no range remaining, return early
7. Determine search radius based on missile type ID:
   - 0x56 (Guided Arrow): radius 0x16
   - 0xC1 (Bone Spirit): radius 0x5D
   - 0x149 (Elemental): radius 0xD3
8. Call FindBestMatchingItem to locate optimal target within range
9. If new target found and valid, set missile target and path
10. If no target found, offset position using missile velocity
11. Calculate final distance and update path if within threshold

Parameters:
- pMissile (UnitAny*): IN - Missile unit to update homing for
- dwSkipOwnerCheck (uint): IN - If non-zero, skip ownership validation

Returns:
- 0: Target update successful
- 1: Update failed (invalid target, disabled, or out of range)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x38: Offset to missile data pointer in UnitAny
- 0x4: Offset to missile type ID in UnitAny
- 0x8, 0xC: MissilesTxt range base and multiplier offsets
- 0x56: Missile type Guided Arrow
- 0xC1: Missile type Bone Spirit
- 0x149: Missile type Elemental
- 0x19: Minimum distance threshold (25 units)

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessUnitSlots
functions.comment:
Validates unit state and processes inter-unit slot interactions for matching attributes.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve unit pointer from hash table using unit ID parameter
2. If unit not found or validation fails, call error handler and return
3. Check if unit's stat data is compressed (return if true)
4. Fetch unit's slot flags via Ordinal_11141 (bit mask)
5. If slot flag 0x01 set: Call pre-processing step (FUN_6fb85820)
6. Load associated unit from slot via Ordinal_10180 using offset 0x38
7. Validate target unit state
8. Compare attributes between source and target units
9. If attributes match: Get comparison count via Ordinal_11124
10. Verify count is multiple of 5 (count % 5 == 0)
11. Get distance/relationship via Ordinal_10397 between units
12. If distance in range [4, 24] (3 < distance < 0x19): Execute interaction Ordinal_10142
13. Post-processing via FUN_6fb771e0
14. Error path: Call FUN_6fb773b0 with NULL and flag 0

Parameters:
IMPLICIT ECX - pUnitId: Pointer to unit ID (passed via ECX register per __fastcall)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Unit not found: Short-circuits to error path
- State validation failure: Indicates corrupted or invalid unit
- Compressed data: Returns early (data not accessible)
- Slot flag check: Only processes if bit 0x01 is set
- Distance check: Requires strict range [4, 24), rejects boundary values (<=3 or >=25)
- Multiple of 5: Count must have zero remainder when divided by 5

Magic Numbers:
0x01 - Slot active flag bit mask
0x38 - Offset into unit structure for associated unit pointer (56 bytes)
5 - Divisor for count validation (modulo check)
0x03 - Minimum distance threshold (exclusive)
0x19 - Maximum distance threshold exclusive (25 decimal)
0x00 - Error flag for error handler call

Called Functions:
- GetUnitFromHashTable: Hash table unit lookup
- ValidateUnitTypeState: State validation
- Ordinal_10342: Get unit stat (likely stat ID for checking)
- Ordinal_10082: Check if data compressed
- Ordinal_11141: Get slot flags
- FUN_6fb85820: Pre-processing
- Ordinal_10180: Load target unit from slot
- CompareUnitsByAttributes: Attribute matching
- Ordinal_11124: Get comparison count
- Ordinal_10397: Get distance/relationship value
- Ordinal_10142: Execute interaction
- FUN_6fb771e0: Post-processing
- FUN_6fb773b0: Error handling

functions.name: UpdateUnitProjectileOnPathMismatch
functions.comment:
UpdateUnitProjectileOnPathMismatch - Updates projectile state when unit path coordinates mismatch.

This function checks if the unit's path has a coordinate mismatch flag set,
and if so, initializes and allocates a new projectile with updated range data.
Always processes unit stats afterward.

Algorithm:
1. Get path coordinate mismatch flag from unit's pPath (offset 0x38)
2. If mismatch detected:
   - Initialize 0x16 DWORDs of message buffer to zero
   - Set message type to 0x200d (projectile update)
   - Set message subtype to 0x27 (39)
   - Get unit references from hash table
   - Call D2Common ordinals for coordinates
   - Calculate effective range = missileRange * 2 - 2
   - Initialize and allocate projectile
3. Always call ProcessUnitStats on the unit

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure being processed

Returns: void

functions.name: InitUnitRandomStatAndProcess
functions.comment:
InitUnitRandomStatAndProcess - Initializes a random stat offset on a unit and processes its stats.

Algorithm:
1. Apply random offset using stat ID 0x8D (141) with range parameters
2. Process unit stats to update derived values

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the unit structure to initialize

Returns: void

functions.name: ApplyRandomUnitOffset
functions.signature: void ApplyRandomUnitOffset(int * pUnit, int nValidate, int nIterations, int nOffsetRadius, int nInitialValue)
functions.comment:
Apply random offset to unit coordinates with validation

Algorithm:
1. Validate input: Check if nValidate is 0 or call RandSeed, then call ValidateUnitState
2. If validation fails, return immediately
3. Get unit hash table entry via GetUnitFromHashTable
4. Initialize 22-dword buffer (dwFlags) with 0x20 in first slot
5. Get unit stat value via GetUnitStatDisplay, store in dwStat
6. Get initial X/Y coordinates via Ordinal_10326 (nTemp) and Ordinal_10329 (nY)
7. Loop nIterations times:
   - Generate random X offset if nOffsetRadius * 2 != 0, else 0
   - Generate random Y offset if nOffsetRadius * 2 != 0, else 0
   - Apply absolute offset: nDeltaX = sign(iVar1 - nOffsetRadius) ? nOffsetRadius : -nOffsetRadius
   - Apply absolute offset: nDeltaY = sign(iVar2 - nOffsetRadius) ? nOffsetRadius : -nOffsetRadius
   - Compute final coordinates: nComputedX, nComputedY by adding to base coordinates
   - Call FUN_6fb77720 with dwFlags buffer (applies computed coordinates to unit)
8. Return (void)

Parameters:
  pUnit (int *): Unit pointer/ID, stored in ECX (first fastcall parameter)
  nValidate (int): Validation flag; if 0, skip validation; if non-0, validate unit state
  nIterations (int): Number of offset iterations to apply
  nOffsetRadius (int): Maximum offset radius for random offset calculations
  nInitialValue (int): Initial value (stored in nValue local, used in loop counter)

Returns:
  void - Side effects only (modifies unit coordinates via FUN_6fb77720)

Magic Numbers:
  0x16 (22): Number of dwords in buffer (88 bytes total)
  0x20 (32): Initial flag value in buffer slot 0
  0x2 (multiply by 2): Check if nOffsetRadius is effectively 0 (nOffsetRadius * 2 == 0)

Related Calls:
  Ordinal_10918: RandSeed - generates random number (called twice per iteration)
  Ordinal_11120: GetUnitStatDisplay - retrieves unit stat value
  Ordinal_11124: ValidateUnitState - validates unit state after RandSeed
  Ordinal_10326: GetX - retrieves base X coordinate
  Ordinal_10329: GetY - retrieves base Y coordinate
  FUN_6fb77720: ApplyUnitOffset - applies computed offsets to unit
  GetUnitFromHashTable: Retrieves unit from hash table by unit pointer

functions.name: InitializeUnitWithRandomOffset
functions.comment:
InitializeUnitWithRandomOffset - Initialize unit with random position offset and process stats.

Algorithm:
1. Call ApplyRandomUnitOffset with parameters (6 validate, 2 iterations, 6 radius, 0x9d initial)
2. Call ProcessUnitStats to finalize unit initialization

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to unit structure to initialize

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessMissileProjectileSpawn
functions.comment:
ProcessMissileProjectileSpawn - Handles spawning of child projectiles from missiles.

Algorithm:
1. Gets missile template record and retrieves timing thresholds
2. Gets remaining duration of the missile
3. If duration exceeds spawn threshold and target unit has path mismatch, spawns child projectile
4. Initializes projectile spawn structure with skill 99 and type flags
5. Processes unit stats after potential spawn

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to the missile unit triggering projectile spawn

Returns: void

functions.name: InitializePlayerSkills
functions.comment:
Initializes player skills by setting up skill table entries and random seed timer.

Algorithm:
1. Load skill table entry from pData[0x38] into dwSkillProcessed
2. Generate random seed value via Ordinal_10918 (RandSeed)
3. Call FUN_6fb97b10 to initialize skill with adjusted seed (seed - 8)
4. Load skill unit reference from pUnit[0x38] into dwSkillIdentifier
5. Process skill data via Ordinal_10158 (skill data processor)
6. Initialize skill via Ordinal_10161_SkillInit with processed data
7. Reset skill state via Ordinal_10203 with processed data
8. Check byte flag at [dwSkillProcessed + 0x58]
9. If flag set (non-zero): Call RandSeed again, shift left 8 bits, store at pUnit[0x50]
10. If flag clear (zero): Store 0 at pUnit[0x50]

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*) - Unit data structure pointer with fields:
  - [0x04] - Item/skill identifier
  - [0x38] - Skill unit reference
  - [0x50] - Timer value storage
- pData (void*) - Data structure with field:
  - [0x38] - Skill table entry

Returns:
- void (all results stored in unit structure at offset 0x50)

Structure Offsets:
pUnit layout:
  Offset | Size | Purpose | Type
  0x04   | 4    | ID ref  | uint
  0x38   | 4    | Skill   | uint
  0x50   | 4    | Timer   | uint

pData layout:
  Offset | Size | Purpose | Type
  0x38   | 4    | Entry   | uint

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10918 - RandSeed: Generate random number
- Ordinal_10589 - GetItemData: Retrieve item/skill data
- Ordinal_10158 - Process skill data
- Ordinal_10161 - SkillInit: Initialize skill
- Ordinal_10203 - Reset skill state
- FUN_6fb97b10 - Initialization routine

functions.name: UpdateMissileAndSpawnProjectile
functions.comment:
UpdateMissileAndSpawnProjectile - Updates a missile unit and spawns a child projectile.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile template record and retrieve target unit from missile path
2. Check if missile remaining duration exceeds template minimum
3. Verify target unit has coordinate mismatch (moved from original position)
4. Initialize projectile data structure with flags and parameters
5. Allocate and spawn new projectile aimed at current target position
6. Set projectile direction and apply stat modifiers
7. Process unit stats for the original missile

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to the missile UnitAny being updated

Returns: void

functions.name: MissileSpawnChildWithRandomOffset
functions.comment:
MissileSpawnChildWithRandomOffset - Spawns a child projectile from a parent missile with random X/Y offsets.

Algorithm:
1. Get target unit from hash table for the parent missile
2. Check if missile target Y is 0 (no target yet)
3. If valid target and no current target, initialize projectile structure:
   - Set missile flags to 2
   - Set missile ID to 0x11d (285)
   - Generate random X offset: 20 - random(0,40)
   - Generate random Y offset: 20 - random(0,40)
   - If both offsets are 0, set X offset to random(0,19)+1
4. Create and allocate the child projectile
5. Set target offsets on the child missile
6. Adjust parent missile target based on remaining duration:
   - <125 frames: target value 25
   - <175 frames: target value 10
   - >=300 frames: target value 15
   - else: target value 5
7. Process unit stats for the parent missile

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to the parent missile UnitAny structure

Returns: void

functions.name: UpdateMissileOscillationPath
functions.comment:
Updates the oscillation path for a missile to create a wavy/serpentine trajectory.
This function modifies the missile's position periodically to simulate a
sine-wave-like motion pattern, making the projectile harder to predict.

Algorithm:
1. Get source unit from missile's hash table link at offset 0x38
2. If no source unit exists, process stats and exit early (orphaned missile)
3. Check if path coordinates have changed via GetUnitPathCoordMismatchFlag
4. If coordinates mismatch, initialize 0x58-byte projectile data structure:
   - Set source unit reference at offset 0x14
   - Set missile reference at offset 0x18
   - Set flags = 1 at offset 0x3C
   - Set missile type = 0x11E at offset 0x20
   - Set update callback function at offset 0x60
5. Allocate new projectile via InitializeAndAllocateProjectile
6. If allocation succeeds, configure drawable object coordinates from GFX field
7. Calculate frame skip: only update oscillation when (duration % 3) == 0
8. Retrieve current target Y coordinate and missile field 24 base value
9. Use GetRandomBoundedValue with max=2 to determine oscillation direction
10. Calculate X and Y oscillation offsets using (value * 3) / 4 scaling formula
11. Apply calculated offsets to current position coordinates
12. Recalculate path from source to target incorporating oscillation offset
13. Update missile target unit references for continued tracking
14. Process final unit stats before returning

Parameters:
   pMissile (ECX) - UnitAny* - Pointer to the missile unit to update

Returns:
   void - Updates missile position and path state in place

Magic Numbers:
   0x38 - Offset to pSourceUnit pointer in UnitAny structure
   0x2C - Offset to pSeed (random number generator seed pointer)
   0x11E (286) - Missile type constant identifying oscillating projectiles
   3 - Frame divisor for update frequency (oscillate every 3rd frame)
   2 - Random direction bound (generates 0 or 1 for left/right)
   (x*3)/4 - Amplitude scaling formula for oscillation magnitude

Special Cases:
   - Returns immediately after ProcessUnitStats if source unit not found
   - Skips projectile allocation phase if path coordinates already match
   - Only modifies trajectory on frames where (duration % 3) equals zero
   - Random direction alternates oscillation between positive and negative offsets

functions.name: InitializeMissileRandomBehavior
functions.comment:
InitializeMissileRandomBehavior - Sets up missile targeting and spawns randomized child projectiles.

Algorithm:
1. Gets target unit from missile's hash table reference
2. Retrieves current target Y coordinate and field 24 value
3. If target exists, decrements target counter and sets new target
4. If field 24 is zero, creates child projectile with random parameters:
   - Random count (1-6), random X offset (-20 to +20), random Y offset (-20 to +20)
   - Ensures at least one non-zero offset by forcing X if both are zero
5. Assigns random target index (0-4) to new projectile
6. Updates missile target unit ID and processes unit stats

Parameters:
  pSourceMissile - The missile unit to initialize random behavior for

Returns: void

functions.name: InitializeRandStateArray
functions.signature: int * InitializeRandStateArray(uint dwParam1, uint dwParam2, uint dwParam3)
functions.comment:
Initializes a random state array for seed operations.

Algorithm:
1. Create 22-element state array, zero-initialize all elements using REP STOSD (0x16 = 22 dwords)
2. Set state[0] = 2 (type flag), state[1] = dwParam1, state[2] = dwParam2
3. Set state offset 0x34 = 1 (flag), offset 0x48 = dwParam3
4. Get first random seed: nSeed1 = 0x14 - RandSeed() via Ordinal_10918
5. Get second random seed: nSeed2 = 0x14 - RandSeed() via Ordinal_10918

functions.name: UpdateMissileTracking
functions.comment:
UpdateMissileTracking - Updates homing missile position and spawns child projectiles.

Algorithm:
1. Look up target unit via GetUnitFromHashTable using missile's stored GUID
2. If no target found, process missile stats and exit early
3. If path coordinates mismatch (target moved), spawn child projectile (ID 0x12d)
4. Check frame alignment: only update position every 4th frame (duration % 4 == 0)
5. Get random quadrant (0-3) to add variance to tracking behavior
6. Calculate position offset based on quadrant:
   - Quadrant 0: Use (targetY - offsetY) * 3 / 4
   - Quadrant 2: Use (targetY + offsetY) * 3 / 4 with negated target
   - Quadrant 1,3: Use raw target Y value
7. Update target unit position coordinates with calculated offsets
8. Recalculate path from missile to new target position
9. Update missile target references for next frame
10. Process final missile stats

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - UnitAny* pointer to the missile unit being updated

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x12d (301) - Child tracking projectile missile ID
  0x16 (22)   - Number of dwords in projectile spawn structure (88 bytes)
  0x5c (92)   - Stack frame size in bytes
  4           - Frame interval for position updates (every 4th frame)
  3/4         - Position interpolation factor for smooth tracking

Special Cases:
  - Early exit if target unit not found in hash table
  - Child projectile spawned only when path coordinates mismatch
  - Position randomization prevents perfectly predictable tracking
  - Signed divide pattern (CDQ/AND/ADD/SAR) handles negative coordinates

functions.name: HandleMissileInfernoEffect
functions.comment:
HandleMissileInfernoEffect - Visual effect handler for Inferno missile lifecycle.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve owner unit from hash table and get missile remaining duration
2. Calculate intensity (0-12 scale) based on duration thresholds:
   - Duration < 10: Exit early (no effects)
   - Duration 10-29: Intensity = 1 (minimum)
   - Duration 30-84: Intensity = (duration - 15) / 4
   - Duration 85+: Consult template for ramp-down curve (12 to 1)
3. Spawn spark projectiles (ID 0x137) based on intensity:
   - Count = min(intensity * 7, 8)
   - Each spark gets random X/Y offsets within intensity range
   - Z offset fixed at -30 (0x1E below missile)
4. On even frames with intensity < 3: spawn fire wave (ID 0x136)
   - Higher intensity spawns 2-4 waves with random spread
5. At duration 0x13B (315): initialize game object properties (0x1C3)
6. Every 25 frames: initialize random state array for 0x134 missile
7. At duration 0x5A (90): trigger screen shake and process unit stats
8. During mid-life (116-314 frames):
   - Frames 201-224: create skill objects at interval 8
   - Every 4 frames otherwise: create skill objects at interval 40

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - UnitAny* to the active Inferno missile unit

Returns:
  void - Updates visual state, spawns child effects, processes unit stats

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x133 - Inferno base missile template ID
  0x134 - Random state missile ID
  0x136 - Fire wave missile ID
  0x137 - Spark visual effect missile ID
  0x1C3 - Game object property type
  0x5A  - Frame 90: screen shake trigger
  0x13B - Frame 315: game object init point
  0x19  - 25 frame interval divisor
  0xC8  - Frame 200: mid-life start
  0xE1  - Frame 225: mid-life end

Structure Access:
  Offset  Size  Field              Type     Description
  0x2C    4     dwFrameRemain      DWORD    Remaining frame counter (RNG seed)
  +0x08   4     dwMaxDuration      DWORD    Template max duration field

Error Handling:
  - Returns early if owner unit is null (no effects spawned)
  - Zero intensity multiplier handled with explicit zero offset

functions.name: CreateSkillObject
functions.signature: void CreateSkillObject(dword dwUnitId, dword dwSkillId, int nLevel)
functions.comment:
Create skill object at randomized position within search radius

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 4-element buffer (adwObjectBuffer) with unit ID at [1], flags at [0]=1
2. Add offset 0x138 to current tick (dwOffsetTimer = Ordinal_10918() + 0x138)
3. Calculate search radius squared: iVar5 = nLevel * nLevel
4. Loop 4 times (nLoopCounter = 0 to 3):
   a. Check if unit already created (pCreatedUnit != NULL) - if yes, jump to apply attributes
   b. Get random offset for X: nXOffset = nLevel/2 - Ordinal_10918()
   c. Get random offset for Y: nYOffset = nLevel/2 - Ordinal_10918()
   d. Validate distance: if nXOffset^2 + nYOffset^2 >= search_radius_squared, skip to next iteration
   e. Get terrain type via Ordinal_10326 (X direction component)
   f. Get terrain offset via Ordinal_10329 (Y direction component)
   g. Get obstacle object via Ordinal_10342 (returns object at position)
   h. Validate can walk via Ordinal_10042 (checks collision/walkability at nXOffset, nYOffset)
   i. Validate line-of-sight via Ordinal_10122 (checks LoS with distance 0 to 1)
   j. If all checks pass: store coordinates (nXCoord=nXOffset, nYCoord=nYOffset) and create unit
5. Apply attributes if unit created:
   a. Call FUN_6fb979a0 (initialize/setup unit)
   b. If nLevel==8: Set 400 with attribute -0x32 (50 negative)
   c. Else: Set 200 with attribute -0x19 (25 negative)

Parameters:
- dwUnitId (ECX): Unit type/class ID to create (IMPLICIT - __fastcall)
- dwSkillId (EDX): Skill identifier or property selector (IMPLICIT - __fastcall)
- nLevel: Difficulty/power level (1-8) determines search radius and attributes

Returns:
- void (side effect: creates unit in valid location or no unit if all attempts fail)

Special Cases:
- Early escape: if valid position found in iterations 1-3, loop exits via conditional at 0x6fb7231b
- Distance check: avoids spawning within nLevel squares (radius = sqrt(nLevel^2))
- Level-based attributes: level 8 uses higher negative value (-0x32 vs -0x19)
- Failure case: if no valid position found after 4 attempts, no unit created

functions.name: ProcessAndApplyTimedSpellStats
functions.signature: int * ProcessAndApplyTimedSpellStats(int nUnitId, int nFrequency, int nFrequencyDivisor, void * pConfig)
functions.comment:
Process and apply timed spell statistics to a unit with frequency-based calculations.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that nFrequencyDivisor is non-zero, exit with error if zero
2. Get current unit value (Ordinal_11124: GetUnitStat) and check divisibility by nFrequencyDivisor
3. If not evenly divisible (modulo != 0), skip processing and return NULL
4. Retrieve unit structure from hash table via GetUnitFromHashTable
5. If unit not found (NULL), return NULL
6. Get unit's base property (Ordinal_10326: GetPropertyX) and random seed value
7. Initialize 22-element stack buffer (88 bytes) with zeros, set element[0] = 0x2003
8. Store retrieved unit pointer and config param in buffer
9. Calculate random offsets: if (nFrequency-1)*2 != 0, call RandSeed (Ordinal_10918), else use 0
10. Calculate adjusted X = GetPropertyX + (nFrequency-1-randomOffset1)
11. Calculate adjusted Y = GetPropertyY + (nFrequency-1-randomOffset2)
12. Get unit Y coordinate via Ordinal_10342 (GetUnitYCoord)
13. If unit has Y coordinate, call Ordinal_10118 (CheckBlockedTile) with adjusted coords and param 4
14. If CheckBlockedTile returns 0 (success), call FUN_6fb77720 with buffer and return result
15. If any check fails, return NULL (error path at 0x6fb7267b)

Parameters:
- nUnitId (int, ECX): Unit ID to process
- nFrequency (int, EDX): Frequency multiplier for calculations
- nFrequencyDivisor (int, [ESP+0x68]): Divisor for frequency check (must be non-zero)
- pConfig (void*, implicit): Configuration/context pointer passed to downstream functions

Returns:
- int*: Pointer to initialized unit buffer (88 bytes) on success, NULL on validation failure or tile blocked condition
- Success: Buffer contains unit data with 0x2003 flag set
- Failure: NULL when modulo check fails, unit not found, or tile blocked

Special Cases:
- If nFrequencyDivisor is 0, function immediately exits with error code -1
- Frequency-based modulo check prevents execution on certain iteration counts
- Random offsets provide variance in coordinate calculations (RandSeed may return 0)
- Blocked tile check prevents placement on invalid positions

Magic Numbers:
- 0x16 (22): Number of elements in stack buffer array
- 0x2003: Flag value set at buffer offset 0 (likely unit type/state indicator)
- 0x4: Fourth parameter to CheckBlockedTile (movement/validity flag)
- 0x133: Error code for invalid divisor (passed to assertion)
- 0xffffffff (-1): Termination code on fatal error

Structure Layout: Stack buffer contains UnitAny structure
| Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-----------|------|-------------|
| 0x00 | 4 | dwUnitFlags | uint | Unit state flags (0x2003 initialized) |
| 0x04 | 4 | pUnit | int* | Pointer to unit structure |
| 0x08 | 4 | pConfig | void* | Configuration context |
| 0x0C-0x58 | 76 | abyReserved | byte[19] | Reserved/temporary space |

functions.name: UpdateMissileTargetingBehavior
functions.comment:
Updates missile targeting behavior including target acquisition and child missile spawning.

2. Calculate target Y coordinate and frame delta from template offset
3. Check if current frame is within valid targeting window (template frame to frame - 0x7d)
4. For valid targeting window:
   a. Find target unit in hash table using type 0x11 (player type)
   b. Update drawable object coordinates for visual targeting

functions.name: SpawnRandomizedProjectile
functions.comment:
SpawnRandomizedProjectile - Creates a randomized projectile (missile type 0x21) with
randomized spawn coordinates around the source unit.

5. Generate Y variance in range [0, 5], compute spawn Y = UnitY + variance - 3

3. Call FUN_6fb771e0 to process unit

Parameters:
pUnit - Pointer to unit structure to check/process (IMPLICIT: ECX register)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
If unit not found in hash table, field is not cleared, function proceeds to FUN_6fb771e0

functions.name: CreateMissileFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateMissileFromUnit - Creates and launches a missile projectile from one unit targeting another.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve the target unit from the hash table using pSourceUnit
2. If target exists, initialize a MissileParams structure (88 bytes, zeroed)
3. Set missile ID to 0x177 (375) at offset 0x1c
4. Set count/flag to 1 at offset 0x30
5. Store source and target unit pointers in params
6. Allocate and initialize the missile projectile
7. Set missile's target to the Y coordinate of pSourceUnit

Parameters:
  pSourceUnit - Pointer to source unit that owns missile data

Returns: void

functions.name: SpawnMissilePattern
functions.comment:
SpawnMissilePattern - Spawns a radial pattern of bone spirit missiles around a target.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve target unit ID from source missile's target Y coordinate
2. Validate target exists in hash table and timing gate (10 ticks remaining)
3. Load missile template record for bone spirit variant (ID 0x176)
4. Initialize 14-position offset pattern array with X/Y spawn coordinates
5. Get owning unit reference for missile inheritance
6. Zero-initialize 88-byte projectile spawn structure
7. Loop through 14 spawn positions (0x38 bytes, stride 4):
   a. Extract X/Y offsets from pattern array
   b. Calculate octagonal distance: (max + min*2) / 2
   c. Compute velocity from template speed * distance / 6
   d. Allocate and spawn new missile instance
   e. Link to target unit and set randomized timing (10 + rand(0-35))
8. Trigger screen flash effect (type 4, 400ms duration)
9. Process unit stats on source missile (cleanup)

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - Source missile unit triggering the pattern spawn

Returns: void (spawned missiles allocated separately)

Magic Numbers:
  0x176 - Bone spirit missile template ID
  10 - Timing gate: ticks remaining to trigger
  0x38 (56) - Pattern array size in bytes (14 positions * 4 bytes)
  0x8102 - Projectile spawn flags
  0x23 (35) - Max random timing offset
  400 (0x190) - Screen flash duration in milliseconds

Structure Layout (anOffsetPattern reuse at offset 0x1c):
  Offset  Size  Field              Description
  0x00    4     dwFlags            Spawn flags (0x8102)
  0x04    4     pOwner             Pointer to owning unit
  0x08    4     pSourceMissile     Pointer to source missile
  0x10    4     nMissileId         Missile template ID (0x176)
  0x1C    4     nOffsetX           X spawn offset from pattern
  0x20    4     nOffsetY           Y spawn offset from pattern
  0x2C    4     nBaseVelocity      Calculated velocity value
  0x30    4     fActive            Active flag (1)

functions.name: CreateMissileEffectProjectiles
functions.comment:
CreateMissileEffectProjectiles - Creates visual effect projectiles from a source missile.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile target Y coordinate for bounds validation
2. Retrieve template record for missile type 0x17b (379)
3. Generate random X/Y offsets (range 0-19, centered by subtracting 10)
4. Zero-initialize 22-dword projectile configuration buffer
5. Create first projectile type 0x17c (380) with flags 0x21 at offset position
6. Bounds check: verify target Y falls within template min/max range
7. If bounds valid, create second projectile type 0x17e (382) with flags 0x20
8. Apply random negative Z offset (-3 to -6) for depth layering
9. Initialize GFX info and clear rendering bit for second projectile
10. Process unit stats to finalize missile state

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - UnitAny* - Source missile unit creating effect projectiles

Returns:
  void - No return value; projectiles created as side effect

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x17b (379) - Parent missile template type ID
  0x17c (380) - Primary effect projectile type ID
  0x17e (382) - Secondary effect projectile type ID  
  0x21 (33)   - Flags: CREATE_EFFECT | ATTACH_PARENT
  0x20 (32)   - Flags: CREATE_EFFECT only
  0x14 (20)   - Random bound for primary offset
  0x0a (10)   - Random bound for secondary offset
  0x16 (22)   - Projectile config buffer size in dwords
  0x0f (15)   - GFX initialization mode

Structure Layout (Projectile Config Buffer at ESP+0x1c):
  Offset  Size  Field             Description
  0x00    4     dwFlags           Projectile creation flags (0x20 or 0x21)
  0x04    4     pOwnerUnit        Owner unit pointer from hash table
  0x08    4     pSourceMissile    Source missile for effect attachment
  0x0c    4     dwMissileTypeId   Missile type (0x17c or 0x17e)
  0x10    4     dwUnused          Unused/reserved field
  0x14    4     dwSourceX         X coordinate from GetUnitOwnerGuid
  0x18    4     dwSourceY         Y coordinate from GetUnitY
  0x1c    4     nTargetX          Calculated target X with offset
  0x20    4     nTargetY          Calculated target Y with offset
  0x24-0x54     Reserved          Zero-initialized padding (22 total dwords)

functions.name: MissileSpawnChildProjectiles
functions.comment:
MissileSpawnChildProjectiles - Spawns child projectiles from a parent missile at intervals.

Algorithm:
1. Get current missile Y position and missile template record (ID 0x14c/332)
2. Check if missile reached spawn trigger height, set target unit ID if so
3. If missile field24 is set and position is at spawn interval, spawn child projectiles
4. Generate random X/Y offsets (0-20 range) for projectile spread
5. Initialize projectile struct with missile ID 0x124 (292) and spawn flags
6. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create child missile
7. Process unit stats for the parent missile

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to the parent missile UnitAny structure

Returns: void

functions.name: SpawnHitEffectProjectiles
functions.comment:
SpawnHitEffectProjectiles - Spawns visual hit effect projectiles based on hit type.

Algorithm:
1. Gets hit effect type from missile target Y value
2. If type is 0x96 (150), sets special rendering state
3. Iterates through hit effect table matching type values
4. Creates projectiles with direction and target based on table data
5. For type < 0xA5 and even values, creates dust effect projectile (0x153)
6. For type < 0x96, creates blood splatter projectile (0x96) with random offset
7. Finalizes by processing unit stats

Parameters:
  pUnit - Unit to spawn hit effects for

Returns: void

functions.name: SpawnMultipleSubProjectiles
functions.comment:
SpawnMultipleSubProjectiles - Spawns multiple sub-projectiles with randomized positions.

Algorithm:
1. Early return if nSpawnMode is non-zero
2. Initialize RNG seed from missile's nState field using MissileGetField24
3. Get sub-projectile count from MISSILES_GetMissileTargetY
4. Initialize projectile configuration buffer (0x16 dwords)
5. Loop up to dwSubProjectileCount times:
   - Generate random X offset in range [-10, +9]
   - Generate random Y offset in range [-10, +9]
   - Skip spawn if offset is exactly (0, 0) to avoid duplicate center
   - Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create sub-projectile
   - Apply text control max value clamp to projectile

Parameters:
  pMissile - Parent missile unit to spawn sub-projectiles from
  nSpawnMode - Spawn mode flag (must be 0 to spawn)

Returns: void

Notes:
  - 0x21 = projectile config type
  - 0x15d = projectile type ID
  - 0x14 (20) = random offset range for X/Y spread

functions.name: ProcessUnitStatProjectileSpawn
functions.comment:
ProcessUnitStatProjectileSpawn - Checks unit stat value against threshold table and spawns a projectile if conditions met.

Algorithm:
1. Gets target Y coordinate as stat value from missile data
2. Looks up appropriate threshold entry in g_ProjectileSpawnThresholds table
3. Checks if stat value is evenly divisible by the corresponding divisor
4. If divisible, retrieves source unit and creates projectile with missile ID from table
5. Sets target unit and ID on the spawned missile
6. Always calls ProcessUnitStats at the end

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the unit being processed

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessUnitAttributeCheck
functions.comment:
Validates unit attribute configuration and conditionally triggers area-based unit processing.

Algorithm:
1. Return 0 if dwFlags is non-zero (flags indicate skip condition)
2. Initialize dwParam=1 and dwAnimationType=3
3. Retrieve unit X coordinate via Ordinal_10329 (D2Common.GetUnitX)
4. Retrieve unit Y coordinate via Ordinal_10326 (D2Common.GetUnitY)
5. Retrieve unit stat value via Ordinal_10342 (D2Common.GetUnitStat)
6. Call Ordinal_10119 (D2Common validation function) with coordinates and stat
7. If validation fails (nResult==0), allocate 0x150 bytes via Ordinal_10589 (Fog.MemAlloc)
8. Load pointer from offset 0x78 in allocated block
9. Call ProcessAreaUnitsAndEffects with effect parameter 0x19
10. Return 1 on success

Parameters:
dwUnit (ECX): Pointer to unit structure to validate
dwFlags (EDX): Control flags; non-zero causes immediate early return

Returns:
1 - validation complete or effects successfully processed
0 - early exit due to dwFlags being non-zero

Special Cases:
Function uses 1 stack-allocated temporary optimized away by compiler.
Validation step (Ordinal_10119) determines if area effects are triggered.
Note: iVar1 is phantom variable (optimized away) and cannot be renamed.

functions.name: SpawnScatterMissiles
functions.comment:
Spawns scatter missiles radiating from the source missile position.

Algorithm:
1. Get target Y coordinate and lookup scatter table entry based on Y value
2. Validate scatter eligibility: targetY must be divisible by table divisor
3. Retrieve owner GUID and unit Y position as base coordinates
4. Initialize 0x58-byte missile parameter structure on stack
5. For each scatter missile (count from table[offset+8]):
   a. Generate random X offset (0-9, subtract 5, enforce minimum spread of 2)
   b. Generate random Y offset (0-9, subtract 5, enforce minimum spread of 2)
   c. Calculate scatter position: base + offset * 2
   d. Allocate and initialize new projectile missile
   e. Set target unit on spawned missile if allocation succeeded
6. Post-scatter effects based on targetY:
   - Y < 25: Set target unit type 3
   - 25 <= Y < 75: Set target unit type 2
   - Y <= 1: Apply special close-range overlay effect

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - Pointer to source missile UnitAny structure

Returns:
  void - No return value; missiles spawned as side effect

Special Cases:
  - No scatter if targetY % divisor != 0
  - No scatter if scatter count <= 0
  - Minimum spread enforced: offsets within 2 units of center forced to +5
  - Close-range (Y <= 1) triggers owner overlay effect with 60-tick duration

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6fba9b74 - Scatter configuration table base address
  0x15F (351) - Scatter missile type ID
  0x3C (60) - Overlay effect duration in game ticks
  0xFF - Maximum overlay intensity value

Structure Layout (Stack at ESP+0x1C, 0x58 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwActive        dword   Active flag (set to 1)
  0x04    4     dwField24       dword   Missile field 24 value
  0x14    4     nTargetX        int     Calculated scatter target X
  0x18    4     nTargetY        int     Calculated scatter target Y
  0x10    4     dwMissileType   dword   Missile type (0x15F)
  0x2C    4     dwActive2       dword   Secondary active flag

functions.name: CreateChildMissileFromTarget
functions.comment:
CreateChildMissileFromTarget - Spawns a new child missile based on an existing missile's target.

Algorithm:
1. Exit early if nParam is non-zero
2. Get target record ID from source missile
3. Find target missile unit in link list (type 3 = missile)
4. Initialize missile configuration structure (0x16 dwords zeroed)
5. Set missile flags (0xa021), type (0x160), and spawn count (1)
6. Get owner unit and target Y position
7. Allocate and initialize new projectile
8. Set target unit on the new missile

Parameters:
  pSourceMissile - Pointer to source missile unit
  nParam - Control parameter (must be 0 to proceed)

Returns: void

functions.name: UpdateMissileHomingBehavior
functions.comment:
UpdateMissileHomingBehavior - Updates homing missile tracking behavior and applies visual effects based on tracking state.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve missile's current tracking state from field at offset 0x24
2. Get graphics info pointer from missile offset 0x38
3. Look up target unit using FindLinkListNodeByIdAndIndex with type=3
4. Exit early if no valid target unit exists
5. Calculate approximate distance between missile and target positions
6. Generate random bounce threshold (0-4, clamped to minimum 1)
7. Execute state machine based on dwTargetState:
   - State 0: Missile within threshold, transition to state 1 (start tracking)
   - State 1: Calculate position deltas and adjust missile toward target with high animation rate (0xA00)
   - State 2: Apply fade effect with color tint (random 0-0x28 + 0xAA base, intensity 6)
   - State 3: Apply brighten effect with random color (intensity -6, fade-out)
   - State 4: Apply glow effect with fixed 400 intensity (0x190)
8. Set animation rate based on current state
9. Recalculate path from missile to target using CalculateUnitPathToTarget
10. Process unit stats at function exit (always called)

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX, UnitAny*) - Pointer to the missile unit being updated

Returns:
  void - No return value, modifies missile state in-place

Magic Numbers:
  0x2C - Offset to dwFrameRemain/RNG seed field in UnitAny
  0x38 - Offset to graphics info pointer in UnitAny
  0x14 (20) - Glow animation intensity
  0xAA (170) - Color effect base value for brighten/fade states
  0x28 (40) - Random color variation range
  0x190 (400) - Fixed color intensity for glow effect
  0x200 (512) - Animation rate for state 3 (slow)
  0x300 (768) - Animation rate for state 2 (medium)
  0xA00 (2560) - Animation rate for state 1 (fast homing)

State Machine:
  State 0 -> 1: When missile is within random threshold of target
  State 1: Active homing - adjusts position toward target with deltas
  State 2: Fade effect - applies color tint with brighten animation
  State 3: Brighten effect - applies fade-out animation
  State 4: Glow effect - fixed high-intensity glow

functions.name: SpawnRandomUnitVisualEffect
functions.comment:
SpawnRandomUnitVisualEffect - Spawns a random visual projectile effect on a unit with 25% chance.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit state value via GetMissileTargetY and check if (value & 3) == 0 (25% chance)
2. If triggered, initialize projectile config struct (0x58 bytes, 0x16 dwords)
3. Set missile ID 0x2521 (ambient visual effect) and skill ID 0x162 (354)
4. Get unit base coordinates via Ordinal_10326/10329
5. Apply random X offset (0-12 range) and Y offset (-6 to +6 from base)
6. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to spawn the visual effect
7. Always call ProcessUnitStats at the end regardless of spawn

Parameters:
  pUnit - Unit to potentially spawn visual effect on

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateUnitProjectile
functions.comment:
CreateUnitProjectile - Creates and fires a projectile from a unit with random variation.

Algorithm:
1. Roll random check (50% chance to exit early)
2. Get random missile type variation and missile range
3. Resolve owner unit from hash table if needed
4. Initialize projectile parameter structure (0x16 dwords)
5. Allocate and create projectile with InitializeAndAllocateProjectile
6. Set projectile direction toward target and invalidate animation

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit firing the projectile (contains owner/target refs)

Returns: void (projectile created as side effect)

functions.name: SpawnMissileEffectsFromAltitude
functions.comment:
SpawnMissileEffectsFromAltitude - Spawns visual particle effects based on missile altitude.

This function creates visual effects (particles, trails) when a missile reaches certain altitudes.
The effect type and frequency depend on the missile's current Y coordinate (altitude) checked
against a threshold table (g_AltitudeEffectThresholds).

Algorithm:
1. Get missile Y coordinate via GetMissileTargetY
2. If altitude equals 0x145 (325), enable special render state for 6000ms
3. Search altitude threshold table to determine effect tier (0-3)
4. If altitude % tier_divisor[0] == 0, spawn primary particle effect (missile ID 0x2A)
5. If altitude % tier_divisor[1] == 0, spawn secondary visual effect (missile ID 0x16C)
6. Configure secondary effect with Z offset, velocity, and target properties
7. Finalize by processing unit stats

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - Pointer to UnitAny missile triggering the effect spawn
                   IMPLICIT: Uses missile field at offset 0x2C as random seed

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x145 (325) - Special altitude that triggers render state change
  0x2001 - Missile flags: spawn enabled with visual effects
  0x2A (42) - Primary particle effect missile ID
  0x16C (364) - Secondary visual trail missile ID
  0x28 (40) - Random offset range for spawn position variance
  0x14 (20) - Center offset subtracted from random to get -20 to +20 range
  0x96 (150) - Z coordinate offset for spawned missile
  0xF (15) - Missile target unit configuration value
  0x80 (128) - Missile target pointer configuration value

Data Structures:
  g_AltitudeEffectThresholds - Array of altitude/frequency entries (stride 12 bytes)
    +0x00: Altitude threshold (dword)
    +0x04: Primary effect frequency divisor (dword)
    +0x08: Secondary effect frequency divisor (dword)

  Missile spawn params structure (88 bytes / 0x58):
    +0x00: dwMissileFlags
    +0x04: pSourceUnit (from hash table)
    +0x10: dwMissileId
    +0x14: nTargetX
    +0x18: nTargetY
    +0x2C: dwSpawnMode

functions.name: HandleSkillAreaAndProjectile
functions.comment:
HandleSkillAreaAndProjectile - Processes skill area effects and creates a projectile.

Algorithm:
1. Early return if nMode is not 0
2. Call ProcessSkillAreaPositions with skill ID 0x16d
3. Resolve unit from hash table if not a direct unit reference
4. Initialize projectile config struct (88 bytes)
5. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile with skill ID 0x16e

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the unit executing the skill
  nMode - Execution mode (must be 0 to process)

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateMissileFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateMissileFromUnit - Creates a missile/projectile from a source unit.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if nFlag is non-zero (condition check)
2. Get missile range from source unit
3. Resolve actual unit from hash table if needed
4. Initialize projectile data structure (0x16 dwords zeroed)
5. Allocate projectile with range and owner info
6. Set missile direction based on path target
7. Set target unit for missile tracking

Parameters:
  pSourceUnit - Source unit creating the missile
  nFlag - Condition flag, must be 0 for missile creation

Returns: void (creates missile as side effect)

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessUnitState
functions.comment:
Validate unit state and dispatch processing to ordinal handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve unit from hash table using unit ID (pUnitId)
2. If unit lookup failed (NULL), call error handler and return
3. Check if unit's type field [0] is within valid range [0, 2)
4. If type in range, validate unit state via ValidateUnitTypeState
5. If validation fails (non-zero result), call error handler and return
6. If validation succeeds, dispatch to Ordinal_10235 for processing
7. Call Ordinal_10374 for post-processing
8. Return

Parameters:
  pUnitId (uint *) - Unit identifier/reference pointer

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - NULL unit pointer triggers immediate error handler call
  - Unit type outside [0, 2) range skips validation and goes to ordinal path
  - ValidateUnitTypeState failure (non-zero) prevents ordinal dispatch

functions.name: SpawnDualEffectProjectiles
functions.comment:
SpawnDualEffectProjectiles - Spawns two visual effect projectiles around a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit from hash table, return if not found
2. Initialize 0x58-byte projectile data structure to zeros
3. Set flags to 1 (preset coord mode) and store source unit
4. Get missile range from source unit
5. Get unit coordinates via D2Common ordinals
6. Spawn first projectile with missile ID 0x244
7. Spawn second projectile with missile ID 0x26f

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit to spawn projectiles around

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x16 (22) - Number of dwords to zero (22 * 4 = 0x58 bytes)
  0x244 (580) - First projectile missile ID
  0x26f (623) - Second projectile missile ID

functions.name: CreateAreaEffectProjectiles
functions.comment:
CreateAreaEffectProjectiles - Creates area effect projectiles for a unit's skill.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile range for the unit via GetMissileRange
2. Calculate iteration count using GetMonsterSkillId(0x120, range)
3. Process area positions via ProcessSkillAreaPositions with effect type 0x19c
4. Resolve unit from hash table if unit type is not 0 or 1 (player/NPC)
5. Initialize projectile config struct (0x58 bytes zeroed)
6. Set struct size (0x20), projectile type (0x1d), and flag (1)
7. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile with the config

Parameters:
  pUnit - Source unit creating the area effect projectiles

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x120 = Monster/skill type constant for skill ID lookup
  0x19c = Area effect type constant
  0x16 = Loop count (22 dwords = 0x58 bytes)
  0x20 = Struct size field
  0x1d = Projectile type ID (29 decimal)
  nIterations/4 = Stride for position randomization

functions.name: ValidateAndUpdateUnitStats
functions.comment:
Validate unit stat cache and update display.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current unit stats value via Ordinal_11141 (returns nCurrentStats or 0)
2. Get stored/cached stats value from unit via FUN_6fb97c60 (accesses offset 0x40)
3. If both stats values exist and differ (cache mismatch), trigger stats recalculation:
   - Call FUN_6fb8d210 with mode 0x970 to force state update/recalculation
4. Pass stored stats to Ordinal_11140 for synchronization/display update
5. Call PrepareUnitStatsDisplay() to refresh UI display

Parameters:
pUnit (dword *) - Pointer to unit structure (passed in ECX per __fastcall)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- If nCurrentStats is 0 (no current stats), skips recalculation
- If nStoredStats is 0 (no cached stats), skips recalculation
- If values match, skips FUN_6fb8d210 call (cache is valid)

Magic Numbers:
0x970 - Mode parameter for FUN_6fb8d210 state update operation

Ordinal References:
Ordinal_11141 - Retrieve current unit stats from game state (unknown - appears to fetch active stat value)
Ordinal_11140 - Synchronize/display unit stats in UI (unknown - appears to update display with new stats)

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_11141 - Retrieve current unit stats (unknown ordinal)
- FUN_6fb97c60 - Get stored stats from unit structure
- FUN_6fb8d210 - Force unit state recalculation/update
- Ordinal_11140 - Synchronize/update unit stats display (unknown ordinal)
- PrepareUnitStatsDisplay - Refresh stats UI panel

functions.name: ProcessRandomizedUnitMovement
functions.signature: void ProcessRandomizedUnitMovement(int nUnitId, int nIterations, int nDeltaX, int nDeltaY)
functions.comment:
Generate randomized movement offsets and spawn projectiles in a spread pattern.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve unit pointer from hash table using nUnitId
2. Initialize movement data array (22 DWORDs), set flags 0x524 and mode 0x1c8
3. Get unit base coordinates (X, Y) using GetUnitOwnerGuid and GetUnitY
4. Random offset iteration loop (nIterations times):
   a. Calculate random range = nIterations * 4
   b. Generate random X offset in range [0, range), center around unit
   c. Generate random Y offset in range [0, range), center around unit  
   d. Calculate distance from unit to offset coordinates
   e. If distance > 3: store coordinates and spawn projectile
5. Get missile range for the unit
6. Initialize hardcoded movement delta table (18 pairs of X/Y deltas)
7. Final spawning loop (18 iterations):
   a. Skip if unit pointer is NULL
   b. Clear temp structure (22 DWORDs)
   c. Calculate final coordinates from base + table delta
   d. Spawn projectile at calculated position

Parameters:
  nUnitId (ECX, fastcall): Unit identifier for hash table lookup
  nIterations (EDX, fastcall): Random offset iteration count (controls spread density)
  nDeltaX (Stack[0x4]): Base X delta offset for projectile spawning
  nDeltaY (Stack[0x8]): Base Y delta offset for projectile spawning

Returns:
  void - Projectiles are spawned as side effect

Special Cases:
  Distance <= 3: Random offset rejected (too close to unit)
  NULL unit pointer: Iteration skipped (prevents crash)
  nIterations <= 0: Random offset loop skipped entirely

Magic Numbers:
  0x524 - Movement data structure type/flags marker
  0x1c8 - Movement mode constant (456 decimal)
  0x16 (22) - Structure clear loop count (22 DWORDs = 88 bytes)
  0x48 (72) - Table iteration limit (18 entries * 4 bytes)
  3 - Minimum distance threshold for valid movement offset
  4 - Multiplier for random range calculation

functions.name: HandleMissileTimedBehavior
functions.comment:
Handles time-based missile behavior triggered at specific duration thresholds.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile's remaining duration timer
2. If duration == 20 ticks (0x14):
   a. Get owner GUID and missile Y coordinate
   b. Initialize spawn parameters structure (22 dwords zeroed)
   c. Set missile flags 0x2001 and skill ID 499 (0x1F3)
   d. Get missile range and spawn first projectile
   e. Loop 3 times spawning additional missiles with random X/Y offsets
   f. Each spawned missile gets target X offset of 0x40
3. If duration == 45 ticks (0x2D):
   a. Get parent missile properties
   b. Set parent flag 0x40000 to mark behavior triggered
   c. Initialize child parameters with flags 0x2000 and skill ID 501 (0x1F5)
   d. Spawn child projectile and call ProcessUnitStats with ID 0x99A
4. Process final unit stats and return

Parameters:
pMissile (ECX) - Pointer to the missile UnitAny being processed

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Only triggers at exact duration thresholds (20 or 45 ticks)
- Spawns up to 4 missiles at duration 20 (1 initial + 3 loop iterations)
- Random offsets bounded by +/-3 units from base position

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x14 (20)    - First behavior trigger threshold in ticks
0x2D (45)    - Second behavior trigger threshold in ticks
0x2001       - Spawn flags for first behavior missiles
0x2000       - Spawn flags for second behavior child missiles
0x1F3 (499)  - Skill ID for first behavior spawned missiles
0x1F5 (501)  - Skill ID for second behavior child missiles
0x40         - Target X offset for spawned missiles
0x40000      - Parent flag to mark behavior triggered
0xEC (236)   - Offset to missile flags in parent structure
0x99A (2458) - ProcessUnitStats identifier for cleanup
0x16 (22)    - Number of dwords in spawn parameters structure

Structure Layout (Spawn Parameters at ESP+0x14):
Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
0x00    4     dwFlags         uint    Missile spawn flags (0x2001 or 0x2000)
0x04    4     pGame           void*   Game context pointer
0x10    4     nSkillId        int     Skill ID for spawned missile
0x14    4     nTargetX        int     Target X coordinate
0x18    4     nTargetY        int     Target Y coordinate
0x2C    4     nRange          int     Missile range value

functions.name: ProcessUnitSkillMode
functions.comment:
Determines and applies appropriate skill mode to a game unit based on game state.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve unit data from hash table using unit ID
2. Call Ordinal_11141 to check if unit has initial state/condition
3. If unit exists and condition check returns 0:
   a. Call Ordinal_10918 (RandSeed) to generate random value
   b. Set skill mode based on random result: 0x1a6 if random==0, else 0x1a0
   c. Apply selected mode via FUN_6fb752f0
   d. Query current skill value via Ordinal_11125
   e. Map skill value to mode number using threshold comparisons:
      - 0x00..0x95 (150): mode 0x13 (19 decimal)
      - 0x96..0xC7 (150-199): mode 0x0E (14 decimal)  
      - 0xC8..0xE0 (200-224): mode 0x09 (9 decimal)
      - 0xE1+ (225+): computed mode = (skill>=0x177 ? -1 : 0) & 0xFFFFFFEC + 0x19
   f. Apply mode value - 1 via Ordinal_11140
   g. Call FUN_6fb771e0 to finalize/render
4. If unit not found or condition failed, skip mode setting
5. Always call FUN_6fb771e0 at exit

Parameters:
  pUnit (dword *): Pointer to unit ID/handle (ECX register - __fastcall)

Returns:
  void

Ordinals Used:
  Ordinal_11141: Check unit initial condition (D2Common - unknown exact function)
  Ordinal_10918: RandSeed - Generate random number seed (D2Common)
  Ordinal_11125: Query unit skill value (D2Common - unknown exact function)
  Ordinal_11140: Set unit mode/animation (D2Common - unknown exact function)

Magic Numbers:
  0x1A0, 0x1A6: Skill mode enum values
  0x96 (150), 0xC8 (200), 0xE1 (225): Skill value thresholds for mode mapping
  0x177 (375): Upper threshold for computed mode formula
  0x13, 0x0E, 0x09: Skill mode constants

functions.name: CreateProjectilesForUnit
functions.comment:
CreateProjectilesForUnit - Creates two projectile visual effects for a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Initializes a 22-dword projectile parameter structure to zero
2. Gets the unit from hash table using the unit ID
3. Creates first projectile with ID 0x25C (604)
4. Creates second projectile with ID 0x26D (621)
5. Sets drawable coordinates for the second projectile if created

Parameters:
  pUnitId - Pointer to the unit ID

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessMissilePeriodicEffects
functions.comment:
ProcessMissilePeriodicEffects - Handles periodic visual effects for missiles.

Algorithm:
1. Gets owner unit from hash table and remaining duration
2. If no owner, processes unit stats and returns
3. Initializes drawable objects for missile-owner relationship
4. Every 20 frames after frame 60: spawns spark effect (missile 0x11d) with random offset
5. At exactly frame 25: spawns two flame projectiles (missiles 0x269, 0x26a) at owner position

Parameters:
  pMissile - The missile unit to process effects for

Returns: void

functions.name: InitializeDrawableObject
functions.comment:
Initializes a drawable object with random positioning and animation mode selection.
Creates a projectile-based visual effect attached to a unit with randomized offsets.

Algorithm:
  1. Allocate stack frame (0x88 bytes) and save registers (EBX, EBP, ESI, EDI)
  2. Initialize position offset tables with sentinel values (-1) and enable flags (1)
  3. Call GetRandomBoundedValue(pModeData, 0x7D) to get random X mode index
  4. Call GetRandomBoundedValue(pModeData, 4) to get random Y mode index
  5. Retrieve unit owner GUID via GetUnitOwnerGuid for linking
  6. Get unit Y coordinate via GetUnitY for screen positioning
  7. Calculate final screen coordinates using mode table lookups
  8. Use switch table (0-3) to select animation mode ID (0x25F-0x263)
  9. Zero initialize projectile structure (22 DWORDs via REP STOSD)
  10. Configure projectile with type=3, calculated coordinates, and selected mode
  11. Call InitializeAndAllocateProjectile to create the drawable object
  12. If allocation succeeds, call SetDrawableObjectCoordinates with init flags
  13. Link drawable to owner via MissileSetTargetUnit and SetMissileTargetUnitId

Parameters:
  dwObjectId (ECX): Object identifier passed to initialization routines
  dwResourceType (EDX): Pointer to resource structure; offset +0x2C contains mode data

Returns:
  void - Drawable object is created and configured in place
  Returns early without action if InitializeAndAllocateProjectile returns NULL

Special Cases:
  Mode selection uses jump table at 0x6fb757f0 for random values 0-3
  Mode ID mapping: 0->0x260, 1->0x261, 2->0x262, 3->0x263, default->0x25F

Magic Numbers:
  0x88 - Stack frame size for local structure
  0x7D (125) - Random bound for X mode selection
  0x4 - Random bound for Y mode selection
  0x1E (30) - Random bound for animation mode (produces 0-3)
  0x2C - Offset to mode data within resource structure
  0x16 (22) - DWORD count for projectile structure zeroing
  0x25F-0x263 - Animation mode identifiers

functions.name: ProcessMissileDescentEffects
functions.comment:
ProcessMissileDescentEffects - Spawns visual effects for missiles descending through Y-axis thresholds.

Algorithm:
1. Get target unit from hash table; early exit if none (just process stats)
2. Get missile's current target Y coordinate
3. Search descent threshold table for current Y level
4. If at spawn interval (Y % divisor == 0) and spawn enabled, create spark missile
5. Set targeting mode based on height: mode 2 if Y < 0xD2, else mode 1
6. Switch on specific Y values to spawn level-specific effect missiles:
   - Y=0x145: spawn missile ID 0x27A (upper level)
   - Y=0x177: spawn missile ID 0x279 (mid-upper level)
   - Y=0x1A9: spawn missile ID 0x278 (mid-lower level)
   - Y=0x1C2: spawn missile ID 0x277 (ground impact)
7. If missile field24 is set, find ground tile and spawn drop effect
8. Process unit stats on exit

Parameters:
  pMissile (ECX) - UnitAny* Missile unit to process descent effects for

Returns: void

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0xD2 (210)      - Height threshold for targeting mode switch
  0x145 (325)     - Y level for upper effect (missile 0x27A)
  0x177 (375)     - Y level for mid-upper effect (missile 0x279)
  0x1A9 (425)     - Y level for mid-lower effect (missile 0x278)
  0x1C2 (450)     - Y level for ground impact (missile 0x277)
  0x209 (521)     - Ground drop effect tile type
  0x272 (626)     - Base spark missile ID (random +0 or +1)
  0x277-0x27A     - Level-specific effect missile IDs
  0x28 (40)       - Random offset range for spark positioning
  0x0A (10)       - Random offset range for drop effect positioning

Threshold Table (g_aDescentLevelThresholds @ 0x6fba9bec):
  Offset  Field       Description
  0x00    threshold   Y level threshold value
  0x04    divisor     Spawn interval divisor (Y % divisor)
  0x08    spawn_flag  Enable spawning at this level (0=disabled)

Missile Spawn Parameters Structure (22 dwords at ESP+0x18):
  Offset  Field         Description
  0x00    mode          Missile mode (1 or 2)
  0x04    pTarget       Target unit pointer
  0x08    pOwner        Owner missile pointer
  0x10    missileId     Missile type ID
  0x1C    offsetX       Random X offset (-20 to +20)
  0x20    offsetY       Random Y offset (-20 to +20)
  0x2C    flag          Spawn flag (set to 1)

functions.name: InitializeMonsterDropEffect
functions.signature: void InitializeMonsterDropEffect(dword dwUnitId, dword dwMonsterType, dword dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Initialize monster unit drop effect with properties.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit type using Ordinal_10342 (D2Common.GetUnitStat)
2. Check validation result via Ordinal_10119 (D2Common.UnitHasSkill)
3. If validation passes (result == 0):
   a. Initialize 0x58-byte stack buffer (set to 0)
   b. Set buffer header to 0x2001 (effect type indicator)
   c. Retrieve unit from hash table via GetUnitFromHashTable
   d. Get base time offset via Ordinal_10918 (D2Common.RandSeed), add 0x27b
   e. Setup configuration in stack locals
   f. Call FUN_6fb77720 to create effect object with config
   g. If object created (non-null pointer):
      - Call FUN_6fb97b10 to set property 0xfa (250)
      - Call FUN_6fb97b40 to set property -10 (property ID)
      - Ordinal_11121: Set unit state 0x19
      - Ordinal_11123: Set unit state 0x19
      - Ordinal_11139: Set unit state 0x80

Parameters:
- dwUnitId (ECX) - Unit identifier to process
- dwMonsterType (EDX) - Monster classification code
- dwFlags (Stack +0x4) - Configuration flags

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2001: Effect object type identifier
- 0x27b: Time offset constant (635 decimal)
- 0xfa: Property value (250 decimal)
- 0x19: Unit state value (25 decimal)
- 0x80: Final property value (128 decimal)
- 0x16: Loop count (22 decimal) for buffer initialization

functions.name: UpdateMissileSeekingBehavior
functions.comment:
UpdateMissileSeekingBehavior - Updates missile seeking/homing behavior based on state.

Algorithm:
1. Get missile's seek state (field 0x24) and target unit ID
2. Look up target unit via FindLinkListNodeByIdAndIndex (type 3 = missile target)
3. If no target found, process stats and return
4. Based on seek state:
   - State 0: Random chance to enable animation flag and rate (0xF00)
   - State 1: Calculate delta position from target and update path
   - State 2: Set fixed position (0x3B1F, 0x170C) and animation rate
5. Update missile position and path to target

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to missile unit being updated

Returns: void

functions.name: ProcessAndRenderSpecificClassUnit
functions.comment:
Validates and renders a unit if its class matches specific types (Amazon/Sorceress/Necromancer).

Algorithm:
1. Look up unit pointer from unit ID using GetUnitFromHashTable
2. If unit not found, call ProcessAndRenderSpecificClassUnit with NULL and exit
3. Retrieve unit's class bits using GetUnitStat (with implicit register params)
4. Extract class value using GetUnitMode - check if class is 0x83 or 0x84 (Amazon/Sorceress)
5. If class invalid, exit without rendering
6. Call setup/preparation functions: Ordinal_10235, Ordinal_10374
7. Call Ordinal_11141 - check if returns 0 or RandSeed returns 0
8. If check passes, call SetRenderingState with params (6, 2000, 3000, 2000) and mark unit with flag
9. Loop through coordinate retrieval: RandSeed calls (3x) for randomization
10. Get screen coordinates using Ordinal_10326 and Ordinal_10329
11. Subtract 0x1e from each coordinate (position offset)
12. Call FUN_6fb75bc0 with adjusted coordinates for rendering
13. Exit normally (return without processing invalid units)
14. Invalid unit/class path: call FUN_6fb773b0 with NULL and 0

Parameters:
IMPLICIT ECX - pUnitId: uint* - pointer to unit ID being processed

Returns:
void - no return value (rendering is done as side effect)

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x83/0x84: Amazon (0x83) and Sorceress (0x84) class codes - may be 0x82/0x85 boundary check instead
Magic number 0x1e (30): Position offset subtracted from screen coordinates
Magic number 0x40: Buffer size for internal operation (Ordinal_10326 call)
Magic number 0x3c (60): Another position parameter passed to coordinate functions
Magic number 0xa (10): Secondary offset parameter
RandSeed (Ordinal_10918): Called 3 times for coordinate randomization
SetRenderingState values: 6=render mode, 2000/3000/2000=timing parameters
Unit state check: Ordinal_11141 gates entire rendering operation

Structure Layout:
Unit structure accessed via pUnit pointer:
Offset | Size | Field      | Type     | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwUnitId   | uint     | Unit identifier
0x2c   | 4    | dwCoordPtr | pointer  | Coordinate/rendering data pointer
?      | ?    | pData      | void*    | Unit class and stat data

functions.name: ValidateRangeValue
functions.comment:
Validates if a value falls within an acceptable range bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Query minimum bound from Ordinal_11141 - Custom ordinal, purpose unknown
2. Query maximum bound from Ordinal_11143 - Custom ordinal, purpose unknown
3. Retrieve value to validate via FUN_6fb97ad0
4. Check if value is within range: -nMinBound <= nValue <= nMaxBound
5. If in range, call FUN_6fb771e0 (success handler)
6. If out of range, call FUN_6fb773b0 with NULL and 0 (failure handler)

Parameters:
pData (uint *) - Pointer to data structure containing validation context

Returns:
void - Calls appropriate handler function based on validation result

Special Cases:
- Range check is inverted for lower bound (negative of minimum ordinal)
- NULL and 0 passed to failure handler for cleanup
- Ordinal_11141 and Ordinal_11143 are custom ordinals not found in docs/KNOWN_ORDINALS.md

Magic Numbers:
0x0 - NULL pointer passed to failure handler

functions.name: CreateProjectileFromUnit
functions.comment:
CreateProjectileFromUnit - Creates a projectile/missile from the given unit.

Algorithm:
1. Gets target unit from hash table using source unit
2. Initializes projectile parameters struct (0x16 dwords zeroed)
3. Sets missile ID to 500 and gets missile range
4. Allocates and initializes projectile via InitializeAndAllocateProjectile
5. Sets projectile target X offset to 0x40
6. Gets path direction from source and sets projectile direction

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to the source unit creating the projectile

Returns: void

functions.name: ConfigureMissilePattern
functions.comment:
ConfigureMissilePattern - Configures a missile pattern structure for projectile rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Extract missile type from unit field (field_4)
2. Initialize 22-dword pattern structure to zeros
3. Set structure type to 3 (missile pattern marker)
4. Call D2Common ordinals to set up context
5. Get owner unit from hash table
6. Check missile type: 0x1B6 -> skill ID 0x1B8, iterations 18; else -> skill ID 0x1B1, iterations 10
7. Get missile range from unit data
8. Store callback pointer (ApplyTextControlMaxValueClamp)
9. Call ApplyDCTTransform to generate pattern coefficients

Parameters:
  pMissile - Pointer to missile UnitAny structure

Returns: void

functions.name: CreateRadialMissileBurst
functions.comment:
Creates a radial burst of missiles emanating from a source unit in 8 cardinal/ordinal directions.

Algorithm:
