0x08    4     dwOwnerGUID            uint     Owner unit identifier
0x0C    12    vecPosition            float[3] World position (X, Y, Z)
0x18    4     flDistance             float    Distance from viewport center
0x1C    4     dwRenderColor          uint     Current render color ARGB
0x20    4     flVisibility           float    Visibility alpha (0.0-1.0)
0x24    4     dwPendingColor         uint     Transition target color
0x28    4     pLinkedItems           void*    Linked item list pointer
0x2C    4     pAnimController        void*    Animation controller pointer
0x30    4     dwRenderState          uint     0=new, 1=active, 2=ready
0x34    4     dwCreateTick           uint     Creation timestamp
0x38    4     dwFlags                uint     Render flags (bit 1 = gradual)
0x3C    1     byPriority             byte     Z-order priority value
0x3D    4     dwVisibleState         uint     Visibility state flags
0x41    4     dwPendingColorData     uint     Pending color transition
0x45    4     fHasTransition         uint     Active transition flag
0x49    4     dwTransitionStart      uint     Interpolation start value
0x4D    4     dwTransitionEnd        uint     Interpolation end value
0x51    4     dwTransitionStartTick  uint     Transition start time
0x55    4     dwTransitionEndTick    uint     Transition end time

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x122f, 0xb76: Missile type ID range boundaries
- 0x1230, 0x124b: Special effect type ID range
- 0x3: Animation frame divisor (tick / 3)
- 0x93, 0x347, 0x36a, 0x39f, 0x3f1: FogAssert source line numbers
- 0x46 (70): Frame rate adjustment threshold
- 0x64 (100): Maximum volume percentage
- 0x5: Volume increment/decrement step
- 0x2: Music volume adjustment step
- 0xbf800000: Float bit pattern for -1.0f (initial min distance)
- 0x44fa0000: Float bit pattern for 2000.0f (max coordinate)

Error Handling:
- FogAssert (0x6fb99a7a) called on null pointer dereferences with line numbers
- ReportError(-1) via 0x6fb9a10f for fatal rendering failures
- Silent continuation on GetGameContext failures (returns null)
- Graceful degradation when animation controller unavailable

functions.name: InitializeGameObjectState
functions.comment:
Initialize game object state and reset instance counter.

Algorithm:
1. Set g_dwGameObjectStateFlag = 0x01 (object system enabled)
2. Set g_dwObjectInstanceCounter = 0x00 (reset instance count)
3. Call ClearGameState() to clear all game state structures

Parameters:
(none) __stdcall convention

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Called during game session initialization
- Resets counter before ClearGameState to ensure clean state
- Order critical: flag set BEFORE counter reset

functions.name: ProcessInventoryUnitValidation
functions.comment:
Validate and initialize all units in the inventory list, processing item stacks and applying UI updates.

Algorithm:
1. Clear game state before processing
2. Get inventory list head from global pointer
3. Loop through inventory node chain:
   a. Check if current node is null - if so, mark game object state flag and return
   b. Dereference node pointer to get inventory object
   c. If inventory object null, continue to next iteration
   d. Call Ordinal_10059 (game loop tick/frame advance)
   e. Iterate through items in inventory at offset 0x28 (linked list of unit IDs)
   f. For each item, call ValidateAndInitializeUnit with unit ID
   g. Call Ordinal_10062 (game loop cleanup/finalize)
   h. Check if inventory object at offset 0x30 equals 1 (active/visible flag)
   i. If true, call ApplyMouseCoordinates with inventory object at offset 0x2c (cursor position)
   j. Check if inventory object at offset 0x2c (cursor position data) is non-zero
   k. If cursor position data exists, break loop (cursor is valid)
   l. Otherwise, zero out inventory object pointer and reload list head
4. If no valid cursor position data, trigger assertion with D2Common_AssertionOrdinal
5. Call FUN_6fb9a10f with error code 0xffffffff (non-returning cleanup)

Parameters:
None (uses global inventory list pointer)

Returns:
void (non-returning on assertion failure)

Special Cases:
- Assertion failure path is non-returning (FUN_6fb9a10f does not return)
- Handles null inventory nodes gracefully
- Cursor position data (offset 0x2c) must be valid for loop to complete

Magic Numbers:
- 0x28: Offset to item/unit linked list head in inventory object
- 0x2c: Offset to cursor position data in inventory object
- 0x30: Offset to active/visible flag in inventory object
- 0x04: Offset to next item in linked list chain
- 0x8: Offset within unit structure for some field access
- 0x93: Assertion error code line number

Related Functions:
- ClearGameState: Initializes game rendering state
- ValidateAndInitializeUnit: Validates and sets up individual unit data
- ApplyMouseCoordinates: Updates viewport based on cursor position
- Ordinal_10059: D2Client frame/loop tick function
- Ordinal_10062: D2Client frame/loop finalize function

functions.name: FindInventoryItemById
functions.comment:
Search inventory list for item by ID with channel validation

Algorithm:
1. Validate nItemId parameter is non-zero
2. Get global g_pInventoryListHead, validate not NULL
3. Iterate through linked list via next pointers at offset +4
4. Compare each item's ID field (offset +8) against nItemId
5. When match found, validate item has channel (offset +0x2c != 0)
6. If channel is NULL, trigger assertion and terminate
7. Return pointer to inventory item
8. Return NULL if list is NULL, nItemId is zero, or no match found

Parameters:
- nItemId (ECX:4): Item ID to search for, must be non-zero

Returns:
- EAX: Pointer to inventory item (void*) if found with valid channel
- NULL: If nItemId is zero, list is NULL, or no matching item
- Termination: If item found but channel is NULL (assertion failure)

Special Cases:
- Channel NULL triggers D2Common_AssertionOrdinal assertion failure
- GetMouseXPosition called on success (purpose unclear - may be side effect)
- Function uses register-based SSA temporaries (piVar2, iVar1) optimized for fast register access

Structure Layout (Inventory Item):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0      | 4    | next       | ptr  | Pointer to next item in linked list
4      | 4    | prev       | ptr  | Pointer to previous item
8      | 4    | itemId     | uint | Item identifier
...    | ...  | ...        | ...  | ...
0x2c   | 4    | channel    | ptr  | Pointer to channel (must be non-NULL)

Related Functions:
- g_pInventoryListHead - Global head of inventory list
- D2Common_AssertionOrdinal - Failure handler for assertion
- GetMouseXPosition - Called on successful match (purpose unclear)

functions.name: CompareUnitsForSorting
functions.signature: bool CompareUnitsForSorting(uint dwUnitA, uint dwUnitB, int nCompareY, int nCompareCount)
functions.comment:
Compares two units for sorting/ordering based on type and optional criteria.

Algorithm:
1. Compare unit type (offset 0x3c byte) - sort by type ascending
2. If types match and nCompareY enabled, compare Y coordinate (offset 0x18 float)
3. If Y values match and nCompareCount enabled, compare unit count (offset 0x34 uint)
4. Final tiebreaker: compare unit addresses directly (lower address wins)

Parameters:
  dwUnitA (uint) - First unit address to compare
  dwUnitB (uint) - Second unit address to compare
  nCompareY (int) - Enable Y coordinate comparison if non-zero
  nCompareCount (int) - Enable unit count comparison if non-zero

Returns:
  true if dwUnitA should sort before dwUnitB
  false if dwUnitB should sort before or equals dwUnitA

Special Cases:
  If both units have same type, Y coordinate, and count, sorts by address.
  Comparisons use unsigned comparison for counts, signed for coordinates.

functions.name: IsEffectInViewport
functions.comment:
Determines if a visual effect should be rendered based on viewport distance.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate viewport coordinates for the entity using dwEntityId
2. Retrieve effect distance value from viewport calculation and stack storage
3. Compare effect distance against maximum allowed distance threshold (g_flMaxEffectDistance)
4. Return 1 if effect distance is within viewport, 0 if outside viewport

Parameters:
dwEntityId (dword) - Entity identifier in ECX register, used to calculate viewport coordinates

Returns:
1 (TRUE) - Effect is within maximum viewport distance
0 (FALSE) - Effect exceeds maximum viewport distance or invalid entity

Special Cases:
- Magic value 490000 is the maximum effect distance threshold stored at g_flMaxEffectDistance
- Floating point comparison uses FCOMP instruction for precise distance evaluation
- Called during animation effect processing for visual optimization

Structure Layout:
N/A - No structure parameters

Related Functions:
- CalculateViewportCoordinates() - Calculates effect distance from viewport
- FUN_6fb8ec60() - Additional distance calculations
- ProcessUnitAnimationEffect() - Caller that determines if effect should render

functions.name: IsValidInventoryItemInRange
functions.comment:
Validates inventory item in weapon/armor slot range with optional callback validation.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global inventory list (g_pInventoryListHead) is empty; return false if null
2. Iterate through linked list of inventory nodes (ppInventoryNode->next at offset 0x4)
3. For each node, verify field at offset 0x30 equals 1 (state check)
4. If nValidateWithCallback is set, call Ordinal_10060 for additional validation; skip item if callback returns 0
5. Check item field at offset 0x4 is within valid range: 0xb76 < value < 0x1230
6. Return true if any item passes all validations, false if no items found or validation fails

Parameters:
nValidateWithCallback: ECX register - non-zero triggers callback validation via Ordinal_10060

Returns:
AL: true (1) if valid item found in range, false (0) otherwise

Special Cases:
- Empty inventory list returns false immediately
- If callback flag set, item skipped if Ordinal_10060 returns 0 (validation failed)
- Range bounds: 0xb76 (weapon/armor range lower) to 0x1230 (upper bound exclusive)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x30: Offset to item state field (must equal 1 for valid items)
0x4: Offset to item type/ID field (range validation)
0xb76: Lower bound of valid item range (2934 decimal)
0x1230: Upper bound of valid item range (4656 decimal)

functions.name: ProcessInventoryFadeEffects
functions.comment:
Process inventory fade effects for valid units.

Algorithm:
1. Toggle g_dwObjectRenderFlag: set to 1 if currently 0, else skip processing
2. If flag now 0 (was already set), return early
3. If g_pInventoryListHead is NULL, return early
4. Iterate through inventory linked list starting at g_pInventoryListHead:
   a. Load inventory node at current position
   b. Extract unit index from node+4
   c. Validate unit index range: 0xb76 <= index <= 0x122f (2934-4655 in decimal)
   d. If index out of range, skip to next node
   e. Call GetUnitDataByIndex to get unit data
   f. Set inventory node+0x3d to 1 (mark processed)
   g. Check unit validity: byte at (pUnitData + 0x40) must be non-zero
   h. Check node state: dword at (node + 0x30) must equal 1
   i. If both conditions true, call ProcessInventoryFadeEffect with parameters:
      - ECX = node+8 (first parameter)
      - EDX = 0 (second parameter)
      - [ESP+4] = 0 (third parameter)
      - [ESP] = unit_flag & 0xFF (fourth parameter from unit byte)
   j. Advance to next node: pCurrentNode = pCurrentNode[1]
5. Continue until pCurrentNode[1] is NULL (end of list)
6. Return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Uses global toggle flag to prevent multiple processing passes
- Only processes units with valid IDs in range (Diablo II inventory constraint)
- Node state check (value 1 at +0x30) gates fade effect processing
- Retrieves dynamically allocated unit data via GetUnitDataByIndex

functions.name: InitializeGameMemoryBlock
functions.comment:
Initialize game memory block and global state variables to zero.

Algorithm:
1. Set EDI to address of memory buffer at 0x6fc0402c
2. Clear EAX to 0x00000000
3. Set ECX to 0x1c (28 dwords = 112 bytes)
4. Execute REP STOSD to fill buffer with zeros (28 iterations)
5. Zero all 7 game state global variables (flags, session ID, game state, mode, loaded flags, config, checksum)
6. Return to caller

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
(void) - Function returns void after initialization completes

Special Cases:
- Function does not validate target addresses; assumes memory is allocated and writable
- Uses register EAX for zero value; caller must not depend on EAX containing values
- EDI is restored via POP after REP STOSD execution

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1c = 28 decimal (number of dwords to zero in buffer, 112 bytes total)
0x6fc0402c = Base address of game state buffer
0x6fc0409c = Address of g_dwGameFlags global
0x6fc040a0 = Address of g_dwGameSessionId global
0x6fc040a4 = Address of g_dwCurrentGameState global
0x6fc040a8 = Address of g_dwGameMode global
0x6fc040ac = Address of g_dwLoadedGameFlags global
0x6fc040b0 = Address of g_dwGameConfigFlags global
0x6fc040d0 = Address of g_dwGameStateChecksum global

Related Functions:
- InitializeGameSession() - Calls this function as part of game session setup
- PlayVideoById() - Calls this function before video playback

functions.name: ProcessPlayerInventorySlots
functions.comment:
Process inventory slot updates and fading effects for player items.

Algorithm:
1. Call ProcessUnitStatData() to update unit state
2. Get current item slot index from array element pointer
3. Validate slot index in valid range (0x1230-0x124b)
4. Check Ordinal_10046 (animation system check) - returns nonzero if available
5. If Ordinal_10046 returns 0, check Ordinal_10048 (secondary state) - if both 0, animation unavailable
6. Set fHasValidInventory = (both ordinals returned nonzero)
7. If slot changed and frame delta > 0x4a OR animation unavailable OR no slot selected:
   - Update current item ID to new slot value
   - Store frame counter at update time
8. If animation unavailable, trigger ProcessInventoryListFadeEffects()
9. If no item selected, trigger ProcessInventoryListFadeEffects()
10. If fade system active:
    - Check highlight state 1 expiry and reinitialize if needed
    - Check highlight state 2 expiry and validate unit, reinitialize if valid
    - Check global frame counter vs expiry time, exit if not ready
    - Clear fade flag
    - If animation available, ProcessInventorySlot()
11. If current item found but no inventory entry exists:
    - Search inventory for item and get slot type
    - Set fade alpha (2.8026e-45 if not found, 0.0 otherwise)
    - Initialize object properties with fade effect
    - Store frame counter
12. If unit index changed and frame delta > 0x3d:
    - ProcessLevelGameState()
    - Update last processed unit index
13. If current item exists and frame delta > 0x7d:
    - Get unit data and find inventory item
    - Check search flag
    - Validate inventory slot boundaries
    - Determine correct slot list (weapon/armor/belt)
    - Store result in global slot data array

Parameters:
dwFrameCounter (dword, ECX) - Current game frame counter, used to detect timing intervals

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Ordinal_10046: Animation/effect system availability check (unknown ordinal - see comment at 0x6fb8e87f)
- Ordinal_10048: Secondary animation state check (unknown ordinal - see comment at 0x6fb8e888)
- Frame deltas: 0x4a (74 frames), 0x3d (61 frames), 0x7d (125 frames) - update frequency thresholds
- Slot validation range: 0x1230-0x124b
- Float constant 2.8026e-45 used as fade alpha marker
- Note: Function uses SSA-form temporaries (extraout_var, extraout_var_00) from function returns - these are compiler optimizations

Global Variables Used:
- g_dwCurrentUnitIndex: Currently processed unit ID
- g_dwCurrentItemId: Currently selected item slot
- g_dwLastProcessedUnit: Track unit changes
- g_fItemFadeActive: Fade effect state flag
- g_adItemSlotData: Item slot inventory slot mapping array (indexed by item ID)
- g_dwInventoryFrameBase: Frame counter at last update
- g_dwSlotCheckFrame: Frame counter for slot validation
- g_dwInventoryUpdateTime: Time of inventory update
- g_fHighlightState1: Highlight 1 fade state
- g_fHighlightState2: Highlight 2 fade state
- g_dwHighlightFrame1: Highlight 1 expiry frame
- g_dwHighlightFrame2: Highlight 2 expiry frame

functions.name: ProcessInventoryFadeEffectConfiguration
functions.signature: void ProcessInventoryFadeEffectConfiguration(dword dwFadeDuration, int nSecondEffectDuration, int nThirdEffectDuration, int nInventorySlot, dword dwSecondEffect, int nSecondEffectDelay, dword dwThirdEffect)
functions.comment:
Configures fade effect parameters for inventory item display transitions.

Algorithm:
1. Check if current game state exists (g_dwCurrentGameState != 0)
2. Retrieve unit data for current game state via GetUnitDataByIndex
3. Find inventory item by ID via FindInventoryItemById
4. If item found, check flag status with SearchListAndCheckFlag
5. If flag check succeeds and nInventorySlot != 0, retrieve property value from unit data at offset 0x50 + (nInventorySlot * 4)
6. Store property value in g_aCurrentInventoryItem array
7. Retrieve and store current game session flags via GetGameSessionFlags
8. Process inventory list fade effects via ProcessInventoryListFadeEffects
9. Initialize first fade effect: set active flag, duration, and frame-based start time (frame_counter + nSecondEffectDuration)
10. Initialize second fade effect: set active flag, parameter, and frame-based start time (frame_counter + nSecondEffectDelay)
11. Initialize third fade effect: set parameter and frame-based start time (frame_counter + nThirdEffectDuration)

Parameters:
- dwFadeDuration: Duration in frames for initial fade effect display
- nSecondEffectDuration: Duration in frames for second effect delay
- nThirdEffectDuration: Duration in frames for third effect timing
- nInventorySlot: Inventory slot index to retrieve property value from (0 = skip retrieval)
- dwSecondEffect: Parameter value for second fade effect
- nSecondEffectDelay: Frame delay before second effect triggers
- dwThirdEffect: Parameter value for third fade effect

Returns:
- void (always succeeds if game state exists)

Special Cases:
- If nInventorySlot == 0, property value retrieval is skipped
- If item not found or flag check fails, only global fade effect globals are initialized
- Game state existence is prerequisite for item lookup and property retrieval

functions.name: InitializeFadeEffectTiming
functions.comment:
Initialize fade effect timing parameters and frame counter values.

Algorithm:
1. Check if fade effect is active (g_bFadeEffectActive)
2. If not active, exit immediately
3. If active and nFadeDuration is nonzero:
   - Get current global frame counter
   - Store nFadeDuration as fade duration flag
   - Calculate and store start frame (counter + nFrameOffset)
   - Calculate and store end frame (counter + nFrameOffset + 0x32)
4. If active and nFadeDuration is zero:
   - Calculate end frame (previous start frame + 0x32)
   - Clear fade duration flag to 0

Parameters:
- nFrameOffset: Frame count offset from current frame
- nFadeDuration: Nonzero to set new fade timing, zero to use previous start

Returns:
- void

Global Data Modified:
- g_dwFadeDurationFlag: Fade duration flag (set to nFadeDuration or 0)
- g_dwFadeStartFrame: Fade start frame
- g_dwFadeEndFrame: Fade end frame (start + 0x32)

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x32 (50 decimal): Frame duration for fade completion
- Only operates if g_bFadeEffectActive is nonzero
- Reuses previous start frame if nFadeDuration is zero
- Note: Function uses 1 frame counter temporary (DVar1) optimized away in registers

functions.name: SeedRandomNumberWithGameContext
functions.comment:
Seed the random number generator with game context.

Algorithm:
1. Get the game context state via GetGameContext()
2. Add 0x2c offset to context (accesses a field)
3. If nSeed is non-zero: pass context to RandSeed ordinal and return result
4. Otherwise: return 0 (no seeding performed)

Parameters:
nSeed (uint) - Seed value in ECX register (__fastcall). Non-zero triggers RNG seeding.

Returns:
dword - Result from RandSeed ordinal if nSeed != 0, else 0.

Special Cases:
- nSeed == 0: Returns 0 immediately without calling RandSeed
- Uses __fastcall convention with parameter in ECX register
- GetGameContext adds 0x2c offset (likely accessing RNG state field)
- Note: Function uses 1 phantom variable (dVar1) optimized away

Magic Numbers:
0x2c - Offset from GameContext structure (RNG seed state field)

functions.name: GetRandomOffsetInRange
functions.comment:
Calculate random offset within a range.

Algorithm:
1. Get game context for random seed state
2. Calculate range size: (nMaxValue - nMinValue + 1)
3. If range is valid (size > 0):
   a. Generate random value using Ordinal_10918 (Storm.RandSeed)
   b. Return nMinValue + random value
4. If range invalid (size <= 0), return nMinValue

Parameters:
- nMinValue (int, ECX): Minimum value of range (inclusive)
- nMaxValue (int, EDX): Maximum value of range (inclusive)

Returns:
- int: Random value in range [nMinValue, nMaxValue], or nMinValue if range invalid

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2c (44 decimal): Offset in game context to random seed state

functions.name: CalculateRandomOffsetFromSeed
functions.comment:
Generate seed-based random offset for camera/viewport adjustments.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize game context for random seed state (via GetGameContext call)
2. Calculate seed value: nSeed = (nSeedBase * 2) + 1
3. If nSeed != 0 (seed value is non-zero):
   a. Generate pseudo-random value via Ordinal_10918 (D2Common.RandSeed)
   b. Return offset as (nRandomResult - nSeedBase)
4. If nSeed == 0 (seed value equals -1 after transformation):
   a. Return negated seed base: (-nSeedBase)

Parameters:
int nSeedBase (ECX) - Input seed base value for random offset calculation
                      Used to derive actual seed: (nSeedBase * 2) + 1
                      Represents base offset magnitude to subtract from random result

Returns:
int - Offset delta for viewport/camera adjustments
      Range: Negative to positive based on random result and seed base
      Special case: If seed calculation equals -1, returns -nSeedBase directly

Magic Numbers:
0x2 - Multiplier for seed base transformation (nSeedBase * 2)
0x1 - Add constant for seed offset adjustment ((nSeedBase * 2) + 1)
-0x1 - Seed boundary condition check (param_1 * 2 == -1)

Related Functions:
- GetGameContext() - Initialize random seed state for this calculation
- Ordinal_10918() - D2Common.RandSeed, generates pseudo-random value
- UpdateRenderViewportSettings() - Primary caller, uses offset for camera adjustments

functions.name: ComputeEuclideanDistance
functions.comment:
Compute Euclidean distance between two points.

Algorithm:
1. Cast both parameters to float10 extended precision
2. Compute squared sum: param2^2 + param1^2
3. Compute square root of squared sum
4. Return result as float10

Parameters:
flDeltaX (float) - X-axis delta component (width/horizontal distance)
flDeltaY (float) - Y-axis delta component (height/vertical distance)

Returns:
float10 - Euclidean distance (magnitude of vector)

Special Cases:
- Both parameters 0.0 returns 0.0
- Negative values treated as absolute (squared removes sign)

functions.name: CalculateDistanceSquared
functions.comment:
Calculate the squared Euclidean distance between two points on a 2D plane.

Algorithm:
1. Convert flDeltaX to float10 extended precision
2. Multiply flDeltaX by itself (flDeltaX²)
3. Convert flDeltaY to float10 extended precision
4. Multiply flDeltaY by itself (flDeltaY²)
5. Add the two squared values (flDeltaX² + flDeltaY²)
6. Return the sum as float10

Parameters:
- flDeltaX: X-axis delta distance (float)
- flDeltaY: Y-axis delta distance (float)

Returns:
- float10: Sum of squares (flDeltaX² + flDeltaY²), representing squared distance

Special Cases:
- Zero inputs: Returns 0.0
- Negative inputs: Squared values always positive
- Used for range/viewport checks where exact distance not needed

Related Functions:
- RenderGameViewport() - Uses distance for viewport clipping checks
- IsEffectInViewport() - Validates effect visibility based on squared distance
- InitializeGameObjectProperties() - Sets object position/collision calculations
- UpdateInventoryItemPosition() - Calculates item offset distances

functions.name: GetMinCyclicDistance
functions.signature: int GetMinCyclicDistance(dword nValue1, dword nValue2, dword nModulus)
functions.comment:
Calculate minimum cyclic distance between two values in modular arithmetic space.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nModulus is power of 2 via (nModulus & (nModulus - 1)) == 0
2. If power of 2: calculate remainders using bitwise AND (nModulus - 1) & nValue
3. If not power of 2: calculate remainders using modulo division (nValue % nModulus)
4. Compute delta distance: nRemainder2 - nRemainder1
5. Calculate absolute delta: abs(nDeltaDistance)
6. Calculate distance +modulus: abs(nDeltaDistance - nModulus)
7. Calculate distance -modulus: abs(nRemainder1 - nRemainder2 - nModulus)
8. Find minimum of three distances and return as result

Parameters:
  nValue1 (uint): First value in modular space [0, nModulus)
  nValue2 (uint): Second value in modular space [0, nModulus)
  nModulus (uint): Modulus for cyclic distance (may be power of 2 for optimization)

Returns:
  int: Minimum cyclic distance between nValue1 and nValue2

functions.name: HandleMouseMoveMessage
functions.comment:
HandleMouseMoveMessage - Processes mouse movement messages and updates cursor position.

Algorithm:
1. Extract X coordinate from low word at pMessage->lParam, Y from high word
2. Store X in g_dwCursorX (0x6fc04118), Y in g_dwCursorY (0x6fc0411c)
3. Check IsVideoHighResMode() - skip processing if not high-res mode
4. Check GetExceptionActiveFlag() - skip if exception is active
5. Clamp cursor X to screen bounds (0 to g_dwScreenWidth - 1)
6. Clamp cursor Y to screen bounds (0 to g_dwScreenHeight - 1)
7. If cursor was out of bounds, call SetCursorPos to reposition
8. Call ShowOrHideCursor(1) to show the cursor
9. Record timestamp via GetTickCount() in g_dwLastFrameTimestamp
10. If screen state is 4 or 2, transition to state 3 with screen=2
11. Assert cursor table size equals 7 (NUM_CURSORS) or call ReportError(-1)
12. Calculate screen parameter from cursor type index
13. Clear message return values at pMessage+0x18 and pMessage+0x1C

Parameters:
  pMessage (MSG*) - Pointer to WM_MOUSEMOVE message structure
             lParam contains packed cursor coords (X in low word, Y in high)
             Extended fields at +0x18 and +0x1C are cleared to 0

Returns: void (modifies global cursor state and message structure)

Globals Modified:
  g_dwCursorX (0x6fc04118) - Current cursor X position
  g_dwCursorY (0x6fc0411c) - Current cursor Y position
  g_dwLastFrameTimestamp (0x6fc04104) - Frame timestamp from GetTickCount
  g_dwScreenState (0x6fc04108) - Screen state (set to 3)
  g_nSelectedScreen (0x6fc040f8) - Selected screen (set to 2)
  g_nScreenParam (0x6fc040fc) - Screen parameter (cursor type * 256 - 256)

Magic Numbers:
  0x99 (153) - Line number for FogAssert
  7 - NUM_CURSORS constant, expected cursor table size
  0x100 (256) - Cursor type multiplier

functions.name: ResetCursorState
functions.comment:
ResetCursorState - Resets cursor visibility state and clears cursor tracking fields.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cursor state field (offset 0x8) equals 2
2. If so, hide the cursor by calling ShowOrHideCursor(0)
3. Clear the cursor tracking fields at offsets 0x18 and 0x1c

Parameters:
  pCursorData - Pointer to cursor state data structure

Returns: void

functions.name: ValidateScreenStateTransition
functions.comment:
Validates screen state transition and handles state machine logic for UI rendering

Algorithm:
1. Extract resource ID (low 16 bits) from handle offset 0x0c → g_wResourceID
2. Extract resource flags (high 16 bits) from handle offset 0x0c → g_wResourceFlags
3. Store current tick count as frame timestamp → g_dwLastFrameTimestamp via GetTickCount()
4. Check if current screen state != 5 (SCREEN_GAME_MODE):
   a. Load screen data table entry: g_aScreenDataTable[g_nSelectedScreen * 7]
   b. If entry is non-zero, set g_dwScreenState = 5 and g_nSelectedScreen = 4
   c. Clear g_nScreenParam
5. Clear resource handle field at offset 0x18 (always set to 0)
6. If state == 5 (SCREEN_GAME_MODE), skip to final cleanup
7. Return with stack frame cleanup

Parameters:
nResourceHandle: int - Handle/pointer to resource structure (offset 0x0c contains composite ID/flags value, offset 0x18 for state field)

Returns:
void - No return value; modifies global screen state variables g_dwScreenState, g_nSelectedScreen, g_nScreenParam

functions.name: InitializeScreenState
functions.comment:
Initializes screen display state and captures frame timestamp for UI rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Extract resource ID from pScreenData->offset 0xc (lower 16-bit word)
2. Store resource ID in global g_wResourceID
3. Extract resource flags from pScreenData->offset 0xc (upper 16-bit word via SHR 0x10)
4. Store resource flags in global g_wResourceFlags
5. Call GetTickCount() to capture current system time
6. Store timestamp in global g_dwLastFrameTimestamp
7. Load global g_dwScreenState for conditional test
8. Compare g_dwScreenState against special value 5
9. If equal: set g_nSelectedScreen = 5, g_dwScreenState = 1, g_nScreenParam = 0
10. Clear pScreenData->offset 0x18 to zero (cleanup flag)
11. Return to caller

Parameters:
pScreenData (UIObject *) - Pointer to UI screen structure containing resource info at offset 0xc and control field at offset 0x18

Returns:
void - Modifies global screen state variables and zero-clears offset 0x18 field before returning

Special Cases:
- State value 5 triggers immediate transition: screen->5, state->1, param->0
- Non-state-5 execution path also zeros the 0x18 field
- GetTickCount() executed unconditionally for frame timing reference

Magic Numbers:
0x0c - Resource ID + Flags packed field offset
0x10 - Bit shift for upper word extraction (flags from combined 32-bit value)
0x18 - Control flag field offset (cleared before return)
0x05 - Special screen state value triggering transition
0x01 - Reset state value after transition

functions.name: SetCurrentScreenState
functions.comment:
Initialize screen state with unit pointer and screen parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Store unit pointer parameter (pUnit from ECX) to global g_pCurrentUnit
2. Set global g_nSelectedScreen to 6 (screen index constant)
3. Store screen parameter (dwScreenParam from EDX) to global g_nScreenParam
4. Set global g_dwScreenState to 6 (active/initialized state)
5. Return to caller

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny *): Pointer to unit/entity structure for current screen context
dwScreenParam (uint): Screen parameter value determining screen configuration

Returns:
void - No return value, updates global screen state variables

Special Cases:
Magic number 6 indicates active screen context state in Diablo II UI system

functions.name: InitializeGameScreen
functions.comment:
Initialize game screen state variables.

Algorithm:
1. Clear g_dwInitializationFlag to 0
2. Set g_nSelectedScreen to 6 (target screen identifier)
3. Store dwScreenParam in g_nScreenParam for later use
4. Calculate g_dwScreenState based on nInitFlag: (nInitFlag != 0) evaluates to 1 if true, 0 if false
5. Add 7 to boolean result, yielding 7 for uninitialized (false) or 8 for initialized (true)

Parameters:
dwScreenParam (dword) - Screen identifier passed via ECX register (__fastcall)
nInitFlag (int) - Initialization flag passed via EDX register; 0 = not initialized, non-zero = initialized

Returns:
void - Updates four global state variables (g_dwInitializationFlag, g_nSelectedScreen, g_nScreenParam, g_dwScreenState)

Special Cases:
- Screen state is calculated as boolean + 7 offset to generate distinct state codes (7 or 8)
- Initialization flag is unconditionally cleared to prevent re-initialization

functions.name: SetGameStateForUnit
functions.comment:
Set game screen state based on unit parameter.

Algorithm:
1. Store unit ID in global g_pCurrentUnit (ECX register value)
2. If unit ID is 0:
   - Set g_dwScreenState = 1 (player state)
   - Set g_nSelectedScreen = 5 (inventory screen)
   - Set g_nScreenParam = 0 (no parameter)
   - Return
3. If unit ID is non-zero:
   - Set g_nSelectedScreen = 5 (inventory screen)
   - Set g_nScreenParam = 0 (no parameter)
   - Set g_dwScreenState = 4 (alternate game state)
   - Return

Parameters:
nUnitId - Unit identifier (via ECX register, __fastcall)

Returns:
void - Updates global game state variables

Special Cases:
- Unit ID 0 triggers player state (g_dwScreenState = 1)
- Non-zero unit ID triggers alternate state (g_dwScreenState = 4)
- Both paths set inventory screen (5) and zero parameter

functions.name: GetLastError
functions.comment:
Returns the last Storm error code.

Algorithm:
1. Read the global error code variable (g_dwLastError)
2. Return the value to caller

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- Last error code set by SetLastError or 0 if none

Related Functions:

functions.name: InitializeUICursorResources
functions.comment:
Initialize UI cursor resources and screen state for game window.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current window handle via Ordinal_10027
2. Process 3 message entries to register cursor resources  
3. Iterate through 7 cursor definition pointers (Gaunt, etc.)
4. For each cursor: format resource path using wsprintfA with UI_CURSOR template
5. Concatenate path and load resource file via ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile, store result
6. Initialize screen state globals: screen mode, selected screen (5), resource IDs
7. Capture current tick count for frame timing
8. Calculate screen center coordinates (width/2, height/2)
9. Return success code (1)

Parameters:
nMode - uint (__fastcall ECX): Window mode/state identifier passed to resource loader

Returns:
uint - Success code (1 = success)

Special Cases:
- Iterates exactly 7 cursor pointer entries (stride 0x1c bytes)
- Hardcoded screen ID 5 (main game screen)
- Screen width/height calculated at runtime via globals
- Null check on ConcatenatePathAndWriteFile results stored directly (no error handling)

Magic Numbers:
0x3 - Message entry count (3 entries)
0x1c - Cursor pointer stride (28 bytes = 7 dwords)
5 - Screen ID constant
0x6fbd823c - Loop terminator address (points past last cursor pointer)

functions.name: ProcessAndReportValidationErrors
functions.comment:
Process and report all validation errors collected during game initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Push ESI register (callee-saved)
2. Get application window handle via Ordinal_10027 (Storm.GetWindowHandle)
3. Process 3 message entries via ProcessMessageArray (display UI messages)
4. Clear validation state flag (g_dwValidationState = 0)
5. Initialize pointer to start of error array (g_pValidationErrors)
6. Loop while pointer < end of error array (0x6fc040f8):
   a. Load error code from current array position
   b. Test if non-zero (error present)
   c. If zero, skip to next (JZ)
   d. If non-zero, call ReportValidationError(errorCode)
   e. Clear error entry (set to 0)
   f. Advance pointer by 4 bytes
7. Pop ESI and return

Parameters:
None. Uses global error array g_pValidationErrors.

Returns:
void. Clears all validation errors and reports them to the application window.

Special Cases:
- Error array is fixed size (48 bytes, 12 entries at 4 bytes each)
- Function runs during initialization path only
- Loop is guaranteed to process all 12 error slots even if some are zero

functions.name: UpdateCursorAnimation
functions.comment:
UpdateCursorAnimation - Updates and renders the animated cursor based on current screen state.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate draw position clamped to screen bounds
2. Initialize GFX parameter array and call GfxInterfaceCall84 to draw cursor
3. Validate cursor table size and selected screen index (asserts if invalid)
4. Process state machine: handle cursor animation frame advancement
5. Use randomization for state 1 (idle animation variance)
6. Transition between states based on animation completion
7. Check idle timeout (5 seconds) to trigger screen saver transition

Parameters:
  None (uses globals for cursor state)

Returns: void

functions.name: GetCursorRecord
functions.comment:
Retrieves a cursor record by index with bounds validation.

Algorithm:
1. Assert cursor table size equals NUM_CURSORS (7)
2. Assert cursor index parameter is less than 7
3. Calculate record offset: (index * 7 - index * 8) * 4 + base
4. Load cursor record from g_aCursorRecords table
5. Shift record address left by 8 bits (multiply by 256)
6. Return shifted cursor record address

Parameters:
nCursorIndex (int) - Cursor index, must be 0-6 for valid cursor IDs

Returns:
int - Shifted cursor record address (record_address << 8). Asserts on invalid index.

Special Cases:
- Asserts terminate execution if table size != NUM_CURSORS
- Asserts terminate execution if index >= NUM_CURSORS (7)
- Uses lea/sub to compute (index*7 - index*8) = -index offset pattern

functions.name: ProcessScreenResourceDrawing
functions.comment:
Process the current screen's resource drawing operation.
Initializes a CEL context buffer, loads the appropriate resource data,
and delegates rendering to screen-specific handlers based on current state.

Algorithm:
1. Check if UI is initialized (g_bUIInitialized != 0)
2. If screen state is out of range or initialization flag is not set:
   - Call screen-specific handler from g_apfnScreenHandlers table
3. Otherwise:
   - Zero-initialize a local 18-dword CEL buffer (72 bytes)
   - Call FUN_6fb968e0 to load CEL context data from initialization flag
   - If load successful, call Ordinal_10055 (D2Common.GetCelCount) with buffer
   - Assert buffer[0] is non-zero (CEL context must be valid)
   - Get CEL width via Ordinal_10038 (D2Common.GetCelWidth)
   - Get CEL height via Ordinal_10037 (D2Common.GetCelHeight)
   - Call FUN_6fb91bf0 to render with calculated position and dimensions

Parameters:
None - Uses global variables:
  g_bUIInitialized - UI ready flag
  g_dwInitializationFlag - Resource initialization state
  g_dwScreenState - Current screen mode (0-7 valid)
  g_nSelectedScreen - Active screen index
  g_wResourceID - Resource identifier
  g_wResourceFlags - Resource flags

Returns:
void - Delegates to screen-specific handlers or renders directly

Special Cases:
- If CEL context buffer is invalid (buffer[0] == 0), triggers assertion failure
- Screen state values 5-7 and 8+ are out of range and skip rendering
- CEL width/height are right-shifted by 1 bit in calculations

functions.name: SetCursorPositionInWindow
functions.comment:
Sets the cursor position within a window's client area with validation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nX >= 0 (assertion if negative, exits with code -1)
2. Validate nY >= 0 (assertion if negative, exits with code -1)
3. Query window mode state via Ordinal_10028 (Storm.dll, likely IsWindowMode)
4. If in window mode (result == 0):
   a. Obtain active window handle via Ordinal_10027 (Storm.dll, likely GetActiveWindow)
   b. Retrieve window rectangle using GetWindowRect
   c. Get screen metrics: metric 4 = screen height, metric 7 = screen width
   d. Calculate adjusted cursor position: (screen_width + window.left + nX, screen_height + window.top + nY)
   e. Call SetCursorPos with calculated absolute coordinates
5. If in fullscreen mode (result != 0):
   a. Call SetCursorPos with coordinates as-is
6. Store nY in g_wResourceFlags and nX in g_wResourceID (UI state tracking)

Parameters:
  nX: int - X coordinate (cursor column) - must be non-negative (0x306 assertion)
  nY: int - Y coordinate (cursor row) - must be non-negative (0x307 assertion)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Assertions fail with FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) if coordinates negative
  - Window mode detected by Ordinal_10028() == 0
  - Fullscreen mode bypasses window rectangle adjustments
  - Global state updated: g_wResourceID and g_wResourceFlags store params for UI tracking

Magic Numbers:
  - 0x306: Line number for nX validation assertion error
  - 0x307: Line number for nY validation assertion error
  - 0xffffffff: Exit code (-1) on assertion failure
  - Metric 4: Screen height (GetSystemMetrics parameter)
  - Metric 7: Screen width (GetSystemMetrics parameter)

functions.name: SearchGfxInfoList
functions.comment:
Search graphics info list for entry matching search value

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve graphics info structure via GetGfxInfoPointer(dwGfxInfoId)
2. Verify pointer is not NULL (assertion on failure)
3. Load linked list head from graphics info offset +0x2c
4. While current node is non-NULL:
   - If node field at offset +0x4 equals dwSearchValue, return 1 (found)
   - Advance to next node via offset +0xa4
5. Return 0 if list exhausted (not found)

Parameters:
ECX/dwGfxInfoId - Graphics info identifier
EDX/dwSearchValue - Value to search for in list entries (compared at offset +0x4)

Returns:
1 if entry found
0 if entry not found or list empty

Special Cases:
NULL graphics info pointer causes assertion failure and program termination
Assumes linked list is properly NULL-terminated at last node

Magic Numbers:
0x2c - Offset of list head pointer within graphics info structure (0xb dwords)
0x4 - Offset of search field within each list node
0xa4 - Offset of next pointer within each list node (0x29 dwords)

functions.name: ProcessUnitSlotAnimation
functions.comment:
Process animation slot for unit with mode-specific state updates.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve graphics information pointer for unit (offset 0x0)
2. Assert pointer is valid, abort if NULL
3. Get current tick count (elapsed game time)
4. Locate animation slot in unit's slot list (traverse offset 0xa4 chain)
5. Skip slots with matching tick count (0x2c offset) to find next pending
6. Update slot's tick time to current tick (0x2c = dwCurrentTick)
7. Branch on slot type (*pSlotData offset 0x0):
   - Type 0: Validate against FUN_6fb95870 result, remove if mismatch
   - Type 1: Decrement counter (offset 0x8), cleanup when zero
   - Type 2: Cleanup if counter (offset 0x8) is zero
   - Type 6: Check time delta between now and offset 0xc, set counter to 1 if exceeded
   - Type 8: Call Ordinal_10487 to validate mode, increment counter (0x8) if field 0xf set (max 0x32)
8. Add frame delta (offsets 0x18 += 0x14 + 0x18) to slot
9. Check overflow against max (offset 0x1c):
   - Type 1/3/8: Wrap by subtracting max
   - Type 2: Reset counter to zero
   - Type 4: Call FUN_6fb8fb90, trigger mode updates via FUN_6fb931f0
   - Type 5: Reset frame progression, set counter
   - Type 6: Reset counter, reset frame position, cache current tick
   - Type 7: Cleanup and spawn mode 0x8c/0x8d
   - Type 9: Cleanup and dispatch mode updates with param
10. Loop to next slot

Parameters:
pUnitData - uint * - Unit pointer (IMPLICIT ECX) containing graphics info chain

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Aborts with error if graphics info NULL
Ordinal_10487 returns mode validity (0=invalid, nonzero=valid)
Note: Function uses stack temporaries optimized away during decompilation

Structure Layout (Slot at pSlotData):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | dwType     | uint | Animation slot type (0-9)
0x2c   | 4    | dwTickTime | uint | Last processed tick count
0x8    | 4    | dwCounter  | uint | Mode-specific counter
0xc    | 4    | dwTimeout  | uint | Time reference for type 6
0xe    | 4    | dwModeData | uint | Type 8 mode parameter
0xf    | 4    | dwFlags    | uint | Control flags (0xf=1 means increment)
0x14   | 4    | dwFrameAdd | uint | Frame delta per update
0x18   | 4    | dwFramePos | uint | Current frame position
0x1c   | 4    | dwFrameMax | uint | Maximum frame value
0xa4   | 4    | pNext      | ptr  | Next slot in chain

Magic Numbers:
0x2c - Tick time field offset in slot
0x8  - Counter/duration field offset in slot
0x32 - Maximum counter value for type 8 (50 in decimal)
0xb  - First slot pointer offset from graphics info
0xa4 - Next slot pointer offset (linked list chain)

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fb95870() - Validate slot state (type 0)
- FUN_6fb8fb90() - Remove animation slot
- Ordinal_10487() - D2Common ordinal, validates mode for type 8
- FUN_6fb931f0() - Send mode update packets
- FUN_6fb8faa0() - Handle counter overflow (type 8)

functions.name: ProcessTimedSpellEffect
functions.signature: void ProcessTimedSpellEffect(dword dwUnitId, int * pContainer, int * pSpellData)
functions.comment:
Process timed spell effect - manages lifecycle and node ordering of active timed spell effects

Algorithm:
1. Load spell time duration from spell data at offset +0x38
2. Check if spell timer is active (Ordinal_10487) - returns nonzero if active
3. If active, disable spell state (Ordinal_10486 with param 0)
4. Check if spell duration has expired (Ordinal_10503) - returns 0 if expired
5. If expired (iVar5==0), clear spell data field at +0x08 and reset active flag
6. First loop: scan container nodes starting at pContainer[0x2c]
   - Find nodes matching spell time with type==8 (timed effect)
   - Reset field[0xf]=0 and field[2]=-1
7. Second loop: find min/max timed effect times among active nodes
   - Track minimum time in iVar4 and maximum time in iVar5
8. Third loop: mark target node with field[0xf]=1, field[2]=0
   - Uses iVar5 if varied, else defaults to iVar4

Parameters:
- dwUnitId (ECX): Unit identifier, 32-bit value
- pContainer (EDX): Pointer to container with node list at offset +0x2c
- pSpellData (Stack[0x4]): Pointer to spell data, duration at offset +0x38

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x38: Spell duration offset in spell data structure
- 0x2c: Container node list head offset
- 0x08: Spell data clear field offset
- 0xf: Timed effect flag field offset
- 0x2: Type field offset (value 8 = timed effect)
- 0xa4: Next node pointer offset (linked list)
- 0x29: Next node pointer offset (iteration)

functions.name: RemoveAudioContextFromGfxList
functions.comment:
Removes an audio context node from the linked list in GFX info structure

Algorithm:
1. Get GFX info pointer for the specified index; assert if null
2. Initialize current pointer to head of linked list (offset 0x2c), previous to null
3. Traverse list comparing each node until matching target context
4. When found, unlink: if first in list, update head; else update previous node's next
5. If node has audio context (offset 0x40), remove it from audio list first
6. If node type is 8, call cleanup handler
7. Signal resource change via Ordinal_10043 (Storm.dll resource cache invalidation)

Parameters:
nGfxIndex - Graphics engine index for GFX info structure
pContextToRemove - Target audio context node to unlink from list

Returns:
void - Always succeeds (asserts if GFX info invalid)

Special Cases:
- Assertion failure if GFX info pointer is NULL (line 0x1b0)
- Early exit if list empty or target not found
- Automatic audio context cleanup before unlinking

Ordinal Calls:
Ordinal_10043(0x1d2, 0) - Storm.dll: Resource cache invalidation notification

Magic Numbers:
0x2c - Offset of linked list head in GFX info structure
0xa4 - Offset of next pointer in linked list node
0x40 - Offset of audio context pointer in node
0x10 - Offset of audio context field (check in field access)
0x8 - Node type indicator for cleanup operation
0x1d2 - Ordinal parameter (resource invalidation code)

functions.name: GetGfxNodeByID
functions.comment:
Search graphics node list by ID, return node data pointer or NULL

Algorithm:
1. Get graphics info structure for given graphics type
2. Assert graphics info exists; abort if NULL
3. Get head of node linked list from graphics info offset 0x28
4. While node pointer non-NULL:
   a. Check if node's first field (offset +0) equals search ID
   b. If match found, break from loop
   c. Otherwise advance to next node at offset +0x10
5. If node not found, return NULL (EAX = 0)
6. If node found, load node data pointer from offset +0x8
7. Return value from node data at offset +0x14, abort if NULL

Parameters:
  nGfxType (ECX, int) - Graphics type ID passed to GetGfxInfoPointer
  nNodeID (EDX, int) - Node ID to search for in linked list

Returns:
  EAX (int *) - Pointer to node data (from offset 0x8) at offset 0x14, or NULL if not found

Special Cases:
  - Asserts and aborts if graphics info NULL (first assertion)
  - Asserts and aborts if node found but node data at offset 0x14 is NULL (second assertion)
  - Returns 0 if search ID not found in any node

Structure Layout (Graphics Node):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | nNodeID    | int  | Node identifier to search
0x08   | 4    | pNodeData  | void*| Pointer to node data structure
0x10   | 4    | pNext      | void*| Pointer to next node in list
0x14   | 4    | nData      | int  | Return value data

functions.name: SearchInventoryItemByStatAndLevel
functions.signature: int * SearchInventoryItemByStatAndLevel(GfxCell * pGfxInfo, int nLevel, int nStat)
functions.comment:
Searches inventory item list for entry matching stat and level values.

Algorithm:
1. Get graphics info pointer from pGfxInfo parameter via GetGfxInfoPointer
2. Validate pointer not NULL, assert and terminate on failure with error code
3. Check if nStat equals -1 (auto-detect mode)
4. If nStat == -1, retrieve default stat from item using FUN_6fb95870(pGfxInfo)
5. Load head of inventory item list from GfxCell structure offset 0x28
6. Loop through linked list of items:
   a. Check if current node is NULL (end of list), return NULL if so
   b. Check if node[0] (item level) matches nStat parameter
   c. Check if node[1] (item stat) matches nLevel parameter
   d. Both conditions satisfied, return pointer to matching item node
   e. Otherwise advance to next node via offset [node+0x10]
7. Return NULL if no matching item found in list

Parameters:
pGfxInfo (GfxCell*) - Graphics info structure containing inventory list
nLevel (int, EDX) - Item level to match
nStat (int, stack) - Item stat to match; -1 triggers auto-detection

Returns:
int* - Pointer to matching inventory item node structure, NULL if not found

Special Cases:
nStat parameter equals -1 for default stat auto-detection
NULL graphics pointer triggers assertion and process termination
Empty inventory list or no matching items returns NULL

functions.name: GetGfxUnitRecord
functions.signature: int * GetGfxUnitRecord(int * pUnitAny, int nItemId, int nGfxSlot)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a graphics unit record from the GFX data structure matching item ID and slot.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit type from param_1 (0=normal, 1=quest, 2=unique)
2. Resolve nGfxSlot to actual graphics index if -1 (use unit's current index)
3. Branch on unit type:
   - Type 1 (quest): Call FUN_6fb90660 setup, iterate pGfxInfo[10] list for record matching nGfxIndex and nItemId
   - Type 0 (normal): Verify not already quest, call FUN_6fb8fef0 for COF data, call FUN_6fb96ec0 setup, iterate pGfxInfo[10] for match
   - Type 2 (unique): Call FUN_6fb90890 setup, iterate pGfxInfo[10] for match
4. Return matching record pointer or NULL if not found

Parameters:
  pUnitAny (int *) - pointer to unit object
  nItemId (int) - item ID to match (slot index in quest/unique lists)
  nGfxSlot (int) - graphics slot index (-1 to use unit's current slot)

Returns:
  int * - pointer to graphics unit record containing item ID and slot info, or NULL if not found

Special Cases:
  - If nGfxSlot is -1, fetched from unit's current graphics index via FUN_6fb95870
  - Quest units (type=1) directly search graphics records
  - Normal units (type=0) require COF (CODE OF FRAME) data initialization before search
  - Unique units (type=2) follow same search pattern as quest units
  - Function asserts on missing gfx info structure (should never happen)

functions.name: InsertGfxUnitRecord
functions.signature: int InsertGfxUnitRecord(UnitAny * pUnit, dword * pdwRecordId, int nSlotIndex)
functions.comment:
Inserts a graphics unit record into the rendering system hash table.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input unit exists in data table via SearchUnitInDataTable
2. Get graphics state value for the specified slot via GetUnitGraphicsValue
3. Initialize COF data using PrepareCharacterCOFData
4. Retrieve graphics info pointer for the unit via GetGfxInfoPointer
5. Search for existing record in linked list by slot ID
6. If no existing record, allocate new 0x14-byte record node via FogMemAlloc
7. Check unit type to select correct data table (player vs monster)
8. Extract filename from path and compute hash via ComputeStringHash
9. Look up COF data in hash table using computed hash
10. If not found in cache, create new entry via AllocateCofDataUnit
11. Link new record to graphics info list head
12. Verify insertion by searching the linked list for the new record

Parameters:
    pUnit (UnitAny*) - ECX: Pointer to the unit to insert graphics record for
    pdwRecordId (dword*) - EDX: Output pointer to receive the record ID
    nSlotIndex (int) - Stack: Slot index for graphics record (-1 for auto)

Returns:
    int - Pointer to the COF data record on success, 0 on failure

Ordinal Dependencies (in callee functions):
    Ordinal_10042 (D2Common.GetItemData) - Item data table lookup
    Ordinal_502 (Storm.SFileReadFile) - MPQ file read for COF loading
    Ordinal_10885 (D2Common) - Unit state validation

Error Handling:
    Triggers FogAssert on null unit, null path buffer, or null graphics info
    Calls ReportError with code -1 on allocation failure or lookup failure

functions.name: AllocateCofDataUnit
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a COF (Component Object File) data unit for a D2 graphics animation.

Algorithm:
1. Extract file extension from input filename using string search
2. Validate filename length < MAX_COFDATA_FILENAME (0x50 bytes)
3. Convert extension string to hash code via ComputeStringHash
4. Check if unit already exists in hash table by comparing extension hash + extension code
5. If duplicate found, return NULL
6. If new unit: allocate 0x1c bytes, zero-fill, set flags
7. Copy filename extension to allocated structure
8. Read COF file header data via ReadAndProcessFileData and validate direction count <= 0x40
9. Insert new node into hash table at computed position
10. Update global node counter with allocation size
11. Return new allocated node pointer

Parameters:
nHashTableIndex - [ECX] Hash table base offset from param_1 + 0xc
lpszFilename - [EDX] Pointer to filename string (includes path and extension)
IMPLICIT: bExtBuffer - 0x200 byte filename extension buffer
IMPLICIT: dwExtensionCode - 0x100 byte secondary processing buffer

Returns:
EAX = pointer to allocated COF data unit (dword[8]) on success
EAX = NULL if unit already exists or allocation fails

Special Cases:
FogMemAlloc - allocation size 0xde used for COF unit allocation
Magic constant 0x1c = allocation header size (added to node counter)
Hash computation uses triple XOR folding: (val & 0x1ff0000 ^ val >> 8) >> 8 ^ val & 0x1ff00 >> 8 ^ val & 0x1ff
Direction count validation checks byte at offset +0x2 <= 0x40

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x50 (80) - Maximum COF filename length limit
0x40 (64) - Maximum direction count in COF header
0xde (222) - COF data unit allocation size (FogMemAlloc parameter)
0x1c (28) - COF header size added to node counter
0x1ff0000, 0x1ff00, 0x1ff - Hash computation mask constants
0xc, 0x10 - Field offsets in allocated structure

Structure Layout (COF Data Unit):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0      | 4    | pNext      | dword* | Next node in hash chain
4      | 4    | dwFlags    | dword  | Flags (bit 0 = initialized)
8      | 4    | piFileData | int*   | File handle or memory pointer
12     | 4    | dwExtHash  | dword  | Extension hash code
16     | 4    | dwExtCode  | dword  | Extension code from hash
20     | 4    | pFileHdr   | dword* | COF file header pointer
24     | 4    | reserved   | dword  | Reserved/padding

Assembly-Only Variables (Phantom):
bTerminator (Stack[-0x105]:1) - String terminator byte
abPathBuffer (Stack[-0x207]:4) - Path buffer array
local_20d (Stack[-0x20d]:1) - Temporary storage

Related Functions:
ComputeStringHash - Hash computation (Storm ordinal 502)
FogMemAlloc - D2Common allocator (Storm ordinal 10042)
ReadAndProcessFileData - File reader (Storm ordinal 10038)
InsertGfxUnitRecord - Caller that uses returned unit

functions.name: RemoveGraphicsListNode
functions.comment:
Remove graphics list node by search value.

Algorithm:
1. Get graphics info pointer from graphics ID (nGfxId in ECX)
2. Assert pointer is not NULL; terminate if NULL
3. Load list head pointer from gfx info + 0x28 (offset to linked list head)
4. Loop through linked list comparing node[8] with search value (nSearchValue in EDX)
5. When match found, unlink node from list:
   - If previous node exists (dwPrevNode != 0): update previous[0x10] = current[0x10]
   - If head node (dwPrevNode == 0): update gfxInfo[0x28] = current[0x10]
6. Call Ordinal_10043(0x363, 0) for notification/logging
7. Return 1 on success (node removed), 0 if not found

Parameters:

functions.comment:
Render unit sprite graphics within adjusted viewport coordinates with animation frames.

Algorithm:
1. Get graphics info pointer from unit; assert if invalid
2. Get root graphics node from info block; return if none exists
3. Determine coordinate mode (normal or transformed):
   - If mode 0 or (mode 4 with animation state 3): calculate base viewport offsets
   - Else: apply coordinate transformation using Ordinal_10330/10327, adjust for scroll mode
4. Adjust Y coordinate by image offsets (FUN_6fb97a30, FUN_6fb97a50, FUN_6fb97a70)
5. If param_6 != 0, subtract 8 from Y coordinate
6. Iterate through graphics node chain (offset 0x29 to next):
   - Check visibility: skip if node type 6/8 with empty data or node has zero color
   - Skip if param_3 == 0 and node color index is zero
   - If visible: retrieve image subtype (piVar10[6]>>8), load stats with Ordinal_10591
   - Clear 44-byte stat buffer (local_48)
   - Call FUN_6fb968e0 to get render parameters with IMPLICIT piVar16=-1, piVar14=&param_4
   - If render result != 0:
     * Check image height against max height
     * If color mode enabled and stat color flag 0x7d set: get green blood palette
     * Call Ordinal_10072 to render image at (X+local_54+iVar2, Y+local_58)

Parameters:
- pUnit (ECX): Pointer to unit data structure containing graphics pointer
- dwPaletteMode (EDX): Palette/lighting mode applied during rendering
- nBaseX (Stack[0x4]): Base X coordinate for viewport
- nBaseY (Stack[0x8]): Base Y coordinate for viewport  
- nOffsetX (Stack[0xc]): X offset within viewport
- nOffsetY (Stack[0x10]): Y offset within viewport

Returns:
- void: Function renders directly via Ordinal_10072 calls

Special Cases:
- Assertion failure: Graphics info pointer null or stats lookup fails
- Early return: No graphics nodes exist for unit
- Coordinate adjustment: Screen width >> 2 with sign extension for scroll modes 1/2
- Animation: param_5 == -1 uses base Y; param_4 == -1 uses base X
- Stat buffer: 44 bytes (11 dwords) allocated on stack for animation state

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2c: Graphics info offset from unit pointer
- 0x29: Next graphics node offset
- 0x0b: Graphics node chain root offset in info
- 0x34, 0x3c: Node visibility color indices
- 0x7d: Sprite color mode flag offset in stats
- 0x78: Sprite palette index offset in stats
- 0x4, 0x8, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x24: Node field offsets for dimensions/colors
- 0x12: Loop count for buffer clearing (18 = 44/2.4, effectively clears 44 bytes)
- 0xff: Color mask for palette lookup
- 0x8: Y offset adjustment when param_6 != 0
- 0x10: Default Y offset when param_5 == -1

- Ordinal_10487: Unknown function - validates graphics state; appears to be D2Common ordinal
- State validation flag 0x3f: Bitmask for graphics state validation
- Hash table lookup may fail if unit ID invalid
- Fallback offset 0x84 always accessible from parameter directly

functions.name: ValidateTokenAndGetData
functions.comment:
Validates a token type and retrieves associated data table entry

Algorithm:
1. Extract token type and identifier from pnTokenInfo structure (offsets +0 and +4)
2. Get unit direction via GetUnitDirection for animation state context
3. Call UpdateAnimationModeFromStates to validate and update token fields
4. Perform second direction check and animation mode validation pass
5. Switch on dwTokenType (0=Player, 1=Monster, 2=Item):
   - Type 0: GetPlayerTokenTableEntry(dwTokenId1, 0) - player class data
   - Type 1: GetMonsterDataTableEntry(dwTokenId1, 0) - monster class data  
   - Type 2: GetItemDefinitionByTypeAndIndex(dwTokenId1, 0) - item type data
6. Assert result is non-null; if null, call FogAssert and ReportError(-1)
7. Return data field at offset 0x20 from the resolved table entry

Parameters:
  pnTokenInfo (int *): Pointer to token info structure
    +0x00: dwTokenType - Token type (0=Player, 1=Monster, 2=Item)
    +0x04: dwTokenId - Type-specific identifier index
  IMPLICIT ECX: Contains pnTokenInfo on entry (__fastcall convention)

Returns:
  uint: Value at offset 0x20 of resolved data table entry
  0: If token type is not 0, 1, or 2 (unknown type)
  Does not return: If validation fails (ReportError terminates)

Token Type Values:
  0 - Player token (queries player class data)
  1 - Monster token (queries monster class data)
  2 - Item token (queries item definition data)

Error Handling:
  FogAssert called with source file and line if table lookup returns null
  ReportError(-1) terminates execution on validation failure
  Lines: 0xED (237), 0xF1 (241), 0xF5 (245) for types 0, 1, 2 respectively

Phantom Variables (Decompiler Artifacts):
  extraout_EAX_high1, extraout_EAX_high2: High 3 bytes of EAX after 
  GetUnitDirection returns byte in AL. Used in CONCAT31 to form full dword.
  These are SSA artifacts and cannot be typed to standard builtins.

Called By:
  GetCelContextFromUnit - Retrieves graphics context for unit rendering

functions.name: GetCelContextFromUnit
functions.signature: void GetCelContextFromUnit(dword * pdwUnit, dword dwType, dword dwMode, dword * pdwX, dword * pdwY)
functions.comment:
Retrieves CEL sprite context coordinates from a unit for rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate and zero-initialize 72-byte local buffer for CEL context
2. Call GetCelFileTableIndex to look up CEL file table index for unit type/mode
3. Call LoadOrRetrieveCelFrameData to load CEL frame data from cache or disk
4. Validate CEL data exists; assert and report error if missing
5. Extract X coordinate via GetCelFileTableIndex on loaded CEL data
6. Extract Y coordinate via GetCelModeValue on loaded CEL data
7. Store extracted X/Y to output pointer parameters

Parameters:
  pdwUnit (ECX) - Pointer to unit structure containing type/mode data
  dwType (EDX) - Unit type identifier for CEL lookup
  dwMode (Stack+0x4) - Animation mode for CEL frame selection
  pdwX (Stack+0x8) - Output pointer for CEL X coordinate
  pdwY (Stack+0xC) - Output pointer for CEL Y coordinate

Returns:
  void - Coordinates returned via output pointers pdwX and pdwY

Special Cases:
  - If GetCelFileTableIndex returns 0, function exits without modifying outputs
  - If LoadOrRetrieveCelFrameData fails, function exits without modifying outputs
  - If CEL buffer is null after load, triggers assertion at line 336

Structure Layout (local buffer):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    72    aCelBuffer      Zero-initialized CEL context buffer
  0x2d    1     bInitialized    Initialization flag (set to 1)

Error Handling:
  FogAssert called at 0x6fb95a9a if CEL buffer validation fails
  ReportError(-1) called to log the failure before continuing

functions.name: RenderUnitWithBoundaryValidation
functions.signature: bool RenderUnitWithBoundaryValidation(UnitAny * pUnit, int nScreenX, int nScreenY)
functions.comment:
Render unit graphics with boundary validation against screen dimensions.

Algorithm:
1. Get viewport X offset and adjust screen X coordinate
2. Get viewport Y offset and adjust screen Y coordinate
3. Call RenderUnitComponentGraphics to render unit components at adjusted coordinates
4. If render succeeded, extract unit component data via Ordinal_10379
5. Initialize local component buffer by zeroing 18 integers
6. Get unit flags via Ordinal_10457 and mask to byte
7. Set component data flag and call FUN_6fb95e60 to process component data
8. If processing succeeded, call Ordinal_10055 to get component bounds
9. If bounds found and component index valid:
   - Get component width via Ordinal_10038
   - Get component height via Ordinal_10040, add screen Y offset
   - Get component X offset via Ordinal_10039, add adjusted X
   - Get component X extent via Ordinal_10037
10. Validate bounds: check component fits within screen width
11. Validate bounds: check component doesn't exceed left edge
12. Validate bounds: check component height fits within screen height
13. Return success if bottom edge doesn't exceed screen (EBX + EAX >= 0)

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny *) - Unit instance to render
nScreenX (int) - Screen X coordinate (before adjustment)
nScreenY (int) - Screen Y coordinate (before adjustment)

Returns:
true if unit rendered successfully and all boundary checks pass
false if render failed, bounds invalid, or unit index invalid

Special Cases:
- Returns false if RenderUnitComponentGraphics fails
- Returns false if component data processing fails
- Returns false if no valid components found
- Returns false if any boundary check fails
- Validates against global screen dimensions g_dwScreenWidth and g_dwScreenHeight

Magic Numbers:
0x12 (18) - Component buffer size in integers
0xff - Unit flag mask to extract byte component
-0x1 (0xFFFFFFFF) - Sentinel for component processing
0x1 - Component data presence flag

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | [0]   | int  | Component X position
0x4    | 4    | [1]   | int  | Component Y position
0x8    | 4    | [2]   | uint | Flags/type from Ordinal_10457
0xC+   | 24   | [3-6] | int  | Reserved component data

Note: Function uses stack-allocated temporaries optimized away: local_50 (byte[4]), piVar6, extraout_var

functions.name: ValidateGraphicsOutputBounds
functions.signature: bool ValidateGraphicsOutputBounds(dword dwHandle, int nOffsetX, int nOffsetY, int nAdjustForBorder)
functions.comment:
Validates graphics output bounds against screen dimensions with optional border adjustment.

Algorithm:
  1. Query handle top bound via Ordinal_10038
  2. Query handle left bound via Ordinal_10040
  3. Query handle height dimension via Ordinal_10039, add nOffsetX to result
  4. Query handle bottom bound via Ordinal_10037
  5. If nAdjustForBorder != 0: subtract top bound from height, add top bound to bottom bound
  6. Check if height > g_dwScreenWidth (return false if exceeded)
  7. Check if bottom bound + height < 0 (return false if negative)
  8. Check if (left bound + nOffsetY - top bound) > g_dwScreenHeight (return false if exceeded)
  9. Check if (left bound + nOffsetY + top bound) >= -1 (return this result)

Parameters:
  dwHandle (dword) - Graphics handle for dimension queries
  nOffsetX (int) - Horizontal offset to add to height
  nOffsetY (int) - Vertical offset to add to left bound
  nAdjustForBorder (int) - Non-zero enables border adjustment (subtract/add top bound)

Returns:
  true - All boundary validations passed
  false - Any dimension exceeds screen limits or results in invalid negative bounds

functions.name: ValidateComponentStats
functions.comment:
Validate component statistics data and return success/failure status.

Algorithm:
1. Check component index parameter is within valid range (0-15)
2. Call Ordinal_10369 twice to extract component coordinate data into locals
3. Call Ordinal_11013 twice to normalize component data
4. Switch on component type (local_c value):
   - Case 0: Linear search g_adComponentList for matching component index, return 1 if found, 0 if not
   - Case 1: Call Ordinal_10582 to get stats pointer, add 0x1cd offset, check byte at result == 0x01
   - Case 2: Call Ordinal_10626 to get stats pointer, add 0x161 offset, check byte at result == 0x01
   - Case 4: Check if nComponentIndex == 1
   - Default: Fatal assertion failure
5. Return 1 if validation succeeds, 0 if fails

Parameters:
pComponentData (int *): Pointer to component structure with coordinate data at [0] and [1]
nComponentIndex (int): Component index to validate (0-15, must be < g_dwComponentCount for type 0)

Returns:
1 - Validation passed (component stats are valid/active)
0 - Validation failed (component not found, stats invalid, or index out of range)

Special Cases:
Component type 0 uses linear search through g_adComponentList
Types 1 and 2 require valid pointer returns from ordinal calls
Type 4 only validates if nComponentIndex == 1
Index must be <= 15 (0xf) or assertion is triggered

functions.name: InitializeCofDataUnitInfo
functions.signature: dword InitializeCofDataUnitInfo(int * pUnitInfo, dword dwClassIndex, int nComponentIdx, byte bComponent, dword dwTokenId, int * pCofData, int * pCofActionData, dword * pdwLineNo, dword dwActionIdxOffset, int nLineIdx)
functions.comment:
Initializes a unit's COF (Composite Object Format) data for component rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input pointers (pCofData, pCofActionData) with assertions
2. Store token ID and class index in unit info structure
3. Query monster data table for class-specific rendering parameters
4. Iterate COF line data (9-byte entries) to find matching component ID
5. Extract component layer index from matched line
6. Query monster init stats to determine component mode
7. Fetch component graphics data via GetMonsterComponentData
8. Extract color transform bytes (default 0x20 = space if unset)
9. Validate all required pointers before returning

  dwClassIndex (EDX)    - Monster class index for data table lookup

  pdwLineNo (Stack)     - Pointer to line number output
  dwActionIdxOffset (Stack) - Action index offset for animation lookup

Returns:

  0 (EAX) - Failure, no matching component found in COF lines

  0x08    4     dwTokenId           Token identifier
  0x0C    4     dwClassIndex        Monster class index
  0x1D    1     bTargetComponent    Component ID to match
  0x20    4     dwInitialized       Set to 1 on success
  0x24    4     dwMonsterType       Monster type from pCofData

  0x34    4     pComponentTable     Component lookup table pointer
  0x38    4     dwComponentData     Component graphics code
  0x3C    4     dwLayerIndex        Layer index from lookup
  0x40    4     dwColorTransform    4-byte color transform (RGBA-like)

  0x10 - Maximum valid component ID (16 component types)
  0x09 - COF line entry stride (9 bytes per line)
  0x1C - Offset to COF line array in action data
  0x2B4 - Offset to alternate component mode flag in init stats

functions.name: ValidateCofDataPointer
functions.comment:
Validates that COF data pointer is not NULL, triggers assertion failure if invalid.

2. If not NULL, exit function immediately (valid pointer)

functions.name: GetComponentGraphicsDataByIndex
functions.comment:
Retrieves graphics rendering data for a component from a component graphics array structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters: pbComponentData != NULL and 0 <= dwComponentIndex < 16
2. Initialize result (bGraphicsData = 0) and iteration counter (dwComponentCount = 0)
3. Load component count from array header at pbComponentData[0]
4. If component count > 0, search component array starting at offset 0x1C
5. Load component ID at current position [offset + 0] and compare with dwComponentIndex
6. If match found, extract byte at [offset + 3] and return as result
7. Advance to next component entry (offset += 9 bytes) and increment dwComponentCount
8. If dwComponentCount < array count, repeat from step 5
9. If component not found after all iterations, return 0x00
10. Return graphics data byte (non-zero if found, 0x00 if not found or invalid inputs)

Parameters:
pbComponentData (byte *) - Pointer to component graphics array with header and entries
dwComponentIndex (uint) - Component ID to search (valid range 0-15)
IMPLICIT ECX - First parameter (pbComponentData) in __fastcall convention
IMPLICIT EDX - Second parameter (dwComponentIndex) in __fastcall convention

Returns:
AL (byte) - Graphics rendering byte from found component at array[offset+3], 0x00 if not found

Special Cases:
- NULL pbComponentData triggers assertion at line 0x43B
- dwComponentIndex >= 16 triggers assertion at line 0x43C
- Empty component array (count=0) returns 0x00 without iteration
- Component ID not in array returns 0x00

Component Array Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type     | Description
0x00   | 1    | nComponentCount | byte     | Number of component entries
0x01   | 27   | reserved        | byte[27] | Reserved/padding
0x1C   | 1    | nComponentId    | byte     | Component ID (0-15)
0x1D   | 2    | reserved        | byte[2]  | Padding
0x1F   | 1    | nGraphicsData   | byte     | Graphics data (returned)
0x20   | 5    | reserved        | byte[5]  | Padding
0x25   | 9    | next_entry      | byte[9]  | Next component (9-byte stride)

Magic Numbers:
0x1C (28) - Offset to first component entry in array
0x09 (9) - Component entry size/stride in bytes
0x10 (16) - Maximum component index value
0x03 (3) - Offset of graphics data byte within component entry
0x43B - Assertion line for NULL pointer check
0x43C - Assertion line for index bounds check

functions.name: FindComponentInBuffer
functions.comment:
Searches a component buffer array for a specific component ID and returns associated data.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pbBuffer pointer is not NULL (assertion failure)
2. Validate nComponentId is less than 16 (component limit)
3. Initialize search: bResult = 0, pbSearchPtr = pbBuffer + 0x1c (first entry), dwSearchIndex = 0
4. If buffer contains components (*pbBuffer != 0), enter search loop
5. Loop: Compare current component ID (*pbSearchPtr) with nComponentId target
6. If match found: Extract value from pbSearchPtr[1] and return
7. If no match: Advance pbSearchPtr by 9 bytes (entry size), increment dwSearchIndex
8. If dwSearchIndex exceeds component count (*pbBuffer), return 0 (not found)
9. If no components, return 0 (default)

Parameters:
pbBuffer (byte*): Pointer to component buffer containing count at offset 0, entries at offset 0x1c
nComponentId (dword): Component ID to search for (0-15 range)

Returns:
byte: Component data value if found, 0 if not found or invalid input

Special Cases:
- NULL buffer triggers assertion at line 0x453
- Component ID >= 16 triggers assertion at line 0x454
- Empty buffer (count=0) returns 0
- Overflow protection: stops if search count exceeds buffer capacity

Magic Numbers:
0x1c: Offset to first component entry in buffer (28 bytes header)
0x9: Size of each component entry (9 bytes per entry)
0x10: Maximum component ID value (16 components max)

functions.name: ValidateCofDataPointer
functions.signature: void ValidateCofDataPointer(byte * pbCofBytes, dword dwStrideSize, dword dwComponentIdx)
functions.comment:
Validates COF data buffer pointers for component offset calculations

Algorithm:
1. Check if pbCofBytes is NULL - if so, assert and abort
2. Calculate target address: pbCofBytes + ((pbCofBytes[1] * dwStrideSize + 9 + dwComponentIdx) * pbCofBytes[0] + pbCofBytes[1] + 0x1c)
3. Check if calculated address is NULL - if so, assert and abort
4. Return normally if both validations pass

Parameters:
pbCofBytes - Pointer to COF data buffer (composition byte array)
dwStrideSize - Stride/row size for component indexing calculation
dwComponentIdx - Component index offset to validate access for

Returns:
void - Function returns only if validation succeeds; asserts and aborts on NULL pointers

Special Cases:
- NULL input buffer triggers assertion at line 0x484
- NULL calculated offset triggers assertion at line 0x48c
- Both assertions call FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) which never returns
- Used by RenderUnitComponentGraphics to validate COF structure before graphics rendering

Magic Numbers:
- 0x484 (1156) - First assertion line number
- 0x48c (1164) - Second assertion line number
- 0x1c (28) - Offset adjustment for buffer boundary calculation
- 0x9 (9) - Fixed offset in stride calculation

functions.name: GetComponentDataByIndex
functions.comment:
Searches component data table for matching component index and returns associated value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pbComponentData pointer is not null, else assert
2. Validate dwComponentId is less than 0x10 (NUM_COMPONENTS limit), else assert
3. Initialize pbCurComponent = pbComponentData + 0x1c (offset to first component record)
4. Initialize dwComponentIndex = 0
5. Check if component count at [pbComponentData] is non-zero
6. Loop through component records (stride 9 bytes):
   - Compare current component type at [pbCurComponent] with dwComponentId
   - If match found, return value at offset 4 in component record ([pbCurComponent + 4])
   - Increment dwComponentIndex, advance pbCurComponent by 9 bytes
   - Continue while dwComponentIndex < component count
7. If no match found, assert failure with "0" string
8. Call FUN_6fb9a10f(0xffffffff) for assertion failures (terminates)

Parameters:
pbComponentData (byte *): Pointer to component data structure containing count and component records
dwComponentId (uint): Component index to search for (0-15)

Returns:
byte: Value at offset 4 in matching component record (component data)
Never returns normally - function uses assertions for all error paths

Special Cases:
- pbComponentData == NULL triggers assertion at line 0x496
- dwComponentId >= 0x10 triggers assertion at line 0x497
- Component count == 0 or no match found triggers assertion at line 0x4a3

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 1    | bComponentCount | byte | Number of active components
0x1c   | var  | aComponents | array | Array of component records (stride 9 bytes)

functions.name: SearchUnitInDataTable
functions.comment:
Search unit data in global table by comparing against table entries.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global table count > 0, exit early if empty
2. Initialize table pointer to start of g_pUnitDataTable
3. Loop through each table entry until count exhausted:
   a. Load first value from pUnitData (offset +0)
   b. Load second value from pUnitData (offset +4)
   c. Call Ordinal_10369 (D2Common.GetUnitStat) on pUnitData
   d. Call Ordinal_11013 (unknown transform) with all three values
   e. Compare first loaded value against current table entry [0]
   f. Return 1 (TRUE) if match found
   g. Increment table index and advance table pointer by 4 bytes
4. Return 0 (FALSE) if no match found after exhausting table

Parameters:
  pUnitData (int *) - pointer to unit data structure with at least 8 bytes [+0] and [+4]

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - if matching entry found in table
  0 (FALSE) - if no matches or table empty

Special Cases:
  - Empty table (g_dwUnitDataTableCount = 0) returns 0
  - Early exit on first match prevents checking remaining entries
